Cottonwood Residential manages a growing national multifamily portfolio, and this position sits at the center of how a property actually performs, from resident satisfaction scores to budget adherence to the speed and quality of turns.

The core of the job is leading the maintenance team: assigning and prioritizing work orders, running the make-ready process, and making sure preventative maintenance gets done on schedule rather than deferred until something breaks. You'll also be hands-on when the work calls for it, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, general repairs across the property. This isn't a desk role with occasional walkthroughs. You're managing people, managing vendors, managing inventory, and doing real technical work when the situation requires it.

Vendor oversight matters here. You'll source, schedule, and hold vendors accountable to scope and timelines, while tracking maintenance-related expenses against the property budget. That means purchase orders, cost tracking, and accurate documentation aren't an afterthought. SDS logs, inspection reports, and work order closeouts all fall under your oversight.

Resident experience connects directly to this role. A slow turn or an ignored work order shows up in renewal decisions. The Maintenance Supervisor sets the tone for how quickly and professionally the team responds, and that reputation compounds over time at the property level.

One thing worth understanding about the Conyers submarket: it's seen steady Class B garden-style demand over the past several years, with residents who tend to value responsiveness and community upkeep. A supervisor who can keep occupancy-supporting standards high without overrunning a maintenance budget is genuinely valued here.

What you'll need to be considered

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • At least two years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • At least two years supervising or leading a maintenance team
  • EPA Type II or Universal Certification (required)
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) preferred
  • CAMT certification preferred
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office; Entrata experience is a plus
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly, with assistance for heavier loads
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation

Strong candidates typically come in knowing how to balance urgency with quality. The supervisors who stand out aren't the ones who close the most work orders in a day. They're the ones whose teams close the right ones correctly the first time, who catch deferred maintenance before it becomes a capex surprise, and who develop technicians rather than just directing them.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Waypoint Management Services runs a high-end luxury community in Jacksonville and needs a Maintenance Technician who can keep things running cleanly, respond fast, and treat residents well. The property is growing, and they want someone who takes ownership of their work rather than waiting to be told what to do next.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day centers on service work and preventive care. You'll diagnose and repair problems across plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, and general building systems. Make-readies are a real part of the job: you'll inspect units before move-in, coordinate with contractors on punch list items, and make sure turns are completed to a high standard. Priority work orders get a 24-hour resolution target, which means you need to be organized and efficient, not just technically capable.

Beyond the unit-level work, you'll run routine preventive maintenance on HVAC equipment and community systems, service the pool (including chemical readings), maintain the trash compactor, and confirm that gate and security equipment stays operational. Grounds upkeep falls into your scope too. At a luxury community, the physical condition of the property directly shapes resident perception, so the bar for presentation is higher than average.

You'll be on an on-call rotation, so after-hours emergency response comes with the role. That's a consistent reality here, not a rare exception.

What You Bring

  • EPA Section 608 Type I and II certification (required)
  • Hands-on experience with building repairs across multiple trade areas
  • Working knowledge of OSHA safety standards
  • Ability to handle make-ready inspections and coordinate with outside contractors
  • Strong service orientation and a professional, resident-facing presence
  • CPO certification is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent, plus relevant field experience

Why This Role Is Worth a Hard Look

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, a 401k with matching, an employee referral program, and an onsite housing discount. For someone who wants to live close to where they work, that discount can meaningfully offset cost of living in Jacksonville.

Technicians at luxury communities tend to develop sharper skills faster than peers at Class C or value-add properties, simply because the expectation for quality is higher and the equipment is newer. If you're building toward a lead or maintenance supervisor role, a stint at a high-end community like this carries real weight on a resume. Owners and operators notice the difference between someone who can fix things and someone who can maintain a premium product at a consistent standard.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Nantucket Cove) $2,500 Hiring Bonus
job.description:
This role runs on three core skills: mechanical diagnosis, team coordination, and operational discipline. If those come naturally to you, the day-to-day at Nantucket Cove will feel like a good fit.

What the Work Looks Like

You'll oversee the full maintenance operation at a BAM-managed residential property in Champaign. That means handling HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems yourself when needed, and directing your team through the rest. Preventative maintenance scheduling, make-ready coordination, grounds upkeep, and curb appeal all fall under your watch.

You're also the person who keeps the team sharp. That includes hands-on training, quality checks on completed work, and regular feedback. When a technician is struggling with a repair or a process isn't working, you fix it. The supervisory piece is real here, not just a title bump.

Budget awareness matters too. You'll manage supply purchasing and keep costs in line without cutting corners on quality. Property management companies expect maintenance supervisors to think about the bottom line, and BAM is no different.

Skills That Drive Success Here

  • 2 to 3 years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification (required)
  • Supervisory experience (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable vehicle
  • Strong verbal and written communication, because you'll document work orders and communicate with both residents and management

The candidates who stand out are the ones who can shift between the physical work and the people work without losing pace. You might spend the morning walking a punch list with a technician, then handle a plumbing diagnosis yourself in the afternoon. The ability to do both well is what separates a good maintenance supervisor from a great one.

What's Distinctive About BAM

BAM Companies was founded in 2010 and operates as a third-party property management firm with a culture that's intentionally close-knit. They refer to their employee group as "BAMFAM," which signals something real about how the company is structured internally. The benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus 15.5 paid holidays and PTO that starts after 90 days. There's also a housing discount available for employees who want to live at a BAM property.

Pay for this role ranges from $26 to $30 per hour depending on experience, and the position includes a $2,500 hiring bonus. For a maintenance supervisor role in central Illinois, that's a competitive starting point with room tied directly to what you bring in.

If you've got the certifications, the mechanical background, and the willingness to develop people alongside doing the work yourself, this is a straightforward opportunity to step into a lead role with a company that takes internal growth seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Rover technicians occupy a specific and underrated niche in multifamily maintenance. You're not tied to one property, which means you see more failure modes, more building types, and more management styles in a single year than a site-based tech might encounter in three. For someone building a career in maintenance, that breadth compounds fast.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Property Management Associates runs a large residential portfolio across Beverly Hills and the greater Los Angeles area. In this rover role, you'll move between communities based on where support is needed, so your schedule has real variety. Most days involve a mix of work orders and make-ready work: plumbing calls, drywall patches, appliance repairs, electrical fixes, and getting units punch-list ready for incoming residents. You'll also do routine inspections, catching deferred issues before they turn into expensive problems. Parts and inventory management falls to you as well, which means staying organized and thinking ahead, not just reacting.

You'll coordinate directly with property managers at each site, which requires solid communication. Residents interact with maintenance staff more personally than with almost anyone else at a property, so professionalism on service calls matters as much as technical skill.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in multifamily residential settings
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, drywall, and appliance repair
  • Experience completing apartment turns and make-readies efficiently
  • Strong troubleshooting instincts and the judgment to prioritize competing demands
  • Comfort working independently across multiple sites with minimal supervision
  • A valid driver's license and proof of auto insurance (an auto allowance is included)
  • Physical capability to lift 25 to 50 pounds and stay active throughout a full workday
  • High school diploma or GED

Where This Role Can Take You

Rover technicians who perform well tend to be strong candidates for Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor roles, because they've already proven they can operate across a portfolio without constant direction. Exposure to multiple property types and management teams also builds the kind of institutional knowledge that makes someone valuable in a regional maintenance capacity down the line. PMA has been operating in Southern California for over 30 years with a portfolio of thousands of residential units, so internal advancement is a realistic path rather than a talking point.

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour with a $300 monthly auto allowance, a $25 monthly cell phone allowance, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) with discretionary company contribution after one year, disability coverage, and paid time off.

job.title: Houston Maintenance Hiring Event - Heights/River Oaks/Museum District Areas - Houston
job.description:
Maintenance hiring events exist because the usual application funnel is too slow for operators who need skilled technicians in the field now. Berkshire Residential Investments is running one of these in-person events in Houston, and if you work in apartment maintenance, it's worth understanding what's actually on the table before you show up.

The communities Berkshire is staffing sit in three of Houston's higher-profile submarkets: The Heights, Museum District, and River Oaks. These aren't Class C workforce properties. The residents in these corridors have high expectations for turn quality and response time, which means the technicians who work here get real reps on make-readies that have to be done right, not just done fast.

The Event Details

The career fair is held at The Ivy Apartments, located at 2311 Mid Lane, Houston, TX 77027. It runs on Friday, October 9 from 11:00 AM to 6:30 PM. Berkshire is conducting on-the-spot interviews, so bring a resume and plan to talk through your experience in person. The format favors candidates who can speak concretely about what they've worked on: HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and unit turns.

What This Type of Role Builds

Maintenance technician work at a well-resourced residential company develops a specific kind of professional discipline. The skills you bring in, such as HVAC certification, general trades knowledge, and turn efficiency, get sharpened through volume and variety. What you build on the job is equally important: work order prioritization under real pressure, cross-functional communication with leasing and management teams, and the judgment to know when a repair is a band-aid and when it signals a bigger capital issue.

Technicians who develop that last skill, the ability to spot patterns in recurring maintenance issues and flag them proactively, tend to move into lead tech and maintenance supervisor roles faster than those who treat every ticket as isolated. Berkshire's stated emphasis on career growth and training suggests the infrastructure to support that kind of development, though the pace of advancement always depends on the individual property's needs and the technician's consistency.

  • Roles are based at communities in The Heights, Museum District, and River Oaks
  • On-site interviews are available the day of the event
  • Berkshire cites competitive pay, benefits, and training as part of the offer
  • The company operates across multiple Houston properties, which creates internal transfer and promotion opportunities

If your background is in apartment maintenance and you want to work for a company with enough scale to have real training programs, this event is a direct line to a conversation that typically takes weeks through standard job postings.

job.title: Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
Affordable housing management runs on a different set of rules than conventional multifamily. The compliance layer is thick, the regulatory calendar never really lets up, and residents depend on the property in ways that go well beyond month-to-month convenience. That's the environment this Community Manager role operates in, at a Fairstead property in Boaz, Alabama.

What This Role Actually Involves

The core of the job is keeping a HUD-regulated property running on every dimension at once: occupancy, compliance, finances, and physical condition. On the compliance side, you'll own the full cycle of certifications, annual and interim recertifications included, and you'll need to know the HUD 4350.3 Handbook well enough to write responses to regulatory agencies and work alongside the Compliance Department when residents fall out of lease or program requirements. REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits all land on your desk to prepare for and coordinate.

Financially, you're watching delinquency closely, pursuing collections through the appropriate legal channels, monitoring bad-debt write-offs, and attending monthly budget reviews with your regional team. On the maintenance side, you'll coordinate preventive and emergency work with your Building Superintendent, manage vendor bids and contractor quotes, document unit inspections, and stay in close contact with the construction team if any renovation work is active on site.

Resident-facing responsibilities are woven into every week. Move-in and move-out coordination, lease violation documentation, eviction processing when necessary, and handling the steady stream of questions and requests that residents bring to the office all require consistency and a calm, organized approach.

What Qualifications You'll Need

  • At least three years of management experience that included supervising a team (property management background preferred, though hospitality, retail, or restaurant management is considered)
  • COS or CPO certification is required
  • TCS certification if the property carries a tax credit component
  • Hands-on experience with EIV, and familiarity with Yardi or RealPage
  • Affordable housing program knowledge, particularly HUD-regulated occupancy
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred but not required

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The compliance requirements here are specific and consequential. A candidate who has personally prepared for or sat through a MOR or REAC inspection carries a real advantage over someone who has only worked conventional multifamily. So does someone who understands how EIV discrepancies get resolved, or who has written a response to a regulatory finding. The technical side of affordable housing occupancy is learnable, but coming in with that foundation means you're contributing from the first month rather than spending it getting up to speed on program rules.

Fairstead operates as an integrated owner and manager with a portfolio across 28 states, which means community managers here have access to centralized compliance and construction resources that smaller operators can't offer. For someone looking to grow in affordable housing management, that organizational infrastructure tends to create clearer paths toward regional or portfolio-level roles over time.

job.title: Grounds Specialist - Botanic Miramar Beach ~ Destin, FL
job.description:
Beachside luxury communities like Botanic Miramar Beach carry a visual standard that residents pay a premium to live inside. A single neglected breezeway or a cloudy pool can undercut everything the leasing team works to sell. The Grounds Specialist role exists to make sure that never happens.

This is a daily-presence, eyes-on-the-property position at Davis Development's Destin community. You're walking the grounds throughout each shift, pulling litter, debris, and pet waste from breezeways, pool decks, and common areas before residents notice them. Trash and recyclables get handled on schedule. Pool chemistry gets checked and logged every day, with a full vacuum cycle weekly. Grills get cleaned and their timers and knobs inspected regularly to keep things safe. You'll also pitch in on general labor tasks supporting the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager as needs come up.

Davis Development operates as an owner-operator from the inside out. Their on-site teams aren't executing orders from a distant regional office; they're making real decisions daily. For a grounds role, that means your judgment about what the property needs matters. You notice the things others walk past.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of general labor experience; multifamily background is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) certification preferred
  • Comfortable with hand tools, cleaning equipment, and related supplies
  • Able to lift approximately 50 lbs regularly
  • Strong time management and communication skills across all channels
  • Availability to work over 40 hours per week when the property needs it

What Davis Development Offers

Benefits begin on the first of the month after 30 days of employment and include medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health coverage. The 401(k) plan includes a 4% employer match that vests immediately. Company-paid life insurance at one times base salary, a PTO package with carryover, a company apparel store allowance, and ongoing training and career development round out the package.

One practical note for candidates: Destin's Gulf Coast climate means this role runs outdoors year-round, through humid summers and variable winters. Pace and physical stamina matter here more than they might at an inland Class B community. CPO certification, even if you don't have it yet, is worth pursuing early. Pool compliance is taken seriously at luxury communities, and holding that credential opens up maintenance career paths that pure groundskeeping doesn't.

job.title: Customer Service Coordinator
job.description:
Single-family rental at scale runs on coordination. At Evergreen Residential, a Dallas-based SFR and build-to-rent platform founded in 2021, the Customer Service Coordinator role sits at the intersection of resident relations, maintenance operations, and the kind of real-time problem-solving that keeps portfolios performing. If you've built communication and organization skills in property management or a high-volume service environment, this role puts both to work every day.

Skills This Role Develops and Demands

Resident-facing work in institutional SFR is different from traditional multifamily. You're supporting residents in scattered single-family homes rather than a single property, which means your coordination instincts matter more than walking a leaseup or monitoring foot traffic at a leasing desk. The skills that compound here: triaging inbound calls and escalations, tracking work order pipelines across a service request dashboard, and translating maintenance updates into clear resident communication. You'll also get exposure to smart home technology, including lock access, account setup, and troubleshooting. As SFR operators increasingly differentiate on tech-enabled resident experience, that's a transferable skill set.

The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 9am to 6pm, with Saturday offering a work-from-home option. Occasional evening and overtime hours are part of the role. That's worth knowing before you apply.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day to day, you're handling inbound calls and routing them correctly, supporting residents on portal questions and ledger inquiries, and coordinating with field operations teams to make sure service requests get resolved on time and meet company standards. You'll conduct resident welcome calls, troubleshoot smart home issues, and serve as the internal subject matter expert for maintenance workflow. The ledger work, both prospect and resident-side, gives you exposure to how income and charges flow in a managed SFR portfolio.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • At least one year of administrative or customer service experience; property management background preferred
  • Prior use of property management software is a plus
  • Calm under pressure, especially on escalated calls
  • Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Adobe
  • Strong organization and time management, with consistent follow-through on deadlines
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills

Where This Role Leads

Coordinators who learn the operational rhythm of an institutional SFR platform, work order management, resident lifecycle touchpoints, ledger basics, and tech-enabled service, tend to grow into operations specialist, portfolio coordinator, or assistant property manager roles. At a company like Evergreen, which is still building its operational infrastructure and has leadership with deep SFR institutional roots, there's real exposure to how a modern third-party management platform is structured. That's a different kind of education than you'd get at a legacy multifamily operator. The candidates who stand out here aren't just organized. They read a situation quickly, stay composed when a resident is frustrated, and close the loop without being asked twice.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Property management at this level runs on a specific blend of financial literacy, team leadership, and operational awareness. At The Whit and Ridgewood Arches, a combined 164-unit portfolio in Minneapolis, the Property Manager keeps occupancy healthy, delinquency low, and the physical asset in good shape while developing a site team that actually performs. Bigos Management has earned Star Tribune Top Workplace recognition eleven times, which tells you something about how the company treats its people internally. That culture runs both directions: toward employees and toward residents.

The financial side of this role is real. You're managing rent collection, tracking delinquent accounts, working evictions when necessary, and submitting accurate reports to your Regional Manager. You'll do market research using public-facing sources to inform pricing recommendations. If you've ever prepared a T-12 or watched NOI move based on concession decisions, that mindset applies here. You're not just executing tasks. You're thinking about what the numbers mean for the property's overall health.

What You're Actually Managing Day to Day

On the leasing side, you're overseeing activity to keep occupancy maximized. That means watching traffic, understanding what's driving or limiting conversions, and making sure the site is positioned correctly in the market. On the maintenance side, you're building the turn schedule, coordinating make-ready inspections, managing the punch list process, and working with the roving maintenance team on anything beyond routine upkeep. You'll also monitor preventative maintenance programs and regularly walk the property to assess its condition and appearance.

The leadership piece is direct. You supervise site employees, handle coaching and development, and maintain a team environment consistent with Bigos' core values around relationships, quality, and accountability. Fair housing compliance and workplace safety are non-negotiable components of how you operate.

  • 3 to 5 years of management experience, with property management preferred
  • 1 to 2 years in a Property Manager or supervisory role preferred
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a strong plus
  • CRM designation preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required; degree in property management preferred
  • Active real estate licenses are not permitted in this role
  • Solid grasp of federal fair housing law and applicable local provisions

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Minneapolis has a competitive multifamily market with a wide range of product types. Managing two named communities under one umbrella means you're balancing distinct resident profiles and operational rhythms simultaneously. Managers who excel here tend to be detail-oriented on the financial side without losing sight of the resident experience. They know how to coach a team through a high-turn period without letting quality slip. They read delinquency reports early in the month, not at the end. And they document unit conditions thoroughly because it protects the property and keeps the make-ready process efficient.

The pay range runs $65,000 to $75,000. Bigos offers a competitive benefits package that includes 401(k) with employer match, HSA with employer contribution active from the first of the month after hire, ten paid holidays with no waiting period, PTO with rollover, volunteer time off, life insurance, short and long-term disability, educational assistance, an employee assistance program, a rent discount, and a Life Time Fitness membership discount.

job.title: Lobby Ambassador (Full-Time)- Century Plaza North Tower
job.description:
A resident steps off the elevator at 6 PM carrying dry cleaning and a pizza box, expecting the front desk to hold a package that arrived three hours ago. You already know the package is there. You hand it over before they ask. That's the job.

Action Property Management, one of the largest privately held HOA management companies in the western U.S., is hiring a full-time Lobby Ambassador for Century Plaza North Tower in Century City. This is an evening shift role: Monday through Friday, 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM, paying $22.00 to $23.00 per hour.

Daily Responsibilities

You're the face of the building during the hours when most residents are actually home. The role covers front desk operations, access control, and lobby presentation. You'll log activity in a daily report, field incoming calls, receive and distribute resident parcels, and handle guest and visitor inquiries. Keeping the lobby, front desk area, and main elevators presentable is part of every shift, not just when someone's watching.

You'll also need a working understanding of the association's governing documents. Residents ask about rules, guest policies, and building procedures. You need to answer accurately, not guess.

What the Right Candidate Looks Like

  • At least one year of customer service experience, required
  • Background in hospitality, luxury retail, or fine dining is a real advantage here
  • Hospitality Management students or recent graduates are a strong fit
  • Professional appearance and demeanor, consistently
  • Calm under pressure, solutions-focused, and proactive rather than reactive
  • Must be 18 or older and clear a pre-employment background check and drug screening

The candidate who stands out doesn't wait for a resident to flag a problem. They notice the lobby door isn't latching right, the package locker is nearly full, or a guest has been waiting longer than expected, and they handle it before it becomes a complaint. High-rise HOA environments attract residents with high expectations. Your instinct to anticipate needs, not just respond to them, is what separates good from excellent in this setting.

Action offers medical, dental, vision, pet insurance, a 401(k) with company match, life and disability coverage, paid vacation, sick time, and observed company holidays for qualifying team members.

job.title: Full-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a sales role. That sounds obvious, but plenty of candidates come in expecting a hospitality gig and get surprised by the close rate expectations. At PeakMade, this position is structured around conversion, and the skills you'll use most are the ones that live at the intersection of sales discipline and resident experience.

The Skills This Role Runs On

The core of this job is multi-touch follow-up. Calls, texts, emails, CRM notes, all of it done consistently and quickly. PeakMade is looking for someone who already knows what a pipeline looks like and who doesn't need to be reminded that a lead that goes cold costs the community real money. Strong product knowledge matters here too: pricing, availability, concessions, and a working understanding of the competitive set in the submarket. You're not just selling an apartment, you're selling this apartment over the three other communities a prospect toured this week.

Tour delivery is the other major skill set. High-traffic leasing seasons reward consultants who can read a prospect, build rapport quickly, and create genuine urgency without being pushy. The best performers in this type of role know how to tailor the walk to what the prospect actually said they needed, not just what's on the brochure.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Day to day, you're converting inbound leads across phone, email, and in-person channels, delivering tours, following up with prospects throughout the sales cycle, and maintaining accurate records in whatever CRM platform the community runs (Yardi, Entrata, and RealPage are all mentioned). You'll also handle lease paperwork, deposit collection, and move-in and move-out coordination, so administrative accuracy is part of the job, not an afterthought. During turn season, you'll support the make-ready process alongside the broader team.

  • 1+ year of sales or leasing experience with measurable conversion results
  • Hands-on experience with a property management CRM
  • Demonstrated multi-touch outreach discipline
  • Availability to work weekends and peak leasing hours

What's Worth Knowing About This Role

Student housing leasing, which is PeakMade's primary space, has a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Lease-up activity tends to compress into defined windows, traffic spikes seasonally, and the prospect pool often includes parents as decision-makers alongside the residents themselves. If you've worked conventional garden-style or mid-rise leasing before, the skills transfer cleanly, but the pace and dynamic shift. Strong performers in this environment tend to combine genuine hustle during peak season with the kind of consistent follow-up discipline that keeps prospects engaged over a longer consideration cycle.

The role is commission-eligible, which means your earnings track directly to your closing performance. PeakMade also offers housing discounts (terms vary by community), PTO, wellbeing days, 401(k) match, and growth opportunities into leadership. The Houston location puts you in one of the more active student housing and multifamily markets in the country, which matters for long-term career development in this industry.

job.title: PART TIME Clubhouse Monitor Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
Summerset Estates is a 116-home manufactured housing community in Westminster, CA, managed by Investment Property Group, a firm that operates over 150 properties across 13 states. This part-time Clubhouse Monitor role is straightforward in scope: open and close the clubhouse, laundry room, and pool area on a set weekly schedule, and keep an eye on things in between.

What You'll Actually Do

The schedule runs Monday through Friday evenings for closing duties, plus Saturday and Sunday mornings and evenings for both opening and closing, including holidays. That works out to roughly 10 hours per week. The work itself is hands-on and routine in the best sense: locking up access points each night, testing and logging pool water chemistry, restocking bathroom and kitchen supplies, clearing debris or standing water from the pool deck, and doing a walk-through after any private clubhouse reservation to confirm the space was left properly. You're also the first line of communication if something urgent comes up on the property, with a direct line to the park manager.

This isn't a maintenance or groundskeeping role in the full sense. The job is specifically built around amenity oversight and closure, with some light general tidiness duties layered in. It suits someone who values a predictable, low-drama schedule and takes pride in leaving a space better than they found it.

What You Bring

  • Availability that matches the schedule: weekday evenings and weekend morning and evening shifts, holidays included
  • Reliable transportation to and from the property
  • Ability to pass a background check
  • Genuine dependability. Punctuality matters here because residents expect amenities to open and close on time, every time
  • Comfort working independently without supervision on-site

A Note on the Role

We've seen plenty of amenity-related liability issues trace back to inconsistent closures or missed pool chemistry logs. The person in this role is quietly preventing those problems every shift. Pool deck slip-and-fall incidents and after-hours trespassing tend to spike when oversight is inconsistent, so reliability here carries more weight than the job title might suggest. At $17.50 per hour for a part-time commitment, it works well as a supplemental income position for someone already in the area who wants a structured, low-stress schedule with a stable employer.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
A prospect calls about a two-bedroom at The Westbury, but after a few questions, Champion Hills at Windyke is the better fit. You know both properties well enough to make that call confidently, schedule the tour, and follow up the same day.

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is hiring a full-time Leasing Manager to own the leasing function across two neighboring southeast Memphis apartment communities: The Westbury and Champion Hills at Windyke. Each property has its own Property Manager and Assistant Property Manager, so you're not running operations. You're running leasing. That means traffic, follow-up, applications, move-ins, and occupancy, across both sites, coordinated with two property teams.

The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, with one Saturday off per month. Pay ranges from $25 to $27 per hour, plus $130 commission per move-in and quarterly and annual bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, disability, and other insurance options, a 401(k) with profit-sharing, paid time off, and paid holidays.

What the Job Covers

Day to day, you're responding to leads across every channel, conducting tours, comparing units across two communities with prospects, and moving applications through to approved move-ins. You'll also provide direction and support to the Leasing Consultant assigned to the two-property campus and help coordinate Saturday leasing coverage.

Beyond the front-end sales cycle, you'll assist with renewals, resident relations, leasing paperwork, and file accuracy. You'll keep both property managers informed on leasing activity, priorities, and pipeline.

What MRG Is Looking For

  • At least two years of apartment leasing experience, required
  • Prior experience in a senior leasing, leasing manager, assistant manager, or multi-site leasing role, preferred
  • Strong follow-up habits and organized approach to managing leads and applications
  • Comfortable providing day-to-day guidance to another leasing employee
  • Proficient with CRM software and general computer use
  • Valid driver's license, proof of auto insurance, and reliable transportation
  • Able to pass background, credit, and drug screenings

The candidate who stands out will have handled multi-site or high-volume leasing before, because splitting attention across two communities while keeping both pipelines moving takes a different kind of organization than single-property leasing. If you've managed your own traffic board, coached a junior leasing consultant, and still kept your close rate up, this role fits that profile well.

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is an established Memphis property management company with room to grow for the right person.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Hiring Event, Downtown Los Angeles, October 21st - 10A-4P)
job.description:
Bozzuto is holding an in-person hiring event for Leasing Consultants in Downtown Los Angeles on Wednesday, October 21st, from 10 AM to 4 PM PST. Candidates who attend can interview on the spot, and qualified applicants may receive offers within 48 hours. Bring an updated resume and dress business professional. A recruiter will confirm your spot and share the exact location after you complete a brief intake questionnaire through the application portal.

What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the front line of occupancy. Your job is converting traffic into signed leases, which means the work is equal parts follow-up discipline and genuine hospitality. Every prospect who walks through the door or fills out a form online is a lead you're responsible for. You'll respond quickly, answer questions about the community and surrounding neighborhood with real knowledge, and conduct tours that feel personal rather than scripted. The goal of every tour is a lease, and the best consultants here know how to read a prospect and adapt the pitch accordingly.

Beyond the one-on-one conversations, you'll support the community's social media presence, creating content on platforms like Instagram and Facebook that builds awareness and keeps the property visible to people still in the search phase. On weekends, when foot traffic peaks and prospects are actively shopping, you'll be on-site. The schedule runs three weekends per month with two weekdays off in exchange.

One thing worth knowing about leasing in Downtown LA: the submarket is competitive, with a dense mix of Class A high-rise and mid-rise product and renters who have done their homework before they ever contact you. Strong performers here close on the strength of neighborhood knowledge and follow-through speed, not just personality. If you can speak to walkability, transit access, and local amenities as fluently as you can quote floor plans and concessions, you'll be ahead of most of the field.

What You Bring

  • A track record of customer-facing work where closing or converting was part of the job
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, polished enough for both in-person tours and digital outreach
  • Comfort creating and posting content on Instagram and Facebook for a professional audience
  • Sales instincts, meaning you listen well, identify what a prospect needs, and guide the conversation toward a decision
  • Proficiency with standard software, apps, and property management platforms
  • A professional appearance and the confidence to represent the community from the moment someone walks in

Compensation and Benefits

Base salary runs $48,000 to $55,000, with additional bonus opportunities tied to performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Bozzuto also maintains a range of employee resource groups for those who want connection beyond their immediate team.

For candidates interested in a longer career arc, leasing roles at well-operated properties like those in the Bozzuto portfolio are a direct path toward Assistant Manager and Property Manager positions. The skills you build here, reading traffic reports, understanding lease conversion rates, managing resident relationships, translate directly into the operational and financial responsibilities of site leadership.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Maintenance roles at well-run, owner-operated communities tend to look different from positions at large third-party management shops. When the company owns what you maintain, there's more consistency in how things get done, clearer expectations, and less friction between the people making decisions and the people doing the work. That's the environment this role sits in.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

You'll be based at The Union Apartments in West Nashville, handling the full range of residential maintenance across occupied and vacant units. Work orders, make-readies, and turns will make up a significant part of your routine. Beyond that, you'll troubleshoot and repair HVAC systems, electrical issues, plumbing, appliances, and carpentry items. Pool areas, grounds, and shared amenities fall under the team's collective responsibility too, so this isn't a role where your work stops at the apartment door.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with participation in a rotating on-call schedule. On-call weeks include a flat $150 payment regardless of whether calls come in, plus additional pay for holiday coverage. That kind of predictable structure matters when you're weighing whether a role fits your life outside of work.

What Weinstein Properties Is Looking For

  • At least 3 years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Certification (Type II or Universal) required
  • Hands-on HVAC troubleshooting and repair skills
  • Comfortable working independently and as part of a team
  • Able to lift up to 75 lbs and work indoors and outdoors year-round
  • Reliable transportation and basic comfort with digital work order systems
  • Strong communication and a genuine customer service orientation

That last point carries real weight here. Residents interact with maintenance staff more personally than almost anyone else on a property team. How you handle a frustrated resident whose AC isn't working at 4pm on a Friday, or how you leave an apartment after a work order, shapes how people feel about where they live. Technicians who take that seriously tend to fit well in communities like this one.

Stability, Pay, and Where This Can Lead

The base rate starts at $25/hour and moves up depending on experience, with quarterly bonuses tied to property and team performance. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, a 401(k) with company match, PTO, paid holidays, a birthday day off, an employee assistance program, a referral program, and a rent discount.

For technicians who want to grow, owner-operated companies with consistent standards and in-house management tend to be the clearest path toward a Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor role. When leadership knows the portfolio intimately and promotes from within, advancement is less about waiting for an opening and more about building a track record. That kind of environment rewards reliability and skill over time in ways that don't always happen at larger, more transactional operations.

A background check is required as part of the hiring process.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
The Overlook at Sugar Hill needs a leasing consultant who understands that occupancy is built one conversation at a time. This is a front-line sales and service role where your daily traffic numbers, conversion rate, and follow-up habits directly shape the community's performance. Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country, runs a purpose-driven culture they call "Live It." That culture starts at the leasing desk.

What You'll Actually Do

Your mornings typically start with incoming leads from the previous evening: web inquiries, voicemails, emails. You respond quickly, because speed-to-contact is one of the most predictable factors in lead conversion. From there, the day moves between tours, application processing, and follow-up calls to prospects still deciding. You're not just showing apartments; you're reading what matters to each prospect and connecting the community's lifestyle to their specific needs.

  • Conduct personalized tours and respond to phone, email, and web inquiries with urgency
  • Convert leads to signed leases through consistent follow-up and relationship-building
  • Complete leasing applications, verification paperwork, and move-in documentation accurately
  • Support occupancy and renewal goals alongside the community management team
  • Coordinate and participate in resident events that drive retention
  • Monitor competitor properties and local market activity to stay sharp on positioning
  • Assist with social media and outreach marketing for the community

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Saturdays from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. One weekday off per week keeps the total at 40 hours. Occasional evening availability may be needed for resident events.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Confidence communicating in person, by phone, and in writing
  • A natural ability to handle objections and guide prospects toward a decision
  • Comfort with leasing software and digital communication channels
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP certification is a plus, not a prerequisite

Trajectory and Compensation

Hawthorne operates a structured Career Path Program, and the leasing consultant role is a known entry point into assistant community manager positions. That promotion typically comes with exposure to budgets, delinquency management, and NOI reporting. Getting there means building a track record in leasing conversion and resident satisfaction first.

Compensation combines an hourly base with monthly leasing and renewal commissions, plus performance incentive programs. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

What separates strong candidates here is follow-through. Plenty of people can give a good tour. The consultants who actually move the occupancy needle are the ones who call back the undecided prospect on day three, who remember what the prospect said about their commute or their dog, and who treat every renewal conversation with the same energy as a new lease. That's the difference between filling apartments and building a community.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community Manager roles exist on a spectrum. At one end, you're essentially a leasing coordinator with a fancier title. At the other end, you're running a real operation: managing people, reading financials, navigating compliance, and making decisions that affect how hundreds of residents experience their homes. This role at Avanath in Stockton sits firmly at the latter end of that spectrum.

What You'll Actually Do

The core of this position is full-site ownership of an affordable housing community. That means you're accountable for occupancy, delinquency, the budget comparison, capex coordination when applicable, subsidy voucher submissions, and the monthly financials your regional manager relies on. You're also the person your team looks to when something goes sideways, whether that's a maintenance emergency at 9pm or a resident escalation that needs a steady hand. Avanath's model centers on workforce housing, so your residents are working people whose housing stability matters. That context shapes how you approach retention programs, resident events, and referrals to outside agencies.

On the compliance side, LIHTC and tax credit knowledge isn't a nice-to-have here. It's a core qualification. You'll need to maintain eligibility requirements and respond to potential violations with the same fluency you bring to your delinquency tracking or your NOI conversations with ownership.

Staff leadership is a meaningful part of the job. You'll set schedules, run performance reviews, deliver real-time feedback, and build a team that can execute without you managing every detail. If you've managed a site where you did everything yourself because it was faster, this role will push you to build something more durable than that.

What You Bring

  • 5 to 7 years in property management, with at least 2 years in a community or property manager seat
  • Demonstrated LIHTC and tax credit compliance knowledge
  • Experience preparing and managing operating budgets and monthly financial reports
  • A track record of driving delinquency down and keeping occupancy up
  • Strong communication skills across audiences: residents, staff, vendors, senior leadership, and regulatory agencies
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and the administrative side of site operations
  • Proven ability to lead a team through feedback, coaching, and clear expectations

Where This Role Takes You

Community managers who succeed at affordable housing properties with compliance layers and full P&L responsibility tend to be more prepared for regional manager roles than peers who've only run conventional sites. The reason is straightforward: LIHTC compliance, subsidy administration, and the relationship skills needed to work with social service agencies build a depth that translates well to multi-site oversight. If your goal is a regional portfolio, getting strong here, where the work is genuinely harder, accelerates that path. Avanath's focus on workforce housing also means you're building relationships with agencies, local partners, and government contacts that most market-rate managers never develop. Those relationships compound over a career.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance leadership is a job that looks like wrenches and work orders on the surface, but it's really a management role with a technical baseline. Village Green is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for their community in Morrisville, NC, and the scope here covers both the hands-on technical work and the people side of running a department.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll start most mornings reviewing open work orders and delegating based on your team's skill levels and the day's priorities. Turns, make-readies, and routine service requests compete for the same hours, so knowing how to sequence the work matters as much as knowing how to do it. Expect to be pulled into technical calls when something escalates, whether that's an HVAC system going down in summer heat or a boiler issue in winter. Village Green also expects this role to have eyes on energy management, which means monthly written recommendations, not just reactive fixes. You'll help identify capex needs and gather bids, so there's a planning component alongside the daily operational grind.

On the people side, you're hiring, training, and mentoring your crew. New technicians need to get up to speed quickly, and existing staff need direction and accountability. The delegation piece is real work: if you're doing every skilled repair yourself, something is off with how the team is being managed.

Who This Role Fits

  • Two or more years supervising a maintenance team in multifamily, hotel, or institutional facilities
  • Strong technical grounding in HVAC, plumbing, boilers, gas furnaces, gas appliances, electrical, and appliance repair
  • EPA Universal Certification required before starting
  • Comfort with preventative maintenance programs and basic budget input
  • Solid communication skills, both with residents and with management

The pay is $28.69 per hour with a quarterly bonus. Village Green also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with match, and what they describe as a genuine path to advancement. They've earned consistent recognition as a top workplace in multifamily, and their investment in training is a real part of how they retain maintenance talent.

One honest note: this role carries after-hours responsibility. Maintenance leadership in multifamily means you're reachable when something goes wrong at night or on weekends. That's the nature of residential property operations, and the candidates who thrive here plan for it rather than being surprised by it.

job.title: Regional Specialist
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Regional work at this level is fundamentally a financial analysis and people management job, with property inspections and owner communications layered on top. If you've carried a multi-site portfolio, you already know that most of your day isn't spent walking units. It's spent reading T-12s, talking to on-site managers about delinquency trends, and explaining budget variances to ownership groups who want a clear answer about why NOI is off. Cirrus Asset Management is a third-party management shop, which means your relationship skills with outside owners matter as much as your operational chops. You're the primary contact between the company and those ownership groups, so the ability to put together a clean, honest presentation and deliver it without getting defensive is non-negotiable.

The financial fluency required here goes beyond reviewing monthly statements. You'll be analyzing occupancy, collections, concessions, and expense lines across a multifamily portfolio, then translating that into actionable plans for site managers and credible updates for owners. If you've managed through a lease-up or pushed a distressed asset toward stabilized occupancy, that experience applies directly.

What You'll Be Managing Day to Day

On the people side, you're responsible for the full employment lifecycle of on-site personnel across your assigned communities. Hiring, training, performance management, and when necessary, separating people who aren't performing. You'll work with each manager on goal setting tied to their individual capabilities, which takes more patience than most job postings acknowledge.

On the physical asset side, you're conducting regular inspections, following up on maintenance completion, reviewing preventative maintenance programs, and making capital recommendations. On the financial side, you're approving invoices above site-level thresholds, reviewing payroll, signing off on budgets, and monitoring receivables weekly. Resident escalations that the property manager can't resolve land with you.

  • Minimum three consecutive years as a multi-site community manager or area manager overseeing three or more properties
  • Direct LIHTC or other affordable housing program experience in Washington (preferred, not required)
  • Must reside in Washington State
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Demonstrated ability to present financial and operational performance to third-party ownership groups
  • Working knowledge of fair housing, landlord-tenant law, and disability accommodation requirements as they apply in Washington

What This Role Looks Like at Cirrus

Cirrus operates as a fee management company, which shapes how this role functions. Third-party owners have their own expectations, timelines, and definitions of success. The Regional Specialist here has to manage both up to ownership groups and down to on-site staff, often simultaneously. That's a different pressure than working for a vertically integrated owner-operator where the asset is internal. Candidates who've worked in fee management before tend to adjust faster because they already know how to communicate operational realities to clients who didn't build the budget themselves.

The preferred LIHTC experience is worth noting. Washington has active affordable housing programs, and if your portfolio includes tax credit communities, you'll find that compliance documentation and file auditing get more attention here than at a straight market-rate shop. Even if LIHTC isn't your background, a comfort level with compliance procedures and resident file auditing is genuinely useful in this role.

job.title: Leasing Professional - Roving - Temporary - Berkeley Heights, Creekwood Apartments
job.description:
Roving leasing roles sit at an interesting intersection of sales ability and operational flexibility. CloudTen Residential is bringing on a temporary full-time Leasing Professional to rotate across properties in the Berkeley Heights area, stepping in where leasing traffic and staffing needs demand coverage. The pay runs $25 to $28 per hour depending on experience, with leasing bonuses available at assigned sites, and the position qualifies for CloudTen's standard benefit plans despite being temporary.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

On any given day, you might be prepping an apartment for a showing (light cleaning, basic make-ready checks), walking a prospective resident through the community, or working through a stack of rental applications in the management system. CloudTen uses OneSite and Entrata, so fluency with at least one of those platforms keeps you productive from day one rather than spending your first week figuring out the software.

Because this is a roving position, you'll carry the full leasing cycle with you from site to site: phone inquiries, in-person tours, objection handling, securing commitments and deposits, and completing move-in paperwork. You'll also keep an eye on community conditions during site visits and flag any deficiencies to the on-site manager. A valid driver's license is required since you'll be transporting marketing materials and moving between locations.

  • Tour and lease apartments across multiple properties, handling the full process from prospect contact through executed lease
  • Process rental applications accurately and in compliance with Fair Housing requirements
  • Assist with move-in and move-out inspections, with attention to consistent documentation
  • Set up and transport signage and marketing collateral as needed at assigned sites
  • Accept and route maintenance requests professionally when on-site
  • Review property database entries for accuracy and flag advertising discrepancies
  • Support market survey preparation when assigned

What CloudTen Is Looking For

One to two years of leasing experience is preferred, and lease-up experience carries real weight here. Lease-up environments demand a faster pace and sharper sales instincts than stabilized communities, and a roving professional who can walk into a high-traffic situation and close deals without a long ramp-up period is genuinely valuable. Prior sales experience (two years or more) rounds out the profile they're building.

Strong candidates tend to be self-directed, organized, and comfortable adapting quickly. When you're rotating across sites, you don't have the luxury of leaning on institutional familiarity with a single property. You need to absorb new floor plans, community features, and pricing quickly, then present them confidently. That adaptability is what separates candidates who thrive in roving roles from those who prefer the consistency of a single-site position.

The Bigger Picture

CloudTen's portfolio spans a wide range of product types, including hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning. For a leasing professional, that kind of exposure across property types builds a resume that travels well. Even in a temporary capacity, working across multiple communities gives you practical insight into how different assets are positioned, priced, and operated. That cross-site experience often accelerates the path toward a community manager role for candidates who are organized and growth-oriented.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor, The Beam
job.description:
Leading Maintenance at a Luxury Mid-Rise in New London

A Maintenance Supervisor role at a luxury mid-rise carries a different weight than one at a garden-style community. At a 203-unit property like The Beam, you're coordinating multiple service categories simultaneously, keeping the physical plant of a multi-story building operating at a standard that matches what residents are paying for. Jefferson Apartment Group, a vertically integrated firm with acquisition, development, construction, and management under one roof, brings that same full-cycle perspective to how they run their communities. That context matters when you're the person responsible for how the building actually performs day to day.

What the Role Actually Involves

This position splits your time between hands-on maintenance work and team leadership. You'll build the priority work schedule for service and janitorial staff, ensure all service requests get completed, and continuously inspect the property to catch deficiencies before residents do. That kind of proactive eye separates good supervisors from reactive ones.

On the operational side, you'll also:

  • Order parts and supplies within budgetary guidelines and actively manage overtime costs
  • Ensure all unit entry notifications are left after each service visit
  • Keep mechanical inspections current and maintain proper key control
  • Work alongside the Community Manager to bid major contracts annually and contribute to the maintenance portions of the annual budget
  • Conduct performance reviews for maintenance and janitorial staff
  • Be available for after-hours emergency calls, including evenings, weekends, and holidays

Budget involvement at this level is worth flagging. Many Maintenance Supervisors spend years without touching a budget. Contributing to the annual budget process here builds a skill that opens doors to Regional Maintenance Director and Director of Facilities roles later in your career.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year of multifamily maintenance experience, a solid foundation in tools and general maintenance trades, and the physical capacity to handle the full demands of the position, including lifting 50 to 100 pounds and moving through a multi-story building throughout the day. HVAC certification is preferred and will put you ahead of other candidates. Lease-up or new construction experience is also preferred, which fits given Jefferson's development background.

What the role builds is equally important. Leading a team through daily triage, communicating professionally with residents, and contributing to capex planning all sharpen the judgment and organizational discipline that define strong maintenance leadership. Supervisors who can hold a high curb appeal standard while keeping service costs controlled are the ones who advance within third-party and in-house management operations alike.

Pay ranges from $35 to $40 per hour. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, performance-based bonus potential, and possible rental discounts.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Bookkeeping precision, compliance fluency, and relationship instincts all get a real workout in this Assistant Community Manager role at Avanath in Portland. This position calls on a specific combination of skills: the financial discipline to manage rent collections, delinquency follow-up, and ledger accuracy, alongside the interpersonal range to serve residents across a wide spectrum of circumstances and needs.

Where Your Skills Actually Matter

Avanath operates affordable workforce housing, which means LIHTC compliance isn't background knowledge here. It's a daily operating reality. You'll work under the direction of the Compliance department to maintain accurate compliance files, and you need to understand how tax credit program requirements shape everything from move-in paperwork to income certification. Candidates who treat compliance as a checkbox rather than a core competency tend to struggle in this environment.

On the financial side, you'll collect and post rents, track outstanding balances, communicate with residents about delinquency, and assist with monthly projection reporting. Yardi Voyager is the platform, so familiarity with it matters. The role also expects you to inspect vacancies and make-ready units, which keeps you connected to the physical condition of the community and not just the office-side numbers.

Resident Relations and Daily Operations

Avanath frames resident service as its core mission, and the daily texture of this role reflects that. You'll handle phones and walk-in traffic, tour prospective residents, organize retention events, and serve as a go-to resource when residents face challenges that affect their ability to stay current or remain stably housed. That last piece, serving as a practical resource for people navigating financial and community pressures, requires patience and problem-solving skills that go beyond typical leasing or admin work.

In the Community Manager's absence, you step into the lead role. That means overseeing staff, maintaining operations, and making judgment calls. It's a position that genuinely prepares you for a Community Manager seat over time, provided you're building the right habits around compliance, team communication, and financial oversight.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Portland's rental market has seen significant regulatory activity in recent years, including just-cause eviction protections and local relocation assistance requirements. Candidates who already understand Oregon landlord-tenant law and can apply Fair Housing principles in real-time conversations with residents will find themselves ahead. Knowing how to handle an eviction proceeding, including the notice requirements and court representation this role may involve, is a genuine differentiator.

  • Minimum 2 years of experience as an Assistant Community Manager
  • LIHTC/Tax Credit program knowledge required
  • Working knowledge of Yardi Voyager
  • Solid bookkeeping and rent collection track record
  • Strong command of Fair Housing and landlord/tenant law
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work with diverse personalities

Avanath has built a reputation in the affordable housing space as an owner-operator with genuine mission alignment rather than a purely transactional approach to workforce housing. For someone who wants their day-to-day work to carry real weight for the residents they serve, that organizational character matters.

job.title: Lead Front Desk Associate - Metropolitan
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Metropolitan is a residential high-rise in Dallas, and the front desk is its operational nerve center. As Lead Front Desk Associate on the 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM shift, you're the person residents see when they come home from work, when a package goes missing, when a guest needs to be cleared, and when something goes sideways after the management office has closed for the day. You set the tone for the building's hospitality experience during its busiest hours.

The lead designation matters here. You're not just covering a post. You're guiding a team of Front Desk Associates through their shifts, reinforcing service standards, helping new hires find their footing, and flagging operational gaps to onsite management. When a resident escalates a concern at 9 PM, you're the one who owns the resolution process. When the front desk log needs to be accurate and complete, that's on you.

Day-to-day, the work covers a wide band of responsibilities:

  • Personalized resident and guest service, including handling escalated concerns with professionalism and follow-through
  • Coordinating visitor registration, package management, and vendor access
  • Managing incoming calls, emails, and resident service requests
  • Maintaining accurate records, reports, and administrative documentation
  • Training and onboarding new front desk staff and reinforcing operational procedures
  • Communicating shift updates clearly to team members and management

What You Bring

Strong candidates for this role come from hospitality, concierge, or high-touch residential service backgrounds. You already know how to read a room, de-escalate a frustrated resident without making it personal, and keep your desk organized when four things are happening at once. The lead component means you've also shown some capacity for guiding others, whether formally or informally.

  • Demonstrated customer service or hospitality experience, preferably in a residential or hotel setting
  • Comfort with administrative tasks: logging, reporting, correspondence, records management
  • Experience mentoring or supporting peers in a team environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to handle escalated situations calmly and find service-oriented solutions
  • Organized, accountable, and reliable during evening hours

Context Worth Knowing

Action Property Management has operated since 1984 and grown into the largest privately held HOA management company in the West, serving more than 300 communities across nine offices. Metropolitan sits within that portfolio as a high-rise residential property, a setting where the front desk carries more operational weight than in a garden-style or low-density community. Residents in high-rise buildings interact with front desk staff constantly, which means service consistency directly affects how people feel about where they live.

The evening shift at a building like this requires real self-direction. Management isn't always reachable. Situations come in without warning. What separates a strong Lead Front Desk Associate from an average one is the ability to handle those moments without waiting to be told what to do, while still keeping leadership informed and the team steady. Compensation for this role runs $27.00 to $28.00 per hour.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's 8 a.m. on a Monday and you're already walking lot lines, noting a resident's skirting that needs attention, checking in with maintenance before the morning fills up, and pulling up last week's delinquency numbers before you sit down with anything else. By noon you've handled a lease inquiry, approved a vendor invoice, and called a resident whose rent is five days late.

The Operation

This is the Community Manager role for Havenpark's property in Canby, OR, a manufactured home community of 270 homesites. You're running the full P&L: collections, occupancy, leasing activity, vendor coordination, and the physical condition of the grounds. Havenpark operates 100+ communities nationally, and this property is one piece of a portfolio with serious operational depth behind it, but on-site, the decisions are yours.

Delinquency management is a real part of the job. Manufactured home communities tend to have a resident base that's relationship-driven, which means collections require judgment and consistency in equal measure. You'll track aging weekly, follow established protocols, and know when to escalate. Occupancy and leasing are ongoing: you'll field traffic, move prospective residents through the process, and keep your eye on how the community's lot occupancy trends month to month. Your budget is your scorecard. You'll manage expenses, report on variances, and understand how capex decisions and vendor spend flow through to NOI.

You'll lead a small on-site team. That means hiring well, setting expectations clearly, and holding people accountable without burning them out. Havenpark's stated values, including Grit and Stewardship, aren't decorative here. They describe the pace and the ownership mentality the company expects from people running their communities.

What Havenpark Is Looking For

  • Prior experience managing a residential community, ideally with direct P&L or budget responsibility
  • Comfort with collections and delinquency follow-up, including resident-facing conversations that require both firmness and professionalism
  • Experience leading on-site staff, even a small team
  • Competency with property management software and basic financial reporting
  • Strong communication skills across resident interactions, vendor relationships, and internal reporting

Manufactured home community management has its own learning curve if you're coming from apartments or conventional residential. The resident relationships tend to run longer and deeper, turnover carries different economics, and the physical management of the land itself adds a layer that doesn't exist in a mid-rise or garden-style apartment context. Candidates who've managed MHC properties before will ramp faster, but strong operators from adjacent residential backgrounds can translate their skills effectively if they're willing to learn the asset class.

What separates a strong candidate here is the ability to treat every metric as a signal rather than just a number. Low occupancy tells you something about your leasing process or your community's curb appeal. High delinquency tells you something about resident screening or follow-through on collections. The managers who thrive in this type of role read the data and then go walk the property to understand what's actually happening.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Student housing maintenance runs at a different pace than conventional multifamily. Turns are compressed into a few weeks before the academic year starts, pool logs need to stay clean all summer, and when something breaks at 11pm the night before move-in, someone has to answer the phone. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their College Station community, and they're clear about what the job actually involves.

What You'll Actually Do

Day-to-day, you're working service requests, keeping up with a preventative maintenance schedule, and helping maintain curb appeal across grounds, breezeways, and common areas. You'll assist with turn events when the lease cycle flips, which in student housing means coordinating make-readies on a tight calendar with little margin for punch list items that drag. Pool maintenance is part of the scope here, including chemical logs that need to stay accurate and current. You'll carry on-call rotation responsibilities, so after-hours calls are a real part of this job. HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances: you're expected to troubleshoot and repair across all of it, not hand everything off to vendors.

You'll also work alongside the Maintenance Supervisor to track inventory, stay within budget guidelines, and support hazard communications compliance. Resident-facing communication matters here too. Student renters have high expectations and a low tolerance for delays, and how you handle a complaint often matters as much as how fast you fix the problem.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year of maintenance experience, apartment industry experience preferred
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • Ability to troubleshoot HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances independently
  • Reliable transportation and ability to live within 30 miles of the property
  • Comfortable with weekend, holiday, and rotating on-call schedules
  • Physically able to lift up to 50 pounds, work on ladders above eight feet, and handle outdoor work in Texas heat
  • Your own hand tools. This is standard in the trade.

The Bigger Picture

PeakMade specializes in off-campus student housing, and College Station is a high-volume college market with a large renter population tied directly to Texas A&M. The community you'd be serving sees predictable seasonal pressure, particularly around August move-in and the summer turn. Technicians who can stay organized during that window and keep their work quality consistent under volume tend to build real credibility fast in student housing operations.

PeakMade offers technical training, HVAC and CPO certification support, and a facilities leadership track for those who want to grow toward a supervisory role. Monthly renewal bonuses and a 401(k) match are also part of the package, along with parental leave benefits that are genuinely above average for this industry.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers the full operational footprint of a residential community. Make-readies are a core part of the workload. When a unit turns, you're responsible for getting it back to rent-ready condition at a quality level that holds up on move-in day inspection. That means punch lists completed correctly, not just quickly.

Beyond turns, you're handling service requests, preventative maintenance, pool upkeep, grounds appearance, and amenity function. Vendor oversight is part of the job too. When a contractor is on site, you're the quality check, not just a bystander. Supply inventory stays organized because you own it. Parts get ordered before the shortage becomes a problem.

On-call runs twice a month and includes weekend coverage. After-hours calls come with the territory. When something urgent surfaces, it goes to the Property Manager with enough detail to act on. You'll also assist with bid processes and help train newer maintenance staff when needed. A valid driver's license is required since you'll travel between nearby properties and handle supply runs.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on apartment maintenance or handyman experience (this is a hard requirement, not a preference)
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • EPA 608 certification is a plus; Certified Pool Operator (CPO) is also a plus
  • Comfort with both power and hand tools used safely and correctly
  • Supervisory or training experience, preferred but not required
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb ladders, work in confined spaces, and stay on your feet for extended periods
  • Fair Housing awareness and willingness to escalate accommodation requests to management appropriately

The Operational Reality

CommonPlace operates with a community-first philosophy. Residents notice maintenance quality more directly than almost any other operational variable. A slow service request response or a poorly turned unit shows up fast in renewal decisions and occupancy trends.
