Technicians who treat make-readies with the same rigor as emergency calls tend to perform better here because the attention to detail carries across both.

Commission opportunities exist for unit turns and renewals, which means your output has a direct financial connection to your paycheck. That's a meaningful incentive structure for a maintenance tech who moves efficiently without cutting corners. Candidates with EPA 608 certification and some supervisory background are well positioned to grow into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as the company expands its portfolio.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon, traffic from a weekend special is still trickling in, and one of your leasing agents just quoted the wrong floor plan price to a prospect. You catch it before the application goes through, correct it, coach the agent on the spot, and keep the tour schedule moving. That's a normal Tuesday at a 600-plus unit property.

The Role at Town & Country Apartments

Peak Management is hiring a Leasing Manager for Town & Country Apartments, a large garden-style community in Urbana, Illinois. At this unit count, you're not leasing yourself very often. You're running a team: setting goals, reviewing performance, monitoring conversion ratios, and making sure everyone on the floor understands Fair Housing compliance cold. The leasing office is your operation to manage.

Day-to-day, you'll develop and execute marketing plans to drive occupancy and maintain it, which means you understand what's moving traffic and what isn't, and you adjust accordingly. Budget preparation and leasing reporting are part of the job. Attention to detail matters here because you'll be accountable for numbers, not just activity. You'll also be expected to build genuine rapport with residents in ways that support retention, because at 600-plus units, delinquency and MTM exposure add up fast when renewals go sideways.

A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required. The property has stairs, outdoor areas, and four seasons of Illinois weather, so physical mobility across the site is part of the routine.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience developing leasing marketing strategies and tracking their effectiveness against occupancy goals
  • Prior team leadership or supervisory experience in a leasing environment
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and the ability to train others on compliance
  • Comfort with budget prep, reporting, and leasing operations at a property of meaningful scale
  • Resident retention instincts, not just leasing instincts

The candidates who struggle in roles like this are usually strong individual leasing consultants who haven't made the mental shift to managing people yet. At this property size, your output is measured through your team's numbers, not your own tours closed. If you've already made that shift, you'll hit the ground faster.

Peak Management offers medical, dental, and life insurance, PTO (including your birthday, which is a nice touch), a flexible spending account, 401(k) with employer matching, on-call premium pay, and a sign-on bonus. Compensation is described as competitive.

job.title: General Manager - Foxchase Apartment Homes
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning at Foxchase Apartment Homes. A resident stops you near the leasing office about a noise complaint from the weekend. One of your leasing agents has a prospect tour in twenty minutes. And your maintenance lead needs a decision on a vendor bid before the afternoon. That's the job, and the General Manager who thrives here is the one who moves through all three without losing composure or momentum.

What You'll Be Responsible For

AIR Communities is hiring a General Manager for Foxchase Apartment Homes in Alexandria, VA. This is a full operational leadership role. You'll carry ownership of the site's financial performance, leasing results, team development, and resident experience. The community runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. as the standard schedule, with some seasonal flex.

Day to day, that means coaching your leasing and maintenance teams, keeping occupancy and traffic metrics where they need to be, managing the property budget, and making sure the physical and service standards that define a best-in-class community are actually maintained. You'll also be the person who sets the tone. When expectations aren't being met, you address it. When a team member is developing well, you invest in that. AIR puts real weight behind resident satisfaction metrics, so you'll be watching more than just delinquency and NOI. The quality of the lived experience on-site is part of how this role is measured.

The compensation range is $85,000 to $115,000 base plus a 20% target bonus, commissions on new leases and renewals, and an on-site apartment benefit option. AIR also offers a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, and tuition and certification reimbursement up to 100%.

Who Fits This Role Well

The baseline requirements include at least four years in sales, customer service, or asset management, with two or more years of direct property management leadership. Familiarity with platforms like Entrata, OneSite, SmartRent, or Salesforce is expected. You should be comfortable reading a budget and having a real conversation about revenue performance, not just deferring to a regional.

  • Proven track record leading and developing on-site teams in a leasing or service environment
  • Experience using performance metrics to drive individual and team accountability
  • Working knowledge of property financials, including budget management and revenue analysis
  • Ability to manage competing priorities across operations, leasing, and resident relations simultaneously
  • Reliable transportation and flexibility for schedule variation based on community and seasonal needs

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level is usually less about technical knowledge and more about how they handle the human dynamics. A General Manager who can coach a leasing agent after a tough week, hold a direct conversation with a difficult resident, and still close the month strong is rare. AIR has support structures and systems, but this role requires someone who doesn't wait for direction to solve a problem at the site level.

Alexandria's rental market is competitive, and Foxchase sits in a submarket where prospective residents have real choices. The GM who understands that leasing performance is built on team culture, not just marketing spend, will have an advantage here.

job.title: Community Relations Manager - Cortland Peterson
job.description:
Multifamily communities at the Class A end of the market carry a specific kind of pressure: residents are paying a premium, and they notice when the experience doesn't match the price point. The Community Relations Manager role exists precisely to close that gap. It's the connective tissue between a leasing pipeline and a resident base that actually stays, renews, and refers.

Cortland's Peterson property in Colorado Springs is hiring for this position, and it sits at an interesting intersection. You're part sales professional, part operations partner, and part community builder. The leasing side demands real pipeline discipline: following up promptly, maintaining accurate CRM records, tracking conversion metrics, and closing with confidence. The resident experience side requires something harder to train, which is genuine attentiveness to what people actually need versus what they say they need. Both matter here, and you'll be accountable to both.

What This Role Actually Involves Day to Day

On any given day, you might be walking vacant units for make-ready compliance in the morning, hosting a resident event in the evening, and handling a leasing inquiry via CRM follow-up in between. You'll support the Community Manager in keeping daily operations on track, including vendor coordination, property inspections, curb appeal standards, and Fair Housing compliance. You'll also carry your own leasing goals and conversion targets, which means the pipeline management piece is real, not secondary.

The social media and marketing component is worth calling out specifically. Cortland expects this person to actively manage the community's brand presence, not just post occasionally. If you've built engagement for a luxury or lifestyle brand before, that experience translates directly.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

  • At least 2 years of measurable sales results in a high-velocity, short-cycle environment: multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, premium automotive, or similar
  • Proven pipeline management habits, including consistent follow-up and organized lead tracking
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM platforms, and Microsoft Office
  • Strong written and verbal communication; you'll interact with prospective residents, current residents, vendors, and the broader onsite team regularly
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Ability to handle resident concerns with empathy and resolve them with urgency

The candidates who tend to stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the longest property management resume. They're the ones who've worked in environments where customer experience was non-negotiable and who treat their follow-up process with the same discipline as their close. Consultative selling skills matter here more than a scripted pitch.

Pay for this role falls between $26 and $31 per hour. Cortland is a vertically integrated operator with in-house design, construction, and management, which means internal career paths are real and varied. Community Relations Managers who demonstrate operational competence alongside leasing results often move into Community Manager roles or broader portfolio responsibilities over time.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company manages more than 720 million square feet of commercial space across the United States and internationally, which means the people who work there operate at genuine scale. This Assistant Property Manager role in Charlotte puts you inside that machine at the commercial level, supporting the day-to-day management of office, retail, or industrial assets under the direction of a senior Property Manager.

The work spans a wide band of responsibilities. On any given week, you might be reconciling CAM charges with the accounting team, reviewing vendor invoices against management agreement thresholds, helping prepare monthly reporting packages for institutional clients, or walking a space with a tenant improvement team during a move-in. Lease administration runs through the role too, including setup, amendments, and keeping applicable systems current. None of this is purely administrative. You're expected to understand what you're looking at financially, communicate clearly with tenants and vendors, and help the property run to the standards a major institutional client expects.

The CAM/OpEx reconciliation piece is worth paying attention to. Operating expense reconciliation is one of those skills that commercial property managers carry with them for their entire careers. Getting comfortable with the calculations, the lease language, and the tenant communication involved in that process is foundational. People who move from assistant to full property manager roles tend to do so faster when they've genuinely owned a piece of that work rather than just supported it.

What you'll bring to this role

  • A bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience
  • One to two years of experience in commercial property management or a closely related field
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills; familiarity with AP and CMMS platforms is a plus
  • Comfort with financial concepts: percentages, discounts, basic financial analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the judgment to match tone to situation
  • Organizational discipline and the ability to meet deadlines across multiple workstreams
  • Authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship, now or in the future

This is a fully in-office position in Charlotte. Property inspections and travel to assigned assets are part of the regular routine, so comfort with time spent on-site matters.

Lincoln's structure gives assistant managers real exposure to institutional-grade clients and complex assets early. For someone building toward a Property Manager title, or eventually toward a portfolio or regional role, the combination of financial reporting, vendor management, lease administration, and tenant relations you develop here covers most of what senior roles will test you on.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - The Point at Town Center
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer in the National Apartment Association rankings three years running, and the culture behind that reflects in how they staff their communities. The Point at Town Center in Jacksonville is looking for a Lead Maintenance Technician who can run the maintenance operation with real authority while staying approachable enough to work alongside office staff, contractors, and residents every day.

What You'll Actually Do

This role carries genuine supervisory weight. You're not just fixing things. You're scheduling your team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads, coordinating third-party contractors, ordering supplies, and making sure the shop and storage areas stay organized and well-stocked. Preventative maintenance and turn-key operations are a consistent part of the rhythm. You'll also manage compliance inspections and conduct regular walkthroughs of apartments, common areas, grounds, pools, and exterior structures to catch issues before they become problems. When a unit turns, you're working closely with the business manager and office staff to confirm it's show-ready and move-in ready on schedule. Software tracking for service requests, inventory, and completed work is part of the job.

On the people side, you'll hire and develop your service team members. That means coaching, setting expectations, and building a crew that runs well even when you're not watching. On-call coverage is required for a minimum of two weeks per month, and emergency availability comes with the territory. Most experienced maintenance leads already account for this, but it's worth naming honestly because it shapes your schedule and your family's.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of apartment maintenance experience, with some time in a lead or supervisor capacity
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • Comfort coordinating structural, mechanical, electrical, and HVAC repairs
  • Full-time availability Monday through Friday, generally 9 AM to 5 PM, with flexibility when the property needs it
  • Experience using property management software or maintenance tracking systems
  • A working knowledge of fair housing, safety regulations, and local compliance requirements

The Team Dynamic Worth Understanding

What separates strong candidates in this kind of role isn't just technical skill. It's communication. The best maintenance leads build a real working relationship with the property's office staff, not just a transactional one. When leasing is showing units and the make-ready list keeps shifting, or when a resident escalates a service complaint to the front desk, the partnership between maintenance and the business manager either holds the community together or creates friction. If you've worked well across that line before, that experience matters here.

Olympus Property offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and paid time off, along with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility for team members. Career pathing is part of their stated culture, and for a lead tech who performs well, moving into a maintenance supervisor or regional maintenance role is a realistic next step within their portfolio.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
By 7:45 on a Tuesday morning, you're already loading the blower and running through the parking lot perimeter before residents leave for work. They notice when it's clean. They definitely notice when it's not.

Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for more than 70 years, managing over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. This Groundskeeper position is based at Bexley at Brier Creek in Morrisville, NC, a community where the exterior presentation matters to residents and to the ownership team that takes a hands-on approach to daily operations.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm position. That schedule is genuinely consistent, which matters when you're doing physical work in outdoor conditions year-round. That said, the job is demanding. You'll work through North Carolina summers and cold snaps alike, and the tasks repeat daily. Picking up litter, clearing pet waste stations, blowing walkways, keeping the community looking sharp. These aren't glamorous tasks. They are, however, the reason a property feels like a place people want to come home to.

Beyond the daily rounds, you'll handle trash-outs on vacant apartments, light painting, pressure washing, and general upkeep of landscaped areas including weeding and planting. You'll also support the maintenance team when needed. The physical requirements are real: prolonged walking and standing, frequent lifting up to 50 pounds or more, bending, stooping, and operating equipment including backpack blowers and power washers. You'll use a golf cart and trailer as part of your routine. If you want a desk, this isn't it. If you want to be outside and see the results of your work every day, that's a genuine perk of the role.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • Reliability. The team depends on you being there, on time, ready to work.
  • Self-direction. A lot of your day runs without close supervision. You need to know what needs doing and do it without being prompted.
  • Attention to detail. Noticing the trash before it piles up. Catching the issue before it becomes a complaint.
  • A tolerance for repetition. The same walkways get blown every morning. That's the job.
  • Willingness to pitch in. When the maintenance team needs an extra hand, you help.

Starting pay is $16 per hour with quarterly bonuses. There's also a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation and sick time, and a rent discount. For a hourly grounds position, that's a solid package.

Groundskeepers who show aptitude and a willingness to learn at Weinstein often move into maintenance technician roles over time. The company invests in internal growth, and this position is a legitimate entry point into a property maintenance career track, not a dead end.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Marc San Marcos
job.description:
MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for more than 30 years. Their portfolio spans multiple states, and they promote heavily from within, which means a leasing role here has a real path forward for the right person.

The open position is at Marc, a residential community in San Marcos, CA. The job centers on converting traffic into signed leases. You'll greet prospects, qualify applicants, walk units, and shepherd people through the leasing process from first contact to move-in day. That last part matters: you'll coordinate with maintenance to make sure new residents aren't moving into a unit with an open punch list.

Administrative work is part of the job too. Rental files need to stay current, lease documents need to be accurate, and data entry has to be done right. When residents have complaints or maintenance concerns, you're often the first point of contact. Rent collection support falls under this role as well.

Weekend availability is required.

What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred)
  • Strong sales instincts and genuine customer service skills
  • Professional communication, written and verbal
  • Comfort with leasing software and data entry
  • Ability to work weekends

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, plus monthly and quarterly bonuses and company profit sharing. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, PTO, and rental discounts.

San Marcos sits in North San Diego County, a market with steady renter demand driven by Cal State San Marcos, a growing life sciences employment base, and limited new supply relative to other parts of the county. Occupancy pressure is real, which means leasing skills here get tested consistently, and a consultant who can close efficiently becomes valuable quickly.

Leasing is where most property management careers start, and at a company that promotes from within, strong performers here move toward assistant manager and property manager roles. If that trajectory interests you, this kind of role builds the foundation: sales, compliance, resident relations, and administrative accuracy all at once.

job.title: Community Manager- Student Housing
job.description:
Student housing management draws on a specific blend of skills that most conventional multifamily experience doesn't fully develop: the ability to run a full annual turn at scale, manage a high-energy leasing cycle tied to an academic calendar, and maintain financial performance against revenue targets that reset every year. The Community Manager role at Lark Baton Rouge calls on all of those at once.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Scion places this position at the center of property operations, and the skill set reflects that. Financial management is a constant: you'll own the budget process from preparation through month-end close, manage NOI through both revenue growth and expense discipline, and produce variance explanations that hold up under scrutiny. Alongside that, you'll carry full responsibility for leasing velocity, gain-to-lease performance, concessions strategy, and market rate positioning. Those two tracks, financial and leasing, run in parallel and require fluency in both.

People management is the third skill set this role demands heavily. You'll hire, develop, and hold accountable a team of leasing and maintenance staff, and you'll need to be the kind of leader who can plan for succession so the property runs smoothly when you're not on site. On-call responsibility is real here. Student housing communities don't pause for off-hours, and the GM is the primary responder when escalations arise.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

  • Lead the annual turnover process: coordinating vendors, setting team expectations, managing overtime budgets, and hitting make-ready deadlines before move-in
  • Monitor KPIs in property management platforms (Entrata preferred) and act on the data rather than just reporting it
  • Oversee facilities compliance including permits, preventative maintenance schedules, and curb appeal across common areas and amenities
  • Manage reputation across review platforms as part of the broader customer experience strategy
  • Partner with legal and accounting teams on vendor contracts, risk management, and monthly financial reporting
  • Ensure Fair Housing compliance and safety training across all onsite staff

The Baton Rouge Context and What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Baton Rouge is a student housing market anchored by LSU's enrollment, which runs well above 35,000 students. The demand cycle here is reliable but compressed: pre-leasing for the following fall starts early, competition among purpose-built student communities is real, and the annual turn window between July and August is intense. A GM who has managed high-volume turn seasons at a similarly sized property will have a clear operational advantage over someone learning that process for the first time here.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is comfort operating at the intersection of numbers and people. Plenty of managers can read a T-12 or run a leasing team. Fewer can do both well while also being the face of the community to residents, the accountability partner for staff, and the primary contact during a 2 a.m. emergency. Scion's model asks for all of that in one person, and the candidates who thrive are the ones who find that range energizing rather than exhausting.

Scion brings a dedicated student housing platform to this role, which means the training, systems, and organizational infrastructure are built specifically for this asset class rather than adapted from conventional multifamily. For a manager who wants to grow within student housing specifically, that focus has real career value.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Assistant Community Manager role at Hawthorne Residential Partners sits at the intersection of leasing execution and financial accountability. You're using both skill sets simultaneously, not alternating between them. That combination is what makes this position genuinely educational for someone building a career in multifamily.

Skills This Role Requires on Day One

You need working knowledge of leasing fundamentals before you arrive. That means reading a prospect's intent during a tour, guiding an application through accurately, and understanding how renewals connect to occupancy goals. On the financial side, you'll be posting rent payments, scanning checks, monitoring delinquency, and reviewing ledgers for billing accuracy. These aren't tasks you'll learn slowly. The community's reporting cadence and the Community Manager's expectations require you to operate with confidence from the start. Two years of property management experience is preferred, along with at least six months in an assistant manager seat. A CALP credential is a plus, though not required.

Conflict resolution is another non-negotiable. Resident concerns will come to you, and the expectation is that you de-escalate with professionalism and follow through with a resolution, not just an acknowledgment. Communities where delinquency and resident disputes pile up are communities where the assistant manager isn't carrying their weight.

Skills This Role Actively Builds

Where this role develops you is in financial interpretation and leadership under pressure. Assisting with financial reporting for regional leadership puts you in contact with the kind of documentation a Community Manager owns outright. You'll learn to read the story behind the numbers, connecting occupancy trends, concessions, and renewal rates to overall NOI performance. When the Community Manager is out, you step into that chair. Those moments build the instincts that the Career Path Program at Hawthorne is designed to formalize.

Hawthorne runs a structured development track specifically to move Assistant Community Managers into Community Manager roles. That path is explicit here, not implied. Their Learning and Development team is involved, not passive.

What the Work Actually Looks Like at Hawthorne at Holly Ridge

The leasing office is open Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays, 10 to 4. You'll receive one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Resident events or community needs may occasionally pull you into evenings or weekends. Social media content creation is part of the role, specifically for promoting community events and resident engagement, so comfort with that is useful.

Candidates who stand out in this role combine two things that don't always travel together: genuine warmth with residents and an exacting eye for ledger accuracy. Strong instincts on the leasing floor mean little if rent collection and account reconciliation are loose. Hawthorne's Live It culture emphasizes service and connection, but this is still a performance-driven position with leasing commissions and quarterly bonuses tied to results.

  • Monthly leasing and renewal commissions
  • Quarterly performance bonuses
  • Hourly base compensation
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401k with company match
  • Paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Pet insurance, telehealth access, and paid time off including your birthday

job.title: Market Assistant Property Manager II
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the operational center of two residential communities in Stoughton: Oxford Apartments and The Essex. Day-to-day, you're supporting leasing activity, approving rental applications, and working to keep occupancy on target. You're also a primary point of contact for residents, which means your mornings might involve following up on a maintenance coordination question before shifting to delinquency outreach or move-in paperwork in the afternoon.

Beyond leasing and resident relations, this position carries real administrative weight. You'll maintain accurate resident files, prepare required reports, coordinate inspections, and manage move-in and move-out logistics. Affordable housing compliance is a genuine part of the job here, and knowledge of Fair Housing regulations isn't background context. It's something you'll apply regularly.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent, with at least three years of property management experience
  • Hands-on experience with affordable housing programs and the compliance obligations that come with them
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations at a practical, not just theoretical, level
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Yardi for day-to-day leasing and administrative tasks
  • Strong organizational habits and the communication skills to manage both resident concerns and internal reporting

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is the combination of leasing competency and compliance literacy. Plenty of assistant managers can handle traffic and applications. Fewer can manage affordable housing paperwork correctly while also keeping delinquency low and residents reasonably satisfied. If you've done both, you'll be genuinely useful from the first week.

The Role in Context

John M. Corcoran and Company has been operating in New England real estate since 1951. The company manages residential communities with a focus on integrity and long-term community development. The culture is described as collaborative, and many team members have built lengthy careers there, which says something real about how the organization treats institutional knowledge and people who invest in the work.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5, which is a genuine differentiator in property management. Residential leasing and operations roles often bleed into evenings and weekends, particularly during lease-up phases or high-traffic seasons. A fixed weekday schedule at a stabilized community with affordable housing compliance requirements is a meaningful quality-of-life factor worth noting. The pay range runs from $29.60 to $37.50 per hour, and a $2,500 sign-on bonus accompanies the offer. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) with company match.

For someone with affordable housing experience who wants to deepen their skills in multi-site coordination and compliance reporting, this role builds exactly that kind of documented track record. It's a realistic step toward a property manager title, particularly within a company that has a stated track record of promoting from within.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a straight-ahead community manager role at a Hillpointe workforce housing property in Cleveland, TN. You're running day-to-day operations: occupancy, financials, resident experience, vendor coordination, and asset condition. The Regional Manager sets the direction; you execute it at the property level.

On any given day, that means walking the property and logging what needs attention, reviewing delinquency and following up accordingly, making sure make-readies are genuinely move-in ready (not just technically turned), and keeping amenities in the kind of shape that justifies the rent. You'll process AP, communicate with the facilities maintenance team, and look for ancillary revenue opportunities where they exist. Entrata experience is a real advantage here since that's the preferred platform.

Hillpointe builds and operates market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt and is among the more active developers in that space right now. Cleveland sits in the Chattanooga metro corridor, a market that's absorbed meaningful multifamily supply over the past few years. Workforce product there competes on value and resident retention as much as lease-up velocity, so keeping occupancy steady and renewals strong is where a good community manager earns their keep.

What You Bring

  • Prior property management experience, ideally in a community manager or assistant manager seat
  • Comfortable with property management software; Entrata specifically is preferred
  • Solid math skills for budget tracking, financial reporting, and basic NOI analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including lease document fluency
  • HS diploma or equivalent required
  • Valid driver's license (you'll need it on-site and for occasional local travel)
  • Availability via phone and email outside standard hours, except during approved time off
  • Physical ability to walk the full property and handle routine lifting up to 20 lbs independently

A Realistic Picture

Workforce housing communities run lean. You're not managing a Class A high-rise with a full support staff behind you. Residents are working people who notice when something's broken or when a common area looks neglected. The job rewards managers who stay ahead of maintenance issues, build real relationships with residents, and treat the asset like it's theirs to protect. If you've managed a garden-style or similar community and you know how to hold occupancy without leaning hard on concessions, that background will translate well here.

The flexible availability requirement is real. Community management at this level means you're the point of contact when things come up, and they do come up. That's not a complaint, just an honest description of what the job is.

job.title: Future Opportunity Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at an apartment community pulls on a wider skill set than most people expect. Plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, curb appeal, key control, inventory management , all of it lands on one person's plate in a given week. Berkshire Ninth Street is collecting applications from maintenance technicians who are ready for that kind of range.

What This Role Actually Demands

Berkshire Residential owns and manages its own portfolio, which means maintenance techs here support a team with a direct stake in asset performance. Every deferred repair affects NOI. Every slow turn affects occupancy. Every safety issue carries liability. The people who do this job well treat the physical plant like it belongs to them, because in an important operational sense, it does.

Day-to-day, you'll handle work orders across systems: appliances, plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry. You'll also help manage the shop, control inventory, and keep equipment organized. Curb appeal is part of the job description, not an afterthought. On a given morning, you might close out three work orders, inspect a vacant unit on the punch list, and help a resident troubleshoot a faulty HVAC before noon. That kind of context-switching is normal here, and it rewards techs who are organized and don't need a lot of hand-holding between tasks.

The Skills That Matter Here

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core systems: appliances, plumbing, electrical, and carpentry
  • Comfort with basic computer use for work order platforms or maintenance tracking software
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English, since work order documentation and resident interaction are both part of the role
  • A track record of treating safety protocols as non-negotiable, not suggestions

What It Looks Like Working for Berkshire

Berkshire Residential operates as a vertically integrated company , ownership and management under one roof. That structure tends to reduce the friction maintenance techs often feel at fee-managed properties, where ownership and operations speak different languages. Here, the priorities align. The company also puts real weight on career development; technicians who build a strong track record have a credible path toward lead tech and maintenance supervisor roles over time.

The candidate who stands out brings genuine technical range, takes pride in make-readies being done right the first time, and communicates proactively when something needs to escalate. Closing work orders fast matters. Closing them correctly matters more.

job.title: Maintenance Lead (Sunset Creek, Sunset Pines, Fair Haven Commons)
job.description:
A maintenance lead role at a nonprofit affordable housing organization carries responsibilities that go beyond typical apartment maintenance work. You're managing operations across multiple communities simultaneously, which means your coordination and leadership skills get tested every single day, not just when something breaks.

What This Role Actually Covers

This position oversees maintenance operations for three Fairfield communities: Sunset Creek, Sunset Pines, and Fair Haven Commons. The scope runs from hands-on trades work in electrical, plumbing, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair to team scheduling, vendor selection, bid review, and contractor oversight. You'll manage unit turns for move-ins and move-outs, coordinate annual inspections, run preventive maintenance programs, and keep common areas clean and safe. On-call emergency rotation is part of the job. So is accurate recordkeeping and managing inventory and supply procurement across all three sites.

MidPen's portfolio includes affordable communities serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. That means inspections here follow REAC, TCAC, and MOR standards, not just standard market-rate property protocols. If you've worked in affordable housing before, you already know the difference. If you haven't, this role will build that knowledge quickly.

Skills Required vs. Skills You'll Build

Coming in, you need at least five years of hands-on maintenance experience across the core trades plus three years supervising a crew. Multi-trade proficiency, working knowledge of affordable housing inspection standards, and the ability to manage vendors from bid to completion are baseline requirements. Strong communication matters too. You'll be working with residents, contractors, community partners, and internal teams, and the ability to write clearly and speak directly shapes how well that all goes.

What this role builds is different. Managing three properties at once sharpens your ability to triage competing priorities under real pressure. Leading a team through inspections with regulatory consequences develops the kind of compliance discipline that transfers across the affordable housing sector. Coordinating with MidPen's onsite Resident Services team also gives you a clearer picture of how maintenance quality connects directly to resident stability, which is a perspective that makes better maintenance professionals.

Who Does Well in This Role

The candidates who thrive here bring a few things that aren't always spelled out in job postings. First, genuine interest in coaching their team rather than just completing work orders themselves. Second, comfort with documentation, because TCAC and REAC inspections reward organized recordkeeping and penalize gaps. Third, a calm, consistent approach to resident interactions. Affordable housing communities often serve residents navigating real hardship, and the maintenance team is frequently the most visible face of management in a resident's daily experience.

  • High school diploma plus five years of broad maintenance experience (or equivalent combination)
  • Three years of supervisory experience with apartment turns and crew oversight
  • Working knowledge of REAC, TCAC, or MOR inspection standards
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and basic computer applications
  • Ability to perform physically demanding work across varying outdoor conditions
  • Valid driver's license (implied by multi-site responsibilities)

The pay range is $30.00 to $33.75 per hour, based on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, and an EAP program.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and operates workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and their maintenance team sits at the center of that mission. A Maintenance Technician here isn't just fixing things, they're the reason residents feel at home and properties hold their value. This opening covers two Central Florida locations: Daytona Beach and DeLand.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your days involve working through resident work orders, conducting inspections, and keeping common areas, amenities, and building systems running properly. Make-readies are a real part of the rhythm here. When a unit turns, you're preparing that apartment for the next resident, which means completing punch lists, addressing any deferred issues, and getting the space genuinely move-in ready, not just surface clean.

Beyond reactive repairs, you'll run preventive maintenance checks, manage your parts inventory, coordinate with vendors and contractors when work goes beyond in-house scope, and keep documentation tight. That last part matters more than people expect. Accurate records protect the property, support budgeting, and make your own life easier when a recurring issue shows up six months later.

This role includes a rotating on-call schedule, so evenings and weekends are part of the deal. That's a real commitment, and it's worth knowing going in.

What Hillpointe Needs From You

  • Hands-on mechanical aptitude with the ability to diagnose and repair issues across building systems
  • Experience with preventive maintenance routines and pre-move-out inspections
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant recycling (or willingness to obtain it)
  • Valid driver's license for on-property golf cart operation
  • Comfortable reading technical manuals, schematics, and blueprints
  • Solid communication habits with residents, management, and contractors
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly and work in varying outdoor conditions
  • High school diploma or GED, plus relevant experience or training
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and PPE requirements

Team Fit and Growth

Because Hillpointe controls development, construction, and operations in-house, their maintenance staff tends to work alongside people who genuinely understand how buildings go together. That context helps. You're not just executing work orders in isolation. You're part of a team that has line of sight into the full property lifecycle.

Technicians who build strong diagnostic habits and take ownership of their units often grow into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles. If that trajectory interests you, this environment gives you the exposure to get there. Hillpointe's focus on workforce housing also means you're working with residents who depend on well-functioning homes, which adds real weight to the work without making it abstract.

job.title: Full-Time Overnight Lead Cleaner (Thu-Mon, 11PM-6AM)
job.description:
Overnight facility cleanliness is one of those operational foundations that residents notice immediately when it slips and almost never consciously appreciate when it's working. For a company like Comstock, whose ParkX brand positions itself around premium parking and mobility experiences, the overnight cleaning crew is doing real brand work between 11 PM and 6 AM while most of the organization sleeps.

This Lead Cleaner position covers Thursday through Monday on the overnight shift at a Reston, VA property. The lead component matters here. You're not just running a checklist; you're taking ownership of the shift, completing required end-of-turn documentation, and ensuring a clean handoff to the next crew. That accountability structure is closer to a shift supervisor function than a standard porter role.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this role is maintaining common areas, lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public-facing spaces to a standard that holds up to daylight inspection. Pressure washing, window cleaning, and trash collection are regular duties. When events run late or the next day brings a scheduled gathering, you'll support setup and breakdown of those spaces as well. You'll also monitor cleaning supply inventory, keep the supply room organized, and flag any equipment damage or maintenance concerns to management. The shift runs independently, so self-direction is genuinely required, not just a line on a job description.

Physical demands are real. Expect extended time on your feet, lifting up to 50 pounds, working in variable temperatures (outdoors in Northern Virginia winters), and regular exposure to cleaning chemicals. A valid driver's license without major violations is required.

Qualifications Worth Having

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to work Thursday through Monday, 11 PM to 6 AM, including occasional extended hours around events
  • Strong reliability and time management; overnight shifts amplify both when supervision is minimal
  • Comfort working with a diverse range of residents, guests, and property staff in a professional, courteous manner
  • Problem-solving instincts for situations that come up mid-shift without a manager on-site

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) matching, life insurance, free parking with EV charging, parental leave, and annual professional development funds. Comstock also notes genuine advancement opportunities within its growing portfolio, which matters for anyone thinking about where overnight facilities work can lead.

On that point: lead cleaner roles at mid-rise and mixed-use properties often serve as a practical entry point into facilities coordination or property operations. The documentation habits, inventory tracking, and shift-handoff discipline you build here transfer directly to maintenance tech roles and, eventually, facilities management positions. The overnight schedule is demanding, but the independence and lead-level responsibility compress your learning curve faster than a supervised daytime role where someone else is making the calls.

job.title: Cleaner - Part-Time
job.description:
Redstone Residential runs over 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a heavy focus on student housing. Part-time cleaning roles at properties like this one in Rexburg tend to move at a steady pace. Curb appeal and common area upkeep directly affect how prospects and residents experience the community every day.

What the Work Looks Like

This is a part-time, non-exempt position paying $12.00 per hour. Shifts run four to six hours and involve a fair amount of time on your feet. The work covers both indoor and outdoor spaces: hallways, common areas, parking areas, landscaping, and general grounds. You'll also conduct scheduled cleaning checks inside resident apartments to confirm units meet the property's cleanliness standards.

  • Clean and maintain all common areas, including the clubhouse, office, and model unit
  • Keep grounds free of trash, debris, and animal waste
  • Water flowers and maintain basic landscaping appearance
  • Assist with basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed
  • Complete scheduled resident apartment cleaning checks
  • Participate in required Redstone training

Physical requirements are real here. You need to lift 50 or more pounds and handle full shifts on your feet. Prior janitorial or cleaning experience helps, but the bigger requirement is the ability to manage your tasks independently without needing constant direction.

Who Fits This Role

Student housing communities in college towns like Rexburg see high turnover by design. That means the cleaning team carries more weight than the job title suggests. Residents and their families notice when common areas are well-kept, and cleaning checks keep unit conditions from quietly deteriorating over a lease term. People who do this job well are consistent, self-directed, and comfortable working around residents without being intrusive.

A friendly demeanor matters, since you'll interact with residents during apartment checks. This isn't a behind-the-scenes role where you only see empty spaces.

Benefits and Company Context

Redstone offers a 401(k) plan with up to 6% matching, which is worth noting for a part-time hourly position. The company operates across 20 states and continues to grow its conventional multifamily portfolio alongside its student housing base. For someone looking for part-time hours with a structured employer, this is a stable option with a company that has real operational depth behind it.

job.title: Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
Fairstead operates more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states as an integrated owner, operator, and developer. That integrated structure matters here: when compliance, construction, and property management sit under one roof, the Community Manager at a Fairstead property isn't waiting on a third party to make decisions. You're close to the platform. That said, this specific role in Annapolis, Maryland carries real weight on its own. Affordable housing compliance means the margin for administrative error is thin, and the regulatory calendar never really stops.

The day-to-day here runs on two parallel tracks: financial performance and compliance. On the financial side, you're watching delinquency closely, directing monthly rent collection, pursuing arrears through legal channels when necessary, monitoring bad-debt write-offs, and attending monthly budget review meetings. On the compliance side, you're staying current with the HUD 4350.3 Handbook, managing REAC prep, clearing EHS violations, coordinating Management and Occupancy Reviews, handling LIHTC reviews, and conducting annual and interim recertifications. Those tracks intersect constantly. A tenant with lease compliance issues is often also a delinquency problem, and resolving it requires coordination across compliance, legal, and regional leadership.

You'll also supervise maintenance operations, conduct unit inspections, manage vendor bids and contractor quotes, and run bi-annual walk-throughs with the Building Superintendent. Fairstead properties often carry ongoing renovation and construction activity, so expect to coordinate site access, track project updates, and work directly with the construction team to keep violations off the books.

What strong candidates bring

  • At least three years of management experience that included direct team supervision
  • COS or CPO certification (required)
  • TCS certification for tax credit compliance
  • EIV system experience
  • Familiarity with Yardi and RealPage (preferred)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Affordable housing experience; HUD compliance knowledge is central to this role
  • Bachelor's degree preferred

The candidates who genuinely thrive in affordable housing community management tend to be detail-oriented on certification paperwork without losing sight of the human side of the work. Recertification seasons get compressed, MOR timelines don't move for anyone's convenience, and residents often have complex circumstances. Keeping occupancy healthy, delinquency in check, and compliance audit-ready at the same time is a skill that takes experience to do well. If you've built that discipline somewhere, this role puts it to use. The salary range for this position is $72,000 to $75,000.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Roving - Couch 9 & Novus
job.description:
Multifamily portfolios that span multiple asset types and multiple sites create a specific operational challenge: properties need consistent, skilled management coverage even when staff is thin. The Roving Community Assistant Manager role exists to solve exactly that problem. At CloudTen Residential, this position covers two Portland-area communities, Couch 9 and Novus, moving between sites based on where support is needed most. If you're early in your property management career and want broad exposure fast, this kind of roving structure compresses years of single-site learning into a much shorter window.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-cycle assistant manager position, just not anchored to one address. Day to day, you'll support each community's operations in three connected areas: administration, leasing, and financial oversight.

On the administrative side, you'll conduct unit and common area inspections, assist with move-in and move-out documentation, and help maintain both current and previous resident files. On the financial side, you'll collect rent, post daily deposits, distribute non-payment notices, track delinquency, and work within company accounting directives for weekly and monthly reporting. On the leasing side, you'll field prospect calls, tour apartments, secure deposits, update traffic logs daily, support renewals, and keep a current read on what competing properties are doing.

When the Community Manager is off-site, you step into full supervisory responsibility for whichever property you're assigned to. That means the role requires Fair Housing fluency and a professional baseline that holds up under scrutiny, not just support-level familiarity.

A valid driver's license is required. You'll be traveling between properties regularly, so this isn't a role where you park once and stay put.

  • Property management software experience (required)
  • Working knowledge of federal and state landlord-tenant and collections law
  • Comfort with leasing conversations, closing commitments, and handling objections
  • Ability to read and work within financial and operational reports
  • Strong written and verbal communication across residents, prospects, and internal teams
  • Valid driver's license

Skills This Role Builds

The skills this position requires and the skills it builds aren't identical. You need to arrive with basic software fluency, financial literacy, and enough leasing experience to run a tour and close a deposit. What you'll build here is something harder to teach from a single-site job: the ability to read a property's operational health quickly, adapt to a different team's rhythms, and identify what needs attention without being told. Roving roles train you to audit fast and act decisively, which is exactly the skill set that leads to a full Community Manager position.

CloudTen's Portland portfolio includes asset types that don't often sit together in one operator's hands, including hotel-to-residential conversions and high-rise lease-ups alongside value-add repositioning. Exposure to that range of deal types at the assistant manager level is genuinely uncommon and transfers well if you eventually move into a portfolio-level or regional role. The pay range for this position is $26.00 to $28.00 per hour, depending on experience.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager, EDE Apartments
job.description:
Most multifamily communities operate in a rhythm: lease, retain, operate, repeat. The Assistant Community Manager role exists to keep that rhythm steady when the Community Manager is pulled toward bigger-picture decisions. At EDE Apartments in Frederick, MD, that means owning the operational middle ground between leasing activity and financial accountability across 350 luxury units.

EDE is a premium residential community close to downtown Frederick, with upscale interiors and a high standard of resident experience baked into the product. Jefferson Apartment Group, a vertically integrated firm handling acquisition, development, construction, and management in-house, staffs its communities accordingly. This role reports to the Community Manager and covers the full scope of on-site operations, from bookkeeping to renewal management to direct resident engagement.

What the Role Requires You to Bring

Two years of property management experience is the floor here, and that experience should be substantive. You'll need to manage collections procedures and keep bad debt below budget. That means understanding delinquency at a ledger level, not just flagging late payers. RealPage/OneSite experience is preferred, and if you've used it to run month-end reporting or track lease expirations, you're already operating at the pace this role expects.

The renewal function is a core responsibility. At a 350-unit community with a luxury price point, retention directly protects NOI. You'll need to proactively manage your MTM exposure and communicate renewal offers clearly and on time. Escalated resident concerns will land on your desk too, and the expectation is resolution, not referral. Social media management for the property's channels (blog, Facebook, and Twitter) is also part of the scope, so comfort with community-facing communication in written form matters.

  • Minimum 2 years of on-site property management experience
  • Strong working knowledge of collections procedures and delinquency management
  • RealPage/OneSite familiarity preferred
  • High school diploma required; college degree preferred
  • Comfort leading site team members while staying focused on leasing and renewal goals

What the Role Builds

For someone with solid leasing or administrative experience, this position is a genuine development opportunity in financial operations. Managing bad debt, producing reports, and working within budget guidelines on resident events all train the kind of financial discipline that Community Manager and Regional roles require. You'll also develop retention strategy skills: designing programs that support long-term residency, planning and executing resident events, and tracking what actually moves renewal rates. Those are transferable to any asset class, from Class A lease-ups to stabilized garden-style portfolios.

The honest challenge worth naming: luxury communities carry resident expectations to match the price point. Customer service at EDE means consistent, fast, and correct responses across every touchpoint. If your instinct is to resolve rather than defer, you'll fit the pace. If you're still building that instinct, this role will sharpen it quickly.

Jefferson Apartment Group offers a competitive hourly rate between $28 and $31, performance-based bonus potential, a full benefits package including medical, dental, and vision, paid time off, and potential rental discounts for eligible employees.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Assistant Community Manager at Avanath's Hollywood Hub property sits at the center of daily operations. Rent collection, delinquency follow-up, ledger reviews, and monthly projection reporting are core to the financial side of the job. You'll collect, post, and deposit rents and security deposits, track outstanding balances, and push through the proper steps when accounts fall behind. On the leasing side, you'll handle walk-in traffic, conduct tours, and support leasing consultants in converting prospects to residents.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the property. That means managing staff, handling resident concerns, inspecting make-ready units and vacancies, and keeping an eye on the overall condition of the community. This is also a compliance-heavy role. Avanath specializes in affordable workforce housing, so LIHTC tax credit compliance is central to how this property operates. You'll work closely with the Compliance department on file maintenance and make sure every lease-up and renewal meets program requirements. Fair Housing isn't a checkbox here; it's a daily operating standard you enforce and model for your team.

Resident retention is another real accountability. You'll organize appreciation events, respond to service requests, and act as a resource for residents who need help understanding anything that might affect their housing or their ability to pay rent on time. Eviction proceedings, when they happen, fall within your scope too. You'll follow proper notice timelines, document everything correctly, and represent the property in court if needed.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of experience in an Assistant Community Manager role
  • Solid working knowledge of LIHTC and tax credit program requirements
  • Hands-on experience with Yardi Voyager for rent posting, ledger management, and reporting
  • Bookkeeping accuracy and a disciplined approach to rent collection and delinquency tracking
  • Clear understanding of landlord/tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Strong communication skills across resident interactions, staff coordination, and vendor relationships
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel for reporting and correspondence

The Broader Picture

Affordable housing compliance adds a layer of complexity that you won't find at a conventional Class A property. LIHTC communities carry income certification requirements, annual recertifications, and regulatory oversight that demand real attention to detail on every resident file. Candidates who've only worked market-rate properties often underestimate this side of the job. If you already know your way around a tax credit file and understand how program rules interact with day-to-day leasing decisions, you'll move into this role with confidence. For someone coming from a compliance-strong background, this kind of assistant manager seat is a natural path toward a Community Manager role, particularly within a portfolio that's specifically built around affordable and workforce housing.

job.title: Access Control Officer (Part-Time Overnight Weekends) - Savina
job.description:
High-rise HOA communities in dense urban markets present a specific security challenge: controlling access points across multiple entry systems while also serving as the first face residents and guests see at odd hours. This role at Savina, a luxury residential community in San Diego, sits at that intersection of security and hospitality.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're working Friday and Saturday overnight shifts, 11 PM to 7:30 AM, at $21.00 per hour. That means your shift starts when the building is winding down and ends when it's waking back up. Most of your hours are quiet, but quiet doesn't mean passive. You're maintaining a visible security presence, patrolling common areas, and monitoring access points throughout the night. You enforce HOA rules, manage who enters the property, and handle whatever comes up, because things do come up at 2 AM in a residential building.

The concierge side of this role is real. Residents returning late, guests who need direction, deliveries that arrive at unusual hours: you're the person on the ground. At a luxury community like Savina, the expectation is that interactions feel professional and calm, not transactional or dismissive. The security function and the service function run at the same time, every shift.

Who Fits This Role

  • Comfortable working overnight hours independently, without a supervisor on-site for most of the shift
  • Able to stay alert and maintain a consistent patrol routine during low-traffic hours
  • Communicates clearly and professionally with residents and guests, including in tense situations
  • Reliable on weekends specifically: this is a part-time role but the schedule is fixed
  • Prior experience in access control, security, or a front-desk/concierge setting is a genuine advantage

One honest note: overnight weekend security work asks something specific of you physically and socially. Your schedule runs opposite to most people's. The shifts themselves are manageable, but if you haven't worked overnights before, it's worth thinking through what that does to your sleep and your weekends before you apply. The people who thrive in roles like this typically already know they're wired for it.

Action Property Management has operated in the HOA space since 1984 and manages over 300 communities across the western United States. Savina is part of that portfolio, and the expectation of professionalism at the property level reflects the company's positioning in the luxury HOA segment.

job.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Part-time leasing roles at student or conventional communities in a market like Charleston carry real weight. The hours may be fewer, but the expectations at the front desk stay the same: convert traffic into signed leases, keep the pipeline moving, and make every prospect feel like the community was built for them.

What This Role Actually Requires

PeakMade is looking for someone who already knows how to close. One year of sales or leasing experience is the baseline, and that experience needs to show up in your results, not just your resume. Familiarity with platforms like Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage matters because CRM accuracy directly affects how well the team tracks leads and forecasts occupancy. You'll work weekends and peak leasing hours, which is when the bulk of qualified traffic shows up, so scheduling flexibility is a practical requirement, not a footnote.

The core of the job is converting leads across every channel: phone, email, text, and in-person tours. Strong follow-up discipline matters as much as the tour itself. Multi-touch outreach (calls plus emails plus texts) is the standard approach, and the candidates who do it consistently outperform those who don't. You'll also support the operational side of the lease cycle, including collecting deposits, completing lease paperwork accurately, and contributing to the annual turn process when the time comes.

What This Role Builds

For someone newer to the industry, a part-time leasing role at a professionally managed company is one of the best ways to build a foundation. You'll develop a sharp read on pricing strategy, competitive positioning, and how urgency gets created in a tour without feeling manufactured. You'll also get real exposure to the rhythm of a leasing office: tracking traffic, managing prospect pipelines, and tying your daily activity directly to occupancy numbers. Those are skills that transfer directly into a full-time leasing role, a leasing manager position, or eventually an assistant manager track.

One thing worth knowing about the Charleston market: it draws a competitive renter pool, especially in the student and young professional segments. Learning to differentiate your community on service and experience, not just price or amenities, is a skill you'll sharpen fast here.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Commission-eligible structure with earning potential tied to leasing performance
  • Housing discounts (varies by community)
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Wellness programs and team recognition
  • Access to growth and leadership development programming

If you bring a closer's mindset and genuine follow-through, a part-time role at a company like PeakMade can move fast toward something full-time.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Essex & Merrick)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Prometheus calls this role a Neighbor Ambassador, and the title reflects something real about how the company approaches leasing. At the Essex and Merrick communities in Portland, you're the first face a prospective resident sees and, often, the person they call when something feels off after move-in. The leasing side is what it sounds like: touring prospects, guiding them through applications, preparing rental agreements, and working to convert traffic into signed leases. The administrative side gets less glamour in job postings but takes up real time. Market surveys, occupancy reports, posting unit availability, keeping records clean. Learn this well and you'll understand how a property actually runs, not just how to close a lease.

Weekends are non-negotiable here. Portland traffic peaks on Saturdays and Sundays, and that's when prospects tour. Your days off will fall during the week. If your personal life is structured around weekends, be honest with yourself about that before applying.

The per-lease incentive, semi-annual bonus, and weekend shift premium mean your take-home can exceed the base rate meaningfully if you're producing. Lease-up bonuses are also listed as applicable, which suggests at least one of these properties may be in a growth or stabilization phase. Worth asking about in your interview.

What You Bring

  • Genuine comfort in customer-facing, sales-oriented work. Prior property management experience is not required.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. You'll be drafting ads, preparing agreements, and talking to prospects all in the same shift.
  • Self-direction. You won't have someone telling you to follow up on every prospect or post updated availability.
  • Availability to work a schedule that includes weekends consistently.
  • Creativity and a willingness to solve small problems on the fly. Leasing offices move fast and rarely follow a script.

Context Worth Knowing

For someone entering property management, this type of role builds the foundation for everything else. Leasing consultants who learn the administrative side well, not just the tours and closes, tend to move into assistant manager and then manager positions with real confidence. You'll exit this role knowing how to read traffic trends, understand concessions in context, and recognize what occupancy pressure looks like before it becomes a problem. Those skills carry across any asset class or market. Prometheus also offers tuition reimbursement and educational assistance, which matters if you're planning to grow within the industry and want to pursue credentials along the way.

The company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage, including dependents, is worth noting plainly. That benefit has real dollar value that rarely shows up in hourly rate comparisons.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Community Manager roles at Hawthorne Residential Partners sit at the center of everything: the team, the residents, the numbers, and the owners. At The NinetyNine in Raleigh, that means running a full multifamily operation where you're equally accountable for NOI and the human experience happening inside the community every day.

What You're Actually Responsible For

Financially, you'll own the budget. That includes rent collection, delinquency tracking, deposit accounting, and the kind of monthly reporting that keeps ownership informed and confident. You'll work inside Yardi and Knock daily, so fluency with those platforms matters from day one.

On the operations side, you'll coordinate with maintenance on work orders and preventative care, manage vendor relationships, and conduct regular property inspections to keep curb appeal and quality where they need to be. Leasing doesn't stop when you become a manager. You'll support the team on tours, guide prospects through the process, and keep occupancy and renewal goals in clear view. Pricing strategy and concession decisions fall to you as well.

Then there's the team itself. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and handle the real work of keeping people aligned and accountable when the pressure is on. Resident escalations land on your desk too. You won't just hand those off. How you handle a difficult conversation with a long-term resident often matters as much as the outcome itself.

Who Fits Well Here

  • At least two years in multifamily property management, with experience as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of direct community manager experience is highly preferred
  • Comfort reading financial reports and making budget-informed decisions
  • Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office experience preferred
  • CAM, CAPS, or a real estate or property management license is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required

The candidates who tend to do well in this kind of role aren't the ones who are great at either people or numbers. They're the ones who hold both at once without letting one slide when the other gets hard. A delinquency spike in the same week as a lease-up push and a difficult resident situation is a normal week. Your ability to stay grounded and keep your team steady through that is what separates strong managers from average ones.

Growth and Schedule

Hawthorne has a formal career path program, and the community manager seat is a real launching point toward regional management. The Learning and Development team is actively involved in that progression, not just at onboarding.

The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Resident events or community needs may occasionally pull outside those hours, which is worth knowing going in.

Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Altura Apartments
job.description:
Ackermann Group has been operating in the Midwest since 1938, and that kind of tenure doesn't happen without operational discipline. The company manages its own portfolio, which means maintenance decisions get made by people who understand asset value, not just work order volume. The Maintenance Supervisor at Altura Apartments, a 201-unit community in Cincinnati, sits at the center of that discipline.

This is a full-scope supervisory role. You're coordinating the make-ready schedule, keeping vacant units market-ready, managing parts inventory, holding vendor relationships, and executing the preventive maintenance plan. You're also the last line of defense on specialist-level troubleshooting across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting. When something at Altura doesn't have an easy answer, this role finds it.

Budget familiarity matters here. You'll manage maintenance-related spending, negotiate rates with local contractors, and document everything through Ackermann's internal systems. Capital improvement projects are also part of the work, coordinated alongside the Community Manager. That means understanding when to spend, what to defer, and how to communicate both.

The day-to-day rhythm runs Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, with an after-hours emergency on-call rotation built in. Snow removal is part of the job. So is running regular team meetings and participating in hiring decisions for the maintenance staff you'll be leading.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of hands-on trade depth and people management. Plenty of technicians can fix an HVAC unit. Fewer can also hold a team accountable to a turn schedule, keep delinquent service requests from stacking up, and walk a capex punch list with a general contractor. If you've done both, consistently, this role fits.

Qualifications

  • 3 or more years of maintenance experience with demonstrated supervisory responsibility
  • EPA Type I and II Certification (required)
  • CPO and CAMT certifications (preferred)
  • Aquatherm system experience (preferred)
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Outlook and Office for documentation and reporting
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent

Ackermann offers competitive hourly pay with quarterly bonus potential and lease renewal commissions, plus medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid time off including your birthday, and an employee rent discount applicable at any Ackermann community.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Fox Point in Old Farm Apartments
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the front desk and front door of Fox Point in Old Farm Apartments in Millcreek, Utah. You're the first person prospects see when they walk in and the first voice residents hear when something needs attention. That covers a wide range of tasks in a single shift.

On the leasing side, you'll answer questions about availability and pricing, guide prospects through the application process, and follow up to convert interest into signed leases. You'll also prep self-guided tour units, making sure they're clean, staged, and ready before anyone walks through the door. When a unit is turning, you may assist with move-in and move-out coordination.

On the resident side, you'll handle work order entry, package pickups, key distribution, and general inquiries. You act as the link between residents and the maintenance team, keeping communication clear and expectations accurate. You'll also walk the community regularly to check that amenities, common areas, and tour paths are presentable and up to Cottonwood's standards.

Beyond day-to-day operations, you'll support social media posts, help plan resident events, and contribute to the overall atmosphere of the community.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year of in-person, customer-facing experience
  • At least one year in customer service, administrative work, sales, or hospitality
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and willingness to learn property management software (Entrata experience is a plus)
  • Strong interpersonal skills across a wide range of personalities
  • Ability to multitask in a busy office environment without dropping details
  • Physical ability to walk the property, stand for extended periods, and lift up to 50 pounds regularly
  • Flexibility for extended hours, including early starts when needed
  • Multifamily experience is a bonus, but not required

Context Worth Knowing

Cottonwood Residential has been an early adopter of self-guided tours, which shifts some of the traditional leasing workflow. In this role, you'll spend time managing and maintaining those tour units rather than escorting every prospect personally. That means your attention to detail on unit presentation directly affects how prospects experience the community before they ever speak with anyone on staff.

For someone coming from hospitality or retail, this role translates well.
