The skills that make a strong hotel front desk associate or service coordinator carry directly into property management, and this type of position often leads to a full leasing consultant role or assistant manager track as you build familiarity with occupancy goals and the leasing cycle.

Cottonwood Residential notes that AI-assisted tools may be part of the hiring process, including scheduling and preliminary outreach, and that interviews may be recorded and summarized for their hiring team.

job.title: Full-Time Overnight Lead Cleaner (Thu-Mon, 11PM-6AM)
job.description:
Comstock's ParkX division operates parking and mixed-use amenity infrastructure across several of its Reston-area developments, and the porter team is the crew that keeps those common spaces presentable around the clock. This overnight lead role runs Thursday through Monday, 11PM to 6AM, covering the hours when most staff are gone and the standard of cleanliness still has to hold.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The bulk of the shift involves systematic cleaning of lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public-facing common areas across assigned sites. Pressure washing, window cleaning, and trash removal are recurring tasks, not occasional ones. You'll follow established checklists and cleaning schedules, maintain your janitorial closet in organized, hazard-free condition, and complete end-of-shift documentation so the next crew has a clean handoff. When events are scheduled at a property, setup and breakdown support falls to this team. You'll also monitor cleaning supply inventory, flag any equipment issues to management, and document safety hazards or maintenance concerns as you find them. The lead designation means you're expected to fill coverage gaps when coworkers are out and to handle cleanliness concerns promptly and professionally when they come up mid-shift.

What This Role Requires

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds; extended periods of standing, walking, and physical activity are routine
  • Comfort working in variable conditions: outdoor temperatures, chemical exposure, and noise
  • Availability for the full Thursday through Monday overnight schedule, including events and peak periods
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to work independently through a shift with minimal supervision
  • Professional demeanor when interacting with property staff, residents, and visitors, even at odd hours

The Reston Context and Where This Can Go

Reston's mixed-use density, particularly around the Silver Line corridor, has raised the bar on what "clean and presentable" means for shared spaces. Properties here compete on the experience they offer residents and tenants, and the overnight porter team is a direct part of that. Comstock's portfolio continues to grow, and the posting notes real advancement opportunities within the organization along with annual professional development funding. For someone who's reliable, detail-oriented, and wants a path upward in facilities or operations, this kind of overnight lead role is often where that trajectory starts.

Compensation is set at $17.50 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance, parental leave, and free parking with EV charging access.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a skill-intensive role that gets underestimated. The best consultants are running sales conversations, reading market signals, managing first impressions across physical and digital touchpoints, and closing deals, all in the same afternoon. At Berkshire Residential Investments's Skyline Towers, the Leasing Consultant position puts all of those skills to work in a structure that rewards both people instincts and disciplined follow-through.

The Skills This Role Builds

Sales conversion is the core competency here. Berkshire sets a clear benchmark of at least a 20% closing ratio, which means you'll develop the discipline to track your own performance and adjust your approach based on traffic patterns and prospect behavior. That's the kind of metric fluency that carries directly into an Assistant Manager role, where you're reading T-3 reports and tying leasing activity to occupancy goals.

Market awareness is the other skill this position sharpens fast. Contributing ideas to the Property Manager on marketing and resident satisfaction means you're not just executing, you're observing the competitive set, understanding what's driving concessions or traffic in your submarket, and forming opinions. Consultants who develop that habit early tend to move into management with a meaningful head start.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

A good portion of your time centers on tour presentation. Your tour routes and model units are your primary sales tools, so maintaining them at a consistent standard is part of the job, not an afterthought. Beyond tours, you're handling resident communications, supporting the leasing office atmosphere, and collaborating with the broader team on ways to improve the resident experience. Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating under third-party management, which means you're working within a company that has a direct stake in the asset's performance and long-term reputation.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, ideally in a role where closing or convincing was part of the job
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, since resident correspondence reflects the property
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to adapt as leasing platforms evolve
  • Genuine attention to detail on administrative tasks, because lease files and follow-up logs matter
  • The kind of energy that holds up through a busy Saturday, not just a quiet Tuesday

One honest note on what separates good leasing consultants from great ones: it's usually curiosity about the business. Consultants who ask why occupancy dipped, who track their own closing ratio without being prompted, and who pay attention to what the competition is offering tend to grow faster and land better opportunities. This role gives you plenty of material to work with if you're inclined to pay attention.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Redstone Residential runs one of the largest third-party student housing platforms in the country, with over 38,000 beds across 20 states. This Community Manager role sits at the top of the site-level org chart for a property in Orem, Utah, reporting directly to a Regional Manager. The compensation lands between $60,000 and $65,000 annually, with a performance bonus opportunity of up to an additional 20%. That's real upside if you know how to run a tight operation.

What You'll Actually Do

This is full P&L ownership at the site level. You're accountable for occupancy, NOI, delinquency, budget adherence, and the day-to-day team that keeps everything moving. Redstone tracks KPIs closely, so expect weekly and monthly reporting cadences up the chain. You'll own the leasing and renewal strategy, which in student housing means you're thinking about lease-up timelines that don't behave like conventional multifamily. You're also coordinating marketing, managing vendor relationships, and handling projects that range from campaigns to construction. The entrepreneurial environment Redstone describes is real: site managers here carry more decision-making weight than you'd find at a typical fee management shop.

Building relationships with campus resources matters in this market. Orem sits adjacent to Utah Valley University, and that proximity shapes both your traffic sources and your resident profile. If you've worked student housing before, you already know that renewals behave differently, concession timing is compressed, and your delinquency patterns shift around semester breaks. If you haven't, that's a meaningful learning curve.

What You Bring

  • At least three years in student housing or conventional multifamily property management
  • A minimum of two years in a property manager seat with direct P&L responsibility
  • Demonstrated experience managing a budget and owning outcomes, not just reporting on them
  • A professional presentation that holds up in client-facing situations
  • The ability to manage multiple projects under pressure without losing track of the details
  • Familiarity with Entrata is a plus, but comfort learning new property management software is the actual requirement
  • Experience developing and coaching a site team, including giving constructive feedback that actually sticks

Context Worth Knowing

Redstone is headquartered in Provo and has been growing its conventional portfolio alongside its student housing base. That dual focus means a Community Manager here may benefit from exposure to both asset types, which translates well if you're thinking about where this role leads. Site managers who perform well at operators like Redstone tend to move into multi-site Regional roles, and that path tends to open faster at growing third-party platforms than at larger, more bureaucratic REITs. The performance bonus structure reinforces that: if you drive results, the compensation reflects it.

One honest note: student housing sites run harder during lease-up season than most conventional properties, and the resident base requires a different kind of patience. If that sounds familiar, you'll fit in. If it sounds exhausting, that's useful information too.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
A tenant calls at 9 a.m. to dispute a lease renewal notice. By 10, you're pulling EIV records for an interim recertification. By noon, you're in Yardi creating a purchase order so the maintenance crew can finish a work order before a move-in tomorrow. That's Tuesday. Wednesday looks different, but it's equally full.

The Work Itself

This Assistant Community Manager role sits at a Fairstead affordable property in Sharpsville, Pennsylvania, and it touches nearly every layer of daily operations. You'll work alongside the Property Manager to keep the community in compliance with HUD's 4350.3 Handbook, which means recertifications (annual and interim), preparation for REAC reviews and Management and Occupancy Reviews, and ensuring LIHTC compliance stays airtight. When lease violations arise, you document them and coordinate with the in-house legal team. When eviction proceedings are necessary, you're involved in that process too.

On the financial side, you're tracking arrears regularly and following up with residents according to company policy. Rent collection, posting, and daily deposits fall within your oversight. Purchase orders go through Yardi, and accounting transactions run through you. Responsiveness is taken seriously here: calls and emails get returned within hours, never more than 24.

The resident-facing part of this role carries real weight. Affordable housing residents often have fewer alternatives and higher stakes when something goes wrong. Responding to complaints and service requests promptly, flagging move-ins and move-outs, and coordinating with the maintenance team are all daily rhythms. The lease renewal program is also yours to oversee, which connects directly to occupancy stability and the community's overall performance.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management (subsidized experience matters here)
  • Working knowledge of EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Comfort with HUD regulatory frameworks, recertification processes, and compliance reviews
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across a range of audiences
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office
  • Familiarity with the local residential market in western Pennsylvania

One thing that separates strong candidates in affordable housing assistant manager roles from those who struggle: the ability to hold firm on compliance requirements while still treating residents with genuine respect. HUD and LIHTC programs have real rules, and tenants are real people. Doing both well at the same time is the skill.

Fairstead operates as an integrated owner, operator, and developer across 28 states, which means the company tends to promote from within and has career pathways that extend well beyond a single property. For someone looking to build toward a Community Manager or Regional role in affordable housing, the compliance depth you'd develop here transfers directly.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Multi site - Redfield Ridge, Brooktree, Plumas Garden, The Creek at South Carson
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Multi-site maintenance work asks more of a technician than a single-property position does. The skills that matter most here are diagnostic speed, trade breadth, and the organizational discipline to stay on top of work orders, inventory, and preventive maintenance schedules across four separate addresses. CloudTen Residential is placing a technician across Redfield Ridge, Brooktree, Plumas Garden, and The Creek at South Carson, all in the Reno area. You'll rotate between sites based on project needs, so the ability to context-switch quickly and maintain consistent service standards across communities is just as important as being handy with a wrench.

The trade range this role draws on is wide: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, pool and spa maintenance, and custodial work all show up in a typical week. Reno's high-desert climate adds a practical layer to that list. Freeze protection, HVAC efficiency under temperature swings, and pool chemistry management through hot summers and cold winters are real considerations for any technician working in Northern Nevada.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Most days start with a property walk. You'll cover grounds, check pet stations, clear debris, and assess what's changed overnight before the first work orders hit. Make-ready turns are a steady part of the workload. You'll prepare vacated units for the next resident, working from punch lists and keeping close communication with your Community Manager on unit status. Work orders carry a 24-hour completion standard, and when parts delays push a job past that window, you own the communication to both the manager and the affected resident.

  • Preventive maintenance across lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety equipment on a monthly schedule
  • On-call emergency response as needed
  • Move-in and move-out inspection support
  • Inventory tracking for tools, equipment, and supplies
  • Hazardous materials recordkeeping and MSDS compliance
  • PPE use is mandatory: back belts, goggles, and gloves are required on your person during all work hours

A valid driver's license in good standing is required. Regular travel between the four properties is a core function of the position, not an occasional ask.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

CloudTen's portfolio includes hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects, so the company is comfortable with complexity. That culture tends to reward technicians who notice problems before they become work orders and who communicate proactively rather than waiting to be asked. A CPO certification gives you a leg up on the pool maintenance side of things, though the company will consider candidates without one. What the role genuinely requires is someone organized enough to manage multiple sites without letting any single property feel like it's getting the leftovers of your attention. The pay range runs $22.00 to $24.00 per hour depending on experience.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at The Regatta Apartments
job.description:
Leasing roles at apartment communities have shifted considerably over the past few years. Self-guided tours, AI-driven follow-up tools, and digital communication across phone, text, and email mean the front-line team member handles a broader mix of touchpoints than the traditional leasing consultant did even five years ago. Cottonwood Residential has leaned into that shift early, and this role at The Regatta Apartments in Houston reflects that approach.

What the Role Actually Involves

The Customer Experience Specialist is the primary face of The Regatta. That means greeting every person who walks into the leasing office, handling inbound calls and digital inquiries with quick, accurate responses, and staying current on pricing and availability across all floor plans so you can answer a prospect's questions on the spot. You'll prep apartments for showings daily and walk the tour path, amenities, and vacant homes to make sure everything meets Cottonwood's standards before a prospect or new resident sees it. Move-in readiness, the package room, community event planning, social media support, and vendor communication all fall within this position's scope.

The schedule is full-time and includes evenings and weekends. That's standard for a leasing role at a residential community, especially one running self-guided tours, which extend traffic well past traditional office hours.

Who Fits This Role Well

Strong candidates here tend to be people who stay organized under a shifting daily workload and who communicate clearly across formats: in person, by phone, and in writing. The Houston apartment market is competitive, with a significant volume of new Class A supply continuing to come online across submarkets like Midtown, the Medical Center corridor, and the Energy Corridor. At a property like The Regatta, that means prospects have options and they know it. The leasing team member who can quickly build rapport, answer questions with actual pricing knowledge, and create a polished move-in experience is the one who converts traffic into signed leases.

Cottonwood positions this role as a starting point with a path toward management. That's worth taking seriously. Leasing consultants who build genuine operational knowledge, including understanding how occupancy decisions connect to NOI and how their day-to-day work affects lease-up performance, tend to move into assistant manager and property manager roles faster than those who treat leasing as purely a sales function.

  • Full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits available within the first 30 days
  • 401k and HSA with company match
  • Three weeks of paid time off available in year one
  • 10.5 paid holidays
  • Quarterly bonus structure on top of base pay

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits right at the intersection of people and numbers. On any given day, you might be walking delinquency reports with the Community Manager in the morning, coaching a leasing consultant on follow-up techniques by midday, and handling a renewal conversation with a long-term resident by afternoon. The work isn't linear, and that's genuinely part of what makes it engaging.

You'll share responsibility for the financial health of the community, including rent collection, tracking delinquencies, supporting eviction processes when necessary, and pulling together accurate reporting. Lease files, rent rolls, and make-ready schedules need to stay current, and that falls partly on you. You'll also have a hand in pricing strategy, using market surveys and occupancy data to recommend rate adjustments to the Community Manager.

On the leasing side, you'll support the team's performance and training, help execute marketing strategies, and stay current on what competitors in the Daytona Beach market are doing. Weekend availability is required, so expect to be part of the rotation when the office is busiest with traffic.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in leasing, sales, or hospitality. Property management experience is preferred, but strong sales instincts and customer service skills from other fields genuinely transfer here.
  • Comfort with financial reporting and attention to detail when managing records. You don't need to be an accountant, but you do need to catch errors before they compound.
  • Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Office and confidence navigating software platforms. Experience with Yardi is a plus.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including with residents who are frustrated, vendors who are delayed, and owners who want answers.
  • A valid driver's license and a high school diploma or equivalent.

The Bigger Picture

Waypoint Management Services offers a competitive compensation package that includes monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount program, 120 hours of PTO in your first year (with increases over time), two floating days annually, and medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one. A 401k with company match is also part of the package.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the ability to hold both sides of the job with equal seriousness. Some people are great with residents but let the administrative side slip. Others are detail-oriented but struggle to build real rapport with a team or a community. The Assistant Community Manager role rewards people who can do both, and do them consistently, even on a busy Saturday.

For someone who's ready to step into more responsibility, this kind of role is a common path toward a full Community Manager position. The financial exposure, team leadership experience, and operational breadth you build here are exactly what makes that transition possible.

job.title: $1,000 Sign-On Bonus - Maintenance Technician (The Reserve)
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance is a retention game as much as a repair game. When work orders pile up and response times slip, resident satisfaction scores follow, and renewals get harder to close. BAM Companies built their model around keeping that gap tight, and the Maintenance Technician role at The Reserve in Evansville is central to how that happens day to day.

The pay range runs $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience, and the position comes with a $1,000 sign-on bonus. BAM has been operating since 2010 and has a stated emphasis on work-life balance and internal culture, which tends to matter more in maintenance than in almost any other property role given the after-hours demands that come with the job.

What the Role Covers

This is a full-scope maintenance position. You'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and structural repairs across interior units and exterior common areas. Preventative maintenance is a real part of the workload, not just a line in a job description. Documenting issues before they escalate is how a well-run property controls costs and protects NOI, and that discipline matters here. After-hours emergency calls are part of the deal, so candidates should factor that in honestly before applying.

The basic qualifications the team is looking for:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2 to 3 years of hands-on maintenance experience
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification (preferred, not strictly required)

The Benefits Picture

BAM's benefits package has some specifics worth noting. PTO starts at 88 hours after the first 90 days and moves to 120 hours after year one. The holiday schedule runs 14.5 days. Medical, dental, and vision coverage is available with BAM covering the larger share of the premium. Life insurance is included at no cost to employees. The company also offers rent discounts at BAM-managed communities for anyone interested in living where they work.

One thing that separates strong maintenance techs in a role like this: the ability to triage accurately under pressure. When three emergency calls come in on a Saturday night, the tech who can correctly assess severity, prioritize the genuine safety issue, and communicate honestly with the other two residents keeps satisfaction scores intact and avoids the kind of escalations that end up on a manager's Monday morning desk. Diagnostic speed and resident communication tend to matter just as much as wrench time in a service-heavy multifamily environment.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
The unit flipped yesterday. Today, a resident moves in. How the make-ready looks, how the punch list got closed, and whether the shop has what it needs to support tomorrow's turns, that falls on this role as much as anyone.

Berkshire Residential Investments, a company that owns and manages its own portfolio, is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Supervisor at Riverpoint. Because Berkshire operates in-house rather than as a third-party manager, the maintenance team carries real accountability for asset quality. That's not a small distinction. The people doing the work and the people responsible for the investment are on the same side of the table.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a support and coordination role as much as a technical one. You're working alongside the Maintenance Supervisor to schedule daily work, keep technicians on track, and make sure make-ready units hit their target dates. You'll help inspect turns, close out punch lists, and step in hands-on when the team needs it to meet a deadline. Beyond unit work, you're responsible for the shop itself: equipment condition, supply inventory, key security, and the general discipline that keeps a maintenance operation running cleanly. Tour routes and models are part of your watch too. If they don't look right, that's on you to flag and fix before a prospect walks through.

Spending approvals run through the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager. You're expected to communicate repair needs and requisitions before money goes out, not after. Safety compliance is non-negotiable and part of daily oversight.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience across general maintenance disciplines
  • Comfort with technology, including maintenance software and related applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Physical ability to meet the demands of daily maintenance work
  • The ability to take direction and give it, depending on the moment

The best candidates at this level know how to manage up and manage down in the same shift. You're relaying information to supervisors about what's needed while also keeping techs focused and moving. The soft skill that matters most here is the one that rarely shows up in job postings: knowing when to troubleshoot independently and when to escalate before a small problem turns into a capital expense conversation.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development plans, medical coverage, and a 25% rent discount, among other benefits. They're direct about valuing the people side of the business, and their in-house model means there's a real career path here for someone who grows into a lead Maintenance Supervisor role over time.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the larger third-party student housing managers in the country. Their Boise property sits within a growing conventional portfolio, and this Leasing Manager role is the kind of position where you're close enough to the operation to matter but still have the Community Manager carrying the heavier administrative load. That's a reasonable place to build from.

The core of the job is occupancy. You'll work toward leasing goals through marketing campaigns, renewal pushes, and keeping your team pointed in the right direction. Day-to-day, that means prospect tours, fielding calls and emails, running the Entrata leasing workflow, and keeping resident ledgers clean. Delinquency doesn't fix itself, and neither does traffic that never converts. You'll need to be comfortable working both sides of that equation.

Redstone uses company-standard tools including Entrata, online listing platforms, and social marketing channels. If you've worked in a lease-up or managed renewals through a CRM before, you'll recognize the rhythm. If Entrata is new to you, it's learnable, but you'll want to come in already comfortable with technology generally. Microsoft Office, Gmail, Google Drive, and Dropbox are part of the daily workflow.

What tends to separate stronger candidates in this type of role is the ability to hold a conversation that actually converts. Leasing is sales, and the people who do it well don't just hand out floor plans. They read what a prospect actually needs, adjust their pitch, and follow up without being obnoxious about it. The resident happiness piece matters too. In student and conventional housing both, online reputation and renewals are downstream of how residents feel about the team they're dealing with.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • Strong customer service and sales instincts
  • Comfortable with technology: Entrata experience is a plus, but solid computer literacy is required
  • High school diploma or GED required; some college preferred
  • Able to keep pace in a busy leasing environment without losing attention to detail on ledger accuracy and communications

Compensation is $21.00 per hour. Benefits include health, vision, and dental coverage, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, three paid service days, paid parental leave, and a 401(k) with up to 6% company match. There's also a continued education program, an employee assistance program, and short-term disability insurance.

Boise has seen real rent growth and population increases over the last several years, which means occupancy pressure can cut both ways. Strong traffic helps, but it also raises resident expectations. A leasing team that communicates well and follows through keeps renewals healthy even when concessions get tighter. This role puts you in the middle of that dynamic daily.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
What This Role Covers

Affordable housing compliance doesn't run itself. At a HUD-regulated property in Boaz, Alabama, the Assistant Community Manager keeps the daily operation moving while staying on the right side of federal requirements. Fairstead runs an integrated platform across 30,000+ units in 28 states, and this position is the engine-level work that keeps a single property performing inside that larger system.

Day to day, you'll work alongside the Property Manager on everything from rent collection and Yardi posting to recertification reviews and lease violations. Residents bring questions, complaints, and service requests. You respond fast, document accurately, and follow through. That rhythm is the job.

Core Responsibilities

  • Support compliance with the HUD 4350.3 Handbook and assist in preparing for REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews (MOR), LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits
  • Conduct annual and interim recertification reviews; execute intervention plans for residents who fall out of lease or compliance requirements
  • Track arrears regularly, follow up with residents per company policy, and work with in-house legal on rent payment status
  • Oversee daily rent collection, posting, and deposits; create purchase orders in Yardi
  • Manage the lease renewal program to maintain target retention rates
  • Document lease violations and coordinate the eviction process where required
  • Coordinate with maintenance staff on service request completion; alert staff to move-ins, move-outs, and emergencies
  • Handle phones, emails, and messages promptly within the same business day

What You Bring

Fairstead requires at least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management. Familiarity with EIV, Yardi, and RealPage is expected from the start. Strong written and verbal communication matter here because resident-facing work and internal documentation both demand clarity.

The candidates who do well in this role understand recertification timelines and don't let them slip. Affordable housing compliance has hard deadlines tied to federal oversight, and the gap between a good candidate and a great one is usually how well they manage those cycles without constant reminders from a supervisor. Experience preparing for a MOR or a REAC review is a real advantage.

Fairstead operates with a tech-forward approach, including data-driven tools and AI-assisted systems at the portfolio level. Being comfortable learning new platforms quickly is a practical requirement, not just a resume line.

This kind of role often leads to a full Property Manager position, especially at a company where affordable housing expertise is central to the business. If you want to build a career in affordable housing operations, this is the type of seat that sharpens the full skill set.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Multi site - Elan Quail Pointe and Elan Playa Mar
job.description:
Multi-site assistant manager roles are less common than single-property positions, and they require a different kind of mental flexibility. At any given point in the week, you might be at Elan Quail Pointe handling a delinquency follow-up, then shifting to Elan Playa Mar in Encinitas to cover leasing traffic while the community manager is off-site. The work is varied by design, and the role builds something single-site positions rarely can: the ability to read two distinct communities simultaneously and apply consistent standards across both.

Sunrise Management operates on a resident hospitality model, which shapes how this role functions day to day. Customer service here isn't an afterthought or a soft skill listed for completeness. It's built into the operational structure, from 24-hour maintenance response expectations to security deposit dispositions completed immediately after move-out. The people who thrive in this position treat those timelines as professional standards, not aspirational targets.

The financial side of the role is real and substantive. You'll collect rent, make daily deposits, issue non-payment notices, track delinquency, and support eviction proceedings when necessary. You'll work inside accounting directives that include weekly and monthly reporting cycles, expense tracking, and income reconciliation. If you've handled delinquency management before, that experience transfers directly here. If you haven't, this role will build that fluency quickly, because the volume across two properties gives you more exposure than most single-site assistant manager positions do.

Leasing is also part of the scope. You'll show units, work leads, help maintain market awareness, and support renewal efforts alongside the community manager. Entrata experience is preferred, and comfort with Excel and Word is expected at a working level.

Because you'll step into the community manager role during absences, you need to arrive with a baseline of judgment, not just task-completion ability. That's the distinction worth noting when you assess your own fit: this role requires the operational foundation and fair housing knowledge of someone who could run a property independently, while offering the structure of a manager above you on the days you're working together.

What you'll bring

  • 2 to 5 years of property management experience, with hands-on leasing and administrative responsibilities
  • Demonstrated understanding of delinquency processes, including notices and eviction procedures
  • Comfort with property management software, particularly Entrata
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws
  • A valid driver's license (required given the multi-site nature of the position)
  • Strong organizational habits and the self-sufficiency to manage competing priorities across locations

The Encinitas coastal market runs competitive, and staying current on comparable properties matters here. That local market awareness, combined with the breadth of experience you'll accumulate across two communities, makes this a position that develops genuine multi-site management capability. For someone looking to move into a community manager role, the exposure this position provides is meaningful preparation.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 7:45 a.m. on a Tuesday and you've already walked three units on the punch list, logged a water heater ticket, and grabbed a radio call about a resident with no A/C. In Austin's summers, that last one doesn't wait.

Griffis Residential is hiring a Maintenance Technician at one of their Austin communities. The work spans the full range of residential upkeep: make-readies, service requests, emergency response, preventive maintenance, and community inspections. You'll report to the Service Manager and work alongside the broader site team to keep occupancy healthy and residents satisfied.

What the Work Actually Involves

Make-ready work is central to this role. You'll turn units between residents, handling plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and appliance repairs to get apartments move-in ready on schedule. Emergency response carries a 30-minute target, so you'll need to triage and act quickly when things go wrong after hours or on weekends. Beyond reactive work, you'll help build and follow preventive maintenance schedules, conduct regular community inspections, document pool and spa chemical logs, and assist with grounds upkeep including litter pick-up and, when Austin's rare cold snaps hit, ice removal.

Budget awareness matters here too. You'll collaborate with the Service Manager and Community Manager on inventory tracking, so understanding where parts and supplies sit relative to financial goals is part of the job, not a secondary concern.

What Griffis Is Looking For

  • At least one year of hands-on experience in multi-family housing, hospitality, or a closely related field
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliances
  • CPO license and EPA certification (preferred at hire, required within your first six months)
  • Physical ability to lift up to 75 pounds and work outdoors across weather conditions
  • Comfortable communicating with residents directly. Spanish fluency is a bonus in this market
  • Basic computer skills and familiarity with maintenance tracking or work order systems
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The pay range runs from $23.50 to $27.00 per hour. Griffis layers in a solid benefits package: 50% rental discount, quarterly bonuses tied to reputation and occupancy, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, three weeks of PTO from day one, 11 paid holidays, six weeks of paid parental leave for primary caregivers, and tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually, among other offerings.

From a career perspective, this kind of role builds the technical foundation that feeds into Service Manager and Maintenance Supervisor positions. Technicians who develop strong HVAC and electrical chops, get comfortable reading a T-12 alongside a service manager, and learn how unit turns affect NOI are the ones who move up fastest in multi-family. Austin's rental market has stayed competitive, which means properties here stay serious about retention and resident satisfaction scores. That focus gives you real exposure to how maintenance performance connects to a property's broader financial outcomes, which is exactly the fluency that separates senior technicians from those who stay in the wrench-turning lane indefinitely.

job.title: Leasing Professional (Cottonwood Creek/Elowyn)
job.description:
Leasing at a Denver apartment community puts you at the front of every interaction a prospective resident has with the property. RedPeak is an owner-operator with a focused Denver portfolio, and this role covers two of their communities: Cottonwood Creek in Littleton and Elowyn Townhomes nearby. You'll split your time between both locations, which gives you exposure to two distinct product types under one operator.

What the Job Actually Involves

The core of this role is lead conversion. You'll handle inbound calls, online inquiries, and walk-in traffic, then move prospects through tours, applications, and lease signing. The goal is to maintain occupancy at 95% or better, which means close rates matter. You'll track everything in Yardi, keep prospect records current, and complete lease paperwork accurately from reservation through move-in.

Before a new resident moves in, you'll walk the unit against the make-ready punch list, prep keys, coordinate lock changes, and confirm the apartment is ready. That attention to detail at move-in directly shapes first impressions and renewal likelihood down the road.

Lead management is the heaviest part of the job (roughly a third of your focus). You'll respond to inquiries within required timeframes, qualify prospects based on their needs and urgency, and follow up consistently after showings. You'll also compile comp surveys weekly and shop competing properties twice a year, so you stay sharp on what the local rental market is doing.

Resident retention is part of the role too. Securing renewals, resolving service concerns, and building a sense of community aren't afterthoughts here. RedPeak's stated philosophy treats residents like neighbors, and that shows up in the day-to-day expectations for this position.

Who Fits This Role

  • Prior leasing or sales experience with a measurable track record
  • Comfortable with phone sales and email follow-up, not just in-person tours
  • Organized enough to manage lease paperwork, Yardi data entry, and multiple lead pipelines at once
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation (required for traveling between both sites)
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

The candidates who do well in roles like this aren't just personable. They treat follow-up as a discipline. A lot of leasing professionals are strong on the tour but inconsistent in the days after. Consistent follow-through from first contact to signed lease is what separates average performers from those who hit or exceed their monthly goals.

Schedule is Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm. Pay runs $21 to $23 per hour plus bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, employer-paid short-term disability, and a 401(k).

job.title: Leasing Professional - Melbourne, FL
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday morning, timeline vague, wish list long. Within fifteen minutes, you've figured out what they actually need, shown them a made-ready unit that fits, and started building the kind of rapport that turns a tour into a signed lease. That's the core of this role at Davis Development in Melbourne, FL.

What You'll Be Doing

Davis Development operates as a privately owned luxury apartment developer and property management company with more than 25 years in the business. Their on-site teams run communities with an owner-operator mindset, which means this leasing position carries real responsibility from day one. You won't be handed a script and left to follow it. You'll be expected to read traffic, understand the local sub-market, and bring informed input back to your Community Manager.

Day to day, the work spans the full leasing cycle: greeting and qualifying prospective residents, walking models and make-ready units each morning to confirm they're show-ready, processing applications and verifications, and keeping the Community Manager informed through daily and weekly reporting. Outreach marketing is also part of the job, so expect to get off-site periodically. A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required for that reason.

You'll also contribute to market survey work, helping the team stay current on competing properties and local conditions. That market awareness is more valuable than most leasing job descriptions let on. It's the kind of intelligence that shapes pricing decisions, concession strategy, and occupancy targets across the community.

What You Bring and Where This Role Can Take You

The requirements are straightforward:

  • At least one year of sales experience
  • At least one year of customer-facing experience
  • Property management or leasing experience preferred (not required)
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Strong communication skills across written and verbal channels
  • Detail orientation and a self-starter attitude

The leasing consultant role is one of the clearest on-ramps into property management leadership. The skills you build here, qualifying residents, reading a market, managing documentation, contributing to occupancy goals, directly translate to an Assistant Manager position and eventually a Community Manager seat. At a company like Davis Development, where management is in-house and teams are given genuine ownership over their communities, that path tends to move faster for people who treat the leasing floor like a business rather than a customer service queue.

Strong candidates in this kind of role tend to be curious about numbers (delinquency, occupancy trends, market comps) even when no one asks them to be. That curiosity signals readiness for the next level.

Benefits include health coverage starting the first of the month after 30 days, a 401(k) with a 4% employer match that vests immediately, company-paid life insurance, paid time off with a carryover provision, and a training and career development program. Davis Development also offers a company apparel store allowance.

job.title: Maintenance Tech | High-Rise Residential - Rainey Street District
job.description:
High-rise residential maintenance sits at the intersection of hospitality and building operations. Residents in a luxury condominium expect fast turnarounds, clean common areas, and a team that handles problems quietly and competently. When that standard slips, they notice immediately. This role exists to hold that standard day-to-day.

Worth Ross Management Company runs luxury multifamily and HOA properties, and this position puts you on-site at a condominium community in Austin's Rainey Street District. You'll report to the Chief Building Engineer and cover the Tuesday through Saturday, 11 AM to 7 PM shift, with on-call availability expected. That schedule means you're handling the bulk of resident activity hours, which is where most maintenance requests actually surface.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most days involve a mix of scheduled maintenance and reactive work orders. You're patching drywall, handling lock repairs, swapping HVAC filters, doing light plumbing and basic electrical, and painting touched-up surfaces between other tasks. You'll support move-ins and move-outs by prepping common areas and assisting with logistics, which in a high-rise means coordinating freight elevator access and keeping the process from disrupting other residents. Vendor and contractor escorts are part of the job too. You walk the work before it starts and after it finishes.

There's also the unglamorous side: porter duties, package handling, general building upkeep. In a luxury high-rise, keeping common areas presentable is taken as seriously as fixing a leaking faucet. Both matter to residents.

On-call shifts mean your phone can ring outside of business hours. That's real, and it's worth knowing before you apply. After-hours calls in a high-rise are typically plumbing failures, HVAC issues, or something mechanical that can't wait. You won't field every emergency alone since the Chief Building Engineer provides backup, but you need to be reachable and ready to respond.

What Makes a Strong Candidate Here

The minimum bar is two or more years in property or building maintenance with working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, HVAC basics, drywall, painting, and general repairs. Residential high-rise experience is a plus because the environment has specific demands: freight elevators, shared mechanical systems, noise-sensitive residents, and tight spaces where the work has to be done cleanly.

  • 2+ years of hands-on property or building maintenance experience
  • Comfort across basic plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, drywall, and painting
  • Willingness to carry on-call responsibility for after-hours emergencies
  • Strong communication with residents, vendors, and building staff
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

What actually separates strong candidates in this kind of role is resident interaction. Luxury condo residents talk to maintenance staff directly, often with high expectations and specific preferences. Technical skill gets you in the door. How you handle a frustrated resident in the hallway determines whether you last. If you're comfortable working with people as much as with tools, this environment fits well.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, an employee assistance program, identity theft protection, pet insurance, retirement, and paid time off.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's 7:45 AM and you're already mapping the day: three unit showings, a follow-up on a work order that's been open four days, and a rent collection call that can't wait until Friday. That's the rhythm of this role at CYM Living in Indianapolis.

The Work

CYM Living operates as a vertically integrated firm, meaning investment decisions and property operations run through the same organization. That structure puts real weight on the people closest to the assets. As an Assistant Property Manager, you'll own a defined geographic cluster of buildings across Indianapolis, which means daily drive-bys, consistent resident contact, and full accountability for how those properties look and perform.

Leasing is a core part of the job. You'll show units, walk prospective residents through the space, and close. That means knowing your inventory cold, understanding what motivates a prospect, and following through on paperwork between the applicant and the corporate office without letting anything slip. Occupancy and traffic are your responsibility to influence.

On the operational side, you'll track and follow up on maintenance requests, handle resident complaints, and collect monthly rent. When rent isn't paid, you'll administer collection procedures. The portfolio includes Section 8 units, so passing annual HUD inspections is part of the calendar, and keeping those units in compliance protects revenue that the T-12 depends on. You'll manage all of this inside Yardi, so comfort with that platform matters.

Because you're covering multiple buildings across a geographic area, a reliable personal vehicle isn't optional. You'll be moving between sites throughout the day, and sometimes in the evening, to keep eyes on the properties at different hours.

What This Role Requires

  • At least 3 years of property management or leasing experience
  • Multi-site management background is a strong advantage
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and mobile communication tools
  • Working knowledge of Yardi or willingness to get up to speed quickly
  • Reliable personal vehicle (required, non-negotiable)
  • Schedule flexibility to accommodate showings outside standard hours

The candidates who do well here tend to be self-starters who don't need someone to remind them to drive past a building or follow up on a ticket. Multi-site work rewards people who can hold a lot of context simultaneously and shift priorities without losing track of anything. If you've managed a scattered portfolio before, you know what it takes to keep delinquency low and residents happy across properties you can't watch all at once. That experience translates directly here.

CYM Living offers competitive compensation based on experience, full health, dental, and vision coverage, a retirement plan with employer match, paid time off, and an employee referral program. Professional development is part of the culture, which fits the firm's stated emphasis on internal growth.

job.title: Leasing Sales Consultant
job.description:
Village Green has been in the multifamily business for over a century, which means this isn't a startup figuring out its leasing playbook. Their consultants work within established systems, with training and tools behind them. For someone early in a leasing career, that infrastructure matters more than people often realize.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-cycle leasing position at a Village Green community in Rogers, AR. You're handling everything from the first phone inquiry through move-in coordination: qualifying prospects, conducting tours, working the follow-up pipeline, and closing. Traffic conversion is the core job. The base is $17/hr with commissions layered on top, so your earnings move with your close rate.

Beyond the lease-up side, you're also the first point of contact for current residents who have questions or concerns. Relationship management with the existing resident base feeds renewals, and renewals directly affect occupancy, so it's not a small part of the role even if leasing is the primary focus.

  • Qualify prospects quickly and match them to the right unit type and price point
  • Conduct tours and articulate the community's value relative to competing properties nearby
  • Manage leads and follow-up with enough consistency to actually move conversion numbers
  • Coordinate move-ins and handle the administrative side of the lease process accurately
  • Participate in marketing events and stay current on what the local comp set is doing
  • Keep records clean in the property management software

What Strong Candidates Bring

The posting asks for one to three years of sales experience, but the more useful question is whether you've actually closed against a quota and tracked your own numbers. Leasing consultants who thrive here know their traffic-to-lease conversion rate, know why they lost deals they didn't close, and treat follow-up as a discipline rather than an afterthought. Comfort with CRM or property management software helps. Weekend and evening availability is required, which is standard for this role type but worth saying plainly.

Rogers sits in the Northwest Arkansas corridor, a market that has seen consistent population growth tied to the broader Bentonville-area economy. That growth keeps multifamily demand relatively healthy, but it also means the comp set is active. Knowing how to position your community's strengths against nearby options is a real part of the job.

Where This Leads

Leasing consultant roles at established operators like Village Green have a reasonably clear progression. Consistent performers move into assistant manager positions, where the focus shifts toward collections, delinquency management, and financial reporting. The leasing skills transfer directly. The commission structure here also means you can meaningfully increase your earnings before any title change, which is worth factoring in.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, a bonus program, and a 401(k) with a company match.

job.title: Multi-Site Maintenance Technician (59279 & 59280)
job.description:
Multi-site maintenance work in Los Angeles asks more of a technician than single-property work does. You're splitting your time between two communities, managing your own schedule across locations, and staying on top of work orders at both sites without letting either one slip. That's the reality of this role at Cirrus Asset Management, covering Magnolia on Lake (46 units) and Chancellor Apartments (101 units).

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this position is keeping two properties running: completing work orders on time, turning units within five days of move-out, and staying ahead of systems issues before residents notice them. That means electrical repairs, plumbing, HVAC maintenance, painting interior and exterior surfaces, and keeping locks, doors, and closers functional. You'll also handle compliance documentation for fire extinguishers, suppression systems, and building alarms, which is paperwork most technicians don't love but that genuinely matters when inspectors show up.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with pay ranging from $25 to $26 per hour. The role does require travel between properties as needed, so your own reliable transportation is a practical necessity, not a formality.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance technician experience
  • Solid working knowledge of general maintenance processes across electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems
  • Comfort with tools, common appliances, and manual repair work
  • Strong time management, because two properties means two sets of deadlines running simultaneously
  • High school diploma
  • Any relevant certifications (HVAC, CMRP, or similar) carry real weight here

What Separates Good Candidates from Great Ones

The technicians who thrive in multi-site roles tend to be self-directed. When you're not physically standing in front of a supervisor all day, you need to prioritize your own work orders, communicate across sites, and make judgment calls about what gets done first. A technician who can walk a property, identify deferred issues before they become emergency calls, and handle the documentation correctly at the end of the day is far more valuable than one who only responds to what's already broken. HVAC certification is a legitimate differentiator in Southern California given year-round cooling demands.

Cirrus Asset Management offers health, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 401k plan, and HSA/FSA/HRA options alongside paid holidays, sick time, and vacation.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing at a 1,600-unit property is a different animal than working a 200-unit garden-style. The sheer volume of traffic, the pace of follow-up, and the number of moving pieces on any given day demand someone who can stay organized without losing the personal touch that actually closes leases. At Legacy North in Plano, TX, LivCor is hiring a Leasing Consultant who can handle that scale.

The Skills This Role Lives On

The core of this position is sales, but not the aggressive kind. It's relationship-based qualifying and closing: reading a prospect quickly, understanding what they actually need, and connecting those needs to what the community offers. Rapport building isn't a soft skill here, it's the mechanism. You'll work every stage of the leasing funnel, from the first phone call or web inquiry through application processing, approval, and move-in coordination. That means your organizational skills matter just as much as your personality at the front desk.

You'll also need to be comfortable with the paperwork side: processing lease files accurately, calculating prorated rents, preparing delinquency correspondence, and logging everything properly. The administrative work isn't glamorous, but errors there create real problems downstream. Attention to detail and speed in equal measure is what keeps this role running.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Handle inbound inquiries by phone, email, and walk-in; follow up with every prospect within 24 hours by phone and 48 hours in writing
  • Tour prospects through the property, including vacant units and amenity areas, and maintain a minimum 20% conversion ratio on total traffic
  • Qualify applicants, collect required data, initiate background screening, and communicate status throughout the process
  • Coordinate move-in readiness with the team; confirm punch list items are complete before keys change hands
  • Perform daily property walks to confirm common areas, models, and vacants meet presentation standards
  • Complete lease files, set up new resident accounts, and handle office administrative tasks including key tracking and package management
  • Monitor competitive properties and bring market intelligence back to the team
  • Support light bookkeeping functions including monthly rent calculations and delinquency letters

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

A 1,600-unit community generates a lot of traffic. The consultants who thrive at this scale aren't just friendly; they're disciplined about follow-up and systematic about their pipeline. Hitting a 20% conversion ratio consistently requires knowing where every prospect stands and acting on that knowledge every day. Social media marketing experience is a plus here too, since lease-up efforts at a property this size often extend beyond traditional walk-in traffic.

Multifamily experience is preferred, and a valid driver's license is required. The role involves operating a golf cart with prospects on board and physically inspecting the entire property daily, including stairs and outdoor areas in a Texas climate. Worth knowing before you apply.

Pay runs $18.00 to $20.00 per hour plus commission. Benefits include company-paid dental and vision, 401k with employer match, an associate apartment discount, and an educational assistance program covering tuition and certifications. For someone looking to grow into an assistant manager role, leasing positions at large communities like this one build the volume of experience that accelerates that path considerably.

job.title: Daytime Resident Experience Associate
job.description:
Where Hospitality Meets High-End Multifamily

This role runs on a specific set of skills that most leasing jobs undervalue: genuine rapport-building, anticipatory service, and the kind of organized front-desk execution that keeps a Class A community running smoothly at the start of the day. Bozzuto is hiring a Daytime Resident Experience Associate for a North Bethesda property, working Monday through Friday, 6AM to 2PM. That shift matters. You're the person who sets the tone before most of the team arrives, and you're interacting with residents at their most time-crunched.

The role sits at the intersection of leasing support and concierge-level hospitality. You'll follow up on leads, coordinate tours with the leasing team, and help convert prospect traffic into signed leases. But equally, you're managing the front desk day-to-day: packages, club room reservations, freight elevator scheduling, resident communications. Anyone who's worked a busy mid-rise or high-rise front desk knows those operational details aren't trivial. A missed package or a botched reservation log erodes resident satisfaction faster than almost anything else.

What This Role Actually Demands

Retention is part of your job description here, and that's worth taking seriously. Bozzuto wants residents to renew, write reviews, and refer neighbors. That outcome depends on consistent, personalized interactions over months, not a single great leasing tour. The expectation is that you learn residents by name, know their preferences, and treat problem-solving like it's personal. That's a hospitality-trained skill set, and the posting draws experience from hotel, retail, and travel backgrounds for good reason.

  • 2 or more years in a hospitality, retail, hotel, or travel environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management platforms
  • Sharp professional presentation and an eye for detail
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds (package volume during peak seasons is real)
  • Willingness to obtain a leasing license within the first 90 days

The leasing license requirement is worth flagging for candidates coming from pure hospitality. It's a real step, not a formality, and Bozzuto builds it into onboarding expectations rather than treating it as optional.

Doing This at Bozzuto Specifically

Bozzuto manages a significant portfolio of Class A multifamily properties in the Mid-Atlantic and beyond, and their reputation for resident experience is genuinely earned. They invest in community programming, social media presence, and brand consistency across properties. If you're someone who takes pride in a meticulous community presentation and wants to work for an operator that actually tracks retention as a metric, the company culture here aligns with that. The posted hourly rate sits between $23.08 and $23.97, with benefits covering medical, dental, and vision, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

For candidates thinking about where this role leads: front desk and resident experience positions at operators like Bozzuto often feed directly into leasing consultant and assistant manager tracks. The skills built here, traffic conversion, retention strategy, operational organization, transfer cleanly upward. It's not a dead-end hospitality transfer. It's a legitimate entry point into multifamily management for someone who brings the right people instincts.

job.title: Leasing & Sales Consultant-Cortland Vesta
job.description:
It's 10:15 on a Tuesday morning. A prospect who toured last Saturday just responded to your follow-up text. Your conversion window is open, and how you handle the next ten minutes determines whether that unit closes this week or sits vacant another turn cycle.

The Role at Cortland Vesta

Cortland is a top-10 multifamily owner and operator in the US, vertically integrated from design and construction through day-to-day management. At Cortland Vesta in Birmingham, the Leasing and Sales Consultant position is the direct engine of occupancy and revenue. You own the sales pipeline: generating traffic, running tours, managing CRM records, tracking conversion metrics, and closing leases. Every percentage point of occupancy has a dollar value attached to it, and this role is where that number gets made.

Consultative selling is the core method here. That means uncovering what a prospect actually needs, matching the community's product to those needs, and building enough value that price objections shrink on their own. You'll handle objections in real time, adjust your approach based on where the market is moving, and follow up with the consistency that separates teams with strong traffic-to-lease ratios from those that bleed leads. CRM hygiene matters: accurate records, timely notes, pipeline stages that reflect reality, not optimism.

Beyond the lease-up side, this role includes resident engagement. You'll plan and execute community events, maintain a social media presence for the property, and build the kind of resident relationships that generate referrals and renewals. Retention is occupancy too.

What Cortland Needs From You

  • At least six months of sales, customer service, or goal-driven performance experience
  • Comfort being measured against targets: conversion rates, closing percentages, follow-up timelines
  • CRM proficiency or a demonstrated ability to learn one quickly
  • Strong personal presentation consistent with a premium brand standard
  • Coachability: the ability to take feedback and implement it without a long adjustment period
  • Organized follow-up habits, because a lead that doesn't hear back in 24 hours is usually a lost lease

Candidates who tend to thrive in this type of role bring sales discipline from outside multifamily, retail, hospitality, or any environment where closing is tracked and rewarded. Multifamily experience helps, but the pipeline management instinct matters more than the industry background.

Birmingham's rental market has seen steady apartment development over the past several years, which means prospects have real choices. The communities that win on conversion do it through follow-up speed and the quality of the leasing experience, not just amenities. That operational reality shapes what this role demands day to day.

job.title: Assistant Manager - The Tessera
job.description:
The Role at a Glance

Assistant Manager positions at mid-size apartment operators tend to sit at the intersection of leasing production, financial accountability, and resident relations. At Olympus Property's Tessera community in Phoenix, that description holds, but the scope leans heavier on the financial and operational side than a typical cross-trained leasing role would. You're owning rent collection, deposits, final account statements, and move-out condition assessments while also staying current on submarket dynamics that could affect occupancy or income. That combination of ledger discipline and market awareness is what separates this from a leasing-first role.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

A typical week involves auditing resident files for accuracy and security, ensuring all payments are deposited before bank close each day, and reviewing make-ready apartments before move-in to confirm they meet standards. You'll handle resident concerns as they surface, often in real-time conversations at the front desk, and step in on the leasing floor when traffic requires it. When the Property Manager is out, you step into that seat entirely. Monitoring delinquency, coordinating with the team on retention events, and flagging liability issues or legal complaints to the appropriate regional and corporate contacts round out the core responsibilities.

Olympus uses RealPage and Knock (Onesite), so prior familiarity with those platforms is a meaningful advantage coming in. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with flexibility for resident events and first-weekend-of-the-month coverage.

Where This Role Takes You

For someone building toward a Property Manager seat, this position offers exactly the right reps. You're handling cash management, delinquency oversight, move-out accounting, and submarket analysis. Those are the competencies that regional managers look for when they're evaluating whether an Assistant Manager is ready to take on a property independently. At a company like Olympus, which has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), the internal career pathing isn't just a benefit line item. It reflects an organization that has enough depth to move people up when they're ready.

Strong candidates here will already have onsite apartment experience as an Assistant Manager or a well-cross-trained leasing consultant. The edge goes to people who are genuinely comfortable with financial processes, can hold a conversation with a frustrated resident without escalating the situation, and bring enough market curiosity to track what's happening with new construction and competing properties in the Phoenix submarket. Phoenix has been one of the more dynamic multifamily markets over the past few years, with significant new supply, which means submarket awareness isn't optional here. Understanding how concessions and occupancy trends in nearby lease-ups might affect your property's pricing is a real part of doing this job well.

  • Full-time, Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM (some flexibility required)
  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • RealPage, Knock, or Onesite experience strongly preferred
  • Starting at $25.00 per hour, plus monthly renewal and quarterly bonuses
  • Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program

job.title: Community Manager- Axcess 15 Apartments
job.description:
MG Properties has spent more than three decades acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S., and the work they do at the property level reflects that depth of experience. The Community Manager role at Axcess 15 Apartments in Portland is a position where that depth actually matters. You're not inheriting a fully stabilized, self-running operation and simply keeping score. You're expected to build and lead a team, drive performance, and take real ownership of everything from occupancy and traffic to budget health and day-to-day operations.

The skills this role requires going in are specific. You need recent, hands-on experience managing a multifamily community at a meaningful pace, along with a track record of supervising and developing staff. Budget oversight is a core function here, not a secondary task. You'll own the numbers: monitoring NOI, controlling expenses, tracking delinquency, and making decisions that show up on the T-12. Marketing the property and maintaining healthy occupancy are equally central. Yardi experience will help you hit the ground running. A valid driver's license is required.

What the role builds is a different list. Community Managers who do this job well tend to develop sharper instincts around team accountability, particularly the ability to set clear expectations, coach underperformers early, and retain the people worth keeping. Managing a property in Portland also means staying attuned to a rental market that has seen real regulatory shifts in recent years, including rent control considerations and tenant protection rules that affect how you handle MTM residents, concessions, and lease renewal strategy. That kind of market-specific judgment develops over time, and this role gives you the environment to build it.

MG Properties ties compensation to performance through monthly incentive bonuses and company profit sharing, which means a strong operator has genuine upside. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, paid personal days, and rental discounts.

What You'll Bring

  • Recent experience managing a multifamily apartment community
  • Demonstrated supervisory and team-building skills
  • Fluency in budget management, marketing, and leasing operations
  • Yardi experience (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance

The candidates who stand out in this kind of role combine operational discipline with genuine leadership presence. Knowing your numbers matters. So does knowing how to get the most out of the people working alongside you.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a calendar that most multifamily managers never deal with: a hard annual turn window where hundreds of residents move out and move in within a matter of days, quarterly inspections, and a leasing cycle tied to academic enrollment rather than organic traffic. The Assistant Community Manager role at Scion's Alight Laramie property sits squarely inside that rhythm, and it's structured to develop someone who can eventually run a property independently.

What the Role Requires From Day One

This position supports the General Manager across every operational layer: staffing, resident accounts, facilities, leasing, and financial reporting. You'll step into the GM seat when needed, which means the expectation is functional fluency across all of those areas, not just one or two. Specific systems you'll work in include Entrata for property management, Turnable for tracking the electronic turn board, Qualtrics for resident and employee experience data, and ClickUp for project coordination. Comfort moving between platforms matters here.

On the financial side, you'll help prepare month-end reports, reconcile accounts receivable, enforce late fee and NSF policies, and keep delinquency below 2% at month end. You'll also manage RUBS-style utility billing coordination and post damage charges from quarterly inspections. The delinquency target is specific, and hitting it consistently requires both systems discipline and direct resident communication.

Leasing responsibilities include weekly market surveys, managing concessions within budget, coordinating with a centralized sales team, and handling escalated resident concerns including public review responses on platforms like Google and Yelp.

What This Role Builds

The annual turn process in student housing is one of the most compressed, high-stakes operational events in property management. Assisting with planning, vendor walks, move-out inspections, punch list coordination, and hands-on make-ready tasks (including moving furniture, organizing high-volume trash, and cleaning units) gives you experience that transfers directly to any multifamily role that involves turn management. Candidates who've run a student housing turn at volume are genuinely more prepared for fast-cycle multifamily operations than many peers who've only managed rolling conventional turns.

The staff development component is also worth noting. You'll assist with recruiting, hiring, scheduling on-call coverage, and coaching team members. That supervisory exposure at the assistant level is the difference between candidates who get promoted to General Manager roles and those who stay in a supporting function longer than they'd like.

  • 1 or more years of experience in property management or residential living communities
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Detail orientation and the ability to manage competing deadlines
  • Willingness to work after-hours on-call shifts as part of the property schedule
  • U.S. work authorization required; visa sponsorship is not available

The position is exempt, and compensation includes a discretionary annual bonus, PTO, floating holidays, medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. The role is based on-site at Alight Laramie in Laramie, Wyoming, with periodic travel possible.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Park 12
job.description:
Park 12 is a well-regarded community in San Diego, and MG Properties has been building and operating apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over three decades. This Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of what keeps the property running and residents happy. If you've spent time in apartment maintenance and you understand that the work is equal parts technical skill and human interaction, this is worth a close look.

What You'll Actually Do

Most days start with the service request queue. Plumbing issues, appliance repairs, electrical troubleshooting, HVAC concerns , you're expected to handle all of it with real competence, not just the basics. Grounds, common areas, and office spaces also fall under your care, so the role involves both reactive and routine work. When a unit turns, you're part of the make-ready process: painting, punch list items, and getting the apartment back to show-ready condition on schedule. You'll also rotate through on-call coverage, which means occasional evenings or weekends when something urgent comes up. That's honest and worth knowing going in.

The resident-facing side of this job matters as much as the technical side. When you walk into someone's home to fix a problem, you represent the property. A friendly, professional presence builds trust and shapes how residents feel about where they live. MG Properties puts a real emphasis on customer service, and the best candidates here carry that mindset naturally rather than treating it as an afterthought.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience
  • Competence across multiple trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Comfort working on a team and coordinating with other staff
  • Reliable personal transportation (this is a firm requirement)
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • A service-oriented attitude with residents and coworkers alike

The Bigger Picture

One thing that separates a strong apartment maintenance tech from an average one is the ability to prioritize under pressure. On a busy day, you might have a dozen open work orders, a turn in progress, and a resident waiting on an urgent repair.
