Knowing what to tackle first, communicating clearly when something will take longer than expected, and staying organized across all of it , that's where experience shows. MG Properties offers monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of a competitive hourly rate ($25 to $27 depending on experience), plus a solid benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts. For someone looking to grow within a regional company that owns and manages its own portfolio, this kind of role also builds the track record that leads to senior tech or maintenance supervisor positions over time.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. two weeks before move-in day, and you're standing in a unit with a punch list in one hand and a vendor on the phone in the other, tracking down a missing appliance while the turn board in Turnable shows three units still not cleared for inspection. That's the rhythm this role runs on.

The Position

The Scion Group is hiring an Assistant Community Manager (titled Assistant General Manager internally) to support five student housing properties across the College Station, Texas area. This is a broad operational role: you'll work directly with the General Manager on day-to-day business functions while partnering closely with the Customer and Sales Experience Manager on leasing performance, resident engagement, and sales initiatives. When the GM is out, you step in and run the operation.

Student housing has its own rhythm, and the annual turn process is the clearest example. Each summer, this role gets hands-on: conducting move-out inspections, walking vendor service calls, tracking unit readiness through Turnable, assessing and billing move-out damage charges, and physically helping where the work demands it. That includes moving furniture, assisting the facilities team with punch items, and managing the high-volume logistics that come with turning hundreds of units on a compressed timeline.

Outside of peak season, the work centers on financial administration, delinquency management (with a hard target of keeping it below 2% by month-end), resident account auditing, utility billing, and monthly property walks to maintain curb appeal and code compliance. You'll also handle escalated resident concerns, respond to reputation platform reviews through Entrata, and use KPIs to track leasing velocity, concessions, and market rate performance alongside the sales team.

On the people side, you'll assist with recruiting, onboarding, and coaching team members, coordinating scheduling including after-hours on-call coverage, and contributing to morale and retention through structured feedback and team development.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

Coming in, you need at least one year of property management or residential community experience, genuine comfort with property management software (Entrata is preferred here), strong written communication, and the ability to handle confidential resident and financial information responsibly. A customer-centric instinct matters too. Student housing residents are vocal, and review management and escalation handling are real parts of this job.

What the role develops is harder to get elsewhere. Managing five properties simultaneously trains you to prioritize under real pressure. The annual turn at a student housing community is one of the most compressed, logistically dense events in property management, and coming through it capable sharpens your ability to oversee large-scale capex coordination, vendor management, and team execution in ways a single conventional lease-up rarely teaches. The financial exposure across multiple properties, combined with direct GM-level substitution responsibilities, positions strong performers for General Manager roles faster than most traditional multifamily paths would.

  • 1+ years of property management or residential community experience
  • Proficiency in Entrata or a comparable property management system
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort with financial reporting, account reconciliation, and delinquency tracking
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours during peak periods and on-call rotations
  • Work authorization in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

The role is exempt and includes a discretionary annual bonus, health, dental and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. This is a full-time, property-based position in College Station with occasional travel required.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Hawthorne at Bay Forest in La Porte, the leasing consultant role is the front line of every occupancy and renewal outcome on the property. You'll greet prospects, run personalized tours, and field inquiries across phone, email, and web. The job doesn't stop at showing units. You'll complete applications, process new move-in paperwork accurately, and follow up on leads until they convert or go cold. Resident events, common area upkeep, and light social media marketing also fall within your scope.

La Porte sits in the Houston-Galveston industrial corridor, drawing a steady mix of petrochemical and port workers alongside families and long-term residents. Traffic to a garden-style community here tends to run reliably, but prospects have options across the 146 corridor and into Seabrook and League City. Knowing what nearby competitors are offering on concessions and pricing, and being able to articulate what sets Bay Forest apart, is real work in this market, not a formality.

Your schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off to keep the week at 40 hours. Resident events may occasionally extend your day beyond standard office hours.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Comfort communicating in person, by phone, and in writing, with the ability to handle objections naturally
  • Accuracy when processing leasing applications and move-in documentation
  • A valid driver's license
  • A Certified Apartment Leasing Professional (CALP) designation is a plus

Trajectory and Compensation

Hawthorne structures a formal career path program, and leasing consultant is a recognized entry point toward assistant community manager. That progression is real in multifamily, and it tends to move faster for people who quickly get comfortable reading traffic patterns, understanding what drives occupancy softness, and helping with renewal outreach. Compensation is hourly with monthly leasing and renewal commissions layered on top, plus participation in leasing incentive programs. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid time off including your birthday, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance.

Candidates who separate themselves in a role like this usually combine genuine sales instincts with patience for the administrative side. The ability to close a lease is valuable. The ability to process paperwork cleanly without shortcuts is equally valuable, because errors in leasing documents create downstream problems for the management team and the resident alike. Both skills matter here.

job.title: Front Desk Associate- Union House
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Front-of-house operations in a luxury HOA building run on two things: composure and consistency. The Front Desk Associate at Union House brings both every shift. This is a high-touch position where resident-facing communication, attention to detail, and the ability to stay organized under pressure are the skills that actually matter day to day.

You're fielding resident requests, coordinating with vendors and building staff, logging activity, and serving as the first point of contact for everyone who walks through the door. In a luxury association, that standard of contact carries real weight. Residents have high expectations, and meeting them repeatedly, not just occasionally, is the baseline.

What the Work Looks Like

A typical shift involves managing the front desk, greeting residents and guests, handling package intake and resident inquiries, and keeping the log current. You'll communicate with building management and other team members to flag issues, coordinate access for vendors, and make sure the front-of-house operation runs without friction during your hours.

The skills that transfer most directly from other service roles include:

  • Professional verbal and written communication
  • Organized task tracking across a busy shift
  • Conflict de-escalation with a calm, solutions-first approach
  • Reliable documentation habits

This is a full-time position, so schedule reliability matters. Luxury HOA communities like Union House expect consistency in who residents see and interact with. The relationship between a front desk associate and the residents they serve builds over time, and that continuity has real operational value.

What This Role Looks Like at Action Property Management

Action Property Management has managed HOA communities since 1984 and now operates across nine offices serving more than 300 communities in the Western U.S. Union House is part of that portfolio as a luxury San Francisco association, which puts this role in a context where professionalism is non-negotiable and operational standards are set accordingly.

One thing worth knowing about this type of position: front desk associates who perform well in luxury HOA buildings tend to develop a strong read on building operations more broadly. You see the rhythm of the property, you understand resident priorities, and you build institutional knowledge that opens doors to assistant community manager roles over time. The front desk is often where long-term PM careers begin in the HOA segment.

Strong candidates bring genuine service instincts, a steady presence under pressure, and the kind of professionalism that holds up at 8 AM on a Monday just as well as it does mid-afternoon on a Friday.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Berkeley Heights
job.description:
Property management companies that run diverse portfolios face a real operational challenge: properties with different histories, different resident profiles, and different financial needs all require consistent daily execution. The Assistant Community Manager role at CloudTen Residential in Berkeley Heights exists to make that consistency happen at the property level, keeping the books clean, the units leased, and the residents taken care of while the Community Manager focuses on the bigger picture.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A good chunk of your day runs through the financials. Collecting and posting rent, preparing deposits, reconciling accounts, and running weekly and monthly reports are core responsibilities, not occasional tasks. You'll process invoices, work in property management software daily, and make sure every entry is accurate because errors compound fast in multifamily accounting. On the delinquency side, you'll serve non-payment notices, follow up on late accounts, and coordinate with the Community Manager when an account escalates toward eviction proceedings. None of that is comfortable work, but it's necessary and you'll own it.

Leasing is part of the role too. You'll respond to inquiries, conduct tours, monitor competing properties, and help keep leasing documents accurate and Fair Housing compliant. Resident retention matters as well: lease renewals and community engagement activities fall under your scope. When the Community Manager is out, you step into the lead role on-site, which means you need to be ready to handle operational decisions, not just execute assigned tasks.

Inspections of common areas, units, and grounds happen regularly. Move-in and move-out administration, including apartment inspections and security deposit dispositions, are yours to manage carefully and on time, with an eye on state law requirements throughout.

What CloudTen Brings and What They're Looking For

CloudTen's portfolio spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects, so the company has real operational range. That breadth can translate into solid career development for someone who wants exposure to different asset types over time. The pay range runs $28 to $31 per hour depending on experience, with leasing and renewal bonus opportunities tied to this specific property.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

Strong candidates for this role bring at least two years of property management or leasing experience and a working knowledge of landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing standards. Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office matters. Basic accounting knowledge is genuinely required here given how much of the role runs through financial operations.

  • Minimum two years of property management, leasing, or directly related experience
  • Proficiency in property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws and state landlord-tenant regulations
  • Solid communication and organizational skills
  • Ability to prioritize and adjust when the day shifts unexpectedly
  • Basic accounting knowledge and comfort with financial reporting

What separates the candidates who thrive in this type of role from those who struggle is the willingness to own the unsexy parts: following up on delinquent accounts, catching a data entry error before it becomes a bigger problem, and handling a frustrated resident's concern professionally on a day when five other things are already in motion. If that kind of steady, detail-oriented accountability suits you, this role has a clear path forward into full community management.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 7 a.m. By 7:45, you've already walked the grounds, checked the maintenance shop inventory, and assigned the ticket to the right tech. That's the pace of this role.

The Position

Avanath is an affordable housing operator with a workforce-focused mission, and this Maintenance Supervisor opening sits at their Hollydale community. You'll work directly alongside the Community Manager, sharing responsibility for physical asset condition, resident experience, and the day-to-day output of your maintenance team and outside vendors.

The work spans the full range of property maintenance. Make-ready coordination, preventative maintenance scheduling, work order management, daily grounds inspections, common area upkeep, and on-call emergency response all fall within your scope. You'll also handle key control, maintain accurate records for service requests and EPA/OSHA compliance, and manage supplies inventory within budget. When vendors and contractors are on site, you're the one directing their work and holding them to quality and timeline standards.

This is a supervisory role, not just a senior wrench-turner. You'll train, schedule, and monitor your maintenance staff daily. That means catching problems early, offering real-time instruction, and pushing your team toward higher performance standards. Avanath puts weight on how you show up for residents too: professional, responsive, and consistent when handling complaints or sensitive requests.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of multifamily maintenance experience, with at least 1 year in a supervisory capacity
  • Hands-on skills in plumbing, HVAC, electrical, appliance repair, and carpentry
  • HVAC certification and CPO certification are strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities without dropping the ball
  • Comfort with on-call rotation and weekend availability
  • Clear, professional communication with residents and staff alike

Candidates who stand out tend to be strong on preventative maintenance thinking. Anyone can respond to a broken unit. The better supervisors catch the slow water heater corrosion, the HVAC filter that's been neglected, or the breezeway light that's been out two weeks before it becomes a liability issue or a resident complaint. Affordable housing communities often run leaner on capex, so the ability to fix rather than replace, extend asset life, and control supply costs makes a measurable difference in NOI.

Avanath's mission is grounded in affordable workforce housing, which means your residents aren't transient. They're long-term community members, and the relationships you build carry real weight. Maintenance Supervisors who thrive here treat service calls as a trust-building moment, not just a task to close.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Leasing consultants at CommonPlace carry the full customer journey, from the first inquiry to move-in day and beyond. You're greeting prospects, leading tours, and making sure model units and common areas are sharp enough to close. When someone's ready to apply, you walk them through screenings, deposits, and lease paperwork. When an existing resident's lease is coming up, you're preparing renewal documents and sitting down with them to work through the conversation. You're also keeping an eye on the local Charlotte market, tracking competitor communities, and using digital channels like social media and listing platforms to drive traffic to your property.

The role has a genuine service dimension too. You'll coordinate with maintenance on make-ready status before move-ins, handle resident concerns with professionalism, and help plan community events that give residents a reason to stay. Fair Housing compliance runs through every interaction, so comfort with those standards is assumed from day one.

What You Bring

  • Prior leasing experience is preferred, though a strong sales or customer service background transfers well
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills, you'll be responding to leads quickly and following up consistently
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with OneSite or AppFolio is a plus
  • Monday through Friday availability, with some weekend flexibility as needed
  • A polished, professional presence and the ability to adapt across different prospect personalities and situations

Where This Role Leads

A leasing consultant position is one of the best on-ramps in property management because the skills compound quickly. You're building fluency in the full leasing cycle, learning to read traffic patterns, understanding what drives occupancy, and getting early exposure to renewal strategy. Consultants who pay attention to delinquency trends, occupancy targets, and how their property sits relative to competitors often move into leasing manager or assistant manager roles within a few years. The ones who distinguish themselves aren't just personable; they treat every lead as a data point, track their own conversion rate, and bring genuine follow-through to renewal conversations rather than treating them as an afterthought.

CommonPlace is hiring for this role in Charlotte, and compensation comes in at $22 to $25 per hour with commission on top, plus a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k, and paid time off including volunteer time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II at Vintage Raleigh West
job.description:
Maintenance work at a multifamily property is a constant negotiation between competing priorities: a stack of open service requests, a unit that needs to turn in time to meet a 7-day make-ready standard, a supply room that needs to stay stocked, and residents who need to feel like someone actually cares about the place they call home. The Maintenance Technician II role at Vintage Raleigh West exists because all of that requires someone skilled enough to handle the technical side and self-directed enough to manage their own day without constant supervision.

Bluecore Residential operates over 10,000 units with roughly $2 billion in assets under management, and they run lean on purpose. Property teams are given genuine authority to solve problems without waiting on regional approval chains. That's a real operational difference from how a lot of management companies work, and it places real responsibility on the people doing the work.

The Work Itself

Day to day, you're moving between service requests and make-ready units, diagnosing and repairing plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general building systems. You'll log work in Yardi and use Sparkle as an inspection tool, so comfort with tech matters here. Bluecore holds a 7-day turn standard, which is tight and requires organized daily planning to hit consistently. You'll also monitor parts inventory, order supplies cost-efficiently, and coordinate with the Maintenance Supervisor on priorities each day. Preventative maintenance and health and safety compliance are part of the role, not afterthoughts.

The office staff and maintenance team work together on resident satisfaction, which means communication with the leasing side isn't optional. A unit that turns fast and clean is a direct contributor to occupancy, and you'll see how your work connects to the property's overall performance.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

You bring apartment maintenance experience, either as a technician or a make-ready tech, along with a working foundation across plumbing, electrical, and appliances. Reliability and your own transportation are baseline requirements. What the role builds is different: Bluecore invests in certification reimbursement covering CAM, CPO, EPA, and other approved credentials, so technicians who want to grow their formal qualifications have a clear path to do that on the company's dime.

The internal culture at Bluecore rewards people who speak up. They call it "No Fear of Conflict," and it's applied consistently, including on the maintenance side. If something in the process isn't working, you're expected to say so. That kind of culture tends to separate technicians who just complete tickets from those who help the property run better over time.

  • Experience in apartment maintenance or make-ready work
  • Hands-on knowledge across plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • Reliable transportation and punctuality
  • Comfort using technology as a daily work tool (Yardi, Sparkle)
  • Strong communication habits with both supervisors and residents

For technicians thinking longer term, consistent performance in a role like this, especially with certification support, is a natural path toward Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor positions. Bluecore's property-level empowerment model means those moves can happen on a single asset or across their broader portfolio.

job.title: LIHTC Leasing Consultant (30024)
job.description:
Affordable housing leasing carries a compliance layer that conventional leasing simply doesn't. At a Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) property, a leasing consultant isn't just selling the community and processing paperwork. They're certifying income eligibility, maintaining file accuracy to satisfy investor and state agency audits, and managing waitlists that often stretch far longer than the available unit count. That combination of resident-facing hospitality and back-end compliance precision is what defines this role at Pines at Castle Rock, a 630-unit affordable community managed by Cirrus Asset Management.

What This Role Actually Demands

The compliance side of this position is non-negotiable. A working understanding of LIHTC income limits, set-aside requirements, and certification rules is listed as a hard requirement, not something Cirrus plans to teach from scratch. If you've processed initial certifications, annual recertifications, and renewals before, that experience transfers directly here. Yardi is the preferred platform, and familiarity with it will reduce your ramp-up time considerably.

On the leasing side, the daily work looks familiar: touring prospects, explaining lease terms and community policies, assisting applicants through the process, and conducting move-in and move-out inspections. But waitlist management at a property this size adds a real layer of administrative discipline. Keeping that list accurate, communicating with applicants appropriately, and coordinating with the property manager and maintenance team around unit readiness all require attention to detail that has to be consistent, not occasional.

Bilingual ability in English and Spanish is preferred, and at a 630-unit community, the practical value of that skill shows up in resident conversations daily, not just during onboarding.

What This Role Builds

For someone earlier in their property management career, this position develops a skill set that opens real doors. LIHTC compliance knowledge is specialized, and professionals who genuinely understand it are in demand across affordable housing operators, tax credit syndicators, and state housing finance agencies. Mastery of the full certification cycle, combined with leasing and retention experience at a large property, positions you well for a senior leasing or compliance coordinator role. Retention work, resident satisfaction, and report management also build the operational fluency that property managers look for when promoting from within.

  • Strong LIHTC compliance knowledge: required before day one
  • Yardi proficiency: preferred, not required
  • Bilingual English/Spanish: preferred
  • Fair Housing law and state landlord-tenant law: must understand and apply consistently
  • Excel, Word, and Outlook: regular use for reporting and correspondence
  • Ability to manage competing priorities without letting file accuracy slip

Schedule is Tuesday through Saturday, 8am to 5pm. Pay ranges from $22 to $24 per hour. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, paid holidays, sick and vacation time, and a 401(k) plan.

job.title: Maintenance Technician ($1,500 Sign-On Bonus)
job.description:
Bozzuto operates across the full property management spectrum, from development through fee management, and their maintenance teams tend to reflect that. This Nashville opening is for a Maintenance Technician at what appears to be a Bozzuto-managed residential community, with a $1,500 sign-on bonus attached. The salary range runs $45,760 to $52,000, which is a reasonable band for someone coming in at beginner-to-intermediate level in the trades.

The work itself covers the standard scope: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, plus turns when units go vacant. Make-readies are a real part of this job. You'll be walking punch lists, pulling work orders, and handling the kind of routine service tickets that pile up fast at a well-occupied property. Customer service matters here in the way it always does in residential maintenance: residents notice how you show up as much as whether the repair holds.

There's an on-call rotation, which is worth saying plainly. After-hours emergencies are part of the deal, and you'll need reliable personal transportation to respond. That's not a footnote , it's a real operational requirement. If you're not set up for that, this role won't work regardless of your technical skill.

One thing worth noting for candidates thinking about growth: Bozzuto will cover the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification after your 12-month anniversary. That's real value. An EPA 608 Universal cert opens more doors on HVAC work, increases your usefulness to any property management operator, and tends to move compensation upward. Tuition reimbursement and career development programs are also part of the package, alongside medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days PTO plus holidays, and a 401k with company match.

What They're Looking For

  • Some background in building maintenance or trades education , this role suits someone still building their technical foundation
  • Beginner to intermediate proficiency across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Availability for on-call rotation and weekend or evening coverage
  • Ability to frequently lift and maneuver 25 to 50 pounds
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Comfort with basic computer skills, work order software, and property apps
  • Strong communication and a professional presentation

Nashville's rental market has stayed competitive, which means occupancy pressure is real and turns need to move. A technician who can run a clean make-ready and keep service ticket response times tight contributes directly to the property's performance. The candidates who tend to stand out at this level aren't necessarily the most technically advanced. They're the ones who communicate well with residents, close tickets completely the first time, and show up ready for on-call without friction.

job.title: Concierge - Cortland Columbia Pike
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Concierge at Cortland Columbia Pike is the operational anchor of the front-of-house experience. Every shift, you own the lobby. That means residents and guests are greeted with consistency, access credentials stay accurate and accounted for, packages move efficiently, and the shared spaces stay polished from open to close. You're coordinating across leasing, maintenance, and vendors throughout the day, so work orders get logged, amenity reservations get handled, and nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.

Day to day, you'll issue and track building access cards and parking passes, field maintenance requests, restock community supplies, and support resident events and communication programs. Opening and closing duties are yours. So is the general rhythm of the property: keeping the lobby presentable, flagging issues before they become complaints, and making sure every person who walks through the door feels like they belong there.

Cortland is a vertically integrated, top-10 multifamily operator with in-house design, construction, and management. At a Class A community like Columbia Pike, the concierge function directly supports resident retention. Renewals don't happen by accident at this price point. The daily experience you create has a measurable connection to occupancy.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years in customer service, hospitality, or front-desk work, preferably in a residential or service-oriented setting
  • Comfort handling mail and packages across carriers (USPS, FedEx, UPS) and familiarity with postage equipment
  • Solid proficiency with Microsoft Office and basic office technology
  • Strong organizational habits and communication skills that hold up across a full shift, not just at the start of one
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to lift and move up to 15 to 20 pounds as needed

What Separates Strong Candidates

At a premium multifamily property, the gap between a good concierge and a great one usually comes down to anticipation. Strong candidates here already know that a resident who hasn't complained yet isn't necessarily a satisfied one. They track patterns, catch the lobby detail that's slightly off before anyone notices, and communicate proactively to the leasing and management team rather than waiting to be asked. Experience specifically in residential settings, even luxury hospitality or high-touch retail, tends to calibrate that instinct faster than general customer service backgrounds. If you've worked in an environment where the product is someone's home, you already understand the stakes are higher.

job.title: Area Manager
job.description:
Area Manager roles at third-party management firms carry a distinct kind of pressure. You're accountable for NOI, occupancy, and team performance across multiple communities, but you're doing it without the direct ownership stake that sharpens focus in a fee management context. Asset Living, one of the larger third-party operators in the country with an NMHC top 50 ranking, is hiring for this position in the Orlando market to oversee a portfolio of multifamily communities under a Regional Manager.

What This Role Actually Covers

The scope here is broad by design. You'll carry financial accountability that includes budget development, NOI performance, and vendor contract oversight across your assigned properties. That means reading a T-12 and identifying where cost controls are slipping or where leasing trends suggest a concession strategy needs adjustment. On the leasing side, you'll own the marketing plan and hold your on-site teams accountable to conversion and follow-up standards, not just traffic numbers.

Personnel management takes up a real portion of the job. You'll screen, hire, coach, and when necessary, document and separate underperforming staff. Maintenance accountability is built in too: you'll walk units to confirm make-ready status, review work order turnaround, and direct rehabilitation activity to keep quality and pace in check. Travel runs 25 to 50 percent of your time, so the role keeps you on the ground at your properties rather than behind a desk.

  • Develop and monitor annual operating budgets across multiple communities
  • Build and execute yearly marketing and leasing plans at each site
  • Train, coach, and manage on-site staff in compliance with company benchmarks
  • Oversee vendor invoicing, rent collections, and property financial close
  • Conduct regular property inspections to confirm maintenance and make-ready completion
  • Lead resident retention efforts and respond to escalated resident concerns
  • Support emergency response procedures and manage liability exposure

Skills the Role Requires vs. Skills It Builds

You need to arrive with a working command of Fair Housing, solid instincts around on-site financials, and enough leasing experience to coach others on technique, not just track their numbers. Property management software fluency is expected from day one. A CAM or ARM credential is preferred, and the role assumes you've already managed through performance problems with documentation and HR coordination.

What the role builds is portfolio-level judgment. Managing multiple communities simultaneously forces you to triage, prioritize capex decisions, and spot patterns across properties that a single-site manager never sees. You'll develop stronger budget forecasting skills and learn to evaluate marketing performance across different asset types within Asset Living's diverse portfolio, which spans multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing. That breadth is a genuine differentiator for someone who wants to move toward a Regional Manager position, where portfolio thinking and financial fluency matter more than any individual property's metrics.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The candidates who thrive in Area Manager roles at multi-property third-party operators tend to be comfortable shifting between strategic thinking and hands-on accountability in the same week. If you can read delinquency reports and then walk a turn the same afternoon without losing efficiency in either task, you're built for this. Orlando's rental market has stayed competitive, which means your leasing instincts and retention programs will get tested against real market pressure, not just internal benchmarks. Candidates who treat resident retention as a revenue strategy, not an afterthought, consistently outperform those who focus narrowly on new lease traffic.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles exist because apartment communities live and die on first impressions. A prospect walks in undecided and leaves either sold or gone, and the person who made that call is the leasing consultant. Weinstein Properties is hiring for two Nashville-area communities: Bexley Stockyards in Germantown and The Union in the Nations neighborhood.

Weinstein has been family-owned for over 70 years, operating more than 60 communities across five states. That scale means real infrastructure behind you: structured training, a clear internal promotion path, and processes that aren't being invented as you go. Starting pay is $21/hour, with increases based on experience, quarterly bonuses, and a $1,000 sign-on bonus.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with rotating Saturdays from 9 to 5. Sundays are off. That's a more predictable structure than you'll find in a lot of service jobs, but don't picture yourself sitting at a desk. A good chunk of the day involves walking units with prospective residents, inspecting homes before move-in, following up with people who toured but haven't signed, and keeping the leasing pipeline moving. You'll also support community marketing and help with resident events when they come up.

The honest version: it's physically active, and it requires you to stay organized while switching between tasks quickly. If you've got three prospects scheduled, a few follow-up calls to make, and a move-in inspection before noon, you'll need to keep up without things slipping through. That's the part of this role that trips up people who underestimate the pace.

Who Fits Here

Weinstein is explicit that prior leasing experience isn't required, and they mean it. People who've come from retail, hospitality, banking, and fitness have landed here and done well. What you need is genuine comfort talking to strangers, the ability to write a clear follow-up email, and enough organization to manage your own task list without constant hand-holding. The training program handles the industry knowledge.

  • Strong verbal and written communication
  • Comfortable working both indoors and outdoors throughout the day
  • Organized and able to juggle competing priorities
  • Reliable and adaptable when the day shifts on you
  • Goal-oriented without needing a manager to stay motivated

One thing worth knowing about the career side: leasing consultant is a real entry point at Weinstein, not just a title. Property managers and regional managers at the company have come up from this exact role. If you're thinking about a longer-term path in property management, starting in leasing gives you visibility into traffic, occupancy trends, concessions, and the resident lifecycle. That foundation carries forward into almost every other role in the business.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Neon Local
job.description:
What This Role Runs On

Leasing is a sales role. At Neon Local in Denver, that means handling traffic from first contact through signed lease, qualifying applicants accurately, and keeping files and data tight behind the scenes. You'll greet prospects, walk units, process applications, and prepare leases. You'll also coordinate with maintenance to make sure move-ins go smoothly and residents don't hit snags on day one.

The customer service side carries just as much weight as the sales side. Residents come to you with maintenance concerns, payment questions, and complaints. How you handle those interactions directly affects retention, and retention affects occupancy. Both matter here.

Skills You'll Use Daily

  • Sales and persuasion: converting prospects into applicants, handling objections, following up on leads
  • Attention to detail: qualifying applicants thoroughly, entering rental data accurately, keeping files current
  • Communication: written and verbal, with prospects, residents, and internal teams
  • Organization: monthly administrative tasks, lease paperwork, coordinating across departments
  • Conflict resolution: addressing resident concerns professionally without letting issues escalate

One year of property management experience is preferred. If you've worked in leasing, retail sales, or hospitality and can demonstrate strong follow-through, that background translates.

Working at MG Properties

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. They promote from within, which means a leasing role here has a real path forward. Leasing Consultants who build strong occupancy track records and get comfortable with the operational side often move into Assistant Manager positions, where they take on NOI responsibilities and delinquency oversight.

Pay runs $22 to $24 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts. Note that this position is anticipated to close in October 2026.

job.title: Community Manager - Lakeside Place
job.description:
The Community Manager role sits at the center of how a multifamily property actually performs. Leasing, maintenance coordination, financial reporting, compliance, team development: all of it converges in this position, which makes it one of the most skill-compounding jobs in residential property management. CloudTen Residential, a Nevada-based multifamily operator with a portfolio spanning hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects across the West, is hiring a Community Manager for Lakeside Place in Bend, Oregon.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

Reporting to a Regional Manager, you'll carry full operational responsibility for the property. That means overseeing delinquency, managing rent collection in accordance with Oregon landlord-tenant law, and keeping the books aligned with company accounting procedures. Budget monitoring and expense control fall on your desk, and you'll be expected to flag cost-saving opportunities as they surface in the day-to-day operations.

On the leasing side, you'll keep occupancy healthy by promoting available units, running showings, and managing renewal outreach to support resident retention. You'll analyze local market conditions and adjust pricing and concessions accordingly, keeping your community competitive without eroding NOI unnecessarily.

Personnel management is a real part of this job. You'll hire, train, and evaluate the on-site team, and you'll be responsible for building the kind of cohesion that shows up in resident satisfaction scores. Regular property inspections, move-in and move-out protocols, and service request follow-through (the target window is 24 to 48 hours) round out the operational picture.

  • Two or more years of property management experience, or an equivalent combination of education and hands-on experience
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations, ADA requirements, and Oregon landlord-tenant law
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and at least one property management software platform
  • Strong financial literacy, including budget preparation and basic accounting principles
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree is preferred

Where This Role Leads

Community Managers who work across portfolio types, as CloudTen's structure allows, build a resume that reads well at the next level. Exposure to value-add repositioning sharpens your understanding of capex planning. Working within a company that operates lease-up properties gives you experience with traffic management and absorption strategy that most stabilized-only managers never develop. The skills you build here, running a P&L, developing staff, managing compliance risk, translate directly into Regional Manager and Director-level roles. Bend's rental market has also matured in ways that require real pricing judgment, which gives you reps that generic suburban markets often don't.

Hourly pay runs $31.00 to $33.00 depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Community Manager - Villa Del Mar Apartments
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning in Oceanside. A resident stops by the office before work to flag a noise complaint from the night before, a vendor is waiting on a signed work order, and you've got a unit turning this week that needs to be walk-ready before the new lease starts. That's a normal morning at Villa Del Mar, and it's the kind of environment where a good Community Manager finds their footing fast.

What This Role Actually Involves

Sunrise Management is hiring a Community Manager for Villa Del Mar Apartments in Oceanside, CA. This is a full-scope operations role. You'll carry responsibility for the property's day-to-day performance under the guidance of a Regional Manager, covering everything from staffing and leasing to fiscal oversight and resident relations.

On the people side, you'll hire, train, and evaluate on-site staff, set expectations clearly, and handle personnel concerns before they become bigger problems. You're the standard-setter for the team's professionalism and follow-through. On the financial side, you'll oversee rent collection, manage delinquency in accordance with California landlord-tenant law, complete daily deposits, monitor operating expenses, and contribute to budget planning. These aren't tasks you delegate away entirely. You stay close to the numbers.

Leasing and marketing are part of your scope too. You'll coordinate showings, maintain accurate records, keep pricing aligned with market conditions, and support renewal efforts to hold occupancy steady. When residents have concerns, you address them with empathy and within Fair Housing guidelines. Service requests get resolved within 24 to 48 hours wherever possible, and when they can't, residents hear from you.

Regular property inspections keep you grounded in what's actually happening on the ground, not just what's in the inbox. Move-in and move-out protocols, common area walk-throughs, compliance checks, these are habits, not checklists you visit once a quarter.

Pay runs $25 to $27 per hour depending on experience, and the compensation package includes an on-site unit.

Who Tends to Thrive Here

Sunrise describes their culture around resident hospitality, which in practice means the Community Manager sets a tone that filters down through every staff interaction and every maintenance response. Candidates who do well in this kind of environment tend to be self-directing without being isolating. They communicate clearly with their team, they don't let tension sit unaddressed, and they treat resident conversations as relationship moments, not transactions.

Qualifications that matter for this role:

  • Minimum one to two years of property management experience
  • Solid working knowledge of California landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing requirements
  • Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Basic accounting fluency, particularly around collections and budget tracking
  • A college degree or related coursework is preferred but not required

One thing worth knowing about California coastal markets: tenant protections here carry real legal weight, and delinquency handling requires precision, not just persistence. Candidates who already understand the difference between what a manager wants to do and what California law allows will have a shorter ramp-up and a lower risk profile for the property. That knowledge gap is one of the most common friction points for incoming managers in this state, and it matters here.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA option, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off. Sunrise is a drug-free workplace and an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Grounds Specialist - The Lawrence at Wellen Park - Venice, FL
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a grounds and general maintenance role at The Lawrence at Wellen Park, a Davis Development community in Venice, FL. You'll spend most of your day walking the property, keeping it clean and well-maintained from the breezeways and pool decks to the common areas and amenity spaces.

  • Remove litter, debris, and pet waste from all exterior areas throughout the day on a continuous rotation
  • Handle trash and recycling removal on schedule, including interior office areas and property waste stations
  • Check and log pool chemical levels daily, vacuum pools weekly, and keep pool equipment in safe working order
  • Inspect and clean grills regularly, including timers and knobs, to make sure everything functions safely
  • Support the Maintenance Supervisor and Property Manager with general labor tasks and upkeep as needed

The pace of this role is steady. Early rounds set the tone for the day, and follow-up walks catch what gets missed. CPO certification is preferred, though not required on day one.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of general labor experience. Multifamily background is a plus but not required
  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • Comfort using hand tools, cleaning equipment, and general maintenance supplies
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work more than 40 hours per week when the property needs it
  • Solid time management and the discipline to self-direct through a full shift
  • Basic verbal and written communication skills

The Bigger Picture

Davis Development is a privately owned developer and operator with over 25 years building and managing luxury apartments across the country. Their management is fully in-house, which means decisions get made at the property level by people who know the asset. They describe their culture plainly: work hard, take care of the details, and treat the property like you own it.

Benefits start on the first of the month after 30 days and include medical, dental, vision, and behavioral health coverage. The 401(k) includes a 4% employer match that vests immediately. Life insurance, paid time off with carryover, and a company apparel allowance are also part of the package.

One thing worth knowing about grounds roles at luxury properties: the standard is visible. Residents pay a premium and notice when things slip. Strong candidates in this type of role take ownership of their rounds without being told twice, flag maintenance issues before they become work orders, and treat common areas with the same attention a resident would expect in their own unit.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role runs the day-to-day maintenance operation at Canvas, an affordable workforce housing community managed by Avanath. You'll work directly alongside the Community Manager to keep the property in strong physical condition, manage a team of maintenance staff, and make sure residents get timely, respectful service.

Day to day, that means triaging and assigning work orders, walking the grounds to catch hazards before they become liability issues, overseeing make-ready turns, and staying on top of a preventative maintenance schedule that protects the asset long-term. You'll also manage vendor relationships, control supply inventory against budget, and hold your team accountable to quality and turnaround time. On-call and weekend availability are part of the job.

Expect to get your hands dirty alongside your crew. This position supervises, but it's not a desk job.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • A minimum of 1 year in a supervisory capacity
  • Hands-on skills across plumbing, HVAC, electrical, appliance repair, and carpentry
  • HVAC certification and CPO certification are strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • Organized enough to track work orders, maintain accurate records, and manage inventory without things falling through the cracks
  • Strong interpersonal skills, particularly with residents who are frustrated or need a patient explanation

The Context Worth Knowing

Avanath focuses specifically on affordable and workforce housing, which shapes how this role operates. Residents in these communities often have fewer resources to absorb a broken AC unit or a plumbing issue that drags on. Responsiveness and follow-through carry more weight here than at a Class A luxury lease-up where amenities can offset maintenance delays. The Maintenance Supervisor at an Avanath property tends to be a visible, known presence in the community, which matters for resident retention and overall community stability.

Strong candidates for this type of role bring more than technical skills. The people who advance in affordable housing maintenance tend to be supervisors who can develop junior staff, communicate clearly with residents across different backgrounds, and think about the property's physical condition as a long-term stewardship responsibility, not just a punch list to close out.

job.title: Community Administrative Coordinator- The Infinity
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do at The Infinity

The Infinity is a luxury high-rise HOA community in San Francisco, and Action Property Management runs the on-site operation there the way you'd expect a building of that caliber to run: tight, professional, and resident-focused. As the Community Administrative Coordinator, you're the operational anchor for the front-facing side of the association. That means handling correspondence, coordinating with vendors and residents, managing records, supporting the community manager, and keeping daily office functions moving without gaps.

This is a Monday through Friday role, 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, with occasional weekend availability when community needs require it. The pay range sits at $29 to $30 per hour depending on experience, with an annual bonus attached.

What You Bring

  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple administrative tasks simultaneously in a high-expectation environment
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication, particularly with residents who expect a hospitality-grade experience
  • Experience in property management, HOA administration, or a related field where attention to detail directly affected outcomes
  • Comfort with property management software and general office systems
  • A calm, reliable presence. Luxury communities generate high expectations, and the coordinator role absorbs a lot of that pressure daily

Where This Role Leads

Coordinators who do this job well tend to move into community manager roles faster than people coming from other entry points, and for good reason. You're building fluency in HOA governance, vendor relationships, resident communication, and administrative compliance all at once. At a building like The Infinity, you're also learning what luxury service operations actually require at the operational level, which is a different skill set than managing a garden-style or Class B community. That exposure compounds quickly.

Action Property Management is the largest privately owned HOA management company in the West, with over 300 communities across nine offices and a team approaching 900 people. That scale means internal mobility is real. If you're thinking about where an administrative coordinator role takes you in HOA or broader property management, the answer is: toward a portfolio, toward a manager title, and toward a much clearer picture of how associations actually function from the inside. Starting at a high-rise luxury property in San Francisco gives you a stronger foundation than most coordinator roles will.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Student housing property management sits at one of the more demanding intersections in residential real estate: you're running a full business operation while managing a resident base that turns over almost entirely every 12 months. At PeakMade Real Estate, this Property Manager role in Davis, California carries that full weight. You'll own the NOI, the leasing strategy, the team, and the resident experience at an off-campus community serving UC Davis students.

What This Role Actually Covers

The scope here is genuinely broad. On the financial side, you'll build and manage the annual operating budget, track performance against it, and report to your Regional Manager with accurate operational and financial data. Rent collection, delinquency monitoring, and reconciliation fall to you, as does identifying cost control opportunities that protect NOI without sacrificing the resident experience.

Leasing strategy is a real part of the job. Student housing runs on a highly compressed leasing cycle, and you'll direct marketing and sales plans designed to hit budgeted occupancy before the annual turn. You'll keep close tabs on competitor properties and make sure your team knows the product and the market just as well as you do.

On the people side, you'll recruit, train, coach, and evaluate your on-site staff. You'll also own the Turn process from start to finish, which in student housing is one of the highest-stakes operational events of the year. Every unit cycling through make-ready in a condensed window demands tight coordination between leasing, maintenance, and administration.

  • 4+ years of property management experience required
  • 2 years in student housing management preferred
  • Comfort reading monthly financial statements and building annual budgets
  • Experience with property management software; Entrata strongly preferred
  • Full-time, on-site presence required
  • High school diploma required; college degree preferred

Where This Role Leads

For a property manager who wants to move toward a Regional Manager position, student housing is one of the better training grounds. The annual lease-up cycle forces you to sharpen leasing strategy in ways that conventional multifamily doesn't always require. The Turn builds operational discipline under real time pressure. And managing a younger resident demographic develops communication and conflict-resolution skills that transfer cleanly to any asset class. Managers who come out of student housing tend to read occupancy trends and traffic patterns with more urgency than their conventional peers. That instinct compounds over time.

PeakMade is an Atlanta-based company with a national portfolio spanning student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities. The Davis property sits in a college town with a stable, enrollment-driven demand base, which gives you predictable traffic patterns to work with even as you manage the intensity of annual renewals and new leases. Compensation for this role is set in the $80,000 to $85,000 range annually, with the final number reflecting experience and fit.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

This assistant property manager position at The Signature at Schilling Farms Apartments in Collierville, Tennessee draws on a specific mix: leasing ability, administrative accuracy, and operational awareness. You're not here to specialize in just one of those. You need all three working together on the same shift.

On the leasing side, you'll handle the full cycle from prospect to signed lease. That means knowing the property cold: floor plans, amenities, pricing, and what sets this community apart. Traffic counts go in daily. Rental payments get collected and posted accurately. Residents submit service requests and expect follow-through, so you'll either handle those directly or make sure they move to the right hands.

The inspection piece is real work. Model units, common areas, vacant apartments, amenities. You walk them. You catch issues before residents do. That habit, done consistently, protects the property's condition and the company's reputation.

What the Role Requires

  • One to two years of residential leasing or property management experience
  • Hands-on experience with OneSite or Yardi (strongly preferred)
  • Availability to work weekends
  • Ability to walk the property, including stairs
  • Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The software requirement matters here. If you've logged real time in OneSite or Yardi posting payments, running reports, and managing resident records, you'll move faster from day one. If you've used comparable platforms, be prepared to talk through what you know.

Working at MRG

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg is a Memphis-area firm with a track record in residential management. The Collierville market sits in one of the stronger suburban submarkets in the greater Memphis metro, with demand that stays relatively steady. Working at a property like this gives you exposure to an active lease-up and renewal environment without the instability of a struggling asset.

The role carries real backup responsibility. When the property manager is out, you step in. That's worth noting for candidates who want to move toward a property manager title within the next year or two. This position is a direct path if you perform.

Compensation includes a base salary, a bonus and commission program, medical and other insurance options, a 401(k) with profit-sharing, and paid training. The company describes the work environment as pleasant, which in practice usually means low turnover and stable leadership.

job.title: Maintenance Technician- Sonoran
job.description:
MG Properties has spent three decades acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. That operational depth shows up in how they run their properties, and it shapes what they expect from the people maintaining them. The Maintenance Technician role at Sonoran Apartments in Phoenix is a hands-on position where the day-to-day work directly affects occupancy, resident satisfaction, and the condition of the asset.

Sonoran is a 200-plus unit community, which means the volume of service requests, turns, and preventive tasks is real. On any given week you might be pulling an a/c capacitor in the morning, patching and painting a unit in make-ready, clearing a service ticket on a running toilet, and handling grounds before residents get home from work. Appliance repairs, common area upkeep, and on-call emergency response are all part of the rotation. The technician who thrives here moves efficiently between trades and doesn't need to be told twice what a punch list looks like.

Turn quality matters here. A clean, well-executed make-ready keeps days vacant low and protects NOI. A technician who can move a unit through turn quickly without skipping steps is genuinely valuable to the property's performance, not just to the maintenance team.

What MG Properties is looking for:

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, preferably on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair
  • Availability for on-call rotation and emergency response
  • Reliable transportation
  • Customer-facing communication skills and the ability to work within a team structure

Phoenix summers put HVAC systems under real pressure. Technicians who can diagnose and resolve a/c issues quickly during peak heat season aren't just fixing equipment. They're protecting resident retention and keeping emergency call volume manageable. Comfort with HVAC work is genuinely useful here, not just a checkbox.

Compensation includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, and a full medical, dental, and vision package. PTO, paid holidays, paid personal days, paid sick time, and a rental discount round out the benefits. MG Properties participates in E-Verify, maintains a drug-free workplace, and requires a background check and drug screen prior to hire.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance Technician roles at student housing properties carry a wider scope than a typical apartment gig. The asset complexity is higher, the resident turnover is seasonal and compressed, and the building systems demand real technical depth. This position at The Lodges in Colorado Springs reflects that.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-scope maintenance role, not a service-request-only position. You'll handle daily work orders, make-ready prep on vacated units, and preventive maintenance across major building systems. That includes air handling units with outside condensers, electrical distribution systems, switchgear, domestic hot water systems, UPS equipment, parking structure drainage, and life safety systems including fire pumps, sprinklers, smoke detectors, CO2 alarms, and fire dampers. You'll log everything through Entrata and a CMMS, and Scion also uses Building Automation Systems for monitoring and diagnostics.

On the unit side, you'll inspect vacated apartments, document needed repairs, and perform the hands-on work to get them rent-ready: appliance repair, carpentry, plumbing, painting, basic electrical. Common area upkeep, pressure washing, pool chemical maintenance, and snow removal are also part of the rotation. After-hours emergency response is real here. On-call coverage is expected outside approved PTO.

What Scion Requires

  • High school diploma, GED, or trade school credential plus 3 to 5 years of full-time maintenance experience
  • HVAC certification and EPA 608 (Type I and II)
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) license, or a commitment to obtain it within six months
  • Comfort with BAS, CMMS, and Entrata (or ability to get up to speed quickly)
  • Ability to read blueprints and interpret warranties
  • Valid driver's license and physical ability to lift up to 100 lbs. and stand for extended shifts
  • Flexible availability for weekends and after-hours emergencies

Where This Role Can Go

Technicians at this level who build strong documentation habits and show comfort with BAS and life safety systems tend to move toward Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor roles. Student housing operators like Scion run multi-property portfolios, which means internal mobility is a realistic path for people who perform. The seasonal turn cycle, typically summer, is where your make-ready efficiency will get noticed most. A tech who can keep turns on schedule during peak season stands out quickly.

Compensation includes a discretionary annual bonus, health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid maternity leave, and PTO. No visa sponsorship is available.

job.title: Horticulturist
job.description:
Grounds maintenance in a residential property portfolio demands more than a green thumb. At the scale John M. Corcoran & Company operates across New England, curb appeal is a managed outcome, not a seasonal afterthought. This Horticulturist role sits at the intersection of skilled horticultural craft and the day-to-day operational expectations of a multi-property portfolio with assets across Massachusetts, Northern Rhode Island, and Southern New Hampshire.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

You'll move across JMC's portfolio as needed, which means no two weeks are identical. One morning might involve pruning mature shrubs and assessing irrigation coverage at a garden-style community in Massachusetts; the next might have you setting railroad ties or coordinating with an outside contractor on a landscaping project at a New Hampshire property. You carry a working knowledge of soil, plant health, and seasonal timing into every site visit, and you apply it with the kind of autonomy that comes from genuine expertise.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Planting, pruning, and maintaining shrubs, trees, flowers, and lawn areas across assigned properties
  • Managing irrigation systems and fertilization schedules to support healthy growth
  • Operating power equipment including mowers, trimmers, hedge trimmers, chainsaws, and leaf blowers safely and per manufacturer guidelines
  • Setting railroad ties and supporting hardscape maintenance
  • Coordinating with outside landscaping contractors and suppliers
  • Supporting snow and ice management and responding to emergency storm situations as needed
  • Assisting with truck deliveries when requested

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., which gives the role a consistent structure uncommon in grounds work at smaller operators.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

Coming in, you need an associate's degree or certificate in Horticulture (or equivalent field experience), hands-on knowledge of landscaping techniques, and confidence operating the full range of power equipment the job demands. Physical capability matters here: the role involves ladders, pruners, chainsaws, and real outdoor labor across New England seasons. Candidates must pass background, drug and alcohol, and physical and agility screenings at hire and on an ongoing basis.

What this role builds is portfolio-scale judgment. When you're responsible for curb appeal across multiple communities rather than a single site, you develop a sense for how plant selection, maintenance timing, and irrigation choices affect the long-term condition of shared outdoor spaces. That kind of systems thinking transfers well into landscape management or facilities coordination roles as your career progresses.

The Company Behind the Role

JMC has operated in New England real estate since 1951, and the company has a track record of retaining people over long careers. That kind of tenure tends to reflect well-structured operations and a culture where skilled tradespeople are treated as professionals. The pay range for this position runs from $26.75 to $38.00 per hour, with placement based on relevant experience. Candidates with 20 or more years in horticulture or grounds maintenance may qualify toward the upper end of that range.

job.title: Multi-Site Service Manager (Stone Gate/Village on the Lake)
job.description:
Van Metre is filling a Multi-Site Service Manager role that covers two residential communities in Spring Lake, NC: Village on the Lake and Stone Gate Apartments. Both properties fall under a single maintenance operation, which means the person in this seat is coordinating labor, vendors, budgets, and work orders across two addresses simultaneously. That dual-site scope is the defining feature of the job and shapes what a typical week looks like.

Day to day, you're managing a maintenance team, triaging service requests, and keeping the make-ready pipeline moving. When a unit turns, you're the one scheduling vendors, walking punch lists, and making sure the unit is rent-ready on time. You're also the point of contact when contractors come on site, and you work closely with the Property Manager to make sure the physical condition of both properties stays within Van Metre's standards. On the financial side, you're responsible for the facility budget, which means tracking spend and flagging variances before they become problems.

The technical requirements here are real. EPA Universal certification and a CPO are required before you start. You need hands-on working knowledge of HVAC systems, including the ability to maintain, repair, and replace units. Electrical, plumbing, appliance repair, carpentry, and painting are all part of the job. You'll also manage the 24-hour emergency maintenance schedule and carry a preventative maintenance program alongside the reactive work. Weekend availability comes with the territory.

What Van Metre Is Looking For

  • 3 or more years of maintenance supervisor experience
  • 3 or more years of direct supervisory experience managing a team
  • EPA Universal / CFC certification (required)
  • CPO certification (required)
  • Strong applied knowledge of electrical, plumbing, and appliance systems
  • Current familiarity with OSHA and building safety standards
  • Valid driver's license
  • Your own basic tools

Compensation sits at $78,000 to $79,040 annually, with an additional $5,000 bonus paid out quarterly. Van Metre also offers renewal commissions, a $900 annual wellness reimbursement, tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, and a matched 401(k). The PTO package is generous and includes 11 paid holidays, vacation, sick days, personal days, volunteer days, a winter break, a day off for your annual physical, and a day off for your birthday.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from single-site roles: multi-site maintenance management puts a premium on prioritization and communication. When two properties have competing needs on the same morning, the ability to deploy your team efficiently and communicate clearly with two property managers becomes the skill that separates solid candidates from exceptional ones. If you've managed that kind of competing-priority environment before, that experience will matter here more than almost anything else on your resume.

job.title: Community Relations Manager
job.description:
Property management has split into two distinct operating models over the past decade: transactional lease shops focused on volume, and experience-driven operators who treat occupancy as a byproduct of genuine resident satisfaction. Cortland sits firmly in the second camp, and this Community Relations Manager role in Nashville reflects that philosophy in its day-to-day scope.

What This Role Actually Does

The position carries real operational weight alongside the resident-facing responsibilities most people associate with a leasing title. You'll support the Community Manager in keeping daily operations aligned with company standards, which means conducting inspections on vacant units, make-ready apartments, and model homes, completing move-in and move-out walkthroughs, and managing vendor relationships to keep projects on schedule. That operational layer matters because it builds a working knowledge of the full property cycle, not just the front-door experience.

On the revenue side, you own your pipeline. That means disciplined CRM hygiene, prompt follow-up, consistent tracking of conversion metrics, and closing leases with consultative techniques rather than pressure tactics. Cortland operates Class A multifamily, so prospects come in with high expectations and real alternatives. The ability to uncover what someone actually values in a home and connect that to what the community offers is what separates strong performers here from average ones.

Community advocacy rounds out the scope: social media presence, resident events, referral cultivation, and handling objections with enough grace that a frustrated prospect becomes a signed lease. Nashville's multifamily market has absorbed significant new supply in recent years, which means concessions and traffic patterns shift quickly. Knowing how to read that environment and adjust your approach accordingly will serve you well in this market specifically.

Who Builds a Strong Career from Here

Candidates who thrive in this role typically have at least two years of measurable sales performance in a short-cycle, high-touch environment. Multifamily experience is a natural fit, but hospitality, luxury retail, and premium automotive backgrounds translate well because the underlying skill set is the same: consultative selling, objection handling, and relationship maintenance after the close. A bachelor's degree is preferred but not required if your track record is strong.

  • 2+ years of sales success with documented quota attainment
  • Comfort with pipeline management and CRM systems
  • Experience with property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including social media content creation
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing guidelines and operational compliance basics

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role is a genuine on-ramp to community management. The operational exposure you get here, inspections, vendor oversight, compliance touchpoints, pairs with the leasing and resident experience skills you'll sharpen daily. Candidates who move up quickly from roles like this are usually the ones who treat the operational side as seriously as the sales side. Community Manager, then Senior Community Manager, then a Regional path, are all realistic progressions for someone who produces results and builds operational credibility at the same time.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-time, in-office administrative support role at Lincoln Property Company's Charlotte location. You'll keep the day-to-day operations of a real estate team running on schedule. That means owning calendars, coordinating meeting logistics, drafting and distributing correspondence, and keeping filing systems organized and current. Expense reports, purchase orders, and invoices flow through this desk, so accuracy matters as much as speed.

You'll also manage office supplies, support onboarding logistics when new team members join, and maintain data across company systems. The work is varied, often fast-moving, and requires someone who can prioritize without being asked twice. Lincoln operates across commercial, multifamily, and mixed-use assets nationwide, so the team you're supporting likely has a full plate and needs a reliable point of coordination behind the scenes.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent; at least two years of administrative or clerical experience
  • Commercial real estate background is a plus, though not required
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, and Outlook specifically
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail, especially when handling financial documents and data entry
  • Ability to manage competing priorities independently, without waiting for direction on routine tasks
  • Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

Context Worth Knowing

Lincoln Property Company manages over 720 million square feet of commercial space across the U.S. and Europe. At that scale, the administrative layer matters. Support staff who learn the business, understand the asset types, and build relationships across departments often move into coordinator and property management roles over time. This position is a real entry point into a national firm with a broad platform.

The role is 100% on-site during standard business hours. Remote or hybrid is not available for this position.

job.title: Leasing Consultant- Russellville Commons
job.description:
Leasing Consultant roles at established Western U.S. operators like MG Properties tend to be more substantive than they first appear. You're not just showing units. You're qualifying traffic, managing the full lease-up process from first contact to move-in, and sitting at the intersection of sales, compliance, and resident relations. That combination of skills, built consistently over a year or two, opens doors that surprise people.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

At Russellville Commons in Portland, you'll greet and qualify prospective residents, guide them through the application process, and coordinate with maintenance to make sure move-ins go cleanly. Punch list follow-through matters here because a rocky move-in often sets the tone for the entire residency. You'll prepare and oversee lease signings, keep rental files accurate and current, and enter data into the property management system with enough precision that reporting doesn't get muddied downstream.

Resident interaction doesn't stop at signing. You'll handle maintenance requests, field complaints professionally, and support rent collection follow-up. Monthly administrative tasks and paperwork organization also fall into your lane. MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, so the systems and processes you'll work within are built by people who've seen a lot of property cycles.
