What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred, not required)
  • Strong sales instincts and genuine customer service skills
  • Comfort in a team environment where collaboration with maintenance is routine
  • Professional communication, both written and verbal
  • Accuracy with data entry and file management

Where This Role Can Lead

Leasing Consultant is one of the better starting points in residential property management because the skills compound fast. Learning to qualify applicants builds fair housing fluency. Coordinating move-ins builds operational instincts. Working delinquency conversations builds the resident relations muscle that Assistant Managers and Property Managers rely on constantly. MG Properties promotes from within, which means the path to a senior leasing or assistant manager title is a real near-term possibility if you perform and signal readiness. Companies with 30-plus years of acquisition and management history tend to have depth in their org charts, and that depth creates room to move.

The compensation package includes monthly and quarterly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, full medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a rental discount. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and paid sick time are all included.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a calendar that most property managers never touch. Annual mass turnover, lease-up pressure tied to an academic year, and a resident base with specific expectations around community and service. The Community Manager role at Copper Beech Harrisonburg sits at the center of all of it, and the skills it draws on are different in important ways from conventional multifamily management.

Skills This Role Requires on Day One

Financial fluency is non-negotiable here. You'll own the full NOI picture: budget preparation, variance reporting, invoice processing, payroll, and month-end close. Concessions, gain-to-lease, and leasing velocity are KPIs you'll be held to directly, so comfort reading and acting on financial data is a baseline requirement. Equally important is vendor management. You'll be pulling bids, evaluating scopes, and escalating capex projects through the Regional Manager and Facilities department. Knowing how to read a bid critically and understand what you're approving matters.

Leadership at this level also means owning the staffing model. You're scheduling, setting on-call rotations, and serving as the primary after-hours responder when issues escalate. If conflict management isn't already a developed skill for you, this role will expose that gap quickly. Three or more years managing a residential community and a team of three or more is the stated baseline, and Scion means it.

Skills This Role Builds

For managers who haven't worked in student housing, the annual turn process at a property like Copper Beech is genuinely formative. The scale and compression of time involved in turning hundreds of units in a short window builds operational planning abilities that transfer to any high-volume residential context. You'll be using Turnable to track unit progress, conducting move-out inspections, doing vendor service walks, and getting hands-on with punch list items when the timeline demands it. This isn't delegated from a distance. You'll be in units.

The tech stack here is broader than most multifamily roles. Entrata for property management, Vena for budgeting, Greenhouse for hiring, Lattice for performance management, Qualtrics for resident and employee experience data, and ClickUp for project tracking. Proficiency across platforms like these makes you a stronger operator in any environment that's moving toward integrated property tech.

What Makes This Role Distinct

Scion treats the General Manager as a business unit leader, not a site-level administrator. You're expected to proactively identify revenue opportunities and cost reductions, not just execute a plan handed down from above. Quarterly apartment inspections, monthly property walks with scored assessments, permit compliance audits, and reputation management all live in this role. The breadth is real.

Student housing also has a community-building dimension that differs from conventional multifamily. Resident events, brand integrity, and a customer experience philosophy are part of how Scion differentiates its properties. Managers who've only focused on numbers and operations without developing that community-facing side tend to find the adjustment meaningful.

  • 3+ years managing a residential community and a direct team
  • Experience with property management systems (Entrata preferred)
  • Demonstrated financial management: budgeting, forecasting, variance reporting
  • Vendor management and bid evaluation experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort working non-traditional hours during peak periods and emergencies

The position is based on-site at Copper Beech Harrisonburg, with periodic travel possible. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Sunset Creek, Sunset Pines)
job.description:
MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable housing across Northern California since 1970, and their portfolio of over 140 properties reflects something you don't see everywhere in this sector: genuine long-term investment in residents and communities. The Assistant Community Manager role at Sunset Creek and Sunset Pines in Fairfield sits at the operational center of that work.

Fairfield's affordable housing market carries real pressure. Solano County sits between the Bay Area and Sacramento, which means residents here often include working families priced out of both metros, seniors on fixed incomes, and individuals with special needs who need stable housing to build any kind of financial footing. The work you'd do at these two properties directly touches all of that.

Day to day, this role covers a genuine range of operational responsibilities. You'll handle income verification appointments, process lease agreements, maintain the waitlist, and assist with re-certifications. HUD Management and Occupancy Reviews (MORs) and TCAC compliance reviews are part of the picture, which means accuracy in resident files and documentation isn't optional. On the facilities side, you'll coordinate with maintenance staff, track work orders, and conduct property inspections to flag any maintenance or security concerns early. Rent collection support, petty cash logs, and bank deposit prep round out the fiscal side of the position.

Resident relations are woven through all of it. Issuing notices, scheduling turns, preparing turnover forms, communicating emergency procedures, and helping coordinate resident meetings are all part of the job. MidPen's onsite Resident Services team works closely with property management, so you'd be operating in an environment where the social services side of affordable housing is present and active rather than something handled at arm's length.

One thing worth understanding about tax-credit affordable housing operations: compliance documentation runs deeper here than at conventional market-rate properties. TCAC and HUD requirements mean that re-certifications, income verifications, and file integrity carry real regulatory weight. Experience or genuine comfort with that documentation layer will separate candidates who hit the ground running from those who spend the first several months catching up.

What the role requires:
  • High school diploma or GED, with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or relevant administrative experience
  • Proficiency in MS Office; experience with RealPage is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Organized and detail-oriented work habits, especially around confidential resident files
  • Ability to work independently while staying aligned with a Community Manager and broader team
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission in affordable housing

Pay runs from $21.15 to $23.80 per hour based on experience and qualifications. MidPen offers a full benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, EAP, pet insurance, and paid time off plus wellness days.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Madera)
job.description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon and you're knee-deep under a kitchen sink when your radio goes off about a tripped breaker in another unit. That's the job. You finish the plumbing, document it, and head to the next one.

Prometheus Real Estate Group is looking for a Maintenance Technician II to join the team at their Madera property in Mountain View, California. Prometheus has operated in the Bay Area since 1965 and holds the largest privately held apartment portfolio in the region, with over 13,000 units across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. The company operates as a Certified B Corporation and manages its properties in-house across acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and day-to-day operations.

What the Work Looks Like

Turns are a significant part of this role. You'll work through all phases of apartment make-ready: appliance repairs and installation, plumbing, carpentry, electrical work, and painting. Service requests from current residents fill the rest of your time, with an expectation that you can troubleshoot and repair most major mechanical systems and handle all minor ones independently. Customer interaction is part of every day. Residents notice how you show up, not just whether the faucet got fixed.

On-call availability is required. That means occasional evenings and weekends, and being reachable when something goes wrong after hours. Prometheus does pay standby and on-call premium pay, which is a real acknowledgment that off-hours availability has a cost.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in apartment maintenance
  • Hands-on competency across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance work
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Basic computer proficiency for work order systems and documentation
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs., stand and move through the day, and work primarily outdoors in moderate temperatures
  • Strong communication in English, both written and verbal

Candidates who stand out at this level tend to diagnose quickly without running through every possibility sequentially. They close their work orders clean, with accurate notes, because the next tech and the property manager both depend on that paper trail. If your instinct is to patch and move on without documenting, that habit will create friction here.

Compensation runs from $31.00 to $32.25 per hour, with a discretionary semi-annual bonus and additional incentives including referral, renovation, and lease-up bonuses where applicable. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision plans covering eligible dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts. Prometheus also offers 12 paid holidays, including your birthday, which is an unusual and concrete acknowledgment that they've thought about their people beyond the standard package.

job.title: Market Property Manager III
job.description:
John M. Corcoran and Company has operated in New England real estate since 1951, and The Halstead in Plymouth, MA is one of their managed communities. This Market Property Manager III role sits at the operational center of the property: you own day-to-day performance, lead the on-site team, and report upward to senior leadership on financial and strategic outcomes.

What the Job Covers

You'll run the full operation. That means rent collection, delinquency management, and initiating corrective or legal action when residents fall behind. You'll review and approve new resident applications alongside your staff, conduct annual property audits, and get properties ready for both internal and external reviews.

On the strategic side, you'll track the competitive market and bring recommendations on rental rates, renewal rents, and marketing approach to senior leadership. You'll also work directly with property owner representatives on performance goals, which means you need to be comfortable translating on-the-ground realities into conversations about NOI and long-term property strategy.

Staff management is a real part of this role. You'll hire, train, and supervise administrative, leasing, and maintenance personnel. You're also accountable for contract negotiations and monitoring capital improvement work, so the ability to stay organized across multiple moving priorities matters here.

What JMC Needs From You

  • At least 5 years of property management experience
  • Demonstrated experience in affordable housing programs (this is a firm requirement, not a preference)
  • Proficiency with Yardi and Microsoft Office
  • Hands-on budget management experience
  • Proven ability to hire, develop, and hold a team accountable

The salary range for this position runs from $86,320 to $102,960, with placement depending on depth of experience. A $2,500 sign-on bonus is included. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Where This Role Fits

The affordable housing requirement is the detail that separates qualified candidates from interested ones. Compliance in this space, whether HUD programs, Low-Income Housing Tax Credit requirements, or income certification processes, demands accuracy and consistency that goes beyond standard market-rate management. If you've only managed Class A or B market-rate product, this may be a stretch. If you've worked the compliance side of affordable communities and also know how to lead a team and read a budget, this is a natural fit.

JMC describes a culture where long tenure is common and internal growth is real. For a property manager ready to move toward a regional or director-level role, the reporting relationship here, directly advising senior leadership on rates and strategy, builds the credibility and visibility that supports that path.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Vero Beach sits in a stretch of Florida's Treasure Coast that draws a genuinely mixed renter profile: retirees, seasonal residents, young professionals, and working families all share the same leasing office waiting room. That variety shapes what this role actually demands day to day. A Leasing Manager here can't run a single script. You read the room, adjust your approach, and still close.

Waypoint Management Services is hiring for that position now. The core of the job is converting prospect interest into signed leases, then supporting those residents through move-in and into their tenancy. That sounds straightforward, but the full cycle is genuinely involved. You're fielding inquiries, running tours, preparing lease files, calculating prorations, and managing applicant qualification, all while keeping the leasing office and model units presentable and tour-ready. Renewals and waitlist management fall into the mix too, because occupancy goals don't pause between new lease cycles.

The follow-up piece deserves honest attention. Prospects who go quiet don't always stay that way, and the difference between a missed lease and a signed one is often one well-timed call or email. If you enjoy that part of sales, not just the tour but the patient, persistent follow-through, this role fits naturally. If you've come from hospitality or retail sales and you're moving into multifamily for the first time, that background translates well here. The human dynamics of leasing aren't far removed from managing guest experience or closing a service sale.

Spanish language skills are preferred, which reflects the community's demographics and gives the right candidate a real edge in building trust with prospective residents who may feel more comfortable in their first language. Yardi and CRM familiarity will help you get up to speed faster, though neither is a hard requirement. Fair Housing knowledge is expected at some level of fluency before you step into the role.

Weekend availability is part of the schedule rotation. That's consistent with almost every leasing role, but it's worth stating plainly: Saturday and Sunday are often the highest-traffic days, and a leasing manager who shows up present and energized on those days carries a lot of weight for the team.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years in leasing, sales, or hospitality, with a track record of converting interest into commitments
  • Comfortable handling the full leasing cycle: inquiry to move-in, including lease preparation and financial calculations
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations
  • Bilingual English/Spanish, preferred
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable property management software, a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent; valid driver's license required

Waypoint offers monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a leaser-of-the-month monetary recognition, an employee housing discount, medical/dental/vision coverage starting day one, 401(k) with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one, and additional floating days. For someone who wants a clear connection between their daily performance and their paycheck, the bonus structure here gives that feedback loop in a real way.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
A Monday morning at this property might start with a rent roll review flagging three delinquent accounts, a call from the compliance department about an upcoming Management and Occupancy Review, and a maintenance supervisor waiting on your sign-off for a vendor quote. By noon, you're in a unit inspection. That's the rhythm here.

The Role

Fairstead owns and manages more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, operating as an integrated owner and operator of affordable housing. This Community Manager position sits at one of their Cleveland properties and carries full accountability for day-to-day operations, site compliance, and financial performance.

The compliance side of this role is substantial. You'll work within HUD's 4350.3 Handbook requirements, coordinate with the internal Compliance Department on regulatory responses, and prepare the property for REAC reviews, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. Annual and interim recertifications fall under your oversight as well. This is affordable housing with real regulatory depth, and the expectation is that you already understand how these processes work, not that you'll learn them on the job.

On the financial side, you'll monitor delinquency, pursue collections through legal channels when necessary, track bad-debt write-offs, and attend monthly budget review meetings. The operations side covers lease enforcement, eviction coordination, move-in and move-out logistics, vendor bidding, unit inspections, and bi-annual building walk-throughs with the Building Superintendent. You'll also stay connected to any active renovation or construction work on site, coordinating access and helping avoid violations during the process.

What Strong Candidates Bring

The hard requirements for this role reflect how compliance-intensive affordable housing management actually is:

  • At least three years of team management experience in property management, hospitality, retail, or restaurant settings
  • COS or CPO certification (non-negotiable given the HUD environment)
  • EIV experience and working knowledge of affordable housing compliance
  • TCS certification for tax credit properties
  • Proficiency in Yardi and/or RealPage (preferred)
  • Comfort in Microsoft Office and the ability to manage competing deadlines across compliance, operations, and finance
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred but not required

What actually separates strong candidates in a role like this is the ability to hold the compliance and operational tracks simultaneously without letting either slip. Affordable housing managers who thrive tend to think about recertification timelines the same way a conventional manager thinks about lease expirations: proactively, with a calendar in hand. If you've managed a HUD or LIHTC property through an MOR or REAC inspection, that experience matters more here than general management tenure.

From a career standpoint, Community Managers who perform well in affordable housing compliance environments often advance to Regional Manager roles overseeing multiple affordable or mixed-portfolio assets, or move into compliance-focused positions at the corporate level. The HUD and LIHTC fluency you build here is genuinely transferable and remains in high demand as affordable housing development continues to scale nationally.

job.title: Porter
job.description:
Porter roles at student housing and build-to-rent communities are ground-level in title but foundational in function. The condition of common areas, make-ready units, and amenity spaces shapes how residents feel about where they live, and that perception drives renewals and referrals. At PeakMade Real Estate, this position sits inside a portfolio that spans off-campus student housing, traditional multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country, all managed out of Atlanta.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The core of this role is keeping the property clean, safe, and presentable. That means daily attention to the leasing office, amenity areas, laundry facilities, and other common spaces, on whatever schedule the property manager sets. When units turn, you'll help prepare them for incoming residents, which in student housing often means tight timelines and high volume during summer turns. You'll track supplies and equipment, respond to resident and management requests with professionalism, and flag anything unusual about the property or residents to the appropriate person. OSHA compliance and safe handling of cleaning chemicals aren't optional here; they're part of the daily routine.

The physical demands are real. This role involves frequent lifting up to 75 pounds, regular bending and stooping, and hands-on work with machinery and equipment. If you've worked in facilities, hospitality, or groundskeeping before, you'll recognize the rhythm quickly.

What This Role Builds

Porters who pay attention to how a property operates, not just their task list, tend to move into maintenance technician roles over time. You start to understand the relationship between unit condition and occupancy, between clean amenities and resident satisfaction scores, between a well-logged punch list and a smooth make-ready. Those are the instincts that property managers notice when they're filling maintenance tech openings. Student housing in particular moves fast during lease-up season, and people who can work under that pressure and still maintain standards get remembered.

PeakMade's company values center on accountability, resident experience, and continuous improvement, which maps well to someone who wants to grow rather than just clock in. The benefits package includes paid parental leave with a year of diapers provided, 17 days of paid time off including two wellbeing days, a 401(k) match, wellness programming, and employee resource groups. There's also a ten-year anniversary trip for long-tenure employees, which signals something about how the company thinks about retention.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Basic reading, written communication, and number recognition needed for daily tasks
  • Safe handling of cleaning fluids and equipment is a must
  • Physical stamina for lifting, bending, and equipment operation throughout the shift

If you're looking for a place to start building a maintenance career inside a company that manages a diverse portfolio, PeakMade's size and variety of community types gives you more exposure than a single-site operator would.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - The Elm
job.description:
The Elm is a well-regarded apartment community in Bethesda, and the maintenance team there carries a real responsibility: residents notice when things work, and they really notice when they don't. AIR Communities is bringing on a Maintenance Technician who can handle the day-to-day demands of a busy community while caring about the quality of every repair.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical day pulls in a few directions at once. You might start the morning working through service requests, diagnosing an HVAC issue in one unit and troubleshooting an appliance in another, then shift to supporting apartment turns in the afternoon, making sure each home is move-in ready and punched out properly before a new resident arrives. You'll work across plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry, so breadth matters here. You'll also assist with move-in and move-out inspections and help manage vendor quality when contractors come on site.

AIR uses maintenance technology to help the team prioritize and track work, and their shops are stocked to reduce the time you spend hunting for parts or tools. There's also an on-call rotation, at least one week per month, so reliable transportation is a real requirement, not a formality.

When you're the more experienced person in the room, you'll offer guidance to other technicians. That's part of the culture here, and it connects directly to AIR's internal development program, Ascend, which gives technicians structured learning paths tied to where they actually want to go in their careers.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of hands-on maintenance experience in apartments, facilities, or a related environment
  • Demonstrated skill in two or more trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, or similar
  • Availability for a flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and monthly on-call rotations
  • Reliable transportation for emergency response during on-call weeks
  • Physical capability to handle demanding work, including moving equipment when needed
  • Comfort using technology as part of your workflow, not just as an afterthought

The Human Side of This Role

Maintenance work in a residential setting means you're in people's homes. That changes the dynamic. A repair done well and a resident treated respectfully are equally important, and AIR ties a monthly customer satisfaction bonus of up to $250 to outcomes that reflect both. The pay range for this position is $25 to $27 per hour, with placement based on experience and skills.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here isn't just technical range. It's the combination of doing repairs right the first time and leaving a resident feeling heard and respected in the process. If you've worked in environments where that balance mattered and you've learned to carry both well, this team will notice.

AIR also offers a 50% rent discount at any of their communities, including the option to live on site, which is a meaningful benefit worth factoring into the full picture of this opportunity.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning, and before 9 a.m. you've already fielded a tenant call about an HVAC issue, flagged a vendor invoice that doesn't match the approved scope, and pulled a lease abstract to confirm CAM exclusions ahead of an operating expense reconciliation deadline. That's the rhythm of this role at Lincoln Property Company.

What This Role Actually Covers

Lincoln is one of the largest private real estate firms in the country, and this Atlanta-based position sits within their commercial portfolio, which spans office, retail, and industrial assets. As an Assistant Property Manager, you'll work directly alongside the Property Manager to keep day-to-day operations running accurately and on schedule.

A significant portion of your time will involve financial work: reviewing vendor invoices for compliance with the management agreement, supporting monthly report and budget package preparation, and managing the data collection behind CAM and operating expense reconciliations. These aren't cursory tasks. CAM rec errors surface quickly during audit season, and the discipline you build here transfers directly to senior property management responsibilities later.

Lease administration is another core area. You'll handle lease setups, process lease changes across applicable systems, and coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs including participation in walk-throughs with tenants, the Property Manager, and tenant improvement teams. On the operations side, you'll respond to tenant needs, support vendor sourcing and bid coordination, help prepare emergency response plans, and provide direction to direct reports as appropriate.

This is a fully in-office position based in Atlanta. Property inspections are conducted monthly or more frequently, and travel to assigned properties is part of the job.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

This role requires a working foundation in commercial property fundamentals. Specific requirements include:

  • A bachelor's degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience (1 to 2 years minimum)
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite
  • Familiarity with accounts payable and CMMS platforms
  • Ability to work through financial calculations including percentages, discounts, and basic financial analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills suited to both tenant relationships and internal reporting
  • Experience with commercial office, retail, or industrial properties is preferred

What the role builds is equally worth naming. Candidates who come in with basic financial literacy will leave this position understanding how to read a T-12, how operating expense reconciliations connect to lease language, and how to manage vendor relationships through a full contract cycle. Those skills position you well for a Property Manager role, particularly in commercial fee management environments where financial accuracy and client reporting carry significant weight.

Strong candidates here tend to be detail-driven without being slow. The ability to keep lease data clean, catch invoice discrepancies before they become problems, and communicate clearly across tenants, vendors, and internal teams is what separates someone who handles the job from someone who advances through it.

job.title: Maintenance Technician I
job.description:
Grounds awareness, hands-on repair instincts, and a service mindset are the core skills this role draws on every single day. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Maintenance Technician I at Overlook Morganton Park in Southern Pines, NC, and the work is grounded in the fundamentals that keep a residential community running well: clean common spaces, make-ready support, and the kind of consistent presence residents notice.

Skills This Role Builds On (and Develops)

This is an entry-level position, and Hawthorne treats it that way in the best sense. A background in yardwork, general facility upkeep, or basic repair work translates directly. Some HVAC or maintenance experience is a plus, but the role is structured to teach. What matters more than credentials is a track record of showing up reliably and taking ownership of physical space.

On the grounds side, the work involves daily debris pickup, pressure washing breezeways and sidewalks, and keeping common areas like the pool deck, fitness room, clubhouse, and mailroom clean and presentable. On the repair side, you'll assist with make-ready turns on vacant units: light painting, lock changes, fixture replacements, and bulb checks. These tasks sound routine, but they directly affect occupancy. A unit that isn't make-ready on time costs the property a lease.

The role also includes pool maintenance support and on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That on-call component is worth understanding clearly before you apply. It's manageable, but it does mean your schedule isn't always 8-to-5, even if that's the standard Monday through Friday baseline.

Where This Role Leads

Hawthorne's internal career path program is a genuine differentiator here. The progression from Technician I to Technician II is structured, not vague, and their learning and development team is actively involved. For someone early in a maintenance career, the combination of on-the-job training across HVAC basics, plumbing, electrical, and turn work creates a skill base that carries across any multifamily property type. Technicians who move up at Hawthorne or elsewhere typically do so because they build diagnostic instincts, not just task completion habits. This role is the starting point for that.

What to Know About This Property and Company

Overlook Morganton Park sits in Southern Pines, part of Moore County's stable residential market anchored by the Pinehurst area. The region draws steady demand from military-adjacent households near Fort Liberty (formerly Bragg), retirees, and golf-industry workers, which tends to produce consistent occupancy and lower turnover volatility than high-growth urban corridors. For a maintenance tech, that context matters: you're likely supporting a community with a relatively stable resident base rather than constant lease-up churn.

Hawthorne Residential Partners manages a regional portfolio across the Southeast and is known in the multifamily space for investing in their site-level teams. The monthly renewal bonus program available at this level is a concrete signal of how the company ties compensation to community performance.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • One year of maintenance, repair, or HVAC experience preferred, not required
  • Familiarity with general yardwork and facility upkeep
  • Ability to participate in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential property splits into two modes: reactive and preventive. This role runs both at the same time. You're closing out resident work orders while also keeping up with scheduled inspections, make-ready turns, and grounds upkeep. The skill this job uses most is mechanical troubleshooting. You need to walk into a unit, diagnose what's wrong, and fix it correctly the first time.

What the Work Looks Like

Day-to-day, you're handling resident repair requests, conducting inspections, and prepping vacant apartments for incoming residents. Make-readies require a sharp eye for punch list items. You're also tracking parts, managing inventory, and coordinating with vendors when work requires outside support. Documentation matters here. Work orders, materials used, safety incidents: all of it needs to be logged accurately.

This position runs on a rotating on-call schedule, so evenings and weekends are part of the job. If that's a dealbreaker, this one isn't the right fit.

Skills This Role Depends On

  • Mechanical diagnosis and repair across building systems and common areas
  • Preventive maintenance planning and execution
  • Pre-move-out inspections and unit turn preparation
  • Vendor coordination and supply management
  • Safety compliance and OSHA protocol adherence
  • Clear communication with residents, management, and contractors
  • Ability to read technical manuals, schematics, and blueprints
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification (or willingness to obtain it)
  • Valid driver's license (required for golf cart operation on property)

Physical demands are real: regular lifting up to 50 lbs, climbing ladders, working outdoors in heat and cold, and spending time in confined or noisy spaces. You need solid manual dexterity and comfort operating both hand tools and power tools.

Working at Hillpointe

Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they handle the full development cycle in-house, from land acquisition through construction and asset management. That structure means the maintenance team operates within a company that understands properties from the ground up, literally. Decisions move faster, and there's direct accountability from ownership down to site operations.

Okatie, SC sits in the Bluffton area, just outside Hilton Head Island. The region has seen steady population growth driven by coastal relocation trends, which keeps demand for workforce housing strong and occupancy pressure real. For a maintenance tech, that means consistent volume and a property that stays active.

Strong candidates for this type of role tend to have a mix of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical knowledge rather than depth in just one trade. The ability to troubleshoot across systems, without waiting on a specialist for every call, is what separates technicians who advance from those who plateau. EPA certification is a clear differentiator if you already hold it.

job.title: Maintenance Technician at Stonebriar of Frisco Apartments
job.description:
Maintenance at a Frisco Community That Keeps Its Standards High

Stonebriar of Frisco sits in one of the fastest-growing submarkets in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro. Residents here expect things to work, and when they don't, they expect a fast fix. That's what this Maintenance Technician role is built around: keeping units tight, systems running, and the make-ready pipeline moving so occupancy stays where it needs to be.

Cottonwood Residential operates with a service-first orientation. They were among the early adopters of Self-Guided Tours, which signals something real about how they run communities: they invest in the resident experience, and they expect their maintenance teams to back that up on the ground level.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're turning work orders across the full range of apartment maintenance. Plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, general carpentry, punch list items on turns. You'll also support the pool and grounds as needed, and when a resident has a Friday night emergency, you're part of the on-call rotation that responds. The Service Manager backs you up on those after-hours calls, so you're not out there without support.

The physical demands are real and worth stating plainly: you'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing ladders, working in tight crawl spaces, and carrying materials up to 50 lbs. Evenings and weekends are part of the schedule, not exceptions to it.

Preferred qualifications include:

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification
  • Strong HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • CPO certification
  • Valid Texas driver's license

Compensation and the Longer View

Cottonwood offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage with eligibility starting as early as day one. The 401k and HSA both carry company matches, and you're eligible for three weeks of PTO in your first year plus 10.5 paid holidays. Competitive pay rounds it out, though specifics aren't listed here.

For technicians with strong HVAC skills and a track record of low callback rates on work orders, this kind of role at a well-run community is a logical step toward a Service Manager seat. The DFW market has no shortage of new apartment inventory, which means experienced technicians who can handle lease-up-level volume and quality standards have real upward mobility. If you're the tech who keeps delinquency-related unit damage under control and turns units clean and fast, that performance gets noticed.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Redfield Ridge
job.description:
CloudTen Residential manages a genuinely varied multifamily portfolio across the West, from hotel-to-residential conversions to high-rise lease-ups to value-add repositioning plays. That range matters for this role because it means the skills you build here go well beyond any single asset type. Redfield Ridge is one piece of a growing Nevada-anchored operation, and the assistant manager position there is structured deliberately as a training ground for the community manager seat.

The day-to-day splits across four areas: financials, leasing, team support, and resident relations. On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection, posting, daily deposits, bank reconciliation, and invoice processing. You'll also own delinquency follow-through, including serving non-payment notices and coordinating eviction proceedings when the community manager requires backup. Weekly and monthly reporting is part of the cadence, so comfort with property management software and a clean understanding of basic accounting isn't optional here.

Leasing responsibilities include responding to inquiries, conducting tours, and keeping all lease documents current and Fair Housing compliant. You'll also help track comp properties and market conditions, which feeds into pricing and marketing recommendations. Move-in and move-out administration rounds out the operational scope, including apartment inspections and security deposit dispositions handled within state-mandated timelines.

When the community manager is off-site, you step into full operational responsibility. That's worth taking seriously during the interview process. This isn't a role where management coverage is theoretical.

Reno's multifamily market has seen real pressure over the past few years, with significant new supply delivering across the metro while rent growth has moderated from its post-pandemic peaks. That context makes delinquency management and resident retention more consequential than they might be in a tighter market. Candidates who've worked through a softer occupancy environment and understand how concessions and renewal strategy interact will stand out.

The pay range runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, an FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

What the role requires

  • At least two years in property management, leasing, or a closely related field
  • Working knowledge of landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing regulations, and local compliance standards
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and at least one property management platform
  • Strong written and verbal communication, plus the organizational discipline to manage multiple priorities without dropping anything
  • Foundational accounting knowledge sufficient to handle daily financial tasks accurately

Candidates who come in with a genuine interest in advancing to a community manager role will fit CloudTen's intent for this position. The company's growth trajectory across the West means that path isn't abstract.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Residential maintenance work builds a skill set that compounds quickly. Every service request answered, every turn completed, every HVAC system diagnosed adds to a practical knowledge base that transfers directly into lead tech roles, maintenance supervisor positions, and eventually facilities or regional maintenance management. At Karya Property Management, a Maintenance Technician role in Baytown, Texas gives you the day-to-day volume and variety that accelerates that growth.

The Technical Core

This position touches the full range of residential systems. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and paint work all fall within scope, which means you're not narrowing your expertise by taking this role. You'll respond to resident work orders, run unit turns and make-readies, and conduct property inspections to catch deferred maintenance before it becomes a larger repair. Tool and inventory management is part of the job too. Knowing what's on the shelf and keeping it stocked keeps your response times tight and your costs predictable.

On-call availability is required, so this isn't a strictly scheduled position. That's honest. After-hours work is part of residential maintenance, and if you've done this before, you already know that emergency calls during peak summer months in the Houston area are real. Baytown's heat and humidity put HVAC systems under consistent stress, which means that comfort with diagnostics and preventive maintenance on those systems is genuinely useful here, not just a checkbox on a job posting.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The basics are a high school diploma or GED and prior maintenance or handyman experience. But the technicians who stand out in a role like this share a few specific habits. They communicate with residents like professionals, not just fix the problem and leave. They anticipate what's likely to fail based on what they're already seeing during inspections. And they work efficiently during turns, because a slow make-ready delays occupancy and puts pressure on the whole team.

  • Hands-on experience with residential plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and carpentry
  • Comfortable working independently and prioritizing tasks without constant direction
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Availability for on-call and flexible scheduling
  • Genuine attention to safety standards and quality workmanship

What This Role Builds at Karya

Karya Property Management offers health and wellness benefits, strong PTO, and maternity and paternity leave. But the longer-term value of a role like this is what you build in your own career. Technicians who learn to read a property's maintenance patterns, document their work clearly, and collaborate well with the management team are the ones who move into lead or supervisor roles. This position puts you inside those daily operations, working directly alongside property management to triage and prioritize, which gives you visibility into how maintenance decisions affect NOI and resident retention. That context matters when you're ready for the next step.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Skilled hands keep occupancy numbers healthy. A well-executed turn gets a unit back on the market in days instead of weeks. A resolved HVAC ticket at 10 PM keeps a resident from churning at renewal. This Maintenance Technician role at Bozzuto's Boston property puts those skills at the center of the work every single day.

The Skills This Role Runs On

HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair form the core of what you'll handle. Bozzuto is looking for someone with beginner-to-intermediate proficiency across those trades, so you don't need a master electrician's ticket, but you do need enough hands-on experience to diagnose problems and resolve them without constant escalation. Make-readies are a real part of the workload too. Turning a vacant unit quickly and correctly, executing a solid punch list before move-in, directly affects how fast the property can convert a vacant day into revenue.

Beyond the technical side, communication skills matter more than most maintenance postings acknowledge. You're interacting with residents directly, and a technician who explains what was fixed and why earns trust that shows up in survey scores and lease renewals. Basic comfort with software and apps for work order tracking is expected. Written communication counts too, since ticket documentation creates the service record that property managers rely on.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

A typical day pulls you across service ticket resolution, preventative maintenance rounds, and general upkeep of the building and grounds. You'll be in apartments, mechanical rooms, and common areas. Boston winters add snow removal and exterior maintenance to the rotation. On-call emergency response is part of the deal, so reliable personal transportation is a firm requirement, not a suggestion. Weekends and evenings come with the territory depending on scheduling needs.

What Bozzuto Brings to This Role

Bozzuto operates at a level where systems, training, and culture are measurably invested in. One concrete example: after your 12-month anniversary, the company covers the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification. That credential expands your HVAC scope significantly and has real market value if you're building a long-term trades career. The compensation range sits at $54,000 to $56,000 annually, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

For technicians who want to grow, Bozzuto's scale across property operations creates visible pathways toward lead tech and facilities management roles. The portfolio depth means you're not stuck in one building with no upward track.

  • Experience in building maintenance or a trades education background
  • Beginner to intermediate HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair skills
  • Ability to handle frequent physical demands in the 25 to 50 pound range
  • Availability for on-call emergency response and rotating weekend shifts
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • Comfort using work order software and property management apps

job.title: Maintenance Technician II at The Marq Highland Park Apartments
job.description:
A resident puts in a request at 7 a.m.: no hot water. By 8, you've already diagnosed the water heater, sourced the part, and updated the work order. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a Maintenance Technician II for The Marq Highland Park Apartments in Westchase, Florida. This is an intermediate-level position, which means you're expected to work independently on most repairs without needing the supervisor to walk you through it. You'll handle the full range of service requests: HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical fixtures, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also contribute to the make-ready process, getting vacant units turned and ready for incoming residents.

Beyond service requests, the role includes preventative maintenance on building systems, regular property walks to keep grounds and common areas in good condition, and support for pool and spa upkeep. You'll document completed work in the property management system and stay in communication with the Maintenance Supervisor on anything that needs escalation or additional resources.

On-call rotation is part of the job. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll be expected to respond when it's your turn. The supervisor provides backup, but residents count on the team to show up.

What Qualifies You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • 2 or more years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Solid hands-on knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and pool/spa systems
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly; weights over 50 lbs. should be handled with assistance
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Basic tools required; HVAC gauges required if EPA certified

The candidates who stand out here aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who can walk into an unfamiliar problem, think through it systematically, and fix it right the first time. Multifamily maintenance moves fast, and units that sit down cost money and frustrate residents. Technicians who close work orders cleanly, communicate clearly, and leave the work area better than they found it are the ones who earn trust on a team like this.

Cottonwood Residential operates a national multifamily portfolio, so there's genuine room to grow within the organization for technicians who perform well and build their skills over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Museum District, Houston, TX
job.description:
Maintenance techs at apartment communities wear a lot of hats. At Plaza Museum District, a Berkshire Residential property in Houston's Museum District, you're not just fixing things. You're the person residents see when something's wrong, which means your attitude matters as much as your tool belt.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Your time splits between completing work orders, supporting make-readies, and keeping the property's physical condition where it needs to be. Curb appeal and common areas fall under your watch. You'll help manage shop inventory, equipment upkeep, and key security, which sounds routine until something's missing at the wrong moment. You'll also back up the management team on enforcing safety standards and community policies, and you'll be expected to document and communicate clearly, both in writing and in person.

The role calls for working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. You don't need to be a licensed specialist in every trade, but you do need enough hands-on experience to diagnose problems quickly and know when something's beyond your scope. A minimum of one year working maintenance in a residential community is expected.

What's Honest About the Job

Maintenance work at an apartment community is physical, repetitive on some days, and genuinely unpredictable on others. Residents don't always report issues at convenient times, and the punch list before a unit turn rarely shrinks on its own. The Museum District location means you're working near a dense, active part of Houston, which brings its own pace. If you prefer a job where the problems are always straightforward and the hours are always predictable, this one will test you.

That said, this is also a role where strong techs build real credibility fast. You see the whole property. You learn what breaks, how often, and why. That operational knowledge is exactly what carries into lead tech or service manager roles over time.

What Berkshire Offers

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party manager, which tends to create more consistency in how decisions get made at the site level. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, health insurance, and a 25% rent discount for employees.

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • Hands-on knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English
  • Comfort using computers and property management-related software
  • Reliable, detail-oriented, and resident-focused approach to the work

Berkshire is an equal opportunity employer committed to fair treatment across race, color, creed, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and all other protected categories.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Fairstead runs a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and the work is genuinely affordable housing, not market-rate with a mission statement attached. They develop, build, and manage under one roof, which means the maintenance operation connects directly to long-term community preservation rather than short-term asset turnover. That context matters if you're the kind of tech who cares where their work ends up.

This posting is a pipeline role. Fairstead is building out its bench of Maintenance Managers ahead of new community launches and portfolio growth, so the location isn't fixed yet. If you apply now and clear the process, you're positioned to be considered first when a site comes online. That's either appealing or it isn't, depending on your timeline.

The Service Manager title is what Fairstead calls this position internally. The core job is what you'd expect: supervise a maintenance crew, keep mechanical systems and electrical equipment running, lead on special projects, and make sure the property stays clean and safe in line with company standards. You'll handle routine work independently and pull in support for the more complex stuff. Overtime happens, usually tied to emergencies or project deadlines, and that's worth stating plainly rather than burying.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is the combination of trade depth and crew management. Fairstead wants someone proficient in a specific trade who can also run a team, not a generalist who's decent at everything and exceptional at nothing. If you've spent years as a tech and recently stepped into a lead role, that trajectory fits. If you've been a solo maintenance tech on a small property, the supervision piece will be the gap to address.

Qualifications

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience
  • Proficiency in at least one skilled trade, with broader general maintenance ability
  • Solid understanding of building and mechanical trade tools, techniques, and terminology
  • Knowledge of safety standards and accident prevention practices
  • Experience supervising or leading maintenance staff
  • Ability to implement and refine maintenance policies and procedures
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office Suite; Yardi or RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong organizational and project management skills

Fairstead uses Yardi and RealPage across its portfolio, and comfort with work order software matters more in affordable housing than people sometimes assume. When you're managing deferred maintenance on an older asset while keeping units habitable, digital tracking of open items isn't optional.

Benefits include medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with a company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12-plus paid holidays, FSA, disability insurance, pet insurance, and employee discounts on appliances and apparel.

job.title: Community Manager (Cottonwood Creek)
job.description:
Managing a 168-unit portfolio across two sites sounds straightforward on paper. In practice, it means splitting your week between Cottonwood Creek in Littleton and Elowyn Townhomes in Denver, keeping occupancy tight, delinquency low, and two onsite teams pulling in the same direction. RedPeak has operated in Denver for 24 years, and this role sits squarely in their owner-operator model, which means decisions move faster and accountability runs deeper than at a third-party shop.

What the Role Actually Covers

Your schedule runs Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at Cottonwood Creek (8801 W Belleview Ave, Littleton) and Tuesday and Thursday at Elowyn Townhomes (4725 W Quincy Ave, Denver). Splitting your week across two assets keeps the operational rhythm interesting but demands strong systems. You'll own the financial performance at both sites: budgeting, variance reporting, NOI oversight, and keeping an eye on the T-12 so nothing creeps up on you at month-end. Delinquency management, lease renewals, and concession strategy all fall under your scope, along with coordinating make-readies and tracking maintenance through to completion.

You'll lead an onsite team, which means coaching, accountability, and setting the standard for resident experience at both properties. RedPeak's philosophy is that residents should be treated like neighbors, and that expectation flows from the Community Manager down.

  • Proven experience in market-rate residential property management
  • Financial literacy: budgeting, reporting, and NOI-focused decision making
  • Comfort with property management technology across leasing, communications, and financials
  • Strong team leadership and the ability to motivate staff across multiple locations
  • Customer service instincts that translate into measurable resident satisfaction

Compensation and Benefits

Base salary runs $60,000 to $75,000, with bonus potential on top of that. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision, a 401(k) with company match that vests on day one, 16 PTO days, 10 paid holidays, and a 20% rent discount. RedPeak also offers a student debt repayment program, monthly maintenance bonuses, cell phone reimbursement, and up to $75 monthly toward a health club membership.

Where This Role Can Take You

Community Managers who handle multi-site portfolios build skills that translate directly into area manager and regional roles. Managing two assets simultaneously, each with its own budget, team, and resident base, gives you the reps that a single-site role doesn't. Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this track their own numbers proactively: occupancy, traffic-to-lease conversion, renewal rates. If you're waiting for a regional to tell you your delinquency is up, that's the gap between average and strong at this level. RedPeak's Denver-focused footprint also means you're building market knowledge in a single MSA, which compounds over time in ways that jumping between markets doesn't.

job.title: Sales and Revenue Manager
job.description:
Student housing sales runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The leasing season compresses into months, traffic spikes are short and unforgiving, and a weak conversion rate in October can haunt your occupancy numbers all the way to August move-in. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Sales and Revenue Manager to own that entire performance cycle at their West Lafayette community, a market anchored by Purdue University and its consistent enrollment demand.

What This Role Actually Manages

This is the onsite sales lead. You're responsible for occupancy, renewal rates, and revenue growth, and you're expected to build the strategies that get you there, not just execute someone else's playbook. That means developing leasing strategies tied to real targets, monitoring conversion metrics at every stage of the lead lifecycle, and identifying underperformance early enough to course-correct before it damages the T-12.

Pricing and concessions decisions happen in partnership with regional and property leadership, but your read on the competitive set matters here. You'll monitor competitor pricing, track market conditions, and bring data-backed recommendations to those conversations. Knowing when to hold rate and when a targeted concession closes the gap on occupancy is a judgment call this role makes regularly.

On the lead management side, you're watching response times, tracking source performance, and working with marketing on campaigns that align with leasing objectives by season. Student housing has specific buying behavior worth noting: parents often co-sign and heavily influence decisions, urgency peaks around roommate matching and early-bird incentives, and reputation management on platforms like Google and ApartmentRatings carries real weight with incoming freshmen and transfers. Experience in that environment matters.

Team Leadership and Coaching

You'll recruit, train, and coach leasing team members, and you'll set clear expectations around outreach activity, tour conversion, application rates, and renewal closing. Regular sales coaching and performance reviews are part of the cadence. The expectation is that you can identify why a leasing consultant isn't converting and fix it, through coaching, role-playing, process adjustment, or some combination of all three.

Renewal strategy also sits in this role. That means segmenting the resident base, building targeted messaging and incentives, and coordinating with operations to address the retention risks that often live outside the leasing office entirely.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 3 or more years in student housing, multifamily, or high-volume sales, with at least one year leading or coaching a leasing or sales team
  • Documented results: occupancy targets met, renewal rates improved, revenue goals hit
  • Fluency with CRM and property management platforms (Entrata, Yardi, RealPage, Knock, Funnel, or EliseAI are all relevant here)
  • Comfort presenting leasing reports, performance data, and action plans to ownership groups and senior leadership
  • Experience with pricing strategy or revenue management discussions at the asset level
  • Ability to work through turn season and peak leasing periods when the pace demands it

The candidates who stand out aren't just strong closers. They understand the full funnel, they can coach others to close, and they know how to create urgency in a way that protects the brand rather than undermining it. Overpromising during a lease-up is easy. Doing it without creating operational headaches or reputation damage takes real discipline.

PeakMade offers commission structures tied to monthly, quarterly, and annual performance, a housing discount, mentorship access, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, 401(k) matching, and leadership development opportunities across their national portfolio of student, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Champion Hills at Windyke is a residential community in Memphis, and Makowsky Ringel Greenberg needs a maintenance technician who can carry real responsibility from day one. This is a full trade role, not a helper position. You'll work independently across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and lock work, and you'll be expected to handle those systems with confidence rather than escalate most things to a supervisor.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical week moves between reactive repairs and scheduled work. Make-readies keep the turns moving between residents, and preventive maintenance keeps the systems from failing in the first place. You'll handle lock re-keying and installation, respond to plumbing and electrical calls, and document your work daily. Rotating weekend on-call is part of the schedule, so after-hours calls do happen. That's just honest.

The role carries a fuel allowance because you'll use your own vehicle to get to and from the property and service calls. MRG also includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, an annual bonus structure, paid time off, holidays, and a full benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, AFLAC options, and a 401(k) with profit sharing.

What You Bring

  • HVAC certification is required. Universal certification is preferred and will matter in the hiring conversation.
  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, meaning you've handled the full range of residential repair work, not just one trade.
  • Solid working knowledge of common tools, appliances, and mechanical systems.
  • Familiarity with applicable building codes and OSHA safety practices. Documentation is part of the job, so you need to be comfortable with that side of it too.
  • A reliable vehicle, valid driver's license, and proof of insurance.
  • Ability to pass background, credit, and drug screenings.

Strong candidates also bring organization and time management. When you've got three open work orders, a make-ready punch list, and a resident waiting on a callback, the techs who stay steady are the ones who prioritize well and communicate clearly. Customer service matters here because residents notice how you show up in their home, not just whether the repair got done.

Context Worth Knowing

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg has been managing properties in the Memphis market for decades. Working for an established local operator tends to mean clearer processes, institutional knowledge on the maintenance side, and a management team that understands the market. For a technician who wants stability and a legitimate path toward a lead or facilities management role, that kind of operator tends to offer more runway than a smaller shop or a national REIT where the local team is thin. If you've got the HVAC cert and the hands-on background, this is a role worth taking seriously.

job.title: Maintance Supervisor
job.description:
CommonPlace puts a real emphasis on the idea that a home is more than just an apartment unit. That framing matters for this role because a Maintenance Supervisor here isn't just keeping equipment running. The condition of every hallway, every make-ready, every courtyard reflects directly on whether residents feel like they actually belong somewhere. That's the standard you're working to.

Day to day, this job is split between leading people and doing physical work yourself. You'll schedule and supervise your team, review their work, and step in alongside them when needed. Vendor oversight is part of it too. When a contractor is on site, you're the one accountable for the quality of what they deliver. You'll manage parts inventory, keep MSDS logs current, and make sure the shop stays organized enough that the next person who needs a tool can actually find it. Turns (make-readies) are a core part of the rhythm here. Units need to be genuinely move-in ready, and that punch list responsibility lands with you.

The on-call piece is worth being direct about. Emergencies don't follow business hours, and you'll be in the rotation. That's a real part of the job. The same goes for being the person who handles lock changes after evictions or responds when something breaks down on a weekend. If you've worked in property maintenance before, none of this is a surprise. But if it's new information, it should factor into your decision.

CommonPlace is also looking for someone who communicates clearly with the Property Manager, flags unusual findings early, and keeps OSHA and company safety policies in place consistently, not just during inspections. That last part separates supervisors who actually build team habits from ones who just check boxes.

What CommonPlace Is Looking For

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in residential property management
  • 1 to 3 years in a supervisory role
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, PTAC units, appliances, and general construction
  • Comfortable with hand tools, power tools, and motorized or electrical equipment
  • Able to regularly lift, carry, or maneuver up to 50 lbs independently
  • Valid driver's license with proof of automobile liability insurance
  • Availability for on-call rotation and a flexible schedule

Pay runs $26 to $28 per hour, with medical, dental, and 401(k) benefits, plus paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering the supervisory side of this role: the strongest applicants tend to be people who've already had to hold a team accountable to a quality standard, not just complete work orders themselves. Training a newer tech to do a turn correctly takes different skills than doing the turn yourself. If that part of the job genuinely interests you, this is a role where it's a significant part of the work.

job.title: Community Relations Manager - Cortland Pembroke Pines
job.description:
Cortland sits inside the top 10 multifamily owners and operators in the country, and the Community Relations Manager role at their Pembroke Pines property puts you at the intersection of two things that drive NOI: occupancy and resident retention. If you're thinking about where a role like this leads, that answer matters as much as the day-to-day.

The position carries real operational weight. You'll support the Community Manager on daily site operations, conduct inspections across vacant units, make-ready apartments, and model homes, and keep vendor relationships calibrated so turns stay on schedule and quality holds. This isn't administrative support in a passive sense. You're the person who catches a punch list issue before a prospective resident does, or flags a curb appeal problem before it shows up in a review. That kind of attentiveness compounds over time into the habits that make a strong community manager.

On the revenue side, you're actively working a leasing pipeline. That means following up with prospects, tracking conversion metrics in the CRM, and closing leases using consultative techniques rather than high-pressure scripts. Cortland's approach is consultative by design: uncover what the prospect actually needs, then connect that need to what the community offers. Strong candidates in roles like this treat their pipeline with the same discipline a sales rep would, because that's essentially what this is. Leasing velocity and follow-up consistency are what separate people who hit their KPIs from those who explain why they didn't.

The resident experience component rounds out the role. You'll plan engagement events, manage the community's social media presence, handle objections from current and prospective residents, and generally function as the face people associate with living there. That relationship-building skill transfers directly if you move into a Community Manager seat, where retention rates and delinquency trends reflect how well the team has connected with residents over time.

Pembroke Pines sits in a competitive South Florida submarket where Class A properties compete hard on experience because the product differences across communities are often narrow. The ability to create a genuine sense of community, rather than just processing applications, matters here more than in slower markets.

What Cortland is looking for

  • At least two years of measurable sales success, ideally in multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or a comparable high-velocity environment
  • Proven pipeline management habits and a track record of hitting or beating leasing targets
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM systems, and social media as a marketing tool
  • Strong communication skills and the kind of professional presence that reflects a premium brand
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing guidelines and basic operational compliance
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

For someone early in their property management career, this role builds the exact combination of sales discipline and operational awareness that Community Manager positions require. It's a role where the skills you develop are directly portable, and at a company with Cortland's portfolio scale, internal mobility is a real path rather than a talking point.

job.title: Onsite Project Manager
job.description:
This role lives at the intersection of construction knowledge and field coordination. The Onsite Project Manager at Asset Living's Omaha location needs to read plans, hold subcontractors accountable, and keep a renovation schedule moving, all at the same time. If those three things feel natural to you, read on.

What This Role Calls On Daily

The core skills here are schedule management, vendor coordination, and quality control. You'll interpret project plans and specifications, track construction progress against contract documents, and compile submittals for the Senior Construction Project Manager's review. You're not just walking the site, you're the person who catches deviations before they become expensive problems.

Subcontractor management takes up a meaningful chunk of your time. That means reviewing proposals, confirming contract compliance, and coordinating work sequencing so trades aren't stacking on top of each other. Strong written and verbal communication is non-negotiable since you're the daily point of contact between the field and the broader project team.

Multifamily renovation experience is a genuine advantage here. Understanding how an occupied or recently vacated unit moves through a make-ready or full rehab cycle, and what quality benchmarks matter at each stage, lets you set expectations with subs rather than just report on what they did.

Qualifications Worth Highlighting

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Certified Apartment Manager (CAM) or Accredited Resident Manager (ARM) designation preferred
  • Previous multifamily renovation supervision experience strongly preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret project plans and specifications
  • Comfortable with independent judgment and real-time problem solving on-site
  • Basic computer skills and familiarity with project or property management software
  • Willingness to travel and flexibility with hours when deadlines require it
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds; regular standing, walking, and physical presence on the job site

Why This Role at Asset Living

Asset Living is a third-party management firm ranked in the NMHC top 50, with a portfolio spanning multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing. The Onsite Project Manager reports directly to a Senior Construction Project Manager, which means you get structure and a clear escalation path, but you're expected to own the day-to-day without hand-holding.

One thing candidates often underestimate about this type of role: the documentation discipline matters as much as the field presence. Submittals, schedule updates, and quality control records are how you demonstrate that work conforms to contract. Candidates who treat paperwork as secondary to "getting things done" tend to struggle. The ones who thrive treat both as the same job.

job.title: Senior Leasing Consultant - Henderson/Las Vegas, NV
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers two properties simultaneously: Prelude at the Park in Henderson and Pearl at St. Rose in Las Vegas. That dual-site setup means your day shifts between communities, so time management and strong communication with on-site teams aren't optional. You'll be the first contact for prospective residents, qualifying applicants, preparing leases, and coordinating with maintenance to keep move-ins clean. You'll also handle the administrative side, including rental file accuracy, data entry, and the monthly paperwork that keeps a property audit-ready.

Resident relations are part of the job too. Fielding maintenance concerns, addressing complaints professionally, and staying on top of rent collection all fall within your scope. Occupancy goals are real here, and you'll be expected to use genuine sales technique to hit them, not just show apartments and hope for the best. Henderson and Las Vegas maintain a competitive multifamily market with consistent renter traffic, but concessions and lease incentives can shift quickly depending on what new supply is doing nearby. Knowing how to close in that environment matters.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience, ideally on-site at an apartment community
  • Sales ability that's genuine and consultative, not scripted
  • Comfort working across two communities and coordinating with multiple teams
  • Strong attention to detail for lease preparation and file management
  • Professional communication skills with both prospects and current residents
  • Familiarity with property management software for data entry and reporting

The Bigger Picture

MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over three decades, with a portfolio that spans acquisition, development, rehab, and fee management. They're known internally for promoting from within, so a Senior Leasing Consultant role here has a real path toward Assistant Manager or beyond for someone who consistently drives occupancy and handles the administrative side with accuracy. The compensation package includes monthly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, full medical benefits, and a rental discount.
