The dual-site structure also builds a skill set that transfers well: managing relationships across multiple communities, adapting your leasing approach by asset and resident profile, and staying organized under competing priorities are all things that carry weight in mid-size and large-portfolio management roles down the road.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing operates on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The entire community turns over in a compressed window once a year, delinquency pressure is constant because you're collecting from 18-to-22-year-olds with inconsistent income, and the leasing cycle runs against an academic calendar rather than market demand. The Assistant Community Manager role at Alight Laramie asks you to carry skills across three distinct areas simultaneously: financial controls, turn execution, and customer experience management. If any one of those wobbles, the whole property feels it.

On the financial side, you'll manage accounts receivable, enforce NSF and late fee policies, keep delinquency below 2% at month end, and assist with monthly close. The Entrata proficiency requirement matters here. Knowing your way around the ledger in a PMS isn't optional at this level. You're also posting damage charges from quarterly inspections and handling dispute resolution when residents push back, which they will.

The customer-facing work runs parallel. Weekly market surveys, managing concession budgets, monitoring Yelp and Google reviews, and working with the centralized sales team on occupancy goals. Laramie is a university town tied entirely to UW enrollment cycles, so traffic patterns and lease-up timelines are predictable but unforgiving if you miss the window.

The Turn Is Its Own Season

Annual turnover in student housing is a full operational sprint. This role takes an active hand in it, including physical tasks like moving furniture, assisting facilities with punch lists, and cleaning units. Scion uses Turnable to track the electronic turn board, and you'll be responsible for ensuring progress stays on pace, damage assessments are completed accurately, and final billing goes out correctly. Move-in, room assignments, transfers, and move-outs all process in a tight window. The General Manager leads this effort, and you're the second in command executing it.

It's worth noting that this role also requires you to step into the General Manager position when they're absent. That's a real expectation, not a formality buried in the job description.

What Makes This Role Work at Alight Laramie

Scion is a student housing operator with a clearly defined internal stack: Entrata, ClickUp, Lattice, Greenhouse, Qualtrics. Candidates who've worked across a purpose-built tech stack in student or conventional housing will move faster here than those learning the category from scratch. The one year of property management experience requirement is a floor, not a ceiling. Strong candidates typically bring familiarity with lease audits, resident account management, and at least one major turn season behind them.

The position includes a discretionary annual bonus, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. On-call responsibility is part of the schedule. That's standard for any community this size, but worth knowing before you apply.

  • 1+ year in property management or a residential living community
  • Proficiency in a property management system, Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with accounts receivable, delinquency tracking, and resident billing
  • Ability to cover General Manager responsibilities as needed
  • Eligible to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

The Assistant Community Manager position at Mezza Premier Apartments draws on three skill sets almost simultaneously: leasing, financial administration, and team leadership. On any given day, you might walk a prospect through a tour in the morning, spend the afternoon reviewing ledgers for billing accuracy, and close out the day de-escalating a resident concern before the office closes. That range is real, and it's what makes this role genuinely useful for building a well-rounded property management career.

Hawthorne Residential Partners ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally and has concentrated its portfolio in the Southeast, where they've developed a recognizable operational culture called "Live It." At Mezza Premier, that translates to an expectation that the assistant manager carries that culture into every resident interaction, not just during events but in routine conversations about renewals, payment plans, and maintenance follow-up.

What You'll Be Doing, Through a Skills Lens

Your leasing skills get used consistently here. You'll conduct tours, respond to incoming leads, guide applications through to completion, and actively support renewal efforts to protect occupancy. Social media content creation for the community is also part of the leasing function, used to drive traffic and highlight resident engagement.

On the financial side, you'll need to be comfortable with rent collection workflows, including payment posting and check scanning, as well as monitoring delinquency and making follow-up calls. Ledger reviews are a regular part of the job, and you'll assist with financial reporting that goes to both the Community Manager and regional leadership. Comfort reading a basic financial report and flagging discrepancies is genuinely useful here, not optional.

Leadership skill comes into play whenever the Community Manager is out. You step into that continuity role, keep the team moving, and maintain the resident experience without a gap. That expectation is baked into the position, which is part of why prior assistant manager experience is preferred alongside at least two years in property management overall.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months in an assistant community manager role preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus
  • Weekend availability required (Saturdays, 10 AM to 4 PM); schedule is 40 hours weekly with one weekday off

What Makes This Opportunity Specific to Hawthorne

Hawthorne's Career Path Program is a real differentiator for candidates thinking past this role. The assistant manager position is the standard entry point into the Community Manager track, and the company's Learning and Development team is structured to support that progression internally. If you've been in leasing or admin roles and want a defined path toward running your own community, that structure is already in place here.

Compensation for this role includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Jacksonville's multifamily market has seen continued demand pressure in the north corridor, where Mezza Premier sits near the I-295 beltway. Communities in that submarket compete on amenity presentation and resident retention as much as on rent, which makes the leasing and relationship-management skills in this role particularly relevant to day-to-day performance outcomes.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Aubrey, TX
job.description:
Maintenance technician roles at vertically integrated ownership groups tend to run differently than third-party fee management shops. When the same company owns and manages the asset, there's more accountability attached to every work order, every turn, and every curb appeal walk. Berkshire Residential Investments operates that way at Park 3Eighty in Aubrey, TX, and this technician position sits in the middle of that day-to-day physical operation.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're covering the full range of hands-on maintenance: plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and general building upkeep. Beyond work orders, you'll help maintain the shop, manage inventory, and keep equipment and key security organized. Curb appeal is treated as a real priority here, not an afterthought. You'll be expected to inspect the property regularly and flag issues before residents do. Supporting the management team on safety compliance and community standards is part of the job, as is delivering consistent, professional service to both current residents and prospects walking the property.

One year of residential maintenance experience is the baseline. You need a working knowledge across the trades, not necessarily a license in every one, but you can't be starting from scratch on appliances or basic plumbing when a resident's unit is down.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The technicians who do well in roles like this are the ones who treat a make-ready punch list the same way they treat an emergency call. Consistency matters more than occasional heroics. If you're the type who takes pride in a clean shop, tracks your parts inventory without being reminded, and communicates clearly with the office team without drama, you'll fit the culture. Berkshire puts weight on people skills alongside technical ability. Residents notice whether the tech who showed up was professional. That matters here.

The Bigger Picture

Berkshire Residential is a nationally operating ownership and management company, so technicians who grow into lead or make-ready roles have a real path toward maintenance supervisor and eventually service manager positions within the same organization. For someone early in their maintenance career, there's value in working for an owner-operator where your work has direct visibility to asset performance. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans.

Aubrey sits in the north DFW growth corridor, and the submarket has seen significant new construction over the past few years. That means residents in the area generally have options, and the quality of maintenance service plays a real role in retention. It's not background noise. It shows up in renewal rates.

job.title: Business Manager - Chevy Chase
job.description:
Full-site accountability in multifamily property management is one of the most complete skill sets this industry produces. A Business Manager touches every operational layer at once: financial performance, team development, resident experience, and physical asset condition. That breadth is both the challenge and the value of the role.

At Olympus Property's Chevy Chase community in Austin, TX, the Business Manager carries full operational responsibility for the property. This means owning the NOI story, not just tracking it. You'll build annual budget forecasts, analyze monthly performance against projections, and present strategies to Regional Leadership when the numbers need attention. Rents, occupancy, delinquency, expenditures, and vendor contract negotiations all fall within your scope. The financial side of this role requires someone who already reads a T-12 with confidence and understands how individual decisions ripple into asset performance over time.

What This Role Requires You to Bring

Olympus expects a minimum of two years of multifamily property management experience at the manager level. That baseline matters because this role doesn't have room for on-the-job orientation in fundamentals. You'll need to arrive knowing how to run a make-ready program, supervise maintenance staff, manage vendor bids, and keep units in market-ready condition without waiting for direction. RealPage, Knock, and Onesite experience is strongly preferred. The schedule is Monday through Friday with hours ranging between 8 AM and 6 PM, and flexibility for after-hours resident events or emergencies is part of the expectation.

  • Minimum 2 years of direct property manager experience in multifamily
  • Demonstrated ability to manage onsite teams across both office and maintenance functions
  • Experience with budget development, financial reporting, and variance analysis
  • RealPage/Onesite/Knock proficiency preferred
  • Comfort with leasing, renewals, and retention program oversight to protect occupancy
  • Vendor management experience, including bidding and contract negotiation

What This Role Builds

Strong Business Managers who spend two or three years in this seat often move into Regional Manager roles, and for good reason. Managing a full asset teaches you to think in terms of portfolio strategy, not just daily operations. You'll sharpen your ability to read the relationship between traffic, concessions, and occupancy trends, which is exactly the lens a regional needs. Olympus supports that progression directly through their Budget Camp and Leadership Conference programs, along with formal career pathing.

The candidates who perform best here tend to be the ones who treat inspection findings and punch lists with the same seriousness as a leasing call. Physical asset condition and financial performance aren't separate concerns. They compound each other, and the managers who recognize that early tend to outperform peers who treat maintenance oversight as a secondary responsibility. Compensation ranges from $75,000 to $85,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility layered on top. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Roofstock operates in the single-family rental space, and that context shapes this role in a meaningful way. Unlike a traditional multifamily technician who works one property with a maintenance supervisor down the hall, this position puts you across multiple homes throughout Columbia, managing your own schedule, your own truck, and your own judgment. The Columbia market has seen steady SFR (single-family rental) growth over the past several years, with a mix of older stock and newer acquisitions spread across suburban corridors. That variety means the work is rarely repetitive.

The pay range runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience and licensure, and HVAC Type II certification is required from day one. Universal certification is preferred and worth having if you want to handle a broader scope of refrigerant work without limitations. Plumbing and electrical repairs are also part of the daily routine, so this is a role for someone with genuine multi-trade competency, not a specialist who only turns wrenches on one system.

Make-readies are a core part of the workload. Between inspecting a vacant home, punching the list, coordinating with or auditing outside vendors, and getting a unit rent-ready, the job demands someone who can assess a property quickly and prioritize what actually needs to happen before a new resident moves in. Move-in and move-out inspections, along with onboarding audits for newly acquired properties, round out the scope. All of this gets managed through mobile apps in the field, so comfort with digital work order tools is a real requirement, not a minor preference.

One thing that stands out about this setup: no on-call, no weekends. For experienced technicians who've spent years on rotation, that's a significant quality-of-life shift. The company provides a vehicle and gas card, which removes the wear-and-tear cost that field roles often push onto the employee quietly.

Strong candidates for this role tend to be self-starters who can close out a full day of dispersed stops without losing track of details. Managing five or six different addresses in a day, each with its own condition and history, rewards people who document well and communicate clearly through their work order platform. The ability to spot deferred maintenance during an inspection and flag it accurately keeps small issues from becoming expensive problems for the owner.

What you'll need:
  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Hands-on experience with HVAC, plumbing, and electrical repairs
  • Comfort using mobile apps for work orders, communication, and documentation
  • Ability to work independently across multiple sites daily
  • Physical capability for the role: lifting up to 50 lbs, bending, climbing
  • High school diploma or GED
  • U.S. work authorization (no visa sponsorship available)

Employment is contingent on a background check. This is a full-time, field-based position in Columbia, SC.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Summer Oaks)
job.description:
What This Role Actually Demands

Maintenance work at an affordable housing community calls on a wider skill set than most job titles suggest. At Summer Oaks in Sonoma, you'll draw on genuine multi-trade competency every single day: electrical troubleshooting on appliances, circuits, and fixtures; plumbing repairs to water and sewage systems; rough and finish carpentry; and landscape and irrigation upkeep. These aren't siloed tasks handed off to specialists. You're expected to move across all of them, assess what's needed, and get it done to standard.

The role also carries a mentorship component. You'll coach and provide day-to-day oversight to Maintenance Groundskeeper staff, which means your communication skills matter almost as much as your technical ones. Clear, direct guidance to junior team members isn't a bonus trait here. It's a core part of the job.

On-call rotation is real and worth understanding upfront. You'll carry 24/7 emergency coverage for seven consecutive days at a time, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. If that kind of schedule disrupts your household, it's worth thinking through before you apply. If you're someone who handles that well and takes pride in being the person residents can count on at midnight, this structure suits you.

Day-to-Day Scope

A typical week will include some combination of the following:

  • Unit turns: painting, flooring, fixture installation, appliance hookups, and anything else needed to get a vacant unit rent-ready within established timeframes
  • Preventive maintenance rounds and work order documentation in the property management system
  • Landscape and irrigation checks to keep common areas clean, functional, and up to MidPen's standards
  • Contractor coordination: helping with bid processes, scheduling vendor work, and confirming it's completed correctly
  • Support for Community Manager on move-ins, move-outs, and annual inspections
  • Inventory management for tools, equipment, and supplies

The paperwork side of this role is real. Work orders, inspection logs, and procurement documentation all require accurate records. Basic computer proficiency isn't optional.

Doing This Work at MidPen

MidPen has operated affordable housing across Northern California since 1970 and manages more than 142 properties serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. That context shapes the culture of maintenance work here in a specific way: the people living in these units depend on well-maintained housing in ways that go beyond convenience. A leaking pipe or broken heater in an affordable community carries a different weight than it might at a market-rate property, and most MidPen maintenance staff will tell you they feel that difference.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the combination of trade depth and interpersonal steadiness. You can have excellent plumbing skills and still struggle here if you can't communicate calmly with a frustrated resident or give clear direction to a groundskeeper who's still learning. MidPen looks for technicians who bring both, and who are comfortable taking ownership without needing constant oversight from the Community Manager.

The pay range for this position runs $25.00 to $28.13 per hour based on experience, and the benefits package includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, and an EAP, among others.

job.title: Part Time Groundskeeper Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
Part-time groundskeeper roles at manufactured housing communities tend to get overlooked, but they carry real weight. An 81-home community lives and dies by its curb appeal and the condition of its common areas. At Mountain View Estates in Longmont, this is a 10-hour-per-week position, so the work is focused and the expectations are clear: show up, keep the property looking sharp, and flag problems before they become work orders.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your time will split between grounds maintenance and common area upkeep. That means operating mowers, trimmers, and blowers; inspecting and adjusting irrigation systems; and doing a morning walkthrough to catch anything that needs attention before residents notice it. The role also includes chainsaw work for larger limbs or debris, pool maintenance during season, and trash-out duties when abandoned items or bulk waste accumulate. You'll also handle interior common spaces: sweeping, scrubbing, disinfecting, keeping the leasing office and community rooms presentable. None of this is glamorous, but it's the kind of work that makes a manufactured housing community feel well-managed rather than neglected.

You'll operate with minimal supervision, which means you're expected to prioritize your time well within a short shift window. You'll report maintenance and safety issues to the on-site team rather than being responsible for repairs, but solid eyes matter here. Catching a leaking sprinkler valve or a parking lot hazard early keeps small problems from turning into capex headaches.

What IPG Is Looking For

  • At least one year of groundskeeping or maintenance experience at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more units
  • Comfortable and safe with power tools and mechanical equipment
  • Physically able to walk, lift, bend, and stay on your feet throughout a shift
  • Professional when interacting with residents and staff
  • Basic landscaping and light general maintenance knowledge is a plus

About Investment Property Group

IPG is a private investment and management firm based in Park City, Utah, with a portfolio that spans 150 properties across 13 states, covering multifamily, manufactured housing, and RV communities. The company puts weight on employee development and internal culture, and given the size of their operation, part-time roles like this one have a track record of becoming full-time when the right person is in them. The pay range for this position runs $20 to $24 per hour depending on experience and qualifications.

One honest note: manufactured housing communities have a different rhythm than conventional apartment properties. Residents often own their homes and have long tenure on-site, so the relationship between staff and community members tends to be more personal. Being consistent and approachable matters as much as the quality of the grounds work itself.

job.title: Maintenance Custodian
job.description:
It's 8:15 on a Tuesday morning. Someone tracked mud through the laundry room overnight, a light fixture in Hallway C is out, and the groundskeeper flagged a broken gate latch on the way in. That's a normal start. By afternoon, you've handled all three and moved on to the next punch list.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Paragon Properties is hiring a Maintenance Custodian for their Clinton Township community. This is a Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm position. No nights, no weekends, no on-call rotation. That's worth saying plainly, because a lot of maintenance roles come with after-hours obligations baked in. This one doesn't.

Day to day, you're keeping the property clean, safe, and functional. That means common area cleaning, trash removal, basic repairs, and light groundskeeping work as needed. You'll use hand and power tools, handle cleaning chemicals correctly, and stay on top of whatever the property throws at you without needing someone to tell you what to do next. Self-direction matters here. The property doesn't stop generating work, and the expectation is that you'll manage your time and tasks without constant supervision.

Pay runs up to $20 per hour depending on experience. Paragon also offers paid time off, nine company-paid holidays, medical, dental, and vision insurance with a short waiting period, company-paid life and disability coverage, a 401(k) with employer contribution, quarterly profit sharing, a rent discount, and an employee referral program. They run a hands-on training facility with weekly education courses, so if you're newer to property maintenance, there's a real structure in place to develop your skills.

What You Bring

  • Experience with cleaning and light maintenance tasks
  • Familiarity with cleaning chemicals, equipment, and proper handling
  • Comfort using basic hand tools and power tools
  • Reliable attendance and dependable transportation. A valid driver's license is recommended
  • Ability to work independently and stay productive without close supervision

Pre-employment requirements include a background check, drug screening, and a physical.

One thing that separates the people who do well in custodial and maintenance roles from those who burn out quickly: the willingness to take ownership of the small stuff. A scuff on the lobby wall or a full trash can by the mailboxes might seem minor, but residents notice them. The candidates who build a real career in property maintenance are the ones who see those details before anyone has to point them out. Paragon's investment in training and profit sharing suggests they're looking for people who want to grow in the work, not just punch a clock.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
This role puts your hands-on mechanical and electrical skills to work every day. You'll handle work orders, troubleshoot systems, prep vacant units for move-in, and keep the property running safely. If you're someone who reads a problem before reaching for tools, you'll fit the pace here.

What the Work Actually Involves

The core of this job is split between reactive and preventive work. On the reactive side, you're responding to resident maintenance requests and emergency calls, which means rotating on-call shifts are part of the deal. On the preventive side, you're doing monthly checks on safety systems, inspecting electrical wiring for code compliance, and catching equipment issues before they become bigger problems.

Make-ready work is also in scope. When a unit turns, you clean and prep it for the next resident, working through a punch list to get the space in move-in condition. That requires attention to detail and the ability to move efficiently through a unit without missing anything.

  • Diagnose and repair electrical, plumbing, and mechanical issues
  • Perform routine preventive maintenance on appliances and building systems
  • Inspect buildings and common areas regularly for safety and repair needs
  • Maintain organized inventory of tools, supplies, and parts
  • Participate in on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies
  • Clean and prepare vacated units for incoming residents

Skills That Matter Here

HVAC certification (or an equivalent credential like CMRP) is preferred, and electrical knowledge is genuinely important, not just a checkbox. You need to be able to look at wiring, identify what's off, and fix it correctly the first time. General mechanical aptitude covers the rest: fixtures, appliances, minor repairs across systems.

Physical requirements are real. You'll be on your feet for extended periods and lifting up to 70 pounds unassisted. Dexterity matters for detailed repair work. Communication matters too because you're relaying status updates to residents and coordinating with the team.

Doing This Work at Fairstead

Fairstead manages over 30,000 units across 28 states and focuses specifically on affordable housing. That matters for how you'll work day-to-day. The company operates with an integrated platform that includes development, construction, and property management, so maintenance technicians aren't siloed from the broader operation. They use data tools and tech systems to support field work, which means you're likely logging work orders and tracking repairs digitally rather than on paper.

One thing worth knowing: technicians who build strong diagnostic habits and get comfortable working across multiple systems (electrical, HVAC, plumbing) tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles over time. If that's a direction you want to grow, the scope of work here gives you the reps to get there.

job.title: Community Assistant Manager - Metro on Main
job.description:
The Assistant Community Manager role at Metro on Main, a CloudTen Residential property in Mesa, AZ, sits at a specific and valuable crossroads in a multifamily career: you're operational enough to run the day-to-day, but still close enough to a working Community Manager to absorb how decisions get made at the property level. CloudTen is explicit that this position is designed to prepare you for a CM seat. That's not boilerplate. The company manages a genuinely varied portfolio across the West, including hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects, so the growth path here has real breadth behind it.

What You'll Actually Do

Most of your days will involve the financial and administrative engine of the property. That means collecting and posting rent, reconciling bank accounts, preparing deposits, processing invoices, and generating weekly and monthly reports. You'll be the person who keeps the numbers clean and the records accurate in the property management system. On the leasing side, you'll handle inquiries, conduct tours, and support lease renewals and resident retention programs. You'll also conduct inspections of units, common areas, and grounds, manage move-in and move-out administration, and prepare security deposit dispositions in line with Arizona landlord-tenant law.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into that role. That's not ceremonial. It means you need to know delinquency procedures, how to serve non-payment notices, and when to initiate eviction coordination. You'll also support the on-site team in day-to-day challenges and help model the operational standards CloudTen holds across its portfolio.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of multifamily experience, ideally at a community of 300 or more units
  • Solid command of property management software and Microsoft Office
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and Arizona landlord-tenant law
  • Comfort with basic accounting principles and financial reporting cycles
  • Strong organizational habits and the ability to reprioritize when the day shifts
  • Communication skills that hold up across residents, vendors, and team members

Where This Role Takes You

The skills that compound fastest in an assistant manager role are the financial ones. Leasing coordinators learn traffic and closing ratios. Maintenance coordinators learn work order flow. But the AM who can read a T-12, track NOI trends, manage delinquency, and explain variances to ownership is the one who gets promoted to Community Manager with real confidence. This role gives you structured exposure to all of that, inside a company that manages complex assets across multiple markets. For someone two or three years into a multifamily career who wants to run their own property, this is a logical and well-supported next step. Pay runs $23 to $26 per hour depending on experience, and CloudTen offers health benefits, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Regional Service Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits above the property level but stays close to the work. You'll spend real time in the field: walking communities, reviewing make-ready quality, inspecting service team output, and coaching Service Managers across a Southern California portfolio. Monthly feedback to Operations Managers and the VP of Maintenance Services keeps you accountable to what you find.

On the capital side, you'll review scope, track timelines, approve progress payments, and sign off on completed projects. That requires staying in close contact with Community Managers and Service Managers so nothing stalls without a clear reason.

Vendor and contract management is a meaningful part of this job. You'll define scope, set service standards, and negotiate pricing with outside contractors. The goal is to reduce contractor reliance where your in-house teams can handle the work, and to control cost per unit across maintenance parts, supplies, turns, and exterior maintenance.

You'll also build the operational infrastructure: preventative maintenance programs, QAR standards, procurement processes, and a training calendar that hits each service team at least quarterly. Service Managers under your oversight will participate in 30-60-90 day forecasting with their Community Managers, and you'll set the standard for how that happens.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of multi-family housing experience, with a track record that includes managing maintenance operations across multiple sites
  • EPA Universal certification (or Type I and II) for refrigerant recycling, required before or at start
  • CPO certification and any other state or local credentials required for California operations
  • Hands-on technical ability in plumbing, electrical, and appliances. You need to troubleshoot alongside your teams, not just direct from a distance
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, and comfort with tools like Bluebeam for blueprint review or Smartsheet for project tracking
  • Strong communication skills. You'll be translating field-level problems into actionable information for operations leadership, and vice versa
  • Willingness to travel across the portfolio as the work requires

Context Worth Knowing

Griffis Residential operates a multi-community portfolio, and this position covers properties in the Anaheim and San Diego markets. Southern California's labor and contractor costs run high, which makes the cost-per-unit focus on this role genuinely consequential. A strong candidate here brings a track record of reducing vendor spend by building internal capability rather than just re-negotiating contracts. The difference between average and strong in this role often comes down to how well you can develop Service Managers. You're being asked to build competency across multiple teams simultaneously, so your ability to coach, identify skill gaps, and run effective field training matters as much as your own technical knowledge.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This Leasing Consultant role at Logan Property Management puts you at the front door of Peachtree, a residential community at 901 F Street in San Diego's East Village neighborhood. East Village has matured considerably over the past decade, shifting from a transitional corridor into one of downtown San Diego's more active rental submarkets. Foot traffic is real here, and so is competition from newer mid-rise product nearby. Your job is to convert that traffic into signed leases.

Day to day, that means touring prospective residents, following up on leads with purpose, and helping applicants move through the screening and approval process without losing momentum. You'll track your own numbers, understand where prospects drop off, and adjust accordingly. Beyond leasing, you'll stay close to current residents during their tenancy, handling renewal conversations and keeping occupancy where it needs to be. Good leasing consultants at conventional properties like this one also develop a feel for concessions, know when to offer them and when to hold firm, and understand how unit availability and traffic patterns shift week to week.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience in residential leasing or a customer-facing sales role
  • Comfort working with property management software for tracking leads and processing applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including timely follow-up
  • Ability to manage multiple prospects at different stages of the leasing funnel simultaneously
  • Weekend availability, since that's when most tours happen in any urban submarket

Who Logan Property Management Is

Logan was founded in 2002 and is woman and Latina-led, which is still uncommon in this industry and reflects a deliberate organizational identity. The company started in affordable housing and has since expanded into luxury and conventional properties across California, Colorado, Nevada, and Arizona, managing more than 3,500 units. That breadth matters: staff who grow with Logan often find opportunities to move between markets or property types, including affordable housing, which carries its own compliance and regulatory demands that can be genuinely career-building knowledge.

For a leasing consultant aiming to advance, this kind of multi-vertical operator offers a clearer path than a single-property owner would. Strong performers who build fluency in occupancy metrics, lead conversion, and resident retention are well-positioned to step into assistant manager or property manager roles. In a market like San Diego, where operating costs are high and owner expectations for NOI are tight, leasing performance gets noticed quickly.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
It's 9:05 AM and someone in the department just realized the conference room wasn't booked for the 10 o'clock. You fix it before they finish explaining the problem. That's the job.

What This Role Covers

Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Administrative Assistant to support a team in their Dallas office. This is a fully in-office, five-days-a-week position. The work is operational: keeping calendars organized, handling correspondence, maintaining filing systems, processing expense reports and invoices, ordering supplies, and making sure meetings actually happen without friction.

You'll also enter and maintain data in company systems, coordinate onboarding logistics for new team members, and draft or proofread memos and reports. Nothing on this list is glamorous. All of it matters. Lincoln operates one of the largest private commercial real estate portfolios in the country, and the administrative function is what keeps the department's day-to-day moving.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least two years of administrative or clerical experience (commercial real estate background is a plus)
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office, specifically Word, Excel, and Outlook
  • Good written communication skills and attention to detail
  • The ability to manage several tasks at once without being prompted on priorities
  • Current authorization to work in the U.S. (no visa sponsorship available)

The candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat follow-through as non-negotiable. Drafting a memo is straightforward. Making sure it reaches the right people, in the right format, on time, every time, is where the work actually lives. If you come from a background where you supported multiple people with competing deadlines and figured out the order yourself, that experience translates directly here.

Lincoln offers medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with traditional and Roth options, paid time off, company-paid life insurance and long-term disability, and an employee assistance program. Benefits eligibility and coverage details are provided during the hiring process.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Property management offices that run well don't do so by accident. Behind every smooth renewal season and every delinquency number that stays in check, there's usually a strong assistant manager holding the administrative and relational side of the operation together. That's the role Hawthorne Residential Partners is filling at Station Savannah Quarters in Pooler, GA.

Hawthorne sits in the top 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country, with a footprint concentrated in the Southeast. This position supports a functioning community, so you're walking into existing operations rather than a lease-up. The work is steady, recurring, and consequential.

The Day-to-Day

The job splits across three areas: leasing, financials, and team coverage. On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, convert leads, process applications, and push renewals to protect occupancy. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which at most properties means keeping it current and authentic rather than running a full content operation.

The financial piece is real work. You're posting payments, scanning checks, monitoring delinquency, making follow-up calls weekly, and coordinating with the Community Manager when accounts escalate toward eviction. Ledger accuracy falls to you. If a resident's account doesn't balance, you need to find out why and fix it. Regional leadership relies on clean reporting, and that starts here.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the office. That means prioritizing the team's daily work, handling resident concerns without backup, and keeping the operation moving. It won't be every week, but it will happen, and you need to be ready for it without treating it as a surprise.

The office is open Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4. You'll work one weekday off to stay at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can pull you outside those hours occasionally, which is worth knowing before you apply.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of assistant community manager experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP designation is a plus

The candidates who do well in this role aren't just good with people. They're comfortable reading a ledger, catching a billing error, and having a firm but respectful conversation with a resident who's past due. The resident relations side gets most of the attention in job descriptions like this one. The financial accountability is equally important and tends to be where underprepared candidates struggle.

Compensation includes an hourly base, monthly leasing and renewal commissions, and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers a formal career path program aimed at moving assistant managers into community manager roles, with structured learning and development support built in.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at The Melrose Apartments
job.description:
Leasing velocity in Nashville's multifamily market has tightened considerably, and properties that convert traffic efficiently are the ones hitting their occupancy targets. The Customer Experience Specialist at The Melrose Apartments is the frontline role that makes that conversion happen. Every prospect who walks in, calls, or texts is a potential lease, and how that interaction goes determines whether the community closes or loses that opportunity.

What the Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

This is a full-time leasing position with a schedule that includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for any community that wants to capture weekend traffic. You'll greet prospects, residents, and vendors when they enter the office, handle inbound inquiries across phone, email, and text, and maintain detailed records on every interaction. You'll also own the readiness of the tour path, which means daily walks through the vacant units, amenity spaces, and common areas to confirm everything meets Cottonwood's standards before a prospect sees it. A unit that shows poorly is a lease that doesn't close. That connection between physical product and leasing outcome is something you'll feel quickly in this role.

Cottonwood has been an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, so prospects may arrive having already toured on their own. Your job in those cases shifts toward follow-up, answering pricing questions, and moving them toward a decision. Knowing current availability, pricing, and any applicable concessions cold is essential. You can't convert a prospect who called three hours ago if you have to dig for that information.

Beyond leasing, you'll support community events and social media marketing, manage the package room daily, and maintain vendor communications. These tasks are real parts of the job, not afterthoughts.

What Cottonwood Is Looking For

  • Clear, prompt communication across phone, email, and text with zero dropped inquiries
  • A natural ability to build rapport quickly with prospects and residents at every interaction
  • Attention to the physical details that affect the showing experience and move-in quality
  • Comfort with technology, particularly self-guided tour platforms and digital communication tools
  • Flexibility to work a schedule that includes weekends and some evenings
  • An interest in growing toward a management track over time

Candidates who stand out in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat follow-up as a reflex, not a task. Responding to a prospect inquiry within minutes versus hours can be the difference between a signed lease and a lost unit. If you've worked in hospitality, retail, or any high-volume customer-facing environment and you've tracked your own performance metrics, that background translates well here.

The compensation package includes a competitive base plus a quarterly bonus structure, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits available within the first 30 days, generous 401k and HSA company matching, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at residential communities carry a lot more than a tool belt. They carry the daily experience of every resident who opens a leaky faucet, trips a breaker, or puts in a work order at 8 a.m. hoping someone actually shows up. At Trellis House, that person is you.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Berkshire Group owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground than they do at third-party management shops. As a Maintenance Technician here, you're not waiting on a chain of approvals to fix something. You're expected to take ownership of the property's physical condition and keep it there.

Day to day, that means working through service requests across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry, helping with make-readies between residents, keeping the shop organized, tracking inventory, and making sure the community looks sharp from the curb in. You'll also be a point of contact for residents when things go wrong, which means your customer service instincts matter just as much as your technical ones. The management team leans on maintenance staff heavily, and this role reflects that. You're supporting community standards, enforcing safety protocols, and contributing to how the property is perceived by people who live there and people considering it.

What You Bring to the Team

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or similar community setting
  • Working knowledge across the core trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep
  • Comfort with computers and work order systems
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills
  • The ability to shift between tasks without losing focus on quality or resident experience

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who treat a unit turn the same way they treat an emergency call: with attention and follow-through. A willingness to own your punch list, not just close it, makes a noticeable difference on a team like this one.

The Team and the Culture

Berkshire describes itself as people-first, and that framing extends to how they treat staff, not just residents. They offer three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance. The culture leans toward high performance without losing a sense of personality. That combination suits people who take their craft seriously but don't take themselves too seriously.

If you're looking to grow into a lead technician or maintenance supervisor role over time, the in-house ownership model gives you real exposure to how a well-run community operates. You'll learn how physical asset preservation connects to NOI, how curb appeal affects traffic, and how fast maintenance response affects renewal rates. That kind of context is harder to come by than most job postings let on.

job.title: Business Manager, Property Operations
job.description:
A regional portfolio manager flags a spike in delinquency across two Reno properties. You pull the T-12, cross-reference collections activity, and get on a call with site teams before noon. That's a typical Tuesday in this role.

What This Role Does

Asset Living, a third-party management firm ranked in the NMHC top 50, is hiring a Business Manager for Property Operations to support a regional portfolio in the Reno and Sparks markets. This is an operational and financial oversight position that sits between site-level teams and regional leadership. You're not running a single property. You're watching metrics across multiple sites and stepping in where execution gaps appear.

Day to day, the work covers a lot of ground. On the financial side, you track delinquency and collections, oversee invoice processing and PO-to-invoice matching, and monitor capex against approved budgets. On the compliance side, you coordinate lease enforcement, eviction workflows, and regulatory requirements at the federal, state, and local level. If tenant-based voucher programs are part of the portfolio, you handle the administration and compliance that comes with them.

Maintenance oversight is part of it too. You work with site teams to make sure work orders are moving, preventive maintenance is tracked, and resident satisfaction doesn't quietly erode while everyone's focused elsewhere. Retention workflows, renewal tracking, and escalation handling also land on this desk.

The role is hybrid with an estimated 5% travel for site visits and internal meetings.

What You'll Need

  • Minimum three years in multifamily property management, operations, or asset management
  • Hands-on experience with Yardi, RealPage, MRI, or a comparable property management platform
  • Solid understanding of financial management, leasing operations, and regulatory compliance
  • Comfort working across Microsoft Office and Google Workspace
  • Strong written and verbal communication; bilingual Spanish/English is preferred
  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Real Estate, or a related field is preferred

Candidates who stand out in roles like this tend to be equally comfortable reading a financial report and walking a maintenance punchlist. The skill that's hard to teach is knowing when a data trend signals an operational problem and acting before it compounds. If you've managed NOI recovery or delinquency reduction across a multi-site portfolio, that experience translates directly here.

job.title: Maintenance Technician- NOVO Broadway
job.description:
MG Properties has spent over three decades building a portfolio of apartment communities across the Western U.S., and their maintenance teams are a core reason their properties hold up. NOVO Broadway in Tempe is looking for a Maintenance Technician who can carry real weight across the full scope of day-to-day operations.

What You'll Actually Do

The work here covers the full cycle of apartment maintenance. You'll handle service requests across plumbing, electrical, and HVAC, perform appliance repairs, paint, and manage turns from punch list to completion. Grounds, common areas, and offices also fall under your care. On-call rotation is part of the job, which means occasional after-hours calls are a real expectation, not a footnote.

Turns are where a technician's skills become especially visible. A tight make-ready process directly affects occupancy, and a tech who can move efficiently through a unit while keeping quality high is genuinely valuable to any site team. If you can anticipate what a unit needs before the punch list is handed to you, you'll stand out here.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repairs
  • Reliable personal transportation
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • A customer service mindset that holds even when the work is stacking up

Where This Role Can Take You

Maintenance Technician is the foundation of every career path in property operations. Techs who build fluency across multiple trades and develop a track record of consistent, quality work tend to move into Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor roles, and from there, the path to Facilities Manager or Regional Maintenance Director is real and well-traveled at companies like MG Properties. The diagnostic and systems thinking you develop here also transfers cleanly into roles with vendors, capital projects, or third-party management operations.

MG Properties offers monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, holidays, paid sick time, and rental discounts. This is a full-benefits position with a regional operator that promotes from within.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Shorebreeze I, Shorebreeze II, San Veron Park)
job.description:
It's Monday morning and you're verifying income documents for a new lease while fielding a call about a work order that didn't get closed out. That's the pace. This role keeps three affordable communities running from the inside out.

MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable housing across Northern California since 1970. Their portfolio covers more than 142 properties housing working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. The Assistant Community Manager position supports daily operations across Shorebreeze I, Shorebreeze II, and San Veron Park in Mountain View, reporting directly to the Community Manager.

What the Work Involves

Compliance is a significant part of this role. MidPen operates tax credit and HUD-assisted communities, which means recertifications, TCAC reviews, and Management and Occupancy Reviews (MOR) are recurring responsibilities. You'll schedule income verification appointments, prepare and process lease agreements, and maintain the housing wait list. You'll also help process rent collections, security deposits, and bank deposits, and track petty cash.

On the facilities side, you'll coordinate maintenance inspections with facilities staff, track work orders, and conduct property walk-throughs to flag maintenance and security concerns. Turns get scheduled and monitored through turnover forms that you'll help prepare. You'll also issue notices, maintain resident and property files, and communicate emergency preparedness procedures to residents.

The role works closely with the Resident Services team and local partners, including law enforcement and emergency agencies. Resident relations is a genuine part of the job, including helping coordinate resident meetings.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED, plus at least one year of experience in residential property management, customer service, or an administrative role
  • Proficiency in MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Organized and detail-oriented, especially with file maintenance and compliance documentation
  • Able to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission in affordable housing

Pay ranges from $21.15 to $23.80 per hour based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, an employee education reimbursement program, EAP, pet insurance, and paid time off.

One thing worth knowing: the compliance load here is heavier than at a conventional market-rate property. Tax credit recertifications and HUD reviews require precision and consistency. Candidates who've worked in affordable housing before, or who have strong administrative experience with regulated documentation, will move faster up the learning curve than those coming strictly from conventional leasing backgrounds.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Cottonwood Bayview Apartments
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles at well-run residential communities share a common thread: the work is equal parts sales, service, and logistics, and the person who does it well holds the front door experience together. At Cottonwood Bayview Apartments in St. Petersburg, that role carries the title Customer Experience Specialist, which is an accurate name for what the job actually involves.

What the Role Covers Day to Day

You'll own the leasing floor experience from the moment someone walks in, calls, texts, or emails. That means greeting prospects and residents, responding to inquiries across every channel with accuracy and speed, and knowing the current availability and pricing well enough to answer any question a prospective renter might ask. You'll also inspect vacant apartments and the tour path daily to confirm everything is show-ready, which requires a trained eye for what "ready" actually means: clean, functional, and presentable against a defined standard.

Beyond direct leasing activity, the role pulls in some community operations work. That includes organizing the package room, supporting community events, assisting with social media marketing, and keeping vendor and community communications on track. These aren't afterthoughts. They're part of what keeps occupancy stable and resident satisfaction consistent.

The schedule is full-time and includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for leasing-facing roles. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any consumer-facing environment on a rotating schedule, that experience translates directly here.

Skills You Bring vs. Skills You Build

This role requires strong verbal and written communication, a genuine comfort with people, and an organized approach to daily tasks. You need to already know how to manage multiple priorities without letting the floor experience suffer. Those aren't trainable in the first 90 days.

What the role builds is different. You'll develop a practical understanding of leasing fundamentals: traffic management, pricing conversations, objection handling, and how a well-run leasing office moves prospects through to move-in. Cottonwood also positions this as an entry point into property management, so if your goal is an assistant manager or eventually a property manager track, this is a legitimate starting point rather than a ceiling.

One Thing Worth Knowing About This Operator

Cottonwood Residential was an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, which means the leasing process here is more tech-integrated than at many conventional operators. Prospects may tour without a leasing agent present, which shifts some of the relationship-building to before and after the tour rather than during it. Strong follow-up and responsive communication become even more important in that model. If you're comfortable with digital tools and understand that the leasing conversation doesn't always happen in person, you'll fit the workflow well.

  • Full-time position with weekend and evening availability required
  • Quarterly bonus structure in addition to base pay
  • Health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within 30 days
  • 401k and HSA with company match
  • Three weeks of paid time off in the first year, plus 10.5 paid holidays
  • Defined path toward future management roles

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The assistant community manager role exists at the intersection of operations and resident experience. You're the person who keeps things moving when the community manager is pulled elsewhere, and the one who spots financial or leasing problems before they compound. At a multifamily property in Davenport, Waypoint Management Services is filling that seat now.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll work alongside the community manager on daily operations, but you'll own a real slice of the workload independently. That means tracking delinquency, supporting the eviction process when it gets there, and making sure rent collection doesn't slip. You'll monitor the make-ready schedule, keep the rent roll accurate, and flag renewal risk early enough to act on it.

On the leasing side, you'll support the leasing team's performance and training, help execute marketing strategies, and stay current on what competitors are doing with pricing and concessions. When occupancy trends shift, you're expected to bring data and a recommendation, not just a problem.

Weekend availability is required. This is a community-facing role, and the schedule reflects that.

What You'll Bring

  • At least two years in leasing, sales, or a hospitality role with transferable skills
  • Solid financial literacy: you're comfortable reading reports, tracking variances, and explaining what you see
  • Strong organizational habits and attention to detail in recordkeeping
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a real advantage here
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The candidates who stand out at this level already understand that leasing numbers and financial performance are connected. If you've worked renewals strategy or helped a team hit occupancy goals during a slow season, that experience carries weight in this interview.

Waypoint offers a compensation package that includes monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, 120 hours of PTO in year one, a 401k with company match, and commuter and referral benefits.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians at affordable housing communities carry a different kind of weight than their counterparts at Class A lease-ups. Residents depend on their homes in a deeper way, and the person who shows up to fix a leaking pipe or a faulty breaker isn't just a service vendor. They're part of why the community functions. Fairstead understands that, and it shapes how they operate their portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-scope technician role at a Fairstead property in Mobile, Alabama. Your day will move between scheduled work and the unexpected. Preventative maintenance inspections, make-ready prep on vacated units, electrical checks, safety system walkthroughs, and inventory management fill the structured parts of your week. The less predictable parts come from residents: an HVAC issue in August heat, a tripped breaker, a safety concern that can't wait. You'll be part of the on-call rotation, which means some calls come after hours. That's the honest reality of this work, and it's worth knowing upfront.

Fairstead runs an integrated platform where development, construction, and property management sit under one roof. That structure matters for technicians because decisions move faster and the maintenance team isn't an afterthought. You're working within a system that treats physical asset quality as a core part of the mission, not a cost center to minimize.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or similar setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems, enough to diagnose problems and handle minor repairs safely
  • General mechanical skills covering plumbing, appliances, fixtures, and building systems
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential (preferred but not a hard stop)
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds unassisted and stay on your feet for extended shifts
  • Clear communication, both with residents who may be frustrated and with a team that depends on accurate handoffs

Attention to detail separates solid technicians from great ones in affordable housing specifically. A punch list item skipped during a make-ready creates problems for a new resident on day one. A missed safety check creates liability. The candidates who do well here are methodical, not just skilled.

The Team and the Bigger Picture

Fairstead describes itself as purpose-driven, and the affordable housing space does attract people who care about more than square footage and cap rates. That doesn't mean the work is easy or the pace is slow. It means the stakes feel real. Residents in these communities aren't choosing to live elsewhere for lifestyle reasons. Keeping their homes functional and safe is straightforward mission-critical work.

Benefits include employer-contributed medical through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company matching (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. There's also a flexible spending account, disability coverage, pet insurance, and employee discount programs.

For a technician who wants room to grow, Fairstead's scale means there's a real path toward senior technician, maintenance supervisor, or facilities management roles across a large multi-state portfolio. The company's tech-forward approach also means exposure to digital work order systems and data-driven operations that build skills transferable well beyond any single property.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Weinstein Properties is offering a $1,500 sign-on bonus for an EPA-certified Maintenance Technician at 3Sixty Flats in Grand Prairie, TX. The pay range runs $24 to $27 per hour, and the on-call structure is worth understanding before you apply: $150 per week guaranteed whether calls come in or not, plus an additional $150 for holiday coverage. That's real money built into the compensation model, not just a vague promise of overtime.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm, with rotating emergency on-call shared across the team. Day-to-day work covers the full range of residential maintenance: HVAC troubleshooting and repair (EPA Type II or Universal required), plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and support with turns and make-readies. You'll also help keep the community grounds, amenities, and pool areas in shape. Weinstein owns and manages its properties in-house, which matters practically. There's no third-party management layer, so decisions move faster and maintenance standards stay consistent across the portfolio.

Three years of apartment or residential maintenance experience is the baseline here. This role calls for someone who can independently diagnose a complex issue and resolve it without needing a supervisor to walk through each step. The customer service dimension is real too. Residents are in their homes, and how a technician communicates and follows through shapes renewal decisions as much as leasing does.

What the role is looking for

  • EPA Certification, Type II or Universal
  • At least 3 years of hands-on apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • Proven ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • Comfort with work order systems and mobile tools
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work outdoors year-round
  • Valid transportation and clean background check

From a career development standpoint, technicians who build this kind of multi-trade competency at a stable, owner-operated property tend to have a clear path forward. Lead Technician and Maintenance Supervisor roles at Weinstein or elsewhere become realistic targets within a few years, particularly for those who develop strong vendor coordination skills and start thinking about the cost side of maintenance decisions. Capex planning, unit turn efficiency, and reducing delinquency-driven damage claims are all things that property managers lean on their maintenance leads to help with. The skills you build in a role like this compound directly into leadership eligibility.

Benefits include rent discount, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, an employee assistance program, and a referral bonus program. Quarterly performance bonuses run up to $980 based on property and team metrics. Sign-on bonus specifics are discussed during the interview process.

job.title: Regional Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This Regional Property Manager role sits at the intersection of student housing operations, financial oversight, and sales strategy across a portfolio of properties in the San Antonio and Austin markets. You're the connective tissue between corporate directives and on-site execution. That means regular property visits to assess curb appeal, maintenance operations, capital improvements, and brand consistency, plus the financial discipline to run monthly variance calls, review delinquency trends, and guide General Managers through budget season. When occupancy softens or closing ratios slip, you're the one building the strategy to correct it, not just flagging the problem.

The turn process in student housing is unlike anything in conventional multifamily. You're coordinating mass move-outs and move-ins within a compressed window, often measured in days rather than weeks. Strong candidates have managed this at scale before and understand what it takes to keep a team focused when the calendar is unforgiving.

On the revenue side, you'll work alongside a Regional Revenue Manager on weekly leasing strategy calls, analyzing traffic, closing ratios, and unit mix configurations to hit targeted occupancy and revenue goals for each sales year. You'll also evaluate renewal incentives, new resident concessions, and premium structures as part of the annual revenue plan. The sales component here is more analytical than most regional roles in conventional PM.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of properties at the regional level, ideally in student housing or lease-up environments with compressed leasing cycles
  • Fluency in financial reporting: variance analysis, capex oversight, delinquency management, and budget development alongside General Managers
  • Experience coaching and developing on-site teams, including holding managers accountable to leasing goals and operational standards
  • Comfort working with leasing intelligence platforms and market data to shape strategy, not just review it
  • Ability to be physically present at properties in the San Antonio and Austin area on a regular basis, with availability for emergency coverage when site leadership gaps arise
  • Eligibility to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Where This Role Leads

Regional Manager is one of the most skill-compounding roles in property management. You're developing fluency in asset-level finance, revenue management, people operations, and vendor negotiation simultaneously. Managers who perform well in this seat typically move toward Regional Vice President roles or into director-level positions overseeing larger portfolios or specific operational verticals. In student housing specifically, the analytical rigor around leasing cycles, rate setting, and revenue planning translates well to conventional multifamily, build-to-rent portfolios, and even asset management functions. The skill set you build here travels.

Scion operates as one of the larger student housing platforms in North America, which means you're working within a system that has actual infrastructure: dedicated revenue management support, training and talent development resources, and capital teams you can consult on major expenditures. For a regional manager, that kind of institutional support makes a meaningful difference in what you can actually deliver for your communities.

job.title: Full-Time Concierge (Mon-Fri 4pm-12am)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is an evening shift role, Monday through Friday, 4pm to midnight, at a Class A residential community in Rockville managed by Comstock. The hours matter: you're the face of the building during the time residents are actually home. That means handling a steady stream of arriving residents, guests, and deliveries, coordinating amenity reservations, managing the loading dock and elevator scheduling, and keeping the lobby looking the part throughout the night. You'll field phone calls, respond to resident concerns, and make judgment calls about building access every single shift.

Daily building walks are part of the rhythm. You're flagging maintenance items, straightening common areas, and doing the small things that keep a Class A property feeling like one. The work is more active than a typical front desk job, and the pace picks up around dinner hours when foot traffic peaks.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year in a concierge or high-end customer service role, preferably in residential property, hospitality, or a similarly guest-facing environment
  • Comfortable working with Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when the schedule requires it
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, and the instinct to handle difficult situations with composure
  • Trustworthy and accountable, two qualities that matter especially when you're working largely unsupervised on an evening shift

Context Worth Knowing

Rockville's mixed-use residential market has grown considerably with Comstock's development around the Shady Grove and Rockville Pike corridors. Residents in these communities tend to have high expectations and many options. The concierge position at this tier of property carries real weight: a confident, polished evening presence directly influences how residents feel about where they live, which connects to renewals and retention in ways that don't always show up on a punch list but absolutely show up in NOI over time.

For candidates with hospitality backgrounds looking to move into property management, this role builds the resident relations instincts that carry well into leasing or property management coordinator positions. Comstock's expanding portfolio also means internal mobility is a realistic path, not just a line in a job posting.

Compensation ranges from $18 to $21 per hour, with bonus potential and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, housing discount, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, and parental leave.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the operational center of a residential property in Waukee, Iowa. You're not just fixing things. You're building and running a maintenance operation. Day to day, that means overseeing HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems, keeping preventative maintenance schedules on track, and making sure turns and make-readies get completed to standard. Curb appeal, common areas, and unit condition all fall under your watch. You'll also carry a budget, which means purchasing supplies thoughtfully and keeping costs aligned with what the property can sustain.

Team leadership is a real part of this job. You'll train technicians, give feedback, assign work orders, and set the standard for quality on-site. BAM Companies operates across multiple properties, so the culture and work ethic you build on your team will reflect directly on the brand.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of hands-on property maintenance experience. Prior supervisory experience is a plus but not required if you have the technical depth and leadership instincts.
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification. This is a hard requirement for handling refrigerants legally and correctly.
  • Practical working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, and electrical. You should be able to diagnose, not just report.
  • A valid driver's license and reliable vehicle.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills. You'll be coordinating with residents, vendors, and property management, so communication gaps cost time and trust.

Where This Role Develops You

Maintenance Supervisors who perform well in multi-site or growing management companies tend to move toward Regional Maintenance Director roles, where they oversee technical standards and capital planning across a portfolio. The skills this role builds specifically, budget management, team development, preventative maintenance programming, and vendor coordination, are exactly what those next-level roles require. If you've been a strong technician looking to step up, this is the position where you make that transition credible.

One thing worth knowing about Waukee: it's one of the faster-growing suburbs in the Des Moines metro, which means the apartment market there sees consistent lease-up activity and steady occupancy demand. For a maintenance supervisor, that translates to a real volume of work orders and turns, which is genuinely good for skill development but does require someone who can manage a pace that doesn't always slow down.

Pay for this position runs between $27 and $32 per hour depending on experience, and BAM offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage alongside a substantial paid time off package and housing discounts at BAM properties.

job.title: Sr. Regional Real Estate Manager - Pacific Northwest Region
job.description:
Where This Role Lives in the Organization

Regional property management at this level is fundamentally a relationship-management discipline dressed in operational clothing. The financials matter, the inspections matter, the compliance matters. But what separates a strong senior regional manager from a capable one is how well they hold together a web of people: site teams spread across a market, clients with real money and real expectations, and a corporate leadership team that needs accurate information to make good decisions. CloudTen Residential is looking for someone who understands that dynamic and thrives inside it.

CloudTen manages a genuinely varied multifamily portfolio across the West, and their Portland metro group reflects that variety. Hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, value-add repositioning plays.
