Each of those asset types carries different operational rhythms, different resident profiles, and different client expectations around performance. The person in this role needs to be comfortable context-switching between a lease-up where traffic and concessions dominate the weekly conversation and a stabilized asset where NOI discipline and delinquency management take center stage.

What the Work Actually Involves

This is a senior leadership position overseeing multiple properties and the managers who run them day-to-day. You're not the person solving a broken HVAC unit at 7am. You're the person who built the team that handles it, coached the manager who escalates it correctly, and reviews the capex line to know whether that unit should be repaired or replaced. The work is a mix of people development, financial oversight, client communication, and strategic planning, and all four have to move together.

Day-to-day, you'll be reviewing monthly financials across the portfolio, preparing and monitoring budgets, and catching variances before they become problems. You'll conduct property inspections with an eye toward operational consistency, not just curb appeal. You'll carry relationships with existing clients and help develop new ones, which means being fluent in how a T-12 tells a story and how to present a repositioning plan that earns trust.

On the people side, you'll provide direct mentorship and oversight to regional managers, assistant regional managers, district and area managers, and property administrators. That's a meaningful leadership span. Performance evaluations, sensitive personnel situations, recruitment, team culture. It all lands here.

Key qualifications CloudTen is looking for:

  • At least five years of directly relevant multifamily experience, ideally at the regional or multi-site level
  • Strong financial acumen, specifically around property financial reports, budget preparation, and income and expense analysis
  • An active real estate license (preferred)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Word and Excel in particular
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; college degree or related coursework is a plus

What tends to separate strong candidates here is the combination of financial sharpness and people instincts. Plenty of regional managers can read a T-12. Fewer can walk into a site that's underperforming, figure out quickly whether the problem is operational, personnel, or market-driven, and then build a credible path forward with the site team rather than around them. That's the skill set CloudTen is hiring for.

The role carries a compensation range of $145,000 to $160,000 depending on experience, structured as a combination of base pay and expected supplemental wages. A hybrid work model is in place, alongside medical, dental, and vision benefits, FSA options, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Cortland Duluth
job.description:
Cortland operates one of the larger vertically integrated multifamily platforms in the country, which means their maintenance staff works inside a system that actually has infrastructure behind it: in-house design and construction teams, standardized processes, and a portfolio-wide approach to asset preservation. For a technician who wants more than just a work order queue, that context matters.

The Duluth property is a community-level role, but the work touches everything. On any given day you might be diagnosing an HVAC issue in one unit, responding to a plumbing call in another, checking that automatic entry doors and surveillance systems are functioning properly, and wrapping up a punch list item from a recent turn. Preventative maintenance on HVAC equipment is a real part of the job here, not an afterthought, which tends to reduce emergency call volume over time for technicians who stay on top of it. You'll also manage parts inventory and document completed work, which sounds administrative but directly supports the property's ability to close work orders fast and keep residents satisfied.

EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) is required before you start. Cortland is also looking for candidates with at least one to three years of hands-on experience across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair. On-call rotation is part of this position, so reliability during off-hours is genuinely expected, not just listed as a formality.

What strong candidates bring

  • EPA Universal certification (preferred over Type I or II alone)
  • Demonstrated HVAC diagnostic and repair skills, not just filter changes
  • Experience managing a personal work order queue across multiple unit types
  • Comfort communicating with residents directly, professionally, and with patience
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Physical readiness for ladder work, outdoor conditions, and lifting

From a career development standpoint, this kind of role inside a top-10 multifamily operator builds a foundation that transfers well. Technicians who develop strong diagnostic depth and learn to work within a standardized PM system often move into lead technician or maintenance supervisor roles within a few years. At a company of Cortland's scale, that path exists in-house. The combination of preventative maintenance discipline, resident-facing service, and asset documentation you'll build here shows up on a resume in ways that generalist handyman experience doesn't.

If you want a role where the technical work is real, the support structure is established, and the company has enough scale to offer a genuine next step, this position in Duluth is worth a close look.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

Student housing runs on relationship velocity. At 18-Seventy Nine in Huntsville, Texas, the Experience Team Member role pulls on three skill sets simultaneously: sales instincts, community marketing, and front-line operations. If you're strong in all three, this position keeps you fully engaged. If you're building toward a leasing career, it's one of the better training grounds available in the student housing sector.

Scion operates in a niche that moves faster than conventional multifamily. Lease-up timelines are compressed, Turn periods are intense, and the resident base turns over on academic calendars rather than month-to-month rhythms. That context shapes everything this role touches.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Your primary function is converting prospect interest into signed leases. That means conducting tours, fielding objections, and feeding useful intelligence back to the management team about what's working and what's not in the sales process. You're not just executing a script; you're expected to identify local marketing angles and pass those recommendations up the chain.

The role also carries real administrative weight. Package management, maintenance coordination, office organization, and after-hours lockout coverage are all part of the job. In student housing, after-hours calls are a genuine part of the rotation, and Turn periods, when hundreds of residents move out and back in within days, demand a level of operational stamina that most traditional leasing roles never require.

Social media and community engagement sit in this role as well. Promoting events, supporting leasing initiatives, and maintaining a professional presence both inside and outside the office are expectations, not occasional tasks.

What Makes Someone Good at This

  • A customer-first instinct that holds up under pressure, not just during slow office hours
  • Adaptability when priorities shift quickly, which they will around renewal campaigns and Turn
  • Clear, confident communication across a diverse resident population
  • Availability during summers, holidays, and Turn periods specifically
  • Self-direction without needing constant supervision to stay productive

Strong candidates in this role tend to be people who treat the sales conversation as information gathering, not just pitch delivery. Understanding why a prospect hesitates, then translating that into actionable feedback, is the kind of contribution that gets noticed in a Scion community. The skills built here, including leasing fundamentals, resident engagement, and operational coordination, carry directly into assistant manager and property manager tracks within student housing and conventional multifamily alike.

Work authorization in the United States is required. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

job.title: Maintenance Technician III
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

A Maintenance Technician III at Hawthorne Residential Partners is expected to bring a full toolkit to the job, literally and figuratively. The technical depth required here goes well beyond basic work order completion. EPA/HVAC certification is required, and hands-on experience across electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair is expected from day one. Three or more years in apartment maintenance or a comparable skilled trade is the baseline. What sets this level apart from a Tech II is the leadership component: you're the person junior techs look to when a diagnosis gets complicated or a make-ready is behind schedule.

CPO certification and a valid driver's license are also required, which signals that pool maintenance and on-site mobility are genuine parts of this job, not incidentals. If you've spent time in apartment maintenance specifically, you already know that the difference between a tight turn and a delayed move-in often comes down to how fast and accurately the maintenance team works through a punch list. That's the pace and precision this role operates at.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The core of this position runs across three areas: repairs and preventative maintenance, building and grounds upkeep, and team mentorship. On the technical side, you'll diagnose and resolve complex service requests, prep vacant units to make-ready status per Hawthorne's standards, and execute scheduled preventative maintenance tasks. Grounds and common areas are part of the daily routine as well, including keeping the shop organized well enough that supply inventory can be assessed at a glance.

The leadership piece is real. Hawthorne expects Tech IIIs to train and mentor the maintenance team, which means your communication skills matter as much as your ability to swap out a compressor or trace an electrical fault. On-call rotation is part of the schedule, with standard hours running Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, and after-hours emergency coverage shared across the team on a rotation basis.

What Makes Hawthorne Worth Considering

Hawthorne Residential Partners has built a career path program across its portfolio, and the Tech III designation is positioned explicitly as a stepping stone toward a Maintenance Supervisor role. That's a meaningful distinction in property management, where upward mobility in the maintenance track often goes unacknowledged. The company backs that commitment with an education reimbursement program and a dedicated learning and development team.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Benefits include free dental insurance, medical and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Candidates who tend to thrive at this level combine technical credibility with the patience to coach. Knowing how to fix things gets you in the door. Knowing how to show someone else how to fix things, without taking over, is what moves you up the ladder at a company like Hawthorne.

job.title: Market Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Metromark Apartments in Jamaica Plain keeps you moving. On a typical day, you're working through a queue of resident maintenance requests: an appliance acting up, a smoke detector that needs installing, a light fixture coming down. Then a flooded unit calls and everything reshuffles. That rhythm, planned work interrupted by real urgency, is just part of the job, and the right person handles both without losing composure.

Beyond reactive repairs, you'll handle the cosmetic side of the building too. Painting, screen swaps, window replacements, door hardware, tiles, handrails. These aren't glamorous tasks, but they're the ones residents notice. A well-kept property holds its occupancy, and your attention to the small stuff directly contributes to that. You'll also coordinate with outside contractors and vendors when the scope goes beyond your tools, tracking paperwork and invoices along the way so nothing falls through the cracks.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That on-call piece is worth taking seriously when you're considering this role. It doesn't dominate your life, but it does require you to be reachable and ready when something urgent comes up.

What You Bring

  • At least six months of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems
  • Comfort making repairs to doors, locks, tiles, handrails, and similar building components
  • An eye for safety concerns and a habit of flagging them proactively
  • Ability to manage contractor interactions and keep basic records organized
  • Specialized trade background in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing is a genuine advantage, not just a nice-to-have

What separates the candidates who thrive in a role like this from the ones who struggle: it's usually temperament more than technical skill. Residents notice how you show up at their door just as much as whether you fixed the problem. Someone who communicates clearly, stays calm under pressure, and takes visible pride in the spaces they maintain tends to build real trust with both the property team and the people living there.

The Company Behind the Role

John M. Corcoran and Company has been operating in New England real estate since 1951. For a firm that size, they've held onto a notably team-oriented culture, the kind where people tend to stay for years rather than treat it as a stepping stone. Compensation for this position runs from $26.50 to $29.50 per hour depending on experience, and the role comes with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off with holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match.

For someone early in a maintenance career, this is a solid environment to build breadth. Working across appliance repair, cosmetic updates, and light mechanical systems at a residential property gives you exposure to the full scope of a make-ready cycle and day-to-day operations. That kind of experience, especially paired with any specialized trade training, positions you well to move toward a lead technician or maintenance supervisor role over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Magnolia, TX
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 a.m. for a leaking faucet. By noon, you've handled that, flagged a tripped GFCI in another unit, restocked the shop, and walked the grounds to catch anything that hurts curb appeal before a prospect tour. That's a normal morning at Park at Magnolia.

What This Role Covers

Berkshire Residential Investments manages and owns its own communities, which means maintenance isn't an afterthought. As a Maintenance Technician at Park at Magnolia in Magnolia, TX, you work directly alongside property management to keep the community in strong physical shape. That means completing service requests across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry. It means supporting make-ready turns so units are clean, functional, and move-in ready on schedule. It means enforcing safety standards, controlling inventory, securing equipment, and making sure the property presents well every single day.

You'll also handle shop organization and key security, assist with maintaining company equipment, and serve as a visible, friendly presence for residents and prospective renters. Customer interaction is part of the job, so communication matters as much as technical skill.

What Berkshire Looks For

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge of appliances, plumbing, electrical systems, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Comfort using computers and property management software or related tools
  • A reliable, self-directed approach: you notice problems before they become work orders

The technicians who stand out here aren't just technically solid. They take ownership of the property's condition as if it were their own. Curb appeal, resident satisfaction, and unit quality aren't separate concerns; they're all the same job.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and competitive benefits. The company operates with an in-house ownership model, so decisions move faster and investment in the physical asset stays consistent. For a maintenance professional looking to build skills across multiple systems without the chaos of a third-party management structure, that kind of stability matters.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Affordable housing management carries a compliance burden that standard market-rate work doesn't. When you're operating under HUD's 4350.3 Handbook, LIHTC rules, and REAC review cycles, the administrative side of property management becomes just as demanding as the resident-facing side. This role sits at that intersection.

Fairstead owns and operates more than 30,000 apartment units across 28 states, with a focus on affordable housing. Their Baltimore property needs an Assistant Community Manager to support day-to-day operations, keep compliance on track, and handle the resident relations work that keeps a community functioning.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical week pulls in several directions at once. You're processing rent collections and posting payments in Yardi, running down arrears, and making sure deposits hit on schedule. You're supporting annual and interim recertifications, flagging EIV discrepancies, and keeping documentation ready for MOR audits or investor site reviews. When a resident has a service request, a complaint, or a lease question, you're the person bridging them to either the maintenance team or the property manager.

On the compliance side, you'll track lease violations, document issues properly, and coordinate with Fairstead's in-house legal team when eviction proceedings are necessary. You'll also help prepare the property for REAC inspections, which means staying ahead of EHS violations rather than scrambling when a review gets scheduled.

Salary for this position ranges from $29 to $31.25 per hour, based on experience and qualifications.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management (not just conventional)
  • Hands-on familiarity with EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Working knowledge of HUD compliance requirements and recertification processes
  • Solid written and verbal communication, especially for resident-facing situations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite

The candidates who do well in affordable housing assistant manager roles tend to be detail-oriented under pressure and comfortable switching between financial tasks and people-facing work in the same afternoon. Recertification errors and missed compliance deadlines have real consequences here. If you've worked in market-rate only, the learning curve on the regulatory side is steeper than it looks on paper.

For candidates who want to grow, this role builds a skill set that translates directly to community manager positions at affordable or mixed-income properties, as well as compliance specialist roles within larger ownership platforms.

job.title: Leasing Professional - Multi site - Wedekind, Patton, and Linden Apartments
job.description:
A prospective resident calls about a one-bedroom at Wedekind while you're finishing a move-in walkthrough at Linden. You wrap the walkthrough, flag a punch list item for maintenance, then head to Patton for an afternoon showing. That's the shape of a normal day in this role.

What This Role Actually Involves

CloudTen Residential manages a varied portfolio across the West, and this multi-site leasing position covers three of their Reno, NV communities: Wedekind, Patton, and Linden Apartments. You'll rotate between locations based on traffic and team needs, which means you genuinely need to be comfortable working independently and transitioning quickly between different site cultures, staff dynamics, and resident populations.

The core of the work is leasing: answering calls, conducting tours, handling objections, securing deposits, and following up with undecided prospects. But this isn't a single-property role where you can rely on a tight-knit on-site team to catch things you miss. You'll process applications, prepare and execute lease paperwork, assist with move-in and move-out inspections, and field maintenance requests at whichever property you're covering. When you're on-site, you're also keeping an eye out for anything that affects curb appeal or resident safety and flagging it accordingly.

CloudTen pays between $19.00 and $21.00 per hour depending on experience, and leasing bonuses are available at your assigned properties. A valid driver's license in good standing is required since you'll be traveling between sites regularly.

Who Fits Well Here

Strong candidates for a multi-site leasing role tend to have sharper organizational habits than their single-property peers. You're managing relationships across three communities simultaneously, which means things fall through the cracks if you're not disciplined about follow-up and documentation. Lease-up experience is a real advantage here because it builds the kind of sales fluency and urgency that multi-site work rewards.

Here's what CloudTen is specifically looking for:

  • 1 to 2 years of leasing or property management experience, with lease-up background strongly preferred
  • At least 2 years of sales experience in any context
  • Familiarity with OneSite or Entrata property management software
  • Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Valid driver's license in good standing
  • Comfort with Fair Housing regulations and related compliance requirements

The self-sufficiency piece matters more than it might on a larger, fully staffed property. You'll sometimes be the only CloudTen representative a resident interacts with for days at a stretch. The ability to project warmth, professionalism, and competence without needing a manager nearby is genuinely useful here.

One thing worth knowing: multi-site leasing roles like this one are solid stepping stones toward a Community Manager position, especially for candidates who build relationships across multiple teams and demonstrate they can manage the operational details at each property, not just the leasing side. Getting exposure to different communities, asset classes, and management styles in a condensed period tends to accelerate that path.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a luxury apartment community runs on a specific set of skills, and this role at Griffis Residential in Portland puts most of them to work daily. HVAC diagnosis, plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, appliance work, carpentry for make-readies , the technical range here is broad. If you've built competency across those trades in a multi-family setting, this is a position where that depth pays off.

The Technical Scope

Make-ready work sits at the center of this role. Getting a unit turn-ready means running through the full punch list: plumbing fixtures, HVAC function, appliance condition, electrical, and finish carpentry. The standard matters because Griffis operates luxury communities, and residents moving into a Class A apartment expect everything to work correctly on day one.

Beyond turns, you'll respond to resident service requests with a 30-minute response window for emergency repairs. That kind of expectation requires solid diagnostic instincts, not just technical knowledge. You also help develop and execute preventative maintenance schedules, which means you're not just reacting , you're working ahead of problems before they affect occupancy or NOI.

Pool and spa maintenance is part of the job as well. Griffis requires a Certified Pool Operator (CPO) license and EPA certification within your first six months if you don't already hold them. Community inspections, grounds upkeep, and seasonal tasks like snow and ice removal round out the physical demands of the position.

Skills That Translate

Strong candidates in this kind of role carry a few qualities that go beyond trade knowledge. Accurate record-keeping on pool chemistry, maintenance logs, and inventory keeps the Service Manager informed and supports compliance with OSHA, EPA, and local codes. Basic computer skills matter here , most work orders run through property management software. The ability to work independently across a mix of scheduled and unscheduled tasks, and communicate clearly with residents when things go sideways, separates technicians who advance from those who stay static.

Multi-family maintenance experience is the preferred background. If you've worked in hospitality or a comparable facilities role, the mechanical skills often transfer, but the lease-driven urgency of turns and the resident communication component have their own learning curve.

Working at Griffis Residential

The pay range runs $25 to $28 per hour. The benefits package is detailed and includes a 50% rental discount, a quarterly bonus program tied to online reputation and occupancy metrics (up to $2,000 annually), 401(k) with up to 4% company match, three weeks of PTO starting immediately, 11 paid holidays, paid parental leave, and tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year. An associate referral bonus, wellness reimbursement, and an EAP round things out.

Bilingual English/Spanish candidates are particularly well-positioned given the communication demands of resident-facing maintenance work in a diverse metro like Portland.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Minimum one year of experience in multi-family, hospitality, or a related field
  • CPO license and EPA certification preferred; required within first six months
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general carpentry
  • Ability to lift up to 75 pounds and work in varying outdoor conditions
  • Basic computer proficiency; bilingual Spanish a plus

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you in the field across a residential portfolio, owning work orders from receipt to close-out. That means diagnosing the issue, sourcing materials within budget, executing the repair, and documenting everything cleanly. Lessen operates at significant scale, completing millions of work orders annually across a large vendor and technician network, so the expectation is that you work independently and move efficiently without sacrificing quality. The company has made a deliberate call to prioritize quality over volume, which means you're evaluated on how well you resolve issues, not just how many tickets you close.

You'll manage your own budget per work order, coordinate with clients when needed, and be the person on-site who represents the standard. A fleet vehicle and fuel card are provided, so your territory is workable without out-of-pocket logistics headaches.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a related trade. This is a firm threshold, not a suggestion.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and repair across multiple trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, appliances, or similar.
  • Comfort managing budgets at the work order level and making sound material decisions in the field.
  • A solution-first mindset. When something unexpected comes up mid-repair, you adapt rather than escalate every decision.
  • Clean documentation habits. Lessen's platform is tech-driven, so your notes and work order updates are part of the product.

What This Role Builds

Lessen has a defined path from Field Technician into Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager roles. If you want to stay technical, that's a valid track. If you want to move into supervising other techs or managing a regional territory, the infrastructure is there. The company is expanding nationally, so early technicians in a given market tend to be well-positioned when leadership roles open locally.

The skills you'll sharpen here, specifically budget management at the work order level and multi-trade diagnostics across a diverse portfolio, translate directly into more senior maintenance operations roles at either a third-party management company or an in-house maintenance department. Technicians who get fluent in work order platforms and client communication tend to advance faster in this industry than those who are purely skilled with tools but less comfortable with the administrative side of the craft.

The schedule runs weekdays with no on-call rotation, which is a meaningful quality-of-life distinction in a trade where after-hours and weekend emergency calls are the norm at most companies. The role also includes a monthly tool and cell phone allowance, OSHA training, and a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Mountain Trail
job.description:
A prospect walks in off the street on a Tuesday afternoon, having driven past three other communities on their way to yours. They're tired, a little skeptical, and carrying a mental checklist they haven't fully articulated yet. What happens in the next twenty minutes at Mountain Trail determines whether Olympus earns a signed lease or loses that person to a competitor down the road.

That moment is the core of the Leasing Consultant role. You're the first real impression of the property, and your ability to read a prospect, present the right unit, and guide someone from curious to committed is what drives occupancy. Olympus Property, a three-time National Apartment Association Top Employer (2023, 2024, and 2025), places this role at the center of community performance for good reason.

What the Work Actually Involves

Day to day, you'll show apartment homes, explain the differences between floor plans and finishes, prepare lease paperwork, coordinate move-in details, and keep prospect and resident data current in the property's database. You'll greet vendors, current residents, and walk-in traffic with the same level of professionalism. You'll also help plan and participate in resident events, which means some of your schedule will extend into evenings on a monthly basis.

Beyond the leasing floor, you'll visit local businesses and apartment locators to build referral relationships and drive traffic back to the property. Administrative work is part of the job too. Responding to resident concerns, maintaining organized records, and supporting your team's broader sales goals are all in scope.

This is a full-time position with rotating weekday hours between 9 AM and 6 PM. Weekend availability is required.

What You Need to Bring, and What You'll Build

Olympus requires at least one year of experience as an apartment leasing consultant, or meaningful time in a customer-facing sales role such as hospitality, retail, or restaurant work. The underlying skills are transferable: reading people quickly, handling objections without being defensive, and staying organized when traffic picks up and multiple prospects need your attention simultaneously.

What this role builds, over time, is something more specific to property management. You'll develop fluency in lease structure and move-in processes, sharpen your ability to translate a property's physical features into lifestyle value for different kinds of renters, and learn to track your own performance against occupancy and traffic metrics. Leasing consultants who develop that analytical awareness, connecting their daily activity to the property's overall occupancy health, tend to advance into assistant management roles faster than those who treat leasing as purely a sales function.

  • Minimum one year of leasing or customer-facing sales experience
  • Comfort working weekends and occasional evening resident events
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage administrative tasks alongside active prospect interaction
  • Genuine interest in helping people find the right home, not just closing a transaction

Compensation runs $18 to $22 per hour depending on experience, with monthly leasing commissions and resident renewal bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, educational assistance and tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, pet insurance, and paid time off, among others.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Role at a Glance

Copper Beech San Marcos is a student housing community, and this Assistant Community Manager position sits right at the center of daily operations. You'll report to the General Manager and carry real operational weight: financials, leasing, resident accounts, staff coordination, and facilities oversight all fall within your scope. When the GM is out, you run the property.

Student housing has its own rhythm. The annual turn is the defining operational moment, delinquency targets are tight, and the resident base turns over on an academic calendar. If you've worked conventional multifamily, the fundamentals transfer, but the pace and the population are different.

What the Work Looks Like

A typical week involves auditing resident accounts, posting charges from quarterly inspections, coordinating move-in and move-out processes, and tracking delinquency to keep it under 2% by month end. You'll handle month-end reporting, manage accounts receivable, and enforce late fee and NSF policies consistently.

On the leasing side, you'll run weekly market surveys, manage concession budgets, and monitor KPIs to flag trends before they become problems. You'll also lead or support resident engagement efforts and handle escalated concerns directly.

Facilities oversight is part of the job too. You'll conduct monthly inspections of vacant units and bed spaces, walk common areas and amenities, coordinate work orders, and hold the standard on curb appeal and building condition.

Staff development rounds it out. You'll coach team members, help manage the on-call schedule, and make sure everyone on site stays current with Fair Housing requirements and company policy.

  • 1+ years of experience in property management or residential communities
  • Proficiency in a property management system, Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail in account management and financial reporting
  • Ability to step into the GM role when needed
  • Flexibility for non-traditional hours during peak periods and emergencies

Where This Role Can Go

AGM and Assistant Community Manager roles in student housing tend to move into General Manager positions relatively quickly, especially at operators that own or manage multiple assets. Scion operates at scale across North America, so internal movement into GM roles or regional support functions is a realistic next step for someone who performs well here. Strong candidates will already understand basic financial reporting and won't need to be coached on why delinquency control matters to NOI.

job.title: Home Base Supervisor
job.description:
What the Role Actually Covers

The Home Base Supervisor title is Prometheus's version of a regional administrative supervisor, and the scope is wider than that label suggests. You're overseeing administrative operations across multiple properties in the Cupertino area, which means your day pulls in several directions at once. In the morning you might be auditing move-in documentation for compliance with fair housing standards. By midday you could be reviewing delinquency reports, coaching a Home Base Coordinator through a tricky application verification, or coordinating with accounting on a neighbor billing issue. The afternoon might bring a performance conversation with a team member or a call with an attorney on an eviction in progress.

That rhythm is the job. You're not a pure leasing role, and you're not a pure people manager. You're the operational anchor connecting on-site teams, the Home Base Director, and cross-functional departments including property management, neighborhood operations, and accounting. Prometheus refers to their residents as "Neighbors" and their properties as "Neighborhoods," and that framing reflects a genuine cultural orientation toward community rather than just occupancy. You'll feel that difference in how complaints are handled and how documentation expectations are set.

Travel between properties is part of the position, so candidates local to Silicon Valley who know the geography of a dense, competitive rental market will settle in faster.

What You Bring to This Role

  • At least three years of property management experience, with a minimum of two years in a supervisory capacity
  • Working knowledge of housing rental laws, fair housing compliance, and lease documentation standards
  • Comfort with delinquency management, move-in/move-out auditing, and rental agreement processes
  • Experience interviewing, training, and evaluating administrative staff
  • Strong written and verbal communication across departments and with residents
  • High school diploma or GED required; a bachelor's degree is preferred

Prometheus explicitly recruits across industries, so a background that includes strong customer service or bookkeeping alongside property management experience is genuinely valued here, not just tolerated.

What This Role Builds

Supervisors in multi-property administrative roles develop a specific kind of operational fluency that's hard to get elsewhere: the ability to maintain consistency across sites without direct, daily presence at each one. You'll sharpen your documentation auditing skills, build judgment around fair housing compliance under real conditions, and develop a management style that works across a dispersed team. Those are exactly the competencies that translate into regional manager and director-level roles in property management.

Prometheus is a B Corporation and the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with a portfolio exceeding 13,000 units. The scale means you're operating within real organizational infrastructure, including in-house acquisitions, development, and value-add renovation teams. That cross-departmental exposure is genuinely unusual at this level and gives you visibility into how a vertically integrated ownership group makes decisions, which sharpens your instincts well beyond what a third-party management role typically offers.

job.title: Portfolio Maintenance Specialist
job.description:
Portfolio-level maintenance roles like this one don't come up often. Most maintenance positions are site-specific. This one puts you across an entire multi-state portfolio, which means the scope of problems you'll see in a single month would take a site tech years to accumulate.

What This Role Actually Involves

BAM Companies, an Indianapolis-based multi-family operator founded in 2010, is looking for a roving maintenance specialist to cover properties across Indiana, Iowa, Missouri, Arkansas, and Pennsylvania. The travel requirement is real: expect 50 to 75 percent of your time on the road, reporting directly to whatever site needs you most that week. Some weeks that's a turn push where the local team is underwater. Other weeks it's a mechanical issue the on-site tech hasn't been able to crack, or a capex project that needs a competent set of hands overseeing execution.

The core of the job is technical diagnosis and hands-on repair across HVAC, electrical, plumbing, appliance systems, carpentry, and general structural work. EPA Type 2 or Universal certification is required. CPO is preferred. You're also doing quality assurance on completed turns and service requests, running roving inspections, and helping maintain portfolio-wide preventive maintenance schedules. There's a mentorship component too: you'll be working alongside on-site supervisors and techs, offering field coaching and sharing best practices. No direct reports, but functional leadership is part of the job.

Who Performs Well in This Role

The candidates who thrive here share a specific profile. They've got 4 to 7 years of multi-family maintenance behind them, they're comfortable with ambiguity, and they don't need someone to hand them a punch list every morning. The ability to walk onto an unfamiliar property, assess what's backlogged, and prioritize effectively without a lot of hand-holding is genuinely the differentiator. Strong communicators who can work with regional leadership and still maintain credibility with on-site techs tend to do well. People who need a fixed routine and a single home base tend to wash out quickly.

Worth being direct about the physical side: this is an active role. Lifting over 75 pounds, working in mechanical rooms, crawl spaces, and outdoor environments across multiple climates. It's Monday through Friday with occasional weekend travel depending on operational needs. A reliable personal vehicle capable of hauling tools across the region is a requirement, not a suggestion.

The Bigger Picture

A role like this builds a resume in ways that site-level positions rarely do. Exposure to multiple property types, varying operational conditions, and different regional markets compresses experience significantly. Maintenance professionals who've done portfolio-level work are consistently more competitive for Regional Maintenance Coordinator and Director of Facilities roles. If that trajectory matters to you, this is a reasonable path toward it.

  • Minimum 4 to 7 years of hands-on multi-family maintenance experience
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification required
  • CPO certification preferred
  • Valid driver's license and reliable vehicle for regional travel
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Ability to work autonomously across multiple sites with shifting priorities

BAM offers PTO starting at 90 days, comprehensive healthcare with meaningful company contribution, complimentary life insurance, and access to a continuing education platform. The company culture is employee-forward, which they take seriously enough to have built a recognizable internal identity around it.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

The Assistant Community Manager role at Waypoint Management Services in Palm Bay draws on a specific combination of skills that don't always show up together: financial literacy, leasing instincts, and people management, all running simultaneously. You'll be reading delinquency reports and coaching a leasing consultant in the same morning. That breadth is what makes this role genuinely useful for someone building toward a community manager seat.

On the financial side, you'll support rent collection, track delinquencies, help manage eviction workflows, and monitor overall financial performance. You'll also be contributing to pricing recommendations based on market surveys and occupancy trends. That's real NOI awareness, not just data entry. Over time, this kind of exposure to a property's full financial picture is exactly what separates candidates who get promoted from those who stay in support roles indefinitely.

The leasing dimension here goes beyond just showing units. You'll support team performance and training, help execute marketing strategies, track renewals, and stay current on competitor activity. If you've come from a pure leasing background, this role builds the operational and administrative fluency that most leasing consultants never develop on their own. Yardi experience is preferred, and proficiency there compounds quickly once you're touching lease records, rent rolls, and make-ready schedules regularly.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Weekend availability is part of this role, which reflects the reality of multifamily. Prospects tour on Saturdays. Residents have concerns on Sunday mornings. Waypoint is upfront about that expectation, and it's worth factoring honestly into your decision.

On a typical weekday, you might start by reviewing the delinquency report, follow up with the Community Manager on a make-ready timeline, respond to resident concerns, and then shift into supporting the leasing team on a slow traffic afternoon. Administrative accuracy matters here: lease files, occupancy reports, and renewal tracking all require consistent attention. The job asks you to hold multiple operational threads without dropping them.

Where This Role Can Take You

Waypoint offers monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, a 401k with company match, an employee housing discount, and 120 hours of PTO in the first year with progressive increases. There's also a professional development program, which signals that internal growth is something the company actually invests in rather than just mentions.

For candidates who treat this role as a training ground, the path forward is clear. Community managers at most multifamily operators are expected to own the full P&L, manage a team, and make pricing calls independently. The assistant manager role, done well, is where all of those skills are built. Two years of strong performance here, with demonstrated financial awareness and leasing results, puts you in a competitive position for a community manager role at nearly any operator in the market.

If you have at least two years in leasing, sales, or hospitality and you're ready to move into something with more operational depth, this is a reasonable next step. Candidates who thrive here tend to be detail-oriented without being rigid, comfortable with numbers, and genuinely good at managing relationships with both residents and team members at the same time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential community means something different every single day. One morning you're turning an apartment after a move-out, tracking down a mystery plumbing leak by afternoon, and getting called on a work order before you've finished your punch list. That's the job at Bedford Commons and Heathermoor, two Berkshire Residential communities looking for a Maintenance Technician who can keep up with that pace without losing their composure.

What You'll Actually Do

You'll own the physical condition of the property. That covers everything from appliance repairs, plumbing, and electrical work to carpentry and general building maintenance. Curb appeal matters here. If something looks off on a walk of the grounds, you're the person who notices it and handles it. You'll manage the shop, keep inventory organized, and maintain key security. You'll also be working alongside management to make sure community standards stay where they need to be, including safety compliance. Residents interact with you directly, so your customer service approach carries real weight for how people feel about living here.

Honestly, the hardest part of this role isn't the technical work. It's the volume and variety. Requests pile up. Priorities shift. You'll need to work through a full plate without letting things slip, and that requires both solid trade skills and decent organizational habits.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with computers and property management or work order software
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • HVAC certification is preferred, but Berkshire will consider candidates without it

What separates a strong candidate here isn't just technical range. It's the ability to interact with residents during frustrating moments (a broken A/C in summer, a leak that damaged their belongings) and still leave them feeling like someone actually cared. That combination of trade competence and calm, genuine customer service is rarer than most postings acknowledge.

A Few Other Details

This position includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, paid out after 90 days of employment. Berkshire also offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and health insurance. They manage their own portfolio rather than operating as a third-party management company, which tends to mean more consistent standards and fewer surprises when it comes to budget approvals for repairs and capex work. That's a practical difference you'll feel when you're trying to get something fixed the right way.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This role lives at the intersection of sales, communication, and organization. The Leasing Manager at Redstone Residential spends a significant portion of each day talking to prospects, guiding tours, and following up through phone and email. Closing a lease requires reading people quickly, handling objections calmly, and keeping the process moving. If you're sharp on customer service and comfortable with digital tools, you'll find a lot of this work familiar from day one.

Redstone uses Entrata as its leasing platform, so comfort with property management software matters. You'll also work across Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and social and online marketing channels to support traffic generation and SEO. These aren't back-office tasks. They're part of how the community hits its leasing numbers each month.

What You'll Manage Day to Day

The Leasing Manager reports to and supports the Community Manager, but this isn't a purely support role. You'll help run daily leasing operations, which includes prospect tours, lead follow-up, and renewal outreach. You'll track resident ledgers to confirm balances are accurate. You'll contribute to marketing efforts, both online and on-site, with the goal of hitting weekly and monthly occupancy targets.

You'll also play a role in staff motivation and team culture. Student and conventional housing communities move fast, especially around lease-up periods, and keeping the team focused during high-traffic weeks is part of the job. Resident satisfaction sits alongside leasing performance as a shared priority.

  • Conduct tours and manage prospect communications across phone, email, and digital channels
  • Execute renewal campaigns to maintain occupancy
  • Monitor and maintain resident ledgers for accuracy
  • Support social media and online marketing as directed
  • Contribute to a positive team and resident experience

Working at Redstone

Redstone manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a portfolio that spans student housing and conventional multifamily. That scale means systems are built out, processes are defined, and there's real infrastructure behind the work. For a Leasing Manager, that translates to better tools, clearer expectations, and more career runway than you'd find at a smaller operator.

One honest note: student housing communities have concentrated leasing seasons, and the pace during peak periods is real. Candidates who handle high-volume traffic well and stay organized under pressure tend to do well here. The compensation for this role is $19.00 per hour, full-time non-exempt, with a benefits package that includes health, vision, and dental insurance, a 401K with up to 6% matching, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, and paid parental leave.

The position is based in Provo, Utah, which is home to Redstone's headquarters and puts you close to the company's core operations.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Fairstead operates at a scale most affordable housing owners don't reach: over 30,000 apartments across 28 states, with development, construction, and property management handled under one roof. That integration matters for this role. When you're the Service Manager on a Fairstead property in North Las Vegas, you're not waiting on a separate corporate maintenance department to weigh in. The platform moves, and you move with it.

The job is what the title says. You'll supervise maintenance staff, keep mechanical and electrical systems running, and make sure the property stays clean, safe, and code-compliant. Special projects will pull you into a lead role. Routine work you'll often handle independently. Complex repairs may bring in additional support, but the expectation is that you know your trade well enough to direct the work even when you're not swinging the wrench yourself.

A few things worth saying plainly: overtime happens. Emergencies don't care about your schedule, and on an affordable housing property, deferred maintenance creates real consequences for real residents. The paperwork side is real too. Fairstead uses Yardi and RealPage to track work orders and maintenance activity, so comfort with those platforms (or a willingness to get there fast) matters. Microsoft Office proficiency is a baseline expectation, not an afterthought.

What separates the candidates who thrive here from those who struggle is usually supervision, not technical skill. Knowing how to do the work is table stakes. Knowing how to lead a small crew, set priorities under pressure, and hold quality standards on a punch list without micromanaging every turn is harder and rarer. If you've made the shift from skilled tradesperson to someone who also manages people and process, this role fits that experience.

What you'll need

  • At least three years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Trade proficiency in at least one area (HVAC, electrical, plumbing) with solid general maintenance skills across the board
  • Real understanding of safety protocols and accident prevention, not just checkbox familiarity
  • Experience supervising or leading maintenance staff
  • Comfort with work order systems; Yardi or RealPage experience is a plus
  • Organization skills strong enough to manage multiple open work orders and project timelines at once

The pay range runs $23 to $25 per hour depending on experience and skill set. Benefits include employer-subsidized medical coverage through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. There's also a flexible spending account, pet insurance, disability coverage, and employee discount programs on appliances and apparel.

Fairstead's affordable housing model puts genuine pressure on operational efficiency. NOI discipline matters, capex decisions get scrutinized, and the residents depending on these properties don't have easy alternatives if maintenance falls behind. That's not a reason to avoid the role. It's a reason to take it seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - The Hixon
job.description:
Maintenance Technician roles at mid-size regional operators like CloudTen tend to be broader in scope than those at large institutional portfolios. You're not handed a narrow specialty. You handle the full range of unit and common-area work, and that variety is exactly what builds a well-rounded skill set over time.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The Hixon is a CloudTen property in Bend, Oregon, and this role supports the day-to-day physical condition of the community. That means handling general repairs across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and appliances, along with keeping common areas, pools, laundry rooms, and grounds in good shape. A significant part of the rhythm here is turns: getting vacant units rent-ready within a 3-to-5-day window. That timeline requires coordination, prioritization, and the ability to move through a punch list efficiently without cutting corners on quality.

Resident service requests carry a 24-hour resolution expectation, which keeps the workload structured but fast-moving. On-call emergency coverage is part of the role, so schedule flexibility matters. The position also involves preventive maintenance work, documented inspections covering fire safety, life-safety systems, lighting, and pool equipment, and an ongoing familiarity with utility shutoffs and safety protocols across the property.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • At least one to two years of hands-on experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • Valid driver's license in good standing (travel between assigned properties is part of the role)
  • Comfort using a mobile device and basic computer tools for work orders and communication
  • Ability to work weekends, evenings, and holidays, including after-hours emergency response
  • Strong attention to detail and the discipline to work independently without close supervision

Where This Role Leads

Technicians who build proficiency across multiple trades and develop a track record for fast, quality turns are the ones who move into Maintenance Supervisor positions. CloudTen's portfolio spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects, which means there's genuine variety in the types of properties and challenges you'd encounter over time. Exposure to that range, especially early in a maintenance career, compounds well. The diagnostic thinking you sharpen on HVAC and plumbing carries directly into more complex systems work at larger or higher-classification properties down the road.

Pay for this role runs $25.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a flexible spending account, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospect just submitted an inquiry at 9 PM. By the time they tour Saturday morning, they've already heard from two competitors. How you handle that 18-hour window is what separates a signed lease from a lost lead.

PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant at their Austin community. This is a front-line sales role, and it's structured that way intentionally. You're the first real human impression most prospects get, and the work asks you to hold that standard across every touchpoint, from the first phone call to the moment someone hands over a deposit.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your core job is converting leads into signed leases. That means working phone, email, and in-person traffic with equal energy, running tours that actually identify what a prospect needs rather than just walking the floor plan, and following up in a way that feels personal rather than scripted. You'll track your own leads in a CRM (Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or similar) and you're expected to keep that data clean and current. Market knowledge matters here too: pricing, availability, and what competitors are doing all factor into how you guide a prospect toward a decision.

Beyond leasing, you'll support the operational rhythm of the office. That includes collecting deposits, processing lease paperwork accurately, maintaining model readiness, and helping during turn season when move-outs and move-ins stack up quickly. It's not glamorous work, but it directly affects how prospects experience the community on tour days.

Who Fits Here

  • At least one year of sales or leasing experience with a track record of hitting conversion targets
  • Real comfort with CRM systems and consistent multi-touch follow-up habits (calls, texts, emails, not just one and done)
  • Availability to work weekends and during peak leasing hours
  • A genuine ability to read people quickly and adjust your approach by prospect

The strongest candidates in roles like this tend to be the ones who treat follow-up as a discipline rather than a chore. Conversion rates in leasing often hinge less on the tour itself and more on what happens in the 24 to 72 hours after. If you've built systems for that, even informal ones, you'll move faster here than someone who relies on natural charisma alone.

This role is commission-eligible, and PeakMade offers housing discounts, a 401(k) match, wellness programs, and development opportunities within their growing portfolio. Austin's rental market stays competitive, which means strong leasing consultants here get real reps at a high volume and tend to build a resume that translates well into full-time leasing, assistant manager, or even property manager tracks down the road.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - McCullers Walk
job.description:
Maintenance techs at institutional operators like AIR Communities work differently than at your typical third-party managed community. The work order volume is real, the technology is actually used, and the expectation is that you're moving through your queue efficiently, not waiting on parts or hunting down tools. McCullers Walk in Raleigh is that kind of operation.

The Work

Day to day, you're handling the full range of residential maintenance: troubleshooting plumbing, swapping out electrical components, servicing HVAC equipment, and keeping appliances running. Turns are part of the rhythm here too. AIR runs a structured make-ready process, so when a unit comes back, you're following a defined punch list to get it move-in ready, not improvising your way through it. Some days you're completing resident service requests back to back. Others you're assisting with vendor quality checks or doing move-out inspections. The mix shifts with the season and the community's needs.

On-call rotation is real and worth knowing upfront. You'll cover at least one week per month and need reliable transportation to respond to after-hours calls. That's the nature of residential maintenance, and it's baked into the schedule expectations here.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Comfortable with physical demands, including moving heavy equipment
  • Flexible availability including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Someone who fixes things correctly the first time and doesn't leave callbacks behind

Compensation and Growth

The pay range runs $20 to $22 per hour based on your actual skill set, plus a monthly customer service bonus of up to $250 for techs who consistently deliver solid resident experiences. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a meaningful benefit if you want to live onsite and cut your commute to zero.

AIR promotes internally whenever possible and has a formal maintenance development program called Ascend that's built around your individual path, not a generic training checklist. Techs who come in sharp at two trades and show an appetite for learning often move into lead or service manager roles within a few years. That's a reasonable trajectory at a portfolio this size.

What separates a strong candidate here from a competent one is comfort with technology-driven dispatching. AIR uses digital tools to prioritize and assign work orders, so if you're used to paper logs and verbal hand-offs, there's a learning curve. Techs who adapt quickly to that workflow tend to carry higher resident satisfaction scores, which is where that monthly bonus actually gets paid out.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Skills That Run This Role

This position draws on a specific combination of hands-on trade knowledge and people management. You're coordinating maintenance staff, setting the tone for how work gets done, and stepping in personally when a task demands it. Organizational thinking matters here as much as technical ability. A maintenance team that's poorly scheduled or poorly supervised creates friction for residents and for the property management team above you. Strong candidates tend to be people who've worked their way up through maintenance roles and understand both sides of that equation: what it's like to be on the tools, and what it takes to manage others who are.

Safety awareness runs through everything in this job. Fairstead has specific safety policies and standards, and the expectation is that you'll model and enforce those consistently, not just reference them when something goes wrong. If you have OSHA familiarity or have managed safety compliance in a previous maintenance role, that translates well here.

What the Day-to-Day Involves

You'll oversee the repair and maintenance of residential buildings, inspect and address electrical and mechanical systems, and keep facilities clean and functional in line with company standards. That includes leading special projects and stepping into a supervisory role on any work that requires coordination across your team. For more routine tasks, you'll often work independently. For complex projects, there's support available, but the expectation is that you're managing the workflow and the people, not waiting to be directed.

  • Supervise and coordinate maintenance staff on daily tasks and special projects
  • Perform skilled maintenance and repair work across mechanical, electrical, and general building systems
  • Ensure all facilities meet Fairstead's cleanliness and safety standards
  • Apply and improve internal maintenance policies and procedures
  • Use Yardi or RealPage for work order tracking (familiarity preferred)
  • Be available occasionally for overtime tied to emergencies or project demands

Three years of property maintenance experience is the baseline. Beyond that, Fairstead is looking for someone who's proficient in at least one specific trade and can hold their own across general maintenance disciplines. Microsoft Office proficiency is expected for reporting and communication purposes.

Working Within Fairstead's Structure

Fairstead manages over 30,000 units across 28 states with an integrated platform that connects ownership, construction, and property management. That integration matters for this role because decisions don't happen in isolation. A maintenance issue that looks like a simple repair might connect to a capital improvement project already in the pipeline. Understanding how to communicate upward, flag concerns clearly, and coordinate with a broader team is part of what makes someone effective here, not just technically capable.

Affordable housing maintenance comes with its own realities. Residents often depend heavily on working systems in ways that market-rate tenants may not, and response time carries more weight. The strongest candidates for this role aren't just skilled with tools. They understand that the work connects directly to people's daily lives, and they manage their team with that in mind.

Fairstead's benefits package includes employer-contributed medical insurance, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%), 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and an FSA option among others.

job.title: Leasing Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role lives at the front end of the revenue funnel. Your job is converting traffic into signed leases at Dream St. Augustine, a community in St. Augustine, FL backed by DLP Capital. Lead response time is a firm 4-hour window, which means your mornings can shift fast depending on overnight inquiries. Tours, follow-ups, CRM updates, and closing conversations fill most of the day. Lease-up experience is required here, not preferred. The expectation is that you already understand how to build occupancy from a cold start and keep it moving.

Beyond the leasing floor, you'll build genuine referral pipelines by networking with major employers, hospitals, and universities in the area. St. Augustine draws a mix of healthcare workers, hospitality industry professionals, and university staff, giving you real targets to build cross-promotion relationships with. Weekly prospecting is a formal expectation, not a nice-to-have. You'll also create and run resident programs that support retention, because keeping a current resident costs far less than filling a vacancy.

Property walks are part of the routine. You're not just selling the community on tour; you're watching it the way a prospect would see it. Punch list items that slip through affect close rates, and you'll be expected to flag them. CRM discipline matters here too. Guest cards, follow-ups, and lease paperwork need to stay current because leadership visibility into your pipeline depends on it.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated lease-up experience (this is a hard requirement)
  • Strong customer service background with a track record of closing
  • Comfort reading income statements and basic financial documents
  • Excellent written and verbal communication across all levels, including senior leadership
  • Experience managing on-site projects and leading through change
  • Familiarity with Appfolio, G-Suite, and Microsoft Office (a plus, not required)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

The Role in Context

Compensation runs $18 to $23 per hour depending on experience. The position is full-time and reports into the community's management structure with direct communication lines to senior leadership at DLP Capital. The parent company has appeared on the Inc. 5000 fastest-growing private companies list for 14 consecutive years, which tells you something about the pace of growth you'd be operating inside.

Candidates who excel in roles like this tend to be the ones who treat traffic-to-lease conversion as a number they own personally, not a team metric to share credit for. If you've managed your own leasing funnel, tracked your own close rates, and built referral sources from scratch during a lease-up, this role fits the way you already think. Benefits include PTO, health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) with matching, and learning incentives.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student housing alongside conventional multifamily and build-to-rent communities across the country. Their Springfield property is hiring a Maintenance Technician to handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep that keeps a community running and residents renewing.

What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on, full-cycle maintenance role. You'll work through service requests, keep the turn process moving during move-out and make-ready periods, and hold down a spot in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. Preventative maintenance is a real part of the job, not an afterthought. You'll follow manufacturer schedules on equipment, keep chemical logs current for pool maintenance, and help the Maintenance Supervisor track inventory so the team isn't caught short on parts mid-repair. Curb appeal and common area cleanliness fall under your scope too, including breezeways, grounds, and exterior spaces.

On the resident-facing side, you'll be expected to communicate professionally with people who are often frustrated when something breaks. That requires patience and follow-through, not just technical skill.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in the apartment industry
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Your own hand tools (required)
  • Reliable transportation and the ability to live within 30 miles of the property
  • Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and rotating on-call shifts
  • Physical capability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at height on ladders, and operate in outdoor temperatures well above or below comfortable range

Context Worth Knowing

Springfield's rental market is heavily influenced by Missouri State University and Drury University enrollment cycles, which means a student-oriented property like this one sees predictable but intense turn seasons. If you've worked turns before, you already know what compressed make-ready timelines feel like. If you haven't, expect a steep but manageable learning curve in the late spring and summer months.

PeakMade offers a real path forward for technicians who want to grow. Their internal leadership program for facilities roles and access to HVAC and CPO certifications means this position can build credentials you carry anywhere in the industry. Technicians who develop strong preventative maintenance habits and resident communication skills tend to move into lead or supervisor roles faster than those who only focus on reactive repairs. That's the practical differentiator at this level.

Benefits include paid parental leave, PTO plus additional wellbeing days, a 401(k) match, monthly renewal bonuses, and a 10-year anniversary trip, among other recognition programs.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Commercial property management runs on details. Lease abstracts, CAM reconciliations, vendor invoices, tenant walk-throughs, monthly reporting packages. Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Assistant Property Manager in Nashville to help keep those details in order across commercial, industrial, or retail assets.

The day-to-day here is genuinely varied. You might spend a morning reviewing vendor invoices against the management agreement's authorization limits, then shift to coordinating a tenant move-out walk-through in the afternoon, then close out the day pulling data for an operating expense reconciliation with the accounting team. Lease administration runs through this role constantly: lease setup, amendments, system updates, reporting. The Property Manager sets direction, but this role carries real execution responsibility.

Tenant communication is a significant part of the job. When a tenant reports a building issue, you're the person making sure the right people respond and that the resolution actually happens. That means working across administrative staff, building technicians, and vendors without letting things fall through the cracks. Written communication matters here because a lot of this coordination happens by email, and clear documentation protects everyone.

One honest note: commercial APM roles can carry a heavier administrative load than people expect coming in. CAM reconciliations and budget prep aren't glamorous, but they're the work. Strong candidates tend to be people who find that kind of detailed financial work satisfying rather than tedious, and who can move between a spreadsheet and a tenant conversation without losing their footing in either.

What Lincoln is Looking for

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • One to two years of experience in commercial property management or a related field
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills; experience with AP and CMMS platforms is a plus
  • Comfort with financial concepts: percentages, basic analysis, reading through lease financial terms
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Solid organizational habits and the ability to deliver on deadlines without constant reminders
  • This position is fully in-office in Nashville; remote or hybrid work is not available

Lincoln manages over 720 million square feet of commercial space across the country, which means this role connects to a large institutional platform with real training and mentorship infrastructure. For someone early in a commercial PM career, that kind of organizational depth has practical value. APMs who build strong CAM and lease administration skills here tend to move into Property Manager roles with a solid foundation that's harder to get at smaller shops.

If you know your way around a lease abstract and take vendor invoice accuracy seriously, this is a role worth taking a close look at.

job.title: Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits inside Asset Living's affordable housing compliance operation, which means your primary function is file review. Specifically, you're pulling Affordable Housing applicant files, verifying eligibility, and confirming everything lines up with current regulatory requirements. The 24-hour turnaround expectation on file review is real, so if you work best with predictable, unhurried timelines, this one may not be the right fit.

Beyond day-to-day file work, you'll track changes in LIHTC regulations and translate those changes into actual process modifications at the property level. You'll also participate in tax credit reviews conducted by outside entities, which means you need to be comfortable with external auditors asking pointed questions about your work. Annual TDHCA training attendance is expected, and if you don't already hold the HCCP designation, you'll be required to complete that training and pass the exam within your first two years.

The travel commitment here is significant. Roughly half your work time involves travel, covering property visits, conferences, and training sessions. That's not a rounding error on the job description. Plan accordingly.

What You Bring

  • Direct experience reviewing affordable housing compliance files, particularly under the LIHTC program
  • Familiarity with RealPage OneSite Tax Credit module. This is listed as essential, not preferred
  • HCCP designation, or the willingness and eligibility to earn it within two years
  • Working knowledge of HUD programs (a plus, not a hard requirement)
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You'll be explaining compliance decisions to site staff and responding to outside reviewers
  • The kind of organizational discipline that keeps a 24-hour file review cycle from becoming a bottleneck

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing compliance is one of the more technically demanding specializations in third-party management. LIHTC files are not forgiving. A missed certification, an income calculation that doesn't hold up, a unit that slips out of compliance status. any of these can have real consequences for a property's tax credit allocation. Specialists who thrive in this work tend to be the ones who genuinely read the regulatory updates rather than waiting for someone to summarize them. TDHCA has made several notable adjustments to compliance monitoring in recent years, and staying current isn't optional in this role.

Asset Living operates across multifamily, student, build-to-rent, and affordable housing portfolios as a fee management firm, so the compliance team here touches a broad range of property types and structures. For someone looking to build deep expertise in affordable housing compliance, the portfolio breadth is a real advantage.
