The HCCP designation, once earned, also travels well if your career eventually takes you toward consulting, ownership groups, or state housing agency work.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's a Saturday morning in August, and move-in day at The Thompson is organized chaos. You're handing out keys, tracking down packages, fielding texts from parents, and somehow still smiling. That's the job, and it matters more than the title suggests.

The Role at The Thompson

The Scion Group operates student housing communities across the country, and The Thompson in San Marcos, Texas sits in a market shaped by Texas State University. This leasing consultant position, which Scion internally calls an Experience Team Member, covers more ground than a standard leasing role. You're part of the sales team, part of the marketing effort, and part of property operations all at once.

Day to day, that means touring prospective residents, handling objections, and feeding feedback on sales barriers back to the management team. It also means helping plan and run resident engagement events, supporting social media content, and keeping the office and amenity spaces in presentable shape. Package logging and maintenance request follow-up fall to this role too. The list of responsibilities is genuinely wide.

The after-hours piece is real. You'll rotate through on-call shifts, which includes lockout calls. That's a known part of working student housing, and it's worth saying plainly before you apply.

What You'll Need

  • Strong communication skills across a diverse resident and family population
  • Comfort working in an environment where priorities shift quickly, especially around turn season and move-in
  • Availability during summers, holidays, and turn periods when traffic peaks
  • Reliability and self-discipline in a role that involves both independent tasks and team coordination
  • A customer-first approach, not just during tours but in every interaction on-site

Scion is not looking for someone who needs the work structured for them at every step. The role rewards people who can read a situation, adjust, and stay composed when the leasing office gets loud. Prior experience in student housing or property management helps, but the requirements here center more on attitude and availability than a specific resume line.

One thing worth knowing: this role is a genuine entry point into property management. Leasing consultants who learn turn operations, build a track record in sales, and get comfortable with the administrative side of a property tend to move into assistant manager positions relatively quickly in student housing. The experience translates well to conventional multifamily too, since the core skills, occupancy management, resident relations, and basic operations, carry across asset types.

This is a full-time, non-exempt position based on-site at The Thompson in San Marcos. Scion requires current U.S. work authorization and does not offer visa sponsorship.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

The Community Manager position at Hawthorne Residential Partners in Kannapolis draws on three skill sets more than any others: financial literacy, team coaching, and leasing judgment. You'll read monthly reports, track delinquency, manage deposit accounting, and make budget decisions. You'll also hire, develop, and hold accountable a mixed office and maintenance team. And when occupancy softens, you'll be in the leasing process yourself, conducting tours, following up on leads, and pushing renewals alongside your team.

This is a full-scope role at Hawthorne at Concord Lake. There's no siloing between the business side and the people side. You own both.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're splitting time between the desk and the property. Morning might mean reviewing Yardi reports, following up on outstanding balances, or checking in with maintenance on work order status and vendor schedules. Afternoons can shift to walking the property for curb appeal, handling an escalated resident situation, or jumping on a leasing tour when traffic is high. Saturdays are part of the schedule (10 AM to 4 PM), and resident events occasionally push into evenings.

  • Budget management, rent collection, and financial reporting
  • Delinquency tracking and deposit accounting
  • Leasing, renewals, and pricing strategy to meet occupancy targets
  • Team hiring, training, and weekly performance alignment
  • Vendor oversight and maintenance coordination
  • Resident communication, conflict resolution, and online reputation management
  • Social media content tied to community events and resident engagement

Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms. Comfort with both puts you ahead on day one.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The posted requirement is two years of property management experience that includes time as both a leasing consultant and assistant community manager. Six months of direct community manager experience is strongly preferred. That path matters here because the role asks you to read a financial statement and conduct a leasing tour in the same workday, often without much transition time between them.

Candidates who do well in community manager roles tend to be comfortable with accountability on both sides: holding the team to standards while staying accessible enough that people actually bring problems to them early. The ones who struggle usually lean too far one direction. A CAM, CAPS, or real estate license strengthens your application but isn't required.

Hawthorne's internal career path program points community managers toward regional manager roles, which makes this position a reasonable next step if you're already in multifamily and looking to grow toward a portfolio-level seat. The company operates across the Southeast and ranks among the 50 largest multifamily management companies nationally, so the infrastructure for career movement is genuine.

job.title: Maintenance Service Technician
job.description:
It's 6:47 a.m. and a resident calls about a water heater that died overnight. By 8:00, you've diagnosed it, pulled the part, and the unit has hot water again before the resident leaves for work. That's the job at Lakeside Village Apartments in Clinton Township.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Paragon Properties is hiring a full-time Maintenance Service Technician for Lakeside Village. The role covers the full range of day-to-day maintenance: handling resident service requests, completing make-readies on vacant units, and keeping the property's curb appeal and physical condition where it needs to be. You'll do basic drywall patching, painting, and rough carpentry as part of unit turns, and you'll troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical, major appliances, pool and spa equipment, and HVAC systems.

This position includes after-hours on-call rotation, including weekends and holidays. That's the part some people underestimate when they apply. The call volume and timing are unpredictable, and the expectation is that you show up and solve the problem. Paragon does pay an on-call bonus for after-hours coverage, and there's a quarterly team bonus on top of base pay, which runs up to $26 per hour depending on experience and certifications.

HVAC certification (Type II or Universal) is strongly preferred. If you don't have it yet, the company offers a training and certification program. A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and a high school diploma are required. Trade school or college-level technical training is a plus. Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and a physical are required before you start.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience, whether from a technical program, vocational training, or direct on-the-job work
  • Comfortable working outdoors in all seasons, Michigan winters included
  • Solid understanding of safety procedures across trades
  • Customer-facing mindset: residents interact with you directly, and how you handle those interactions matters as much as how you handle the wrench
  • Consistent, dependable attendance. The property doesn't run itself when someone doesn't show up

The benefit package includes paid time off, nine company-paid holidays, a rent discount, 401(k) with employer contribution, and medical, dental, and vision insurance with a short enrollment waiting period. Company-paid life and disability insurance are included. You'll also receive a tool kit after completing the initial 30-day training period and a company uniform.

Strong technicians who build their HVAC knowledge and demonstrate reliability here tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles over time. The hands-on breadth of a role like this, covering everything from appliance repair to pool equipment to electrical troubleshooting, builds a foundation that carries across any multifamily property.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
The Role at a Glance

Maintenance Technicians at apartment communities handle a wide mix of work: service requests, make-readies, preventive maintenance, and the occasional after-hours call. At Waypoint Management Services in Palm Bay, this role sits at a high-end luxury community, so the expectation for quality and presentation is higher than at a typical garden-style complex.

What You'll Handle Day-to-Day

You're responsible for the overall upkeep of the property and its residents' day-to-day maintenance needs. That includes diagnosing and repairing plumbing issues, HVAC units, appliances, and general building systems. Preventive maintenance on HVAC and community equipment happens on a regular schedule. Priority work orders get resolved within 24 hours.

Make-ready prep is a core part of the job. You'll confirm units are rent-ready and coordinate with contractors on punch list items as needed. Beyond units, you'll maintain pool chemistry, service the trash compactor, check that gates and security equipment are functioning, and handle light grounds and carpentry work. OSHA compliance isn't optional here; you're expected to know the standards and operate within them.

On-call availability is part of the schedule. Residents at luxury properties tend to expect faster response and a higher standard of finish, so attention to detail matters more than it might elsewhere.

What Waypoint Is Looking For

  • EPA Section 608 certification, Types I and II (required)
  • CPO certification (a plus)
  • Hands-on experience with building systems, plumbing, and general repairs
  • Familiarity with service supplies, materials, and equipment
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards
  • High school diploma or equivalent, with relevant trade experience or training
  • Strong service orientation and a professional, resident-facing attitude

Technicians who do well in luxury settings combine solid technical skills with strong communication. Residents notice when someone shows up on time, explains what they're doing, and leaves the unit clean. That combination, reliable work plus a professional presence, tends to separate strong candidates from average ones in this type of community.

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, 401k with matching, an onsite housing discount, and bonus opportunities. The company is in a growth phase, which typically means more communities coming online and room to move up.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Lease-up maintenance is a different job than steady-state property maintenance, and the distinction matters. At a stabilizing property, you're managing systems that have already been tested by residents. At a brand-new community like Dream St. Augustine, you're setting the baseline. Every punch list item, every first service request, every vendor relationship gets established on your watch. That's the context for this Maintenance Supervisor role.

What the Job Actually Involves

Dream St. Augustine is a new construction community in St. Augustine, FL, and the Maintenance Supervisor hired here will build the maintenance operation from the ground up. That means establishing preventative maintenance schedules, standing up the maintenance shop, vetting vendors, and training a team before the property reaches stabilization. Day-to-day, you'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and pool systems yourself when needed, while also directing your crew on service request completion within 24-hour windows and vacancy turns on a 5-day cycle. The administrative side is real too: budget tracking, purchasing through AppFolio, security deposit dispositions, and detailed maintenance records all sit in this role.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Leading and scheduling the maintenance team, including on-call rotation
  • Performing and overseeing make-readies, targeting 5-day turns on vacant units
  • Troubleshooting and repairing HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems
  • Coordinating landscaping and vendor services, managing contracts and supply costs
  • Maintaining the OpEx maintenance budget and identifying cost-saving opportunities
  • Keeping common areas, grounds, and amenities in top condition from the initial lease-up phase forward
  • Mentoring technicians and setting service standards for the team

The schedule requires flexibility, including weekend availability and on-call rotation. You'll need a valid driver's license, a clean driving record, a reliable vehicle, your own basic tools, and the physical capacity to lift 50-plus pounds and cover multiple floors on foot throughout the day.

What Strong Candidates Bring

HVAC certification is strongly preferred, and hands-on HVAC management experience is the core technical credential this role is built around. Lease-up experience is a real differentiator here. Candidates who have opened a new property before understand the difference between a system failure at month 18 and one at month 2 of occupancy. First impressions during lease-up shape resident retention, and maintenance quality is a direct driver of both renewal rates and online reputation.

Beyond technical skill, the candidates who tend to excel in this kind of role are those who can shift between managing people and picking up tools themselves, sometimes within the same hour. If your instinct is to lead from the front rather than delegate everything downward, this structure fits that style well.

Company and Growth Context

Dream Live Prosper Communities operates as a subsidiary of DLP Capital, which has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for 14 consecutive years. The company focuses on attainable housing and has stated goals around community impact at scale. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that organizational backing typically means access to systems and resources that smaller operators can't match, alongside the accountability that comes with a performance-driven culture. Monthly and quarterly bonus potential is tied to performance. This role positions well for anyone targeting a Regional Maintenance Director or Director of Facilities path as the portfolio grows.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor- Russellville Commons
job.description:
Maintenance supervisors in multifamily carry more operational weight than the job title suggests. At a property with meaningful unit count, they're the difference between a well-run community and one that bleeds NOI through deferred repairs, slow turns, and resident frustration. MG Properties, a Western U.S. operator with three decades of acquisition, rehab, and management experience, is staffing this role at Russellville Commons in Portland.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope maintenance leadership position. You'll diagnose and perform hands-on repairs, but the job is equally about running the team: scheduling staff, delegating work orders, inspecting completed jobs, and making sure the preventive maintenance calendar doesn't slip. Resident service requests need a system behind them, not just a person. You'll own that system. Safety meetings are a scheduled responsibility here, not an afterthought, and you'll keep accurate records on PM work and expenditures. When outside vendors or contractors come in, you coordinate that too.

Portland's housing stock trends older in many corridors, and properties like Russellville Commons can carry HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems that require real trade fluency, not specialists for every call. MG's expectation is that you bring working knowledge across all trades. That breadth lets the property avoid unnecessary vendor costs while keeping turns and make-readies on schedule.

What MG Properties Is Looking For

  • At least 2 years in a maintenance supervisor role (preferred)
  • Direct experience at a community of 150 units or more
  • Demonstrated competency across multiple trades (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Strong customer service instincts and a collaborative approach to working with site staff and the property manager

The candidates who do well in this kind of role typically combine technical range with organizational discipline. Knowing how to fix things gets you in the door. Knowing how to prioritize a queue of 30 open work orders, keep your team accountable, and communicate clearly with residents and management is what makes you effective at scale. If your background is mostly hands-on tech work with limited team oversight, this role will ask more of you on the leadership side than you may be used to.

Compensation includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, and a 401(k) with employer match. MG also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, sick time, and a rental discount benefit.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Station Center I, Station Center II)
job.description:
Affordable housing operations carry a layer of compliance complexity that most market-rate properties never encounter. At MidPen Housing's Station Center I and Station Center II in Union City, the Assistant Community Manager role exists at exactly that intersection: day-to-day property administration plus the regulatory work that keeps affordable units funded and legally occupied.

MidPen has operated in Northern California since 1970 and manages more than 142 properties across 12 counties. These aren't market-rate communities with concessions and lease-up pressure. They serve working families, seniors, and residents with special needs, and keeping those homes stable requires precision in income verification, recertification, and Tax Credit Allocation Committee (TCAC) compliance. Experience with that regulatory layer will separate strong candidates from those who need significant ramp-up time.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

The Assistant Community Manager reports to the Community Manager and carries a wide operational scope. On the leasing and compliance side, you'll schedule income verification appointments, process lease agreements, manage the waitlist, assist with recertifications, and support Management and Occupancy Review (MOR) and TCAC reviews. On the financial side, you'll assist with rent collection, security deposits, petty cash logs, and bank deposit preparation. Turns are part of the work too: you'll schedule vacancies, prepare and monitor turnover forms, and coordinate with facilities staff to keep work orders moving on a reasonable timeline.

Resident relations here go beyond the typical leasing conversation. You'll communicate emergency preparedness procedures, coordinate logistics for resident meetings, and help maintain working relationships with local law enforcement and emergency agencies. Property inspections for maintenance and security issues are also part of your regular rhythm.

  • Proficiency in MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • High School diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or equivalent combination)
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission serving diverse, income-qualified residents

Context Worth Knowing

Union City sits in the eastern Alameda County corridor where affordable housing demand consistently outpaces supply. MidPen properties in this area carry waitlists that reflect that pressure, which means waitlist management and recertification accuracy aren't administrative formalities. They're how the community maintains compliance with funding sources and keeps deserving residents housed.

For candidates building a career in affordable housing property management, this role develops skills that transfer directly into Community Manager positions: LIHTC compliance knowledge, HUD review preparation, and resident services coordination. Those are qualifications that carry real weight with mission-driven housing organizations up and down the Bay Area. The pay range is $21.15 to $23.80 per hour, based on experience.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Montrose)
job.description:
Leasing roles at apartment communities in the Bay Area carry real weight. Mountain View's rental market stays competitive year-round, and the person on the front line of touring, qualifying, and closing future residents directly affects occupancy and NOI. This is that front-line role.

What the Job Actually Involves

Prometheus calls this position a Regional Neighbor Ambassador, which reflects something real about the scope. You're not just running tours and collecting applications. On any given day you might be conducting a market survey in the morning, preparing rental agreements at midday, posting updated availability, and then pivoting back to a walk-in prospect who has questions about move-in timelines. The mix of sales, customer service, and administrative work is genuine.

Weekends are a required part of the schedule. Traffic peaks on Saturdays and Sundays, so that's when the community needs coverage. Your regular days off will fall during the week. That trade-off is worth understanding before you apply.

Pay starts at $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, with a $200 incentive per signed lease on top of base. There's also a discretionary semi-annual bonus, weekend shift premium pay, and additional bonuses tied to referrals, lease-up performance, and training. Benefits include 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and eligible dependents.

Who Fits This Role

Prometheus explicitly hires across industries. A background in retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing sales environment translates well here. Prior property management experience isn't required.

Strong candidates in leasing roles like this one tend to share a few traits worth calling out:

  • They move between tasks without losing momentum. Leasing offices don't queue work neatly.
  • They follow up. A prospect who tours on Saturday and doesn't hear back by Monday afternoon is likely already looking elsewhere.
  • They can read what a prospect actually needs and adjust their approach, rather than running the same script on everyone.
  • They handle administrative details accurately. Errors in rental agreements or lease files create downstream problems for the whole team.

This role sits at the entry point of a property management career path that can move toward assistant manager, property manager, and eventually regional or portfolio-level positions. The administrative and sales exposure you get here builds a foundation that transfers directly into those steps.

job.title: Service Manager
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday and you've got two service requests from the weekend sitting in the queue, a unit turning this week, and a contractor showing up at nine to work on building exteriors. That's a normal morning at West Pointe Apartments, and this role is built for someone who can triage all of it without losing composure.

The Work

West Pointe is a 100-unit residential community in Burlington, NC, currently being built out under Van Metre's portfolio. As Service Manager, you'll oversee one Maintenance Technician and report to both the Property Manager and the Director of Facilities. The scope is hands-on and operational. You're managing daily service requests, coordinating the make-ready process for vacant units, scheduling vendors, meeting with contractors, and keeping the preventative maintenance program on track. HVAC maintenance, repair, and replacement fall squarely in your lap, as does carrying the 24-hour emergency maintenance schedule. That last part is real: after-hours calls happen, and this position requires someone who's comfortable with that reality.

Beyond the day-to-day, you'll manage the facility side of the budget, submit weekly reports to the corporate office, and stay current on OSHA standards and any state or federal compliance programs the property is subject to. Work also includes hands-on repairs across electrical, plumbing, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting, so this is a working supervisor role, not a desk job with a title.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of maintenance experience, or equivalent formal training
  • EPA Certification (required)
  • CPO Certification (required)
  • Prior supervisory experience (preferred)
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems and electrical circuitry
  • Solid skills in appliance, electrical, and plumbing repair
  • Current knowledge of OSHA, building codes, and safety standards
  • Your own basic tools and the ability to use them safely
  • Valid driver's license

The interpersonal side of this job matters too. You'll interact with residents, visitors, and contractors regularly, and how you handle a frustrated resident waiting on a repair reflects directly on the property. Professionalism under pressure is part of the job description, not just a line in the posting.

Candidates who tend to do well in roles like this are the ones who take the make-ready process seriously. At a 100-unit property, a slow turn costs money and occupancy. If you've owned that process before, including managing the punch list, coordinating vendors, and keeping the timeline tight, that experience will matter more than anything else you bring to the interview.

Van Metre offers a base salary between $58,240 and $62,400 annually, with up to $5,000 in annual bonus potential paid quarterly. Benefits include 11 paid holidays, vacation, sick leave, personal days, a birthday day off, parental leave, company-matched 401(k), up to $900 in annual wellness reimbursement, and professional development support including tuition reimbursement and company-paid certifications.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Roving - Pine Vista, Vogue Manor, Castilian and Las Palmas
job.description:
Roving maintenance roles exist because multi-family portfolios rarely distribute deferred work, turnover volume, or staffing gaps evenly across sites. Sunrise Management's solution is a Maintenance Supervisor who moves across four San Diego communities , Pine Vista, Vogue Manor, Castilian, and Las Palmas , plugging in where the need is highest on any given week. The role pays $29 to $31 per hour depending on experience.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core accountability is keeping four communities physically healthy and market-ready at the same time. Turns are a significant part of that. Sunrise expects make-ready apartments to be painted, cleaned, and punched out within three to five days of vacancy. At multiple sites simultaneously, hitting that window consistently requires real scheduling discipline and the ability to direct a crew without micromanaging every task.

Beyond turns, the day-to-day spans a wide range of trades: HVAC, plumbing, appliance repair, electrical, pool and spa maintenance, carpentry, and custodial work. Preventive maintenance runs on a monthly directive cycle covering lighting, fire safety, life and safety hazards, pool systems, and signage. You'll maintain the logs, track inventory across sites, and flag any capital-level repairs or deferred maintenance to the property manager. Emergency on-call service is part of the job. Service requests carry a 24-hour completion target, and when parts delay a repair, the expectation is proactive communication to both management and the resident , not silence.

Because this is a supervisory position, you'll also coordinate with site management teams on scheduling, assist with hiring and performance reviews for maintenance staff, and run monthly safety meetings. MSDS recordkeeping, PPE compliance, and adherence to Sunrise's hazard materials policies are non-negotiable. Fair Housing awareness applies to maintenance staff just as it does to leasing , you're expected to understand why that matters operationally.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The multi-site structure is where this role gets interesting and where underprepared candidates struggle. You won't have the luxury of owning one property's rhythm and settling in. Priorities shift depending on which site has the highest vacancy, the most urgent work orders, or the thinnest staffing. The strongest candidates here are the ones who can triage quickly, communicate clearly across multiple managers, and maintain consistent standards at each stop.

  • 2 or more years of hands-on property maintenance experience, required
  • Prior supervisory experience, required
  • Valid driver's license, required (travel between sites is a core function)
  • Familiarity with Entrata or AppFolio, preferred
  • Broad trades competency across plumbing, HVAC, electrical, pool systems, and carpentry
  • Comfort working within preventive maintenance programs, PPE requirements, and safety compliance frameworks

Experience with portfolio-wide or roving maintenance work is a genuine differentiator here. Someone who has only ever managed one property's physical plant will find the context-switching demanding at first. Someone who's done it before will recognize the pattern and adapt quickly. Entrata experience in particular helps, since work order tracking and communication across sites runs through the platform.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and three walk-ins just showed up at the same time. You greet all three, pull up available floor plans, and start working the room. By noon, two of them have submitted applications. That's the job.

The Role

Karya Property Management is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Dallas portfolio. This is a front-line sales and hospitality position where your output shows up directly in the occupancy number. You'll carry the property's traffic from first contact to signed lease, which means greeting walk-ins, working internet leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and staying on top of follow-up until a lead converts or goes cold. The closing ratio and the vacancy report are your scorecards.

Day-to-day, you'll match prospects to floor plans, process income and credit screenings, prepare lease documents and addenda, and keep guest cards and traffic logs current in the property management system. Before any showing, you'll confirm units are market-ready. You'll walk the property regularly and flag curb appeal or maintenance issues as you go. Move-in orientations, renewal outreach, and lease-expiration follow-up are all part of the cycle.

Beyond direct leasing, the role includes competitor market surveys (pricing, specials, concessions), contributing content for social media and listing sites, supporting outreach to local employers and referral partners, and helping staff resident events. Fair Housing compliance and general office coverage round out the responsibilities.

What Karya Needs From You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year in a customer-facing role: leasing, sales, hospitality, retail, or similar
  • Comfortable asking for the sale and following up persistently without crossing into pushy
  • Strong phone, email, and in-person communication
  • Basic computer proficiency; Microsoft Office or Google Workspace
  • Weekend availability and flexibility for evening hours during peak leasing season
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Prior multifamily experience, working knowledge of Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or a comparable platform, and bilingual ability in English and Spanish are all preferred but not required to apply.

The candidates who stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the most leasing experience. They're the ones with tight follow-up habits, a genuine ability to read what a prospect actually needs in a home, and the discipline to treat every guest card as an open task until it's resolved one way or another. Leasing coordinators who come from restaurant or retail backgrounds often bring exactly that instinct, and it translates quickly in this environment.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Chestnut Square Senior, Chestnut Square Family)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers two adjacent affordable communities in Livermore: Chestnut Square Senior and Chestnut Square Family. That dual-site setup means your day moves. Income verification appointments, lease processing, waitlist management, recertifications, bank deposits, and turn scheduling can all land in the same week. MidPen operates under TCAC and HUD compliance frameworks, so familiarity with MOR reviews, welfare exemptions, and tax credit recertification timelines will matter here. Compliance paperwork in affordable housing doesn't forgive shortcuts.

Beyond the desk work, you'll do regular property walks to flag maintenance and security issues, coordinate work orders with facilities staff, and keep resident and property files organized without letting confidential information slip. You'll also be a point of contact for emergency preparedness communications and resident meeting logistics. MidPen's property management team works closely with their onsite Resident Services staff, which is a meaningful difference from conventional market-rate operations. You'll have support, but you're also expected to carry your weight independently.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential property management, administrative, or customer service experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Comfort with MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially under pressure
  • Detail orientation that holds up during recertification season
  • Genuine alignment with affordable housing as a mission, not just a job category

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing compliance is a discipline of its own. Candidates who've only worked conventional market-rate properties often underestimate how different the documentation burden is. Tax credit properties run on strict income and occupancy rules, and annual TCAC reviews reward thorough file management. If you've worked affordable, you already know this. If you're making the transition from market-rate, the learning curve is real but manageable with the right attitude toward process.

The pay range for this position runs from $21.15 to $23.80 hourly, based on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, life and disability coverage, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, employee education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, and pet insurance, among others.

For an assistant-level candidate with some affordable housing exposure, this is a solid foundation. ACMs who build strong compliance and resident relations skills here have a clear path toward Community Manager roles, particularly within a portfolio as large as MidPen's across Northern California.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Freewell, Carson, Raleigh, & Saltwood)
job.description:
Prometheus Real Estate Group runs a portfolio of over 13,000 apartments across the Bay Area, Portland, and Seattle, and they've been at it since 1965. That kind of tenure means their properties get maintained, not deferred. This Maintenance Technician II role covers four Portland communities: Freewell, Carson, Raleigh, and Saltwood. If you've worked multi-site before, you know the rhythm. If you haven't, expect to learn it quickly.

The work is bread-and-butter apartment maintenance. Turns, service requests, appliance repairs, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting. You'll troubleshoot major mechanical systems and handle minor repairs independently. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," which signals something about how they expect you to treat people. Residents who feel ignored or dismissed will let you know about it, and you'll need to de-escalate that while still getting through your punch list. That's the real job.

On-call is part of this position. That's not buried in the fine print here. After-hours calls happen, and if you've been in apartment maintenance for more than a few months, you already know what that means for your personal schedule. The standby pay and on-call premium are real compensation for that time, not token gestures, but the expectation is genuine availability.

Prometheus is a vertically integrated company, which matters for a tech because capital improvement projects, value-add renovations, and lease-up activity all create additional work at the property level. There are bonus opportunities tied to some of these, including renovation and lease-up bonuses, which means a busy property can translate into more take-home pay.

What this role requires

  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Hands-on competency across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and perform physically demanding work outdoors in varying conditions
  • Basic computer proficiency for work order systems
  • Availability for on-call rotations
  • High school diploma or GED

Pay runs $26.00 to $27.25 per hour, and the benefits package is genuinely strong. Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums for employees and eligible dependents, which stands out. There's a 401(k) with employer matching, a semi-annual discretionary bonus, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts. They also offer tuition reimbursement, which matters if you're thinking about an HVAC certification or electrical license down the road.

One thing worth noting for candidates who are serious about growth: multi-site technician experience at a company with in-house renovation and development capabilities tends to build a broader skill set than a single-property position would. Techs who do turns efficiently, keep delinquency in maintenance work orders low, and communicate well with property managers often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles faster than they expect. The exposure across four communities accelerates that.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Grounds work at a multifamily community is physical, visible, and immediate. Residents notice it every single day, and the skills it builds, attention to detail, familiarity with exterior systems, and an eye for curb appeal, carry forward into every maintenance role above it. At Liam at Hays Farm in Huntsville's growing south corridor near Jones Valley, Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Groundskeeper to keep this community's exterior looking the part.

What This Role Actually Demands

The core skill here is observation. A good groundskeeper walks the property and registers what's off before anyone else does: a light out in a breezeway, debris collecting near the compactor, a pet station that needs attention, a pool deck that's lost its presentation. You won't be handed a checklist at 8 AM and left alone. You'll be expected to develop an instinct for what the property needs and act on it.

Day-to-day, that means cleaning and picking up debris throughout exterior areas, maintaining sidewalks, parking lots, and green spaces, and keeping amenity areas like courtyards, grilling stations, and pool decks clean and presentable. Light landscaping tasks like raking, trimming, and weeding come with the role, as does assisting the maintenance team with exterior touch-ups, bulb replacements, and make-ready support for vacant units when needed. You'll also help distribute resident communications and pitch in on seasonal prep and cleanup.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Comfort working outdoors in variable Alabama weather, including summer heat
  • Some background in yardwork or general facility upkeep
  • A valid driver's license
  • Reliability and a consistent presence the team and residents can count on
  • Willingness to learn from the maintenance team and take direction without friction
  • A high school diploma or GED equivalent

Prior maintenance or HVAC experience is a plus, but Hawthorne has structured this as an entry point. The work ethic matters more than the resume here.

Where This Role Can Take You at Hawthorne

Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program, and the Groundskeeper role is explicitly positioned as a stepping stone toward Maintenance Technician I. That's a meaningful distinction. Many companies say they promote from within; Hawthorne builds that progression into their training infrastructure. If you want to expand into HVAC, plumbing, or electrical work over time, this is a legitimate place to start building toward those credentials while earning a paycheck.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus program. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies and occasional support for resident events when needed.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Miami's rental market moves fast, and leasing consultants are the ones actually closing the gap between traffic and occupancy. Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Leasing Consultant to handle the full cycle: generating interest, qualifying prospects, executing leases, and keeping residents happy enough to renew. This is a sales role with a service wrapper, and the two have to coexist.

The Work Itself

You'll manage prospect relationships across every channel, phone, email, in-person tours, and follow-up sequences that actually move people toward a decision. That means knowing your floor plans cold, having a working read on the competitive set, and responding with enough urgency that leads don't go cold while the prospect shops three other communities down Brickell or Doral. Lease preparation, applicant qualification, proration calculations, and file assembly for manager approval all fall to you. So does keeping the leasing office, model, and amenity spaces tour-ready at all times. Waypoint also wants this person contributing to renewal activity and maintaining an organized waitlist, which means your occupancy impact extends well past the initial lease-up push.

Marketing outreach and referral networking are part of the role too, not an afterthought. If you've only ever waited for leads to come in through ILS traffic, you'll need to adjust that habit here.

Fair Housing compliance isn't optional. Waypoint expects you to know the regulations and apply them consistently, not just acknowledge that they exist.

What Waypoint Is Looking For

  • At least two years in leasing, sales, or a hospitality-facing role
  • Comfort managing the full leasing process, including financial calculations and lease documents
  • Familiarity with Yardi and CRM platforms (a plus, not a hard requirement)
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred, which in Miami is less a bonus and more a practical daily asset
  • Weekend availability for rotation
  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

Compensation includes a competitive base wage, monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a leaser-of-the-month monetary award, and an employee housing discount. Benefits start on day one and include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one (growing with tenure), two floating days, commuter benefits, and an employee referral program.

One honest observation worth making: bilingual ability in this market genuinely separates candidates. Miami's renter population is heavily Spanish-speaking, and a leasing consultant who can close a tour in the prospect's preferred language converts at a measurably higher rate. If you're fluent, lead with that.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Fairstead operates a large affordable housing portfolio across 28 states, and this Maintenance Technician role in Fayetteville is a hands-on, boots-on-the-ground position. You'll be responsible for keeping a residential property running well for the people who actually live there. That means everything from routine work orders to make-readies to emergency calls that come in after hours.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

A typical week involves regular building and equipment inspections, completing preventative maintenance tasks before small problems become expensive ones, and handling repairs across plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems. When a unit turns, you're helping get it ready for the next resident: cleaning, patching, checking appliances, working through the punch list until it's move-in ready. You'll also track supplies and maintain inventory so you're not scrambling for parts in the middle of a repair.

The on-call rotation is real. Affordable housing communities tend to have residents who depend heavily on the property team, and when something breaks after hours, someone has to show up. That's part of this role, and it's worth knowing upfront.

  • Inspect buildings and equipment on a regular schedule and flag issues before they escalate
  • Perform preventative and corrective maintenance as needed across the property
  • Check electrical systems for code compliance and safety systems monthly
  • Prepare vacant units for occupancy, including cleaning and repair work
  • Respond to emergency maintenance issues outside of normal business hours as part of the on-call rotation
  • Maintain accurate inventory of tools, equipment, and supplies

What Fairstead Is Looking For

You'll need prior experience as a service or maintenance technician, solid general maintenance skills, and enough electrical knowledge to diagnose and handle minor repairs safely. HVAC certification is preferred, not just a nice-to-have on paper. Physical requirements are straightforward: you'll be on your feet most of the day and need to lift up to 70 pounds without assistance.

The candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this are the ones who communicate clearly with residents and management alike. A lot of maintenance techs can fix things. Fewer can explain what they did and why, or flag a systemic problem before it gets buried in a backlog of work orders. If you're organized, keep clean notes, and treat residents with patience even when they're frustrated, you'll fit well here.

Company and Compensation

Fairstead brings development, construction, and property management together under one platform, which means the maintenance team isn't siloed. Benefits include medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. Compensation is based on experience and market benchmarks for this location.

job.title: Community Manager - Multi site - Van Mall North and Arborlane Apartments
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Multi-site community management runs on a specific combination of skills that single-property roles don't fully develop: rapid context-switching, strong financial literacy across multiple ledgers, and the kind of leadership that holds teams accountable without daily proximity. CloudTen Residential is hiring a Community Manager to oversee Van Mall North and Arborlane Apartments (formerly Corporate Woods) in Vancouver, WA, splitting time across both properties as operational needs shift. If you've managed delinquency curves, coached leasing staff, and kept occupancy healthy at more than one asset simultaneously, this role matches that experience directly.

Vancouver's rental market sits in an interesting position relative to Portland. Renters priced out of the west side increasingly cross the river, which keeps demand reasonably steady but also means pricing decisions matter. The ability to read traffic patterns, adjust concessions thoughtfully, and keep renewal rates strong through genuine resident engagement is something CloudTen will expect you to bring to both properties from day one.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your week will distribute across both sites depending on what each property needs. Some days that means running inspections, reviewing make-ready timelines, and walking punch lists with maintenance. Other days it means sitting with leasing records, monitoring delinquency against State landlord-tenant requirements, and preparing budget notes for your Regional Manager. The financial side of this role is real: you'll oversee rent collection, complete daily bank deposits, monitor expenses against budget, and flag cost-saving opportunities before they become problems.

On the people side, you're responsible for hiring, training, and evaluating on-site staff at your assigned properties. That means building cohesive teams across two locations that may have different cultures, different needs, and different gaps. Fair Housing compliance, move-in and move-out protocol enforcement, and resident service response windows of 24 to 48 hours all fall under your watch. A valid driver's license is required given the travel between sites.

  • Two or more years of property management experience, with multi-site exposure a genuine plus
  • Working knowledge of State landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing regulations
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and property management software platforms
  • High school diploma required; college coursework or a degree preferred
  • Strong accounting fundamentals: budgets, deposits, expense tracking, delinquency management
  • Self-directed and organized enough to manage priorities across locations without daily direction

What Makes CloudTen a Specific Fit

CloudTen operates a deliberately varied portfolio across the West, including hotel-to-residential conversions and high-rise lease-ups, which means their managers tend to build broader operational experience than peers at single-asset companies. The Portland metro group is established, and this role sits within a regional structure with a supervising Regional Manager providing oversight. Compensation is hourly in the $33 to $34 range depending on experience, with leasing bonus eligibility at the assigned properties. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA access, company-paid life insurance, and paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.

Candidates who tend to stand out in multi-site roles have one quality above all others: they build systems rather than relying on memory. When you're splitting time between two properties, the managers who succeed are those who create consistent processes their teams can execute independently, so that site performance doesn't drop the moment the manager is at the other location.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Dream Montrose community in Houston runs on the work this role produces every day. Residents depend on it. As a Maintenance Technician here, you'll carry a full slate of responsibilities that go beyond fixing leaky faucets. You'll manage service requests on a 24-hour turnaround, respond to emergency calls during on-call rotation, and keep vacant units moving through a five-day turn cycle. That last point matters: five days from move-out to move-in ready means you're coordinating repairs, painting, appliance checks, plumbing, HVAC, drywall, and lock replacements on a real schedule, not an ideal one.

You'll also mentor and direct other members of the maintenance team, which means your interpersonal skills matter as much as your trade skills. Coaching a junior tech through a repair, communicating clearly with a frustrated resident, coordinating with a vendor while keeping costs in check , these are the human dynamics that fill a normal week. You'll manage the maintenance shop inventory, handle purchasing with an eye on cost control, and track security deposit dispositions. Groundskeeping and exterior cleanliness are part of the job too, not delegated away.

Dream Live Prosper properties sit in the affordable housing space, which carries real purpose. Residents here are counting on their homes being safe and functional. When something breaks, the stakes feel personal to them. That context shapes the service expectation in this role.

What You Bring

  • HVAC certification (required)
  • Hands-on experience with plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Demonstrated ability to complete apartment turns within five days
  • Plaster, drywall, and painting proficiency
  • Experience with lock replacement and basic hardware
  • Familiarity with both older and newer building systems
  • Valid driver's license, clean driving record, and a reliable personal vehicle
  • Your own basic tools
  • Comfort with budgeting and cost-control basics
  • Clear, practical communication skills with residents, vendors, and teammates

Property management experience is a plus, but trade competence and a steady, dependable work ethic will carry significant weight in the hiring decision.

Context Worth Knowing

This role carries a flexible schedule with nights and weekend availability required. That's honest. On-call rotations are part of maintenance work at any community, and this one is no different. If you've done apartment maintenance before, you already know what that means for your personal planning. If you're newer to the property side and coming from a trade background, it's worth factoring in before you apply.

For technicians who want to grow, this kind of role , where you're already managing team hours, coaching others, and touching budgets , is solid preparation for a Maintenance Supervisor or Facilities Manager position down the road. The combination of technical breadth and team leadership exposure is exactly what separates a journeyman tech from someone who moves into a senior or oversight role.

Dream Live Prosper has built its portfolio within the affordable housing segment, which tends to attract team members who find meaning in the work itself. If that kind of environment sounds like a good fit for how you operate, this is worth a closer look.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a high-contact, high-turnover function at most apartment communities. The consultant role exists because occupancy doesn't manage itself. Someone has to answer the phone, run the tour, close the application, and follow up after move-in. At Lakeside Village Apartments in Clinton Township, Paragon Properties is filling that seat.

What the Job Actually Involves

This is a full-cycle leasing position. You're handling traffic from first contact through signed lease, which means phone and email inquiries, in-person tours, application processing, and move-in paperwork. You'll also stay involved after the lease is signed: work order follow-up, renewal conversations, and resident retention are all part of the scope. Community inspections, model apartments, and vacant units need to meet standards before prospects ever walk through the door, and keeping that in order falls to you too.

Beyond the leasing desk, you'll support site marketing and outreach to local businesses and employers, and help plan and attend resident events. It's a broad role for a single title.

The schedule is guaranteed full-time at 40 hours per week. Starting pay is $18.50 per hour, negotiable based on prior leasing experience. The company offers move-in bonuses, a rent discount, 401(k) with employer contribution, medical/dental/vision with a short waiting period, and paid life and disability insurance. Nine paid holidays and PTO are included.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year in a customer service or sales role; six-plus months of on-site leasing experience preferred
  • High school diploma required; some college coursework preferred
  • Comfortable with MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); Yardi experience is a plus
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tasks during busy traffic periods

Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and physical are required before start.

The candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be the ones who treat the phone lead with the same energy as the walk-in. Plenty of consultants are good in person and let their phone and email conversion slip. Consistent follow-through across every touchpoint is what separates average occupancy numbers from strong ones. If you've got the sales instinct and the follow-up habit, there's real room to grow here into a senior leasing or assistant manager track.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Managing three properties across a combined 94 units isn't a sprawling portfolio, but it's not a lightweight assignment either. At that scale, you're close enough to the operation to know every problem before it becomes a complaint, and accountable enough that there's nowhere to hide when things slip. This role with Property Management Associates fits that profile: a hands-on, live-on-site position covering conventional multifamily in Long Beach.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Your morning probably starts with a walk. PMA puts real weight on preventative maintenance and daily property inspections, which means you're developing a feel for each asset rather than waiting for work orders to tell you what's wrong. From there, you're juggling leasing activity, coordinating maintenance staff and vendors, managing delinquency, and staying on top of reporting in Yardi Voyager. Voyager proficiency isn't a nice-to-have here. It's the operating system for the job.

Because you're living on-site, the line between work and off-hours is softer than most PM roles. On-call status and one weekend day per week come with the territory. That's an honest trade-off, and the compensation reflects it: $23 to $25 per hour, a free one-bedroom unit, and a $300 monthly auto allowance. A valid driver's license and proof of insurance are required.

What PMA Is Looking For

  • At least three years of conventional multifamily property management experience
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Yardi Voyager
  • Proven leasing and marketing ability, including closing traffic into signed leases
  • Experience supervising maintenance staff and scheduling vendors
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office and general computer fluency
  • Valid driver's license with clean DMV record (DMV check is part of the screening process)
  • Ability to pass a background check and pre-employment physical

PMA has operated in the greater LA County market for over 30 years across residential and commercial assets. At a company that size, a manager who performs well on a 94-unit portfolio tends to have a clear path toward larger or more complex assignments. The structure here rewards people who treat the role like an owner would: watching the details, communicating proactively, and keeping occupancy and collections tight without waiting to be asked.

Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short and long-term disability coverage, supplemental plans, and paid vacation, holiday, and sick time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Berkshire Residential Investments runs an in-house management model, which means the maintenance team here isn't contracted out or rotating through a third-party vendor arrangement. You're part of the community itself. That context matters because it shapes how residents experience your work, and how you experience the job.

The Maintenance Technician role at Berkshire Main Street sits at the center of daily property life. Residents notice when things get fixed fast and done right. They also notice when curb appeal slips, when a work order drags, or when the person who showed up seemed like they'd rather be somewhere else. This role asks for genuine engagement with both the physical plant and the people living in it. That combination of technical competence and resident-facing warmth is harder to find than most job postings acknowledge.

Day to day, you'll handle the full range of maintenance needs across the community: plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You'll support management in keeping the property aligned with community standards, help maintain the shop and equipment, manage inventory, and take key security seriously. Curb appeal is part of the job too. A property that looks cared for tells residents something about how they'll be treated, and you're one of the people making that statement.

You'll also be someone teammates rely on. Maintenance work in a residential community doesn't happen in isolation. There's coordination with leasing, communication with management, and plenty of moments where a resident is stressed about something in their home and you're the person standing in front of them. Composure and a decent attitude go a long way.

What separates a strong candidate here from someone who's technically qualified but a poor fit: the willingness to take ownership. Berkshire's in-house model means the property's condition reflects directly on the people who work there. Technicians who treat their community like their own tend to do better work, build stronger resident relationships, and move into lead or supervisor roles faster.

What you'll bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or similar setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with basic computer use and written communication in English
  • Reliability, attention to detail, and the ability to shift priorities without losing track of open work orders

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development support, a 25% rent discount, and solid insurance coverage. The company's ownership of its own assets means there's real investment in the teams who keep those properties running well.

job.title: Leasing Specialist - Part-Time
job.description:
Redstone Residential runs a large book of business: more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, split between student housing and conventional multi-family. They're one of the bigger third-party student housing operators in the country, and their conventional portfolio is growing. This part-time leasing role sits at their Logan, Utah community and pays $18.00 per hour with performance bonuses on top.

The day-to-day is front-desk focused. You'll greet prospects and residents, handle package intake, keep the lobby running smoothly, and answer questions as they come in. When the leasing team needs support, you step in: tours, application processing, and whatever else moves traffic through the door. The role is part-time, so the hours flex, but the expectation around reliability and consistency doesn't.

Entrata experience helps. A lot of student housing operators run on it, and Redstone is no exception. If you've used other property management software, that background transfers. If you haven't used any, be upfront about it.

Student housing leasing has a rhythm that's different from conventional. Prospects often tour with parents, leasing cycles compress into a short window, and move-in periods hit hard. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing role where the pace spikes without warning, that experience reads well here. The ability to stay composed when three people need something at once is genuinely useful in this setting.

Qualifications

  • 1 to 2 years of customer service or sales experience
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Basic computer proficiency: email, correspondence, data entry
  • Familiarity with Entrata or similar PM software (preferred, not required)
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Calm and dependable under pressure

This kind of role tends to be a starting point. Leasing specialists who learn the software, get comfortable with the sales process, and show up consistently are the ones who move into full-time leasing or assistant manager positions. Redstone has the portfolio size to make that path real rather than hypothetical.

job.title: Regional Property Manager - Atlanta Market
job.description:
Where Financial Acumen and People Leadership Meet

Regional property management is one of those roles where the skills you sharpen don't stay siloed. Reading a T-12, coaching a Community Manager through a tough delinquency month, and pushing occupancy in a competitive market all pull from the same core: pattern recognition, influence, and accountability. This role with AIR Communities in Atlanta asks you to do all of that across a portfolio of apartment communities, and to do it consistently enough that it compounds into something real.

AIR Communities operates in major markets with a reputation for running high-quality assets. The Atlanta Regional Property Manager position means you're responsible for the financial and operational performance of multiple communities. You're setting direction on budgets, revenue growth, and NOI while also staying close enough to leasing activity and resident satisfaction to catch problems before they show up in the numbers. The portfolio has Community Managers in place, and developing those managers is central to the job. The expectation is that you build the team's capacity, not just respond to gaps.

The Skills This Role Sharpens Most

Multi-site leadership accelerates certain skills faster than almost any other role in property management. You'll develop fluency in reading operational data across properties simultaneously, spotting which site needs a pricing adjustment versus which one has a maintenance backlog dragging satisfaction scores. A few specific capabilities this role will deepen:

  • Budget oversight across multiple assets, with direct accountability for revenue targets and expense control
  • Sales process coaching, helping leasing teams use metrics and traffic data to close more effectively
  • Platform proficiency across tools like OneSite, SmartRent, and Salesforce in a real operational context
  • Leading diverse teams through performance conversations, coaching cycles, and high-turnover stretches
  • Compliance and legal standard adherence across a multi-property footprint

Candidates who succeed here typically arrive with at least five years in property management or a high-performance service environment, and at least five years leading sizable teams through competitive, results-measured work. Hospitality and retail backgrounds translate well if the fundamentals are sharp, but the financial layer of this role requires genuine comfort with budgets, not just familiarity with the vocabulary.

What's Distinctive About This Position

AIR's model leans toward institutional discipline. They own and operate, which means Regional Managers work within a structure that has real capital behind it and clear performance expectations. For a Regional with ambitions beyond Atlanta, that context matters: you're building a track record at a company where operational results are visible and career development is explicitly supported through training programs, tuition reimbursement, and certification funding.

The Atlanta multifamily market has enough submarkets and Class A supply pressure to make this a genuinely demanding portfolio to run. Strong candidates will read that as interesting rather than intimidating. The compensation range of $120,000 to $130,000 base plus bonus reflects the level of accountability involved, and the full benefits package includes a 401(k) with a 6% employer contribution and paid parental leave of up to 16 weeks.

From a career arc standpoint, Regional Manager roles at well-capitalized operators like AIR tend to position people well for VP of Operations, Director-level roles, or ownership-side asset management. The skills you'll sharpen here: multi-site P&L accountability, talent development, and performance culture creation, transfer cleanly into any senior leadership path in multifamily.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's Tuesday morning, and a tenant on the third floor is flagging a maintenance issue while an operating expense reconciliation sits half-finished on your screen and a vendor invoice is waiting for your review before it can go to the property manager for approval. That's not a bad day. That's the job.

What This Role Actually Covers

Lincoln Property Company is looking for an Assistant Property Manager in Dallas to support day-to-day operations across commercial, industrial, or retail assets. This is a broad, hands-on role inside one of the largest private real estate firms in the country, managing more than 720 million square feet across its combined portfolio. You'll work closely with the property manager and engage directly with tenants, vendors, and internal accounting teams on a regular basis.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Responding to tenant needs and coordinating with building and administrative staff to resolve issues in line with lease obligations and company policy
  • Reviewing and recommending vendor invoice approvals within the parameters of the management agreement and authorization limits
  • Supporting monthly report and budget package preparation to meet client deadlines and accuracy standards
  • Collecting data and drafting CAM and operating expense reconciliations in coordination with accounting
  • Handling lease administration tasks including setup, amendments, and system updates
  • Coordinating and documenting tenant move-ins and move-outs, including walk-throughs with tenants and tenant improvement teams
  • Assisting with vendor sourcing, bid coordination, and procurement support
  • Contributing to emergency response planning and participating in required drills
  • Providing work direction and performance feedback to direct reports where applicable

This is a fully in-office position based in Dallas. Property inspections are part of the routine, so expect to be on your feet and at the asset, not just behind a desk.

What You Bring and What You'll Build

The role requires a working knowledge of financial terms and concepts, including the ability to run basic financial analysis and calculate figures like percentages accurately. Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office is expected. Familiarity with AP systems and CMMS platforms is a plus, as is prior exposure to commercial office, retail, or industrial properties. Strong written and verbal communication skills matter here, because you'll be the face of the management team in a lot of tenant interactions. A bachelor's degree is preferred, though relevant experience combined with education is also considered. One to two years of related experience is the baseline.

What this role builds is equally worth naming. CAM reconciliation work is a skill set that carries real weight in commercial property management and opens doors to senior PM and portfolio roles. Strong candidates coming out of this position tend to move into full property manager responsibilities, particularly those who develop fluency across lease administration, financial reporting, and vendor management at the same time. The professionals who distinguish themselves here are the ones who own the administrative details with the same attention they bring to tenant relationships. Both sides of that equation matter at Lincoln.

Lincoln supports career development through mentorship, training programs, and a culture that encourages initiative within a structured platform. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) options (traditional and Roth), flexible time off, and company-paid life insurance and long-term disability, among other offerings.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What This Role Actually Builds

The Assistant Community Manager role at a multifamily property is one of the most skill-dense positions in residential property management. You're touching leasing performance, financial operations, compliance, and team development at the same time. At Waypoint Management Services in Vero Beach, that means working alongside the Community Manager to keep a premier multifamily community running well across all of those dimensions simultaneously.

The financial side gets real here. You'll work through delinquency, support rent collection, track the rent roll, and flag reporting issues before they compound. If you've only done leasing up to this point, this is the role where you start reading numbers, not just running traffic. That shift from leasing consultant to ACM is one of the most important career transitions in multifamily, and the financial exposure you build here is exactly what separates future Community Managers from people who plateau in leasing.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The week-to-week workload covers a lot of ground:

  • Supporting the leasing team through coaching, training, and operational accountability
  • Tracking make-ready schedules and occupancy reports to keep turns on schedule
  • Monitoring renewals and helping execute pricing recommendations based on market surveys and occupancy goals
  • Executing sales and marketing strategies to bring in qualified prospects and retain current residents
  • Keeping lease files, resident records, and administrative reporting accurate and current
  • Maintaining compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations
  • Assisting with evictions when delinquency reaches that point

Weekend availability is required, which is standard at stabilized multifamily properties. If that's new information, factor it into your decision. If it's familiar, you already know the tradeoff: weekday flexibility often compensates for it.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

Waypoint prefers Yardi experience, and that preference matters. Candidates who already know how to pull reports, process charges, and manage lease data inside a property management platform can contribute from week one instead of spending the first month learning the software while also learning the property. Microsoft Office proficiency and comfort with social media round out the tech expectations, but Yardi fluency is the real differentiator at the application stage.

Beyond software, the ACMs who move up quickly tend to be the ones who treat the financial reports as seriously as the leasing board. If you're already tracking NOI at a conceptual level, monitoring where delinquency is trending, and thinking about concessions in terms of their effect on net effective rent, you'll find this role accelerates your trajectory toward a Community Manager seat faster than most positions at this level.

Waypoint offers a compensation package that includes monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount program, subsidized medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one, a 401(k) with company match, 120 hours of PTO in year one with progressive increases, and a professional development program. The bonus structure ties your income to the property's leasing performance, which keeps incentives aligned and rewards people who actually drive results.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Westgate on Third)
job.description:
Leasing is a conversion game. Traffic comes in, your job is to turn it into signed leases, and every interaction between a prospect's first call and their move-in date runs through you. At Westgate on Third in Bloomington, BAM Companies is looking for a Leasing Consultant who can work that full cycle well: fast follow-up, confident tours, clean paperwork, and residents who feel taken care of before they ever get their keys.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

You're the first point of contact for prospective residents reaching out by phone, email, or walk-in. The expectation is quick response times and genuine conversation, not a scripted pitch. You'll tour units, explain pricing and features, and walk prospects through the application and deposit process all the way to lease execution. Between tours, you're maintaining show units and the leasing office so everything stays sharp, logging activity in the CRM, and supporting the property manager on marketing pushes, outreach events, and community programming.

Weekends are part of the schedule here. Bloomington is a university market, and leasing activity doesn't pause for a Monday-Friday workweek. A reliable vehicle is required since outreach and off-site activity come with the role.

What BAM Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent; some college experience is a plus
  • Background in leasing, retail, hospitality, or any sales-adjacent role
  • Strong follow-up habits and genuine comfort talking to people through a major decision
  • Basic CRM and computer proficiency
  • Organized, reliable, and able to juggle multiple prospects at different stages of the funnel
  • NALP credentials, bilingual skills, or prior real estate interest are preferred but not required

Compensation and Benefits

Base pay runs $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience, location, and overall fit. On top of that, leasing commissions add performance-based income tied directly to signed leases. BAM also offers 15.5 paid holidays starting on day one, PTO that builds after 90 days and grows again at your one-year mark, and a full insurance package covering medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and pet coverage. Housing discounts at BAM properties are available if you want to live where you work.

Bloomington's rental market is heavily driven by Indiana University's enrollment cycle, which means leasing activity hits predictable peaks around application and renewal season. Consultants who learn to read that rhythm, stay on top of their follow-up queue during high-traffic windows, and close cleanly under volume pressure tend to build a strong performance record quickly. That track record is what typically opens doors to Assistant Manager and Property Manager roles within a company like BAM.

job.title: Groundskeeper/Porter - Los Angeles, CA
job.description:
What This Role Is Really About

At a well-run multifamily property, curb appeal is a direct line to occupancy. A prospect pulling into the parking lot forms an impression before they ever meet a leasing agent, and that impression affects traffic-to-lease conversion. The Groundskeeper/Porter at Ames Lofts in Los Angeles owns that first impression.
