Berkshire Residential Investments operates a vertically integrated platform, meaning they own and manage their own communities, so the standards here reflect a real investment stake in the asset, not just a third-party contract obligation.

Berkshire is offering $18.50 to $22.00 per hour for this position, depending on experience, with a benefits package that includes health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a 25% rent discount.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

This is a physically active, outdoor-forward role. You'll walk the grounds and common areas on a regular cycle to keep the property clear of litter and debris. Curb appeal isn't a buzzword here: it's a measurable standard that shows up in how the property photographs, how it reads during a prospect tour, and how current residents feel about renewing. Beyond grounds maintenance, you'll assist the maintenance team when needed, which can include helping with turns and make-ready prep work between residents. Strong customer service matters too. You'll interact with residents and prospective renters on the property daily.

  • Routine grounds and common area walkthroughs to remove debris and maintain appearance
  • Support maintenance staff with tasks as directed
  • Uphold service standards when interacting with residents and prospects
  • Attention to physical detail across the entire exterior of the property

What Strong Candidates Bring

Prior experience in cleaning, construction, or general maintenance gives you a practical foundation, though Berkshire lists this as preferred rather than required. What matters more is that you're genuinely comfortable with physical work, you take pride in how a property looks, and you stay consistent even when no one is watching. In a market like Los Angeles, where Class A lease-ups compete hard on presentation and resident experience, a Groundskeeper who treats the property like it's their own asset is a real operational advantage.

Basic computer proficiency and strong English communication skills round out what Berkshire is looking for. This role carries more visibility than many people expect. A well-kept property retains residents, supports renewals, and keeps delinquency issues from compounding due to dissatisfied tenants looking for reasons to leave. The Groundskeeper is part of that retention equation.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's 8:45 on a Tuesday morning. A resident is at your door about a maintenance issue that was supposed to be closed out last week, your leasing consultant just flagged a delinquency report that needs attention before noon, and you have a call with your Regional Manager at ten. That's a normal morning in this role.

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a portfolio that spans student housing and a growing conventional multifamily side. The Community Manager position in Rexburg, Idaho is the top site-level role, meaning the property's operational and financial outcomes run through you. You report to the Regional Manager, but day-to-day, you're the decision-maker on the ground.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll own the lease-up strategy and occupancy goals, track KPIs through Redstone's systems, and manage the property to an approved operating budget with P&L accountability. Delinquency collections, renewal outreach, and marketing coordination are all part of your scope. You'll also submit weekly and monthly performance reports and may oversee projects that range from marketing campaigns to construction-adjacent capex work.

Because this is a student housing market, the leasing calendar is compressed and cyclical. Renewal season arrives fast, traffic spikes come in waves, and concessions strategy matters more than it does at a typical conventional lease-up. Rexburg is a college town built around BYU-Idaho, which means your resident base is transient, your turnover is predictable but high-volume, and community relationships with campus contacts carry real weight for referral traffic.

You'll also be the person setting the tone for customer service on your team. That means training staff, running performance evaluations, and being honest when someone needs to improve.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • At least one year of property management experience, with direct experience in student housing or multifamily
  • Demonstrated budget management and P&L ownership
  • Professional presentation and prior experience in client-facing situations
  • Ability to juggle multiple processes simultaneously under real pressure
  • Comfort with property management software (Entrata experience is a plus, but not required)
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office
  • A team-oriented approach, including the ability to give constructive feedback and hold people accountable

The compensation for this role is $16.00 per hour (non-exempt, full-time), with the ability to earn up to an additional 20% through performance bonuses. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer matching, short-term disability, an employee assistance program, and continued education and professional development support.

The candidates who tend to thrive here aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who can hold a leasing conversation and read a budget in the same afternoon without losing focus on either. Student housing rewards people who stay organized under volume, communicate directly with residents and staff, and treat occupancy targets like real commitments rather than suggestions.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance work at an apartment community is physical, repetitive, sometimes inconvenient, and genuinely important. At Fairstead's Scottsville, Kentucky property, a Maintenance Technician keeps housing functional for residents who depend on affordable, well-managed homes. The role draws on a specific combination of skills every single day: mechanical aptitude, electrical knowledge, systems thinking, and the kind of attention to detail that catches a problem before it becomes an emergency.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Electrical diagnostics are a real part of this job. You'll check wiring for compliance, identify problems, and handle minor repairs correctly. That requires comfort with basic electrical systems, not just a willingness to try. Mechanical skills come into play across HVAC, plumbing, appliances, and general fixtures. Preventative maintenance is a core discipline here, not an afterthought. You're running scheduled inspections on buildings and equipment, checking safety systems monthly, and managing an inventory of supplies and tools so nothing falls through the cracks when a repair comes up.

Make-ready work is part of the rotation too. When a unit turns, you're cleaning and preparing it so the next resident moves into a home that's actually ready. That work is unglamorous and physically demanding, and it matters a great deal to occupancy.

The on-call rotation is honest about what this job asks of you. Emergency maintenance problems don't wait for business hours. If you've worked apartment maintenance before, you already know this. If you're coming from a similar service technician background, it's worth being clear-eyed about: after-hours calls happen, and they're part of this role.

Qualifications Worth Knowing

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or commercial setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems and the ability to diagnose and repair minor issues
  • General mechanical skills across plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and fixtures
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential preferred
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds without assistance and stand for extended periods
  • Written and verbal communication skills sufficient to document work and communicate with residents and staff

Working Within Fairstead's Operation

Fairstead owns and manages over 30,000 units across 28 states, with development, construction, and property management handled under one platform. That integration matters at the property level because decisions about capital work, vendor relationships, and maintenance standards move through a company that actually understands operations from the inside. For a technician, that typically means clearer systems, better tools access, and management that knows what maintenance work involves.

The company also takes a data-driven approach to operations, including maintenance tracking. That won't eliminate the physical side of the work, but technicians who document well and communicate clearly tend to have a longer runway at organizations like this. Strong candidates in this role combine trade skill with the discipline to keep records accurate and communicate problems before they escalate. That combination is what separates a good technician from one who just fixes things when asked.

job.title: Community Manager - Delaware Pines
job.description:
Community managers at conventional properties carry a deceptively broad mandate. You're running a small business: hiring, collections, leasing, maintenance coordination, vendor oversight, and resident relations, all inside a single job title. At a property like Delaware Pines in Huntington Beach, that breadth is exactly what this role demands.

This is a part-time position, which is worth saying plainly. The pay range runs $24 to $25 per hour depending on experience, and the role does not include benefits eligibility. For someone building their PM resume or returning to the industry, it can be a solid fit. For someone who needs full-time income and benefits, that's a practical mismatch to weigh before applying.

The Scope of the Work

Reporting to a Regional Manager, you'd carry full operational responsibility for the property. That means staffing: hiring, training, and evaluating on-site personnel, not just supervising them once they're settled. It means financial oversight, including rent collection, delinquency management, and daily bank deposits under California landlord-tenant law. Budget prep and expense monitoring fall here too.

On the leasing side, you'd manage available units through approved advertising, conduct showings, keep leasing records clean, and support renewals to protect occupancy. Market awareness matters here. Huntington Beach carries a competitive coastal submarket, and pricing decisions need to stay calibrated to what's actually happening in the comp set, not just what the budget assumed six months ago.

Resident relations includes the full range: service request follow-through within 24 to 48 hours when possible, fair housing compliance at every touchpoint, and the general work of keeping people satisfied enough to renew. Regular inspections of units, common areas, and grounds round out the day-to-day.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • One to two years of direct property management experience, meaning you've actually run leasing activity and collections, not just assisted
  • Working knowledge of California landlord-tenant law and Fair Housing, applied in practice rather than just on paper
  • Comfort in property management software alongside Microsoft Office
  • Genuine organizational discipline, because a community manager without a system for tracking delinquency, open work orders, and lease expirations will feel it quickly
  • A college degree or relevant coursework, preferred but not hard-required

What separates a solid applicant from a great one here is usually the delinquency piece. Managers who treat collections as a monthly scramble tend to struggle under California's procedural requirements. The ones who run clean ledgers and communicate early with residents before accounts age are the ones who actually keep NOI stable. That discipline shows up in interviews if you know what to look for.

Sunrise Management describes its operating philosophy around what they call resident hospitality, a practical orientation toward retention and service quality rather than just occupancy targets. If that framing resonates with how you've approached resident relations in past roles, that's a reasonable culture signal worth taking seriously.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Third-party management at scale creates a specific kind of regional role. Asset Living oversees portfolios that cut across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing, which means their regional managers don't just monitor one asset class. They manage across property types, ownership structures, and reporting relationships simultaneously. This Raleigh-based Regional Manager position sits inside that complexity.

Raleigh's rental market has remained competitive through recent years of sustained in-migration and new supply coming online. That combination puts real pressure on NOI: concessions are a live conversation at many properties, and occupancy targets require active marketing strategies rather than passive lease renewal cycles. A regional manager here needs to read T-3 and T-12 trends together, because short-term dips in a supply-heavy submarket can obscure fundamentals that are actually sound.

What This Role Covers

This is a full portfolio operations role. You'll carry responsibility for personnel, leasing performance, financial outcomes, maintenance standards, and compliance across all sites you oversee. On any given week that means reviewing budget variances and writing explanations for line items that have drifted significantly over projection, approving timesheets, conducting property inspections, and working with on-site Community Managers on staffing decisions including hiring, coaching, and when necessary, termination. The personnel management piece here is real work, not oversight from a distance. You'll screen candidates, document performance issues properly, coordinate with HR, and sign off on salary requests before they move up the chain.

Financially, you'll build yearly operating budgets, track income and expense performance monthly, and flag capital improvement needs before they become deferred maintenance problems. You'll also review vendor proposals and monitor work in progress on larger projects. On the leasing side, you'll develop annual marketing plans, assess staff closing techniques, and build resident retention programs that reduce turnover costs at the property level.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple properties simultaneously, with measurable NOI results
  • Comfort reading financial reports at the ownership level, not just the property level
  • Direct experience with personnel decisions: coaching plans, written evaluations, and terminations handled correctly
  • Familiarity with fair housing compliance as an operational habit, not an occasional training topic
  • Ability to develop a marketing strategy that responds to actual local traffic data, not generic templates

The candidates who struggle in regional roles at third-party management firms are usually strong at one function but thin in another. Operators who are excellent with financials but passive about staff development find that site performance erodes quietly. The reverse is equally common. Asset Living's portfolio breadth means the regional manager who performs well here typically develops a cross-property type fluency that opens paths into senior vice president roles or asset management functions over time.

job.title: Business Manager - Station 250
job.description:
Most Class A lease-ups eventually settle into a stabilized rhythm, and that's exactly where a property's financial discipline gets tested. The Business Manager role at Station 250 in Mundelein exists to own that rhythm, keeping occupancy strong, budgets grounded in reality, and a team performing at the level a luxury asset demands.

Olympus Property has held a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which is worth noting for candidates weighing company culture alongside the role itself. For a Business Manager, culture isn't abstract. It shapes how onsite teams respond to difficult residents, how maintenance approaches make-readies, and how front-office staff treats a prospect walking in on a Wednesday afternoon.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope property management position. You'll own the financial performance of the asset, which means building and tracking budgets, reviewing monthly financials, projecting NOI, and presenting strategy to Regional Leadership. On the operational side, you'll oversee both office and maintenance staff, manage vendor contracts (bidding, negotiating, and holding vendors accountable to scope), and make sure units, common areas, and amenity spaces stay market-ready. Leasing and retention programs fall under your direction as well. Keeping occupancy up at a luxury address means the renewal program has to be sharp and the traffic conversion has to be consistent.

RealPage/Knock/Onesite experience is strongly preferred. At a Class A property, those platforms touch everything from prospect communication to lease execution to delinquency tracking, so a candidate who already works fluently in that stack will ramp up faster.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least two years of multifamily property management experience, with preference for luxury or Class A assets
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial reports, not just generating them
  • Experience managing a mixed team of leasing and maintenance staff
  • Familiarity with vendor contract negotiation and project oversight
  • Availability Monday through Friday with flexibility for after-hours resident events and occasional emergencies

The candidates who stand out at this level tend to be the ones who've already managed a stabilized asset through at least one full budget cycle. Understanding how to build an annual business plan, defend line items with a Regional VP, and adjust mid-year when actuals drift from projections separates a solid leasing manager from a property manager who can genuinely run a building.

Compensation is $80,000 to $90,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others. Olympus also offers structured career pathing and leadership development, which matters if you're thinking about where this role goes next. Business Managers at well-run operators tend to move toward Regional Manager tracks, and Olympus has built internal infrastructure to support that progression.

job.title: Maintenance Technician- Axcess15
job.description:
Apartment maintenance at a 200-plus unit property is a volume game. Service requests stack up, turns come in waves, and the on-call rotation means a leaking water heater doesn't care what time it is. MG Properties is hiring a Maintenance Technician for Axcess15 Apartments in Portland, and the posting is straightforward about what the work actually involves.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

The bulk of your time will split between completing resident service requests and keeping the property's common areas, grounds, and offices clean and functional. When units turn, you're doing the make-ready work: painting, appliance repairs, punch list items, and whatever else it takes to get the unit rent-ready. Trades coverage is broad here. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repairs all fall within scope, so this isn't a role where you can be strong in one area and shrug at everything else. MG Properties specifically wants someone with at least two years of apartment maintenance experience at a property of comparable size. That background matters because the pace and the variety of problems at a 200-unit community are different from smaller sites.

The on-call rotation is real. Emergency calls happen after hours, and reliable transportation is a firm requirement, not a preference. If that part of the job is a dealbreaker, it's worth knowing upfront rather than finding out during orientation.

What MG Properties Offers

  • Monthly bonuses and company profit sharing
  • 10 days PTO accrued per year, plus 10 paid holidays and 2 personal days
  • 40 hours paid sick time
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus an Employee Assistance Program
  • Life insurance, FSA, and dependent care spending account
  • Rental discounts

MG Properties has been operating across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, with a portfolio that spans acquisition, development, rehabilitation, and ongoing management. That scale means internal mobility is a real possibility for technicians who perform well. The step from technician to lead tech or maintenance supervisor is a common trajectory at regional operators of this size, and those roles come with meaningful pay differences and responsibility over a team rather than just a work order queue.

Strong candidates will bring multi-trade competence and a customer service orientation that holds up when a resident is frustrated about a slow repair. The combination of technical skill and communication is what separates technicians who stay and grow from those who burn out. If you can work a full turn efficiently, handle an emergency call calmly, and follow up with residents in a way that leaves them feeling heard, you'll do well here.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's the first week of August at The Parlor, and every bed on the property needs to turn in roughly 72 hours. Your punch list isn't a list anymore. It's a war room. That's the heartbeat of student housing, and this role sits right at the center of it.

The Role

The Scion Group is hiring an Assistant Community Manager (titled internally as Assistant General Manager) for The Parlor, their student housing community in San Marcos, Texas. This is a full-scope operations role. You'll work alongside the General Manager on financial performance, resident accounts, leasing activity, and facilities. When the GM is out, you're running the asset.

On the financial side, your benchmark is clear: delinquency below 2% at month end. You'll manage accounts receivable, post damage charges from quarterly inspections, process final billing at move-out, and assist with month-end reporting and account reconciliation. You'll also enforce late fee and NSF policies consistently, which matters more than most candidates realize. A student housing property with loose collections practices can see delinquency creep up fast given the transactional nature of the resident base.

Leasing and revenue are part of the job too. You'll manage sales interactions directly and coach your team through them, run weekly market surveys, oversee concessions and promotional materials within budget, and use KPIs to spot trends before they become problems. Traffic-to-lease ratios, occupancy targets, renewal velocity. You'll be expected to know these numbers and act on them.

Facilities and curb appeal fall under your watch as well. That means regular inspections of vacant bed spaces and common areas, coordinating work orders, and keeping the property in a condition that supports both leasing and resident retention. In student housing, the physical condition of a community is a direct sales tool.

Annual turn planning is one of the most operationally demanding stretches in this business. You'll help lead the team through that process, which in student housing means managing hundreds of move-outs and move-ins in a compressed window, all while keeping service quality intact.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential community operations
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata experience preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to handle resident escalations, collections enforcement, and compliance with Fair Housing requirements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort working non-traditional hours during peak leasing periods and on-call rotations

Candidates who stand out in student housing ACM roles typically come in with a solid handle on collections discipline and a genuine interest in the leasing side. The properties that hit their occupancy and NOI targets usually have an ACM who treats delinquency as a daily metric, not a month-end cleanup task. Familiarity with the San Marcos market and the Texas State University enrollment cycle is a real advantage here, though not a stated requirement.

San Marcos is a competitive student housing market given its enrollment growth trajectory. Knowing how to read concession trends and time lease-up decisions around academic calendars separates good operators from average ones at properties like this.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, learning reimbursement, and a discretionary annual bonus.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The leasing consultant role at Hawthorne Residential Partners' Integra Landings community in Orange City, Florida puts you at the front of the resident experience from first contact to move-in. On a typical day, you're fielding inquiries by phone, email, and online portals, converting that traffic into tours, and walking prospects through apartments in a way that connects the floorplan to their actual lifestyle. That last part takes more skill than it sounds. Closing a lease requires listening well enough to understand what someone actually needs, then showing them how this community meets it.

Beyond leasing, you'll work on occupancy and renewal goals alongside the broader site team, help coordinate resident events, and keep the leasing office and common areas presentable. Hawthorne also expects you to track competitor properties and stay current on local market conditions, which sharpens your ability to position the community accurately against alternatives a prospect might be considering.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or apartment leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Comfort communicating across channels: in person, phone, and written correspondence
  • A genuine ability to read people and move a conversation toward a decision without being pushy
  • Accuracy when handling leasing applications, verifications, and move-in paperwork
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Valid driver's license; CALP accreditation is a plus
  • Availability for the standard schedule: Monday through Friday 9 AM to 6 PM, Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off each week

Skills This Role Builds and Where It Goes

Leasing is one of the best entry points into property management because it gives you hands-on exposure to the full resident lifecycle: lead generation, qualifying prospects, the application and approval process, move-in coordination, and retention through renewals. The skills you develop here, specifically objection handling, occupancy awareness, and relationship-building with residents, transfer directly into an assistant community manager role, which Hawthorne explicitly supports through a structured Career Path Program.

Strong candidates come in knowing how to sell without pressure and leave having learned how to read occupancy trends, respond to delinquency early through renewal efforts, and contribute meaningfully to a site's NOI through consistent lease conversions. The difference between a leasing consultant who stays in the role and one who advances quickly usually comes down to how well they understand the numbers behind the community, not just the people in front of them. Hawthorne's compensation structure, which includes monthly leasing and renewal commissions on top of an hourly base, gives you a financial incentive to develop that understanding early.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II (Ironworks)
job.description:
Maintenance at a Company That Invests Long-Term

Prometheus Real Estate Group has been holding and operating apartments in the Bay Area since 1965, and their approach shows it. They don't flip properties or chase short-term yield. That means the maintenance team is expected to care for communities the way a long-term owner would, not just patch things up until the next sale. For a technician, that distinction matters day to day.

This Maintenance Technician II role sits at the Ironworks community in Sunnyvale, a market where residents have high expectations and operational standards follow suit. You'd be part of the team keeping the physical experience of living there consistent and reliable.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A significant part of this role is turns. When a resident moves out, you're running the make-ready process from start to finish: completing the punch list, troubleshooting whatever the previous occupant left behind, and getting the unit back to a condition that earns the next resident's confidence. The work spans appliance repair and installation, plumbing, carpentry, electrical, and painting. No single discipline dominates, which means you need real breadth rather than deep specialization in one area.

Service requests fill the rest of your schedule. Prometheus calls their residents "Neighbors," and the expectation is that you treat the relationship that way. When someone submits a work order, they're trusting that you'll show up prepared, communicate clearly, and actually fix the problem. The customer service component here isn't a soft add-on to the job description. It's central.

On-call availability is required, so this role does carry after-hours responsibility. That's honest. It also comes with standby pay and on-call premium pay, which reflects that Prometheus has thought about how to compensate people fairly for that commitment.

  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and painting
  • Comfortable using basic computer tools (work order systems, email)
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally; most work is performed outdoors in moderate temperatures
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Strong English communication skills for resident interaction and workplace safety

The Team and the Upside

Prometheus is a vertically integrated company with over 500 employees and a portfolio of more than 13,000 apartments across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. That scale creates real internal mobility. Technicians who develop strong diagnostic skills and build trust with their site teams often grow into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles over time. The company also offers a Training Coach Bonus and educational assistance, which signals that they'll invest in developing people who want to grow.

Pay runs $31.00 to $32.25 per hour, with a semi-annual discretionary bonus and additional incentive programs including referral and renovation bonuses. The benefits package covers medical, vision, and dental at 100% for employees and eligible dependents, along with 401(k) matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and twelve paid holidays including your birthday.

If you care about the physical quality of the place where people live and you want to work for an owner who does too, the fit here is worth taking seriously.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Regional management at Asset Living pulls on a specific mix of skills that few property management roles demand simultaneously: financial analysis, personnel development, leasing strategy, and physical asset oversight, all applied across a multi-property portfolio rather than a single community. This position covers sites across Fairfield, Vacaville, Walnut Creek, and San Francisco, a geography that spans Class B garden-style suburban submarkets and the denser Bay Area and East Bay corridors. The operational and market conditions can shift significantly from one city to the next, so portfolio thinking matters here as much as site-level execution.

What This Role Actually Requires Day to Day

The financial side of this position is substantive. You'll develop annual operating budgets, review T-12 performance, monitor NOI trends across your portfolio, and write monthly variance explanations on income and expense line items that fall outside plan. When capex projects come up, you're evaluating bids, tracking work in progress, and confirming ownership reports close accurately. That kind of financial accountability means you need to read a P&L comfortably and understand what's driving delinquency or occupancy shifts before you see them in the numbers.

On the personnel side, you're hiring and coaching community managers and their teams, handling performance documentation, approving timesheets, and managing the full cycle from onboarding to, when necessary, termination. Asset Living operates as a third-party management firm, so consistency with company policy and client reporting standards is non-negotiable. Your site staff represent both Asset and the property owner, and it's your job to ensure those standards hold across every property in your region.

Leasing oversight means reviewing traffic conversion, evaluating whether concessions are warranted, assessing make-ready timelines, and building annual marketing plans that reflect local demand. If a property is running high MTM exposure or struggling with lease-up velocity, you're the one developing the strategy to correct it, not just flagging the problem.

Skills That Carry Weight Here

  • Demonstrated ability to manage NOI at the portfolio level, including budget development and monthly financial reporting
  • Experience supervising onsite teams across multiple properties, with a track record of effective coaching and performance management
  • Familiarity with fair housing compliance and risk management in an offsite leadership capacity
  • Competency with leasing strategy, including occupancy management, concession analysis, and resident retention programs
  • Experience reviewing vendor contracts, monitoring construction or rehab work, and coordinating maintenance standards across sites

Working Within Asset Living's Structure

Asset Living is one of the larger third-party management operators in the country, ranked in the NMHC top 50, and holds Accredited Management Organization status through IREM. That structure gives regional managers real institutional support, including HR, training benchmarks, and reporting systems, but it also means you're accountable to both company standards and individual ownership groups simultaneously. Strong regional managers in this kind of environment tend to be people who can hold the line on policy while still building genuine relationships with onsite staff and ownership stakeholders.

The Bay Area and East Bay markets where this portfolio operates have seen meaningful rent moderation in some submarkets over the past few years, which puts a premium on retention and operational efficiency rather than riding market tailwinds. That context makes the NOI discipline and resident retention programming parts of this role genuinely important, not just boxes to check.

job.title: Groundskeeper/Porter -City Ctr, Houston, TX
job.description:
Groundskeeping at a Class A urban property like Tinsley on the Park requires a specific skill set: sharp attention to detail, physical stamina, and the ability to represent a community well in front of residents every single day. This role centers on those three things.

What This Work Requires

The core skill here is observation. A good groundskeeper doesn't wait for problems to get reported. They catch litter, debris, and damage during routine property walks before residents notice. Curb appeal drives first impressions for prospective residents and sets the tone for existing ones, so the eye for detail matters constantly, not just at scheduled intervals.

Physical fitness is a genuine requirement, not a checkbox. This work involves regular movement, lifting, bending, and outdoor exposure across the property grounds and common areas. Prior experience in cleaning, construction, or facilities maintenance helps you hit the ground running, but the mindset of ownership over your space matters more than credentials.

Basic computer literacy and clear written and spoken English are needed for logging work orders and communicating with the maintenance team. You'll also assist maintenance staff when they need an extra set of hands, so some comfort working alongside technicians on general tasks is useful.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Walk property grounds and common areas regularly to collect litter and debris
  • Maintain curb appeal standards across the exterior, amenities, and shared spaces
  • Support maintenance staff with tasks as directed
  • Interact professionally with residents and guests during daily operations

Working at Berkshire

Berkshire Residential Investments owns and manages its own portfolio, which means decisions about properties happen in-house. For groundskeeping staff, that typically translates to more consistent standards and direct support from the management team rather than split accountability across a third-party structure. Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, insurance coverage, and personal development plans.

The strongest candidates in this type of role take genuine ownership of their section of the property. The difference between a good porter and a great one usually comes down to whether they treat the grounds as their own or just a task list to complete. At a community like Tinsley on the Park, that distinction shows.

job.title: Resident Manager - Lanai Village
job.description:
Resident management at the property level is one of the most skill-intensive roles in this industry. You're doing leasing, collections, maintenance coordination, compliance, and resident relations simultaneously, often before 9 a.m. on a Tuesday. The Resident Manager position at Lanai Village in Spring Valley leans on all of it.

The Skills This Role Runs On

California landlord-tenant law shapes almost every decision a site manager makes here. Security deposit procedures at move-out, proper notice requirements, Fair Housing compliance during leasing, Cal/OSHA awareness on property. Candidates who've operated in other states often underestimate how much California-specific knowledge this work requires. That's not a knock on anyone; it's just the reality of this market.

Beyond compliance, the role demands a specific combination of financial discipline and interpersonal range. You're collecting rent, monitoring delinquency, issuing receipts, and making bank deposits on one hand. On the other, you're the face of the community, handling resident concerns, conducting tours, and keeping retention from slipping. Bilingual ability in English and Spanish is a real operational advantage here, not just a checkbox, given the demographics of the Spring Valley area.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Conduct unit, amenity, and common area inspections to stay ahead of maintenance and safety issues
  • Manage work orders and push toward 24-48 hour completion windows
  • Oversee move-in and move-out inspections in compliance with California security deposit law
  • Handle leasing from inquiry through executed lease, maintaining accurate applicant records
  • Collect rents and deposits, track delinquency, and coordinate with supervisors before any legal action
  • Verify that contractors and vendors carry proper licensing and insurance
  • Support budgeting and expense tracking alongside regional leadership

This position is on-site and live-in, so if you haven't done resident management before, understand what that means practically. The property is also your address. The line between work and personal time softens. Experienced site managers adjust; people new to the format often don't anticipate how that dynamic feels until they're in it.

What Makes the Difference Here

Sunrise Management operates with a hospitality-forward philosophy, which in practice means resident experience is taken seriously as an operational metric, not just a cultural talking point. Strong candidates for this role tend to have sound judgment on when to handle something themselves and when to escalate. The ones who struggle typically either over-escalate minor resident issues or sit on problems too long before looping in regional. Neither extreme works well in a lean on-site structure like this one.

Two or more years of property management experience is the baseline expectation. Comfort with property management software and Microsoft Office rounds out the technical side. The compensation range is $16.90 to $20.00 per hour, with a medical, dental, and vision package, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Field maintenance at scale is a different animal than site-based apartment maintenance. At Lessen, you're not assigned to one property where you learn every quirk of the HVAC over time. You're moving across a portfolio, reading work orders cold, diagnosing fast, and executing without a lot of hand-holding. That demands a specific skill set: strong diagnostic instincts across multiple trade areas, solid time management, and the ability to own a job from intake to close without constant oversight.

Lessen operates a tech-enabled platform that routes work orders across a network serving over one million properties nationally. In the Frisco market, that means you'll work across a range of residential property types. The DFW suburb corridor has seen significant build-out over the past decade, and the portfolio demand reflects that: newer construction with its own maintenance profile, alongside older stock that needs more hands-on intervention. Technicians who've worked both ends of that spectrum tend to hit the ground running here.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your day centers on assigned work orders. You'll manage your own schedule, track against budgets tied to each job, and handle the full scope of general property maintenance across residential units. Lessen's model emphasizes quality over volume, which means you're expected to close work correctly the first time rather than rush through a punch list and leave callbacks behind.

Core competencies the role draws on daily:

  • Plumbing repairs and fixture work
  • Electrical troubleshooting within scope (outlets, switches, fixtures)
  • HVAC filter maintenance and basic mechanical diagnostics
  • Appliance repair and replacement
  • Carpentry, drywall, and interior finish work
  • General exterior and common area upkeep

You'll document your work through Lessen's platform and coordinate with the operations team as needed. The company provides a fleet vehicle with a fuel card, so you're not putting miles on your own truck. A $50 monthly tool allowance and $50 cell phone allowance round out the field support.

What Makes This Position Worth Considering

The structure here is genuinely different from most property maintenance roles. There's no on-call rotation and the schedule runs weekdays. For experienced techs who've spent years on rotating emergency lines, that's a meaningful quality-of-life change. The $1,500 sign-on bonus and a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings add upside beyond the base hourly rate, which starts at $23 and goes to $27 depending on verified experience and skill level.

Lessen is a venture-backed company expanding nationally, and they're explicit about internal growth paths into Lead Technician and Field Maintenance Manager roles. Technicians who document well, close work orders cleanly, and demonstrate sound judgment on-site tend to move into those tracks. OSHA training is provided, which matters for techs who haven't had a corporate employer cover that credential before.

The minimum bar is real: three or more years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a related trade. If you've built that foundation, the role offers a structure that rewards self-direction and consistent execution.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Palo Alto Gardens)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Palo Alto Gardens is an affordable housing community managed by MidPen Housing, a non-profit with over 50 years of experience and one of the larger affordable portfolios in Northern California. This Assistant Community Manager role sits squarely in the operational center of the property. You'll handle income verifications, lease prep, waitlist maintenance, and rent collection. You'll process turns, monitor turnover forms, and coordinate with facilities staff to keep work orders moving. Compliance work is a real part of this job: re-certifications, MOR prep, TCAC reviews, welfare exemption documents. If you've worked affordable housing before, you know that compliance is not a once-a-year event. It's a steady drumbeat.

Resident relations are woven through all of it. You'll issue notices, communicate emergency procedures, and coordinate logistics for resident meetings. You'll also maintain resident and property files with appropriate confidentiality and support relationships with local law enforcement and emergency agencies when needed. The reporting line is directly to the Community Manager.

One genuine advantage of the affordable housing side of our industry: the compliance framework gives new managers a structured way to build their skills. Tax credit and HUD requirements teach you documentation discipline that transfers well to any property type later. It's not glamorous, but it builds real competency.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Proficiency in MS Office; familiarity with RealPage is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with genuine follow-through
  • Ability to work independently and stay organized without someone checking over your shoulder
  • Comfort with the compliance demands of affordable housing, specifically tax credit and HUD regulatory environments
  • Multilingual skills in Mandarin, Russian, or Spanish are preferred and likely useful given the resident community
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable housing and community stability

Context Worth Knowing

The pay range is $21.15 to $23.80 hourly, based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options for childcare, medical, and commuter expenses, an employee education reimbursement program, an EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days. This is a non-profit employer, so the 403(b) structure is standard here rather than a 401(k).

Candidates who do well in affordable housing operations tend to have genuine patience for process and a resident-centered orientation that isn't performative. The compliance side of this work rewards people who find satisfaction in getting details right the first time. If you're coming from conventional market-rate housing and haven't worked with TCAC or HUD regulatory frameworks before, expect a learning curve on the compliance piece. It's manageable, but it's real.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (HVAC Required)- Olympus Fenwick
job.description:
Olympus Fenwick in Savannah, GA is adding a Maintenance Technician to the service team. This is a full-time, site-based role covering the standard Monday through Friday schedule with emergency on-call availability folded in. The pay range runs $24 to $25 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility on top of that.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of your day will look familiar if you've worked residential maintenance before: working through the service request queue, completing turns, handling preventative maintenance on HVAC units, and fielding the occasional after-hours emergency. HVAC is the non-negotiable here. Coil cleaning, filter changes, and full diagnostic work on units are expected skills, not things you'll learn on the property's dime.

Beyond HVAC, the role covers a wide scope of general maintenance: plumbing repairs and fixture replacement (sinks, showers, toilets), appliance troubleshooting and replacement across the standard kitchen and laundry lineup, electrical fixture and switch work, lock changes and door hardware, and basic carpentry and painting. You'll also support grounds and common area upkeep, including pools, and keep the maintenance shop organized and properly inventoried. Service requests are tracked in software, so comfort with basic digital tools is part of the job.

You'll work directly with the Lead Maintenance Technician on daily and weekly priorities, which keeps the workload structured rather than reactive. That said, emergencies don't schedule themselves, and weekend availability is part of the agreement.

What You Bring

  • Minimum two years of maintenance experience in residential, apartment, or commercial settings
  • EPA/HVAC certification (preferred, and genuinely expected given the role's focus)
  • Working knowledge across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and painting
  • Availability for the Monday through Friday schedule and emergency call coverage

The Broader Picture

Savannah's rental market has seen consistent demand, which means properties need service teams that can hold occupancy through responsive maintenance. Resident retention has a direct relationship with how quickly and cleanly work orders get closed. A technician who can handle HVAC competently, keep the shop tight, and communicate well with the office team will have more impact on the property's performance than the role title might suggest.

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years. The benefits package is genuinely competitive for the industry: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and sabbatical eligibility among others. For a technician looking to build a long-term career rather than just fill a slot, there's real infrastructure here for growth.

job.title: Field Support Supervisor - Multifamily Regional Maintenance
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operating for over 70 years, which matters more than it might sound. Self-managed, vertically integrated ownership means decisions don't run through a five-layer approval chain, and the people doing the work are accountable to the same company that cuts the checks. They own and operate apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. This role sits within their Asset Management and Support team and covers the Dallas-Fort Worth portfolio.

The Field Support Supervisor title is accurate to what the job actually is: field-heavy, regional, and technical. You're out on properties regularly, not reviewing reports from a home office. The work involves assessing maintenance operations across multiple communities, helping site teams prioritize and scope projects, evaluating vendors, and managing capex work from bid to completion. You'll also help bridge the gap when the Construction Group hands a project off to the property team, which is one of the more genuinely useful things a regional support person can do. That transition is where documentation falls apart and institutional knowledge gets lost. Doing it well requires someone who can read a set of blueprints and also explain what's on them to a maintenance tech who's never seen a set before.

The technical depth here is real. Weinstein is specifically looking for experience with exterior building repairs, water intrusion, erosion issues, and the ability to write coherent work requirements. Vendor management is a meaningful part of the job. You're not just approving invoices. You're evaluating scope, pushing back on cost reasonableness, and actively recruiting quality contractors to bid projects, which in a competitive DFW market takes more effort than it used to.

The strongest candidates in this kind of role are the ones who've been the person on-site long enough to know what maintenance teams actually need versus what they say they need, and who've also spent enough time on the regional side to translate that into project scope and vendor accountability. EPA Universal certification (or at minimum Type I and II) is required, along with a valid driver's license and five or more years of hands-on multifamily maintenance experience, at least three of which in a regional or multi-site support capacity.

What separates a good regional maintenance supervisor from a great one is usually vendor relationships and credibility with site staff. If technicians and service managers don't trust your read on a problem, the support role breaks down fast. This position requires both.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of multifamily maintenance experience, with 3+ years in a regional or multi-site support role
  • EPA certification, Type I and II or Universal
  • Hands-on experience with capital projects: exterior repairs, water intrusion, erosion, blueprint reading, and writing work scopes
  • Working knowledge of job site safety requirements
  • Valid driver's license

Weinstein offers competitive compensation, benefits, and a 401k. Given the structure of the organization, this role also carries real visibility with asset management leadership, which tends to matter for people who want to grow into broader operational or construction oversight responsibilities over time.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners runs nearly 50,000 apartment homes across the Southeast, and the Assistant Community Manager role at Hawthorne Palmetto in Simpsonville, SC is where you'll feel the full weight of that operation at the property level. This is a working role. You'll be in the leasing office handling traffic, following up on delinquency, reviewing ledgers, and covering for the Community Manager when she's out. The job has real range, and that's both the appeal and the honest challenge of it.

On any given day you might run a leasing tour in the morning, spend part of the afternoon on payment posting and ledger audits, then de-escalate a resident complaint before the office closes. The financial side is real work: rent collection, check scanning, delinquency tracking with weekly follow-up calls, and supporting eviction procedures when it gets to that point. It won't always get to that point, but you need to be comfortable with it when it does. Renewals, lease document accuracy, and occupancy goals are yours to own alongside the Community Manager.

Hawthorne leans into internal growth. Their Career Path Program is a real part of how they develop staff, and the ACM seat is explicitly positioned as the step before Community Manager. If you want to get to the CM chair, this role builds the habits that get you there: financial literacy at the property level, confident conflict resolution, and the ability to hold a team together when leadership is absent.

What the role calls for

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager capacity preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus, not a requirement

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturdays from 10 to 4. One weekday off keeps it to 40 hours, but resident events and community needs can shift things occasionally. That's standard for this work and worth knowing upfront.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, a 401k match, paid time off including your birthday, pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance. Telehealth access is included as well.

Strong candidates here tend to be people who already understand the rhythm of a multifamily office, know how to read a resident ledger without needing a tutorial, and don't freeze when a situation gets tense. The leasing piece matters, but the financial and administrative side is what separates a capable ACM from one who's still figuring it out six months in.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing leasing moves at a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. The academic calendar drives everything: your busiest periods cluster around fall move-in, spring renewals, and summer turn, and the residents you're working with often have parents involved in the decision, roommate dynamics to sort out, and zero prior renting experience. Scion operates Copper Beech Harrisonburg on Virginia's James Madison University corridor, and this Experience Team Member role sits at the center of that resident relationship from first tour to ongoing community life.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A good chunk of your week involves direct resident and prospect interaction: touring the community, answering questions about floor plans and amenities, and following up with people who haven't committed yet. You'll also help management understand where deals are getting stuck, so your observations on objections and pricing friction genuinely matter here. Beyond leasing, you'll assist with resident engagement programming, contribute to social media content, and handle operational tasks like package logging, office upkeep, and coordinating maintenance request follow-through. There's an on-call rotation that includes after-hours lockout assistance, so flexibility isn't optional.

Summer and turn periods deserve a specific mention. Student housing communities can see most of their resident population turn over in a matter of weeks. During those windows, the pace is compressed and the coordination required is real. If you've worked retail or hospitality during a holiday rush, you have some frame of reference, though the physical and logistical scale of a turn is its own thing.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Someone who genuinely enjoys talking to people across a wide range of backgrounds, including both students and their families
  • Strong communicators who can shift tone depending on whether they're texting a prospect, posting on Instagram, or explaining a lease policy to a concerned parent
  • People who stay organized under variable workloads, because quiet weeks and chaotic weeks can follow each other quickly
  • Candidates available for weekend hours and key seasonal periods including turn

Growth and Team Fit

Experience Team Members who develop a feel for both the sales and operational sides of this role often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions as they build tenure. Student housing is a distinct specialty, and people who understand the academic-calendar-driven leasing cycle carry that knowledge into any future multifamily role. Scion offers learning reimbursement, which signals that internal development is something the company actually invests in rather than just lists on a job posting. This position is full-time, non-exempt, and based on-site at Copper Beech Harrisonburg.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Lake View
job.description:
A prospect walks into the leasing office at Lake View on a Tuesday afternoon, having already toured two other buildings that morning. What you say, how you show the space, and how quickly you follow up afterward will determine whether Reside Living gets that lease or not. That's the core of this role.

The Work Itself

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago, with this position focused on properties in East Lake View and Gold Coast. Both are high-demand neighborhoods where occupancy expectations are real and traffic needs to convert. You'll handle the full leasing cycle: responding to inquiries by phone, text, and email; scheduling and conducting tours; recording every touchpoint in the CRM; and closing applications in compliance with fair housing law, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and all applicable state and federal regulations.

Beyond the direct leasing work, you'll physically inspect vacant units and common areas, flag anything that needs attention from maintenance, and help coordinate resident events. You'll also run monthly audits of the property's online presence, looking for gaps in how the building shows up in search, on ILS platforms, and in reviews. Findings go directly to the Property Manager, and Reside Living expects consultants to bring ideas, not just observations.

Daily and weekly reporting is part of the job. You'll track your own numbers closely, because the path to earning commission and quarterly bonuses runs through your ability to hit and hold occupancy targets.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

You need to bring at least one year of leasing or sales experience, strong written and verbal communication, and a working knowledge of Microsoft Office and a property management platform like Yardi. Attention to detail and follow-through aren't optional here: a missed callback or a sloppy CRM entry can cost a lease.

What the role builds is more interesting. Leasing consultants at Reside Living have a stated path into property management and leadership. You'll start developing the NOI awareness and occupancy management instincts that property managers use every day. Strong performers here learn to read their own traffic trends, adjust marketing strategy in real time, and build the kind of resident relationships that reduce turnover. Those skills transfer directly upward.

Candidates who stand out tend to already understand that leasing is a sales role with a service component baked in permanently. The follow-up after the tour matters as much as the tour itself. The best consultants treat every prospect touchpoint as part of a longer conversion process, not a one-time pitch.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum one year of leasing or sales experience
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable CRM platform preferred
  • Personal smartphone required (iPhone or Android); $50/month stipend provided

Compensation includes a base salary plus commission and quarterly bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and life insurance, paid time off, 401(k) matching, a commuter benefit, a 25% monthly apartment discount, and $100 per month in student loan assistance.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
You're on a call at 8 a.m. reviewing last month's T-12 for a property that missed NOI targets, and by noon you're walking a site with a community manager who needs coaching on leasing follow-up. That's a Regional Manager's day at Asset Living. The role covers the full range, and it moves fast.

What This Role Covers

Asset Living is a third-party management firm, and this Regional Manager position oversees a portfolio of multifamily communities in the Atlanta market. You're the offsite leader accountable for operations, personnel, financial performance, leasing strategy, and compliance across every property in your book.

On the personnel side, you screen, hire, coach, and develop on-site staff. You handle counseling documentation, performance management, and terminations when necessary. You approve timesheets and salary requests, and you work directly with HR and senior leadership when situations escalate.

Financially, you build and own the yearly operating budgets. You track income and expense variances monthly, write evaluations when line items drift off-budget, and flag capex needs before they become emergencies. You also oversee vendor contracts, invoice coding, and deposit reconciliation to keep each property's financials clean at closeout.

Leasing strategy falls to you as well. You develop annual marketing plans, sharpen site-level leasing techniques, and monitor conversion and follow-up across your portfolio. Resident retention programs, including events and outreach, are part of the mix. So is handling escalated resident complaints when on-site staff can't resolve them.

On the administrative and maintenance side, you conduct regular property inspections, monitor service request turnaround, and make sure punch list items get closed. You coordinate emergency response procedures and ensure your teams follow company guidelines when something goes wrong on-site.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a multifamily portfolio as a regional or multi-site leader
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial statements, including budget-to-actual variance analysis
  • Experience developing site-level staff, including performance documentation and HR coordination
  • Solid working knowledge of fair housing regulations and risk management practices
  • Ability to manage multiple community managers and keep each site accountable without micromanaging

Because Asset Living operates as a third-party management company, regional managers here often oversee properties with different ownership groups, asset classes, and reporting expectations simultaneously. Candidates who have worked in fee management environments adapt faster than those who've only managed in-house portfolios. That context matters when you're presenting ownership reports and fielding client calls alongside your day-to-day operations work.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing operates on a rhythm that most multifamily professionals never experience. The lease-up timeline compresses into a single academic calendar, traffic spikes in waves tied to housing fairs and move-in weekends, and the resident population turns over almost entirely once a year. If you want to understand leasing fundamentals under real pressure, this is a strong place to start.

What You'll Actually Do

Scion's Experience Team Member role at Redpoint Tuscaloosa sits at the intersection of leasing, marketing, and customer service. Day to day, you're giving property tours, fielding prospect questions, and handling the back-and-forth communication that moves someone from curious to signed. You'll also support social media content, help plan and run resident engagement events, and flag what's working (and what isn't) in terms of sales conversations and objections. On the administrative side, expect package management, office upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and rotating after-hours on-call coverage including lockouts. Turn periods at student properties are dense, fast, and require everyone on the team to show up ready to execute.

What You Bring

  • A genuine comfort with talking to people from different backgrounds, in person and online
  • Reliability and self-discipline, especially during high-volume periods like summer and Turn
  • Flexibility to work evenings, holidays, and rotating on-call shifts as the schedule demands
  • Strong organizational habits that hold up when the office gets busy
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Where This Role Takes You

The skills you build here transfer directly into roles like leasing manager, assistant community manager, or marketing coordinator at conventional multifamily properties. Student housing teaches you to close under urgency, communicate across a wide demographic, and manage operations during one of the most logistically demanding events in property management: a full community turn. Operators in Class A garden-style and mid-rise communities actively recruit people with student housing backgrounds because of that experience. The ETM position at Scion is a legitimate entry point into a career track, not just a leasing job. Candidates who advance quickly tend to be the ones who treat every resident interaction as a data point, actively report what's slowing down conversions, and take the on-call rotation seriously rather than treating it as an inconvenience.

job.title: Paint & resurface tech
job.description:
The make-ready cycle is where resident impressions get set, and a sloppy paint job or a bubbling countertop resurface will undermine everything else the team did right on that turn. Karya Property Management is building out the maintenance side of their residential portfolio in Phoenix and adding a dedicated Paint and Resurface Technician to keep that work consistent and in-house.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your time will split between unit turns and ongoing property upkeep. On a turn, you're prepping surfaces, patching holes and cracks, sanding, priming, and laying down finish coats on interior walls and trim. You'll also handle countertop and cabinet resurfacing, which is the kind of work that significantly changes how a unit photographs and how it feels to a prospective resident walking in. Exterior surfaces come into the rotation too, so you're not confined to unit interiors.

Beyond the turn work, you'll coordinate with the broader maintenance and property management teams to schedule jobs and move efficiently across properties. That scheduling piece matters more than it sounds. A tech who can sequence prep, cure times, and resurfacing work without holding up a unit goes-live date is genuinely valuable. Phoenix heat affects dry times and material behavior, so knowing how to adjust application technique in high temperatures is a real skill here.

What Karya Is Looking For

  • Prior experience in painting and surface resurfacing, residential preferred
  • Familiarity with different finishes, application techniques, and appropriate materials for various surfaces
  • Detail orientation and consistent workmanship quality
  • Ability to manage your own schedule and work independently across sites
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Clear communication with maintenance coordinators and property teams

Karya offers health and wellness benefits, PTO, and maternity and paternity leave. The role includes the standard safety protocol expectations that come with any maintenance position.

One honest note: techs who do this work well tend to become indispensable on any maintenance team, because consistent, quality paint and resurface output is hard to find and easy to notice when it's missing. It's a role with a clear path toward senior maintenance or facilities coordination for someone who wants to grow.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Lake Ridge Ridge
job.description:
It's 6:30 p.m. on a Tuesday. Residents are getting home from work, dogs need walking, and the valet trash window is open. Your route needs to run clean and on time, because in multifamily, the details residents notice most are the ones that happen right outside their front door.

What the Role Actually Involves

Cortland is hiring a Front Door Waste Technician at their Lake Ridge community in Hilliard, OH. This is a valet trash position, which means you're running a nightly collection route through the property, picking up resident waste bags set outside unit doors, loading them into leak-proof carts, and transporting everything to the onsite compactors or waste containers. You'll also clear trash from dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, parking lots, and common areas throughout the property.

The job has a real physical component. You're climbing stairs, covering ground on foot, and lifting up to 50 pounds through the full shift. Outdoor work in all weather is part of it, and so is the occasional strong odor. That's just the reality of the role. If you've worked in waste services or a service-focused job before, you already know what you're signing up for.

Cortland tracks route completion through a mobile app. You'll log start and end times, document your work with photos, and flag any improper or prohibited waste you encounter. Staying visible on property and communicating clearly with residents and staff is a daily expectation, not an afterthought. This is a resident-facing position, and how you carry yourself matters.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • At least one year of experience in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations for waste handling
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual ability is a plus
  • Ability to operate basic equipment, including compactors
  • Valid driver's license for local driving as needed
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan for app-based reporting
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk long distances, and lift up to 50 lbs throughout a shift

What separates the candidates who stick around in this role from those who don't is consistency. Routes run five or more nights a week. Residents notice immediately when service slips, and property managers notice too. Reliability, a professional attitude with residents, and attention to site cleanliness are the things that actually matter here day to day.

Cortland is a large, vertically integrated multifamily operator, founded in 2005 and ranked among the top ten multifamily owners in the country. They run their own design, construction, and operations, which means their properties tend to be actively managed with clear standards. For the right person, this kind of environment offers stability and a defined set of expectations, which can be easier to succeed in than a loosely run smaller operation.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, with more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity doesn't happen by accident. It reflects a consistent commitment to how people are treated, both residents and employees. This Assistant Property Manager role in Henrico's West End sits at the center of that philosophy.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

This role touches nearly every part of community life. In the morning, you might be responding to internet leads and scheduling tours. By midday, you're walking a make-ready unit with maintenance to confirm it's truly move-in ready. The afternoon could bring a lease renewal conversation, a security deposit disposition, or helping a resident work through an account question. No two days stack up the same way.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Working with prospective residents from first contact through lease signing, including phone and internet inquiries, tours, applications, and paperwork
  • Providing ongoing resident support: renewals, notices to vacate, transfers, pet addendums, work order follow-ups, and general account questions
  • Posting rent, tracking balances, and following up on amounts owed
  • Coordinating with maintenance on unit readiness and property upkeep
  • Processing move-outs and handling security deposit dispositions
  • Planning and hosting resident events
  • Supporting the Property Manager and helping train and lead the on-site team

Saturday hours are part of the schedule, worked on a rotating basis with the team. Occasionally, resident events or weather situations will ask something extra of you. That's the nature of on-site property management, and Weinstein is straightforward about it.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

Prior property management experience is a plus, but Weinstein genuinely recruits from hospitality, sales, and customer service backgrounds. If you've managed people or handled difficult customer situations with composure, the leasing and operations knowledge can be taught. What's harder to teach is the ability to hold a conversation with a frustrated resident, de-escalate without getting defensive, and then pivot to showing a prospective resident the community with genuine warmth. That's the real skill set this role demands.

Strong candidates tend to be organized without being rigid. They keep the punch list moving on a make-ready while also catching an incoming call and not making either person feel like they're second priority. Attention to detail matters here because mistakes on lease paperwork or security deposit dispositions create real problems downstream. Leadership experience is required because this role carries real responsibility for team outcomes, not just individual tasks.

Growth and Company Culture

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. Many of their current leaders started in leasing or assistant roles. The training program here is structured and intentional, so if you're newer to property management, you won't be left to figure things out on your own. The company wants this to be a career you grow into over time, which shows up in how they invest in coaching and professional development at the site level.

Compensation starts at $21 per hour, increases with experience, and includes quarterly bonuses. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, an employee assistance program, and a rent discount.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Part-Time)
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, having toured three other communities that week. They're tired, they're skeptical, and they haven't signed anywhere. What happens in the next thirty minutes depends entirely on you.

That's the central skill this part-time leasing consultant role at Berkshire Residential Investments builds, day after day: reading people quickly, earning trust, and converting genuine interest into a signed lease. Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means the team you join has real stake in outcomes. This isn't third-party management where directives come from a distant asset manager. The people above you in the org chart care about occupancy and resident satisfaction for the same reasons you will.

What the Work Actually Involves

Your primary job is guiding prospective residents from curiosity to commitment. Berkshire holds consultants to a closing ratio of at least 20%, which is a real benchmark that keeps you honest about your sales technique. Beyond the close, you'll maintain tour routes and model units so they consistently make the right first impression, track local market conditions so your pitches stay grounded in reality, and handle resident communications with enough professionalism that people feel heard rather than processed. Administrative accuracy matters here, because leasing paperwork done sloppily creates downstream problems for the whole team.

You'll also contribute ideas on marketing and resident satisfaction to the property manager. That collaboration matters more than it sounds. Consultants who pay attention to what objections come up repeatedly, or which concessions actually move traffic, bring real operational value beyond their closing numbers.

What You're Building Toward

Part-time leasing roles are often where strong property management careers start, and for good reason. The skills compound fast.
