The leasing consultant role sits at the front edge of a property's revenue. Every lease signed, every prospect converted, every renewal retained flows through this position first. At Karya Property Management's Portland-area community, that responsibility belongs to you.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day centers on converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting prospects, walking them through the property, and presenting the community's features in a way that connects to what they're actually looking for in a home. You'll explain lease terms clearly, including the TAA Lease Contract, so future residents understand exactly what they're signing before move-in day arrives.

Beyond the initial sale, you'll coordinate move-in packets, prepare units, and manage the day-of experience for incoming residents. You'll also do at least one full property walk daily to assess curb appeal and flag anything that needs attention before a prospect sees it. Resident events and marketing coordination fall into this role as well, so there's a creative side alongside the sales work.

Weekend and evening availability on a rotating schedule is part of the job. Leasing traffic doesn't follow a Monday-through-Friday pattern, and the strongest consultants treat weekend shifts as opportunities rather than inconveniences.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; a college degree is preferred
  • Clear, confident verbal and written communication skills
  • Strong customer service instincts with residents, prospects, and vendors
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Word, and Outlook
  • A sense of urgency and the ability to manage competing deadlines
  • Physical ability to walk the property daily, climb stairs, and lift up to 15 pounds

Skills This Role Builds

A leasing consultant role is where most property management careers start, and for good reason. You'll develop a working command of lease administration, fair housing compliance, and the full prospect-to-resident lifecycle. The objection-handling and closing skills you build here translate directly into assistant manager and property manager roles, where leasing performance becomes one of several metrics you're responsible for rather than your primary focus. Consultants who learn to read traffic patterns, track their own closing ratios, and take ownership of curb appeal tend to move up faster because they're already thinking like operators.

What separates a strong candidate here is the ability to hold a genuine conversation with a prospect while staying accurate on lease terms and community details. The sales piece matters, but residents who feel well-informed at move-in create fewer headaches down the line and renew at higher rates. If you bring that combination of warmth and precision, this is a solid place to build the foundation of a property management career.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - Verdant Peachtree Creek
job.description:
Maintenance work in multifamily housing covers a wide range of skill levels, and this role at AIR Communities' Verdant Peachtree Creek community in Atlanta sits squarely in the hands-on technical tier. You'll carry out resident service requests, complete turns to get units ready for incoming residents, and handle routine upkeep across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry. The expectation is that you're already proficient in at least two of those trades and can move through work orders independently with general direction rather than constant supervision.

What this role builds on top of that foundation is real breadth. Because community needs shift by season and by what mechanical systems are in play, you won't spend every week doing the same two tasks. One stretch might be weighted toward HVAC as summer leasing ramps up; another might call for more appliance work and punch list completion during a turn cycle. Technicians who stay curious about the trades they're weaker in tend to develop faster here than those who stay in their lane.

AIR uses technology to manage task flow and prioritization, which means you'll work with digital tools to track and close out work orders rather than relying on paper logs or verbal handoffs. That's worth knowing if you're coming from a smaller operation where systems were informal. The upside is that organized shops and stocked supplies are part of the model, so you spend less time hunting for parts and more time actually fixing things.

The role pays $23.00 to $26.00 per hour depending on your experience and trade skill level, and there's a quarterly customer service bonus structure that can add up to $250 per month for technicians who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores. A 50% rent discount at any AIR community is also available, which matters if you want to eliminate your commute by living onsite.

What you'll need coming in

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in two or more trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry
  • Willingness to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (roughly one week per month)
  • Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency response
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery as needed

One thing worth understanding about on-call in multifamily: it's not decorative. Residents call when something fails, and that includes nights and weekends. If you've done on-call before, you already know how to triage what's urgent versus what can wait until morning. If you haven't, that judgment develops quickly and it's one of the more transferable skills this role gives you, applicable at any property type or ownership structure you work for later in your career.

AIR's internal development program, Ascend, is designed to map a path forward based on where you want to go, whether that's a lead technician role, a service manager position, or something more specialized. The company has a stated preference for internal promotion, so the ceiling here is higher than the job title suggests.
